articles.title: Future Call of Duty Modern Warfare game could be set in Sydney - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Australia could become the setting for a future Call of Duty game according to a key game design director who has just landed in Sydney ahead of the launch of Modern Warfare 4.
“It’s such a stunning and beautiful city,” says Alex Norris, Associate Design Director at Infinity Ward – the developer behind the Call of Duty Modern Warfare games.
“I cannot go anywhere without looking at the surroundings and thinking about how to have combat in those surroundings – so you never know.
“At a minimum there would be some inspired elements but yeah, absolutely. Definitely a possibility.”
Norris is part of the Infinity Ward team that has shaped the memorable Call of Duty campaigns for more than a decade but he says Modern Warfare 4 takes a different approach.
“The thing I think is really separating it from Modern Warfare 1, 2, and 3 is that we’ve gone a bit back to our Call of Duty roots with this one,” Norris told Tech Guide.
“It really touches back into the infantry perspective, the grunt cog-in-the-machine approach.
“A lot of the previous Modern Warfare games were really about smaller directed raids going after terrorists in small townhouses or chasing them into the mountains.
“This is a bit of a change-up in that now we’re answering and resolving the storyline of Price and the things that happened to him, pushing the line wherever he needed it, and seeing how that kind of came to a head in Modern Warfare 3, reinvigorating the franchise by bringing us back to our Modern Warfare with a touch of infantry roots.
“We’ve got our grounded perspective from our South Korean grunts mixed in with U.S. Marines, that’s kind of our big swing on this one.”
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 goes on sale on October 23.

articles.title: Belkin's new SureFind Bluetooth tracker range can quickly locate your belongings - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Belkin has launched a new lineup of Bluetooth trackers to help customers locate their belongings whether they’re using an iPhone or an Android device.
Belkin’s SureFind collection consists of three products: the SureFind Spot, SureFind Card, and SureFind Loop Cable Tag.
And every product in the range works with Apple’s Find My and Google’s Find Hub so you’ll be able to locate what’s important to you no matter what smartphone you’re using.
Each device features audio alerts through the built-in speakers so you can find nearby items faster, while left-behind reminders can alert you if you and your phone are leaving your belongings behind.
And they can also be tracked on the Find My app on iPhones and the Find Hub app on Google devices.
SUREFIND SPOT BLUETOOTH TRACKER – $29.95, $54.95 (2 Pack), $99.95 (3 Pack)
The SureFind Spot Tracker is compact and small enough to attach to keys, backpacks, and luggage, along with other belongings that you may misplace.
Spot can help you find the things you’re looking for when you need them most.
SureFind Spot key features include:
– Works with Apple Find My and Google’s Find Hub on Apple and Android devices
– Easily locate keys, bags, luggage and everyday items from your smartphone
– Built-in loop and included lanyard attach easily without an extra holder
– Loud audio alert helps find nearby belongings fast
– Left-behind reminders help prevent loss before it happens
– Up to 12 months of battery life with replaceable battery
– Water-resistant design for everyday carry
– Made with 85% recycled plastic
SUREFIND CARD BLUETOOTH TRACKER – $44.95
The SureFind Card tracker is ideal to fit into wallets, passport holders, and other slim carry items. It has an IP68 rating and all the same features as the other SureFind trackers to ensure you and your belongings are not separated.
SureFind Card key features include:
– Works with Apple Find My and Google’s Find Hub on Apple and Android devices
– Ultra-slim design fits easily into wallets, passports and bags
– Included strap offers flexible attachment to luggage and everyday essentials
– Loud audio alert helps find nearby belongings fast
– Left-behind reminders help prevent loss before it happens
– IP68-rated for water and dust resistance
– Up to 3 years of battery life
– Made with plant-based bioplastic
SUREFIND LOOP CABLE TAG RECHARGEABLE BLUETOOTH TRACKER – $44.95
The SureFind Loop cable tag combines two essentials into one.
First, it contains item tracking technology and second, it has a built-in USB-C to USB-C charging cable.
It’s also secure enough to attach to luggage, backpacks, and handbags and can also be used as a charging cable whenever you need it.
SureFind Loop Cable Tag key features include:
– Works with Apple Find My and Google’s Find Hub for broad compatibility
– Hidden 2-in-1 braided USB-C cable doubles as a secure carry loop
– Easily attaches to keys, bags, luggage and everyday essentials
– Loud audio alert helps find nearby belongings fast
– Left-behind reminders help prevent loss before it happens
– Up to 4-month battery life per charge
– IPX4-rated water-resistant design for everyday carry
– Made with 85% recycled plastic
Pricing and Availability
The SureFind Collection is available now on belkin.com/au, Amazon and at JB Hi-Fi. 
SureFind Spot is available in Black and White for $29.95 (Single). $54.95 (White, 2-pack). $99.95 (White, 4-pack).
SureFind Card is available in Black and White for $44.95
SureFind Loop Cable Tag is available in Black and White for $44.95

articles.title: L’Europe part aussi à la conquête de la Lune : voici OASIS, la future “station-service” de l’ESA sur notre satellite
articles.text:
L’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA) ne compte pas regarder passer la course à la Lune. Elle prépare sa propre infrastructure, pensée avec des briques européennes de bout en bout.
Alors que la Chine et les États-Unis se tirent la bourre pour implanter la toute première base lunaire permanente, le rôle que jouera l’Europe dans cette conquête est plus que jamais remis en question. Jared Isaacman, patron de la NASA, a été clair : personne n’est garanti d’être partenaire, même s’il s’agit d’alliés de longue date. Dans ce contexte, l’ESA dégaine sa propre carte.
À quoi va servir OASIS, exactement ?
L’agence spatiale vient en effet de présenter OASIS, pour « Outpost for Advanced Scientific Investigation Station », une « station-service » lunaire. Son rôle : fournir l’énergie, les communications et le stockage de données dont les instruments ont besoin pour travailler sur le sol lunaire pendant de très longues périodes, et cela inclut la nuit.
Or, privée de Soleil et soumise à un froid extrême, l’électronique peut y être gravement endommagée. OASIS doit donc capter l’énergie solaire le jour et la stocker dans une batterie. « Il permettra aux charges utiles de fonctionner pendant des années à la surface de la Lune, en activité pendant les jours lunaires et en mode veille pendant les nuits lunaires », étaye l'agence.
Elle annonce des capacités d’au moins 75 W en continu le jour et 15 W la nuit. De quoi permettre aux ingénieurs derrière ces dispositifs scientifiques de se concentrer « presque exclusivement » à leur technologie sans se soucier des systèmes énergétiques lourds pour les accompagner.
Une chaîne européenne
L’idée n’est pas totalement neuve. Elle prolonge celle de l’ALSEP, ce dispositif d’Apollo, lorsque des instruments reliés à une station centrale continuaient à transmettre après le départ des astronautes. OASIS transpose ce principe à l’exploration robotique, avec une infrastructure partagée capable de soutenir plusieurs charges utiles en même temps. L’une des premières envisagées s’appelle ECHO. Cet observatoire étudierait l’environnement lunaire tout en testant l’infrastructure.
Et l'ESA mise sur une chaîne d'approvisionnement totalement européenne. Ainsi, OASIS voyagerait à bord de l’atterrisseur Argonaut, propulsé par une Ariane 6 équipée de quatre boosters. Une fois sur place, les données seront relayées vers la Terre par l’infrastructure Moonlight de l’ESA, en commençant par le satellite Lunar Pathfinder.
L’agence a sélectionné l’allemand OHB pour mener les études de faisabilité et de définition préliminaire. Après une revue des exigences lancée cet été, la configuration de référence associe une station dotée d’un panneau solaire et une unité de batterie séparée. On en reste toutefois au stade des études : aucune date de lancement ni aucun budget n’ont été annoncés.
Autonome et modulaire, la station pourrait évoluer pour ensuite soutenir des instruments plus éloignés de l’atterrisseur. Elle pourrait même offrir un abri aux rovers pour la nuit, faisant office « garage lunaire ». Objectif : poser les bases d’une science et d’une exploration durables sur la Lune.

articles.title: “Nothing has to be”: New York mayor Zohran Mamdani tells citizens to fight back against the AI doom and gloom
articles.text:
“Nothing has to be”: New York mayor Zohran Mamdani tells citizens to fight back against the AI doom and gloom
Not enough is being done to regulate AI, Mamdani says
- Mayor Zohran Mamdani has urged New Yorkers to push back against AI
- He says there has been a 'complete abdication of federal law' when it comes to regulating the technology
- Mamdani has banned AI use in some schools in New York and has banned AI from being used to generate images on property listings
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani has urged city residents to push back against the doom and gloom feelings around AI, telling them that “Nothing has to be.”
Speaking at The People’s AI Assembly, hosted by the AI Now Institute in Webster Hall, Manhattan, Mamdani noted there has been a “reckless adoption of technology without any kind of a reckoning with the limitations of that technology.”
“There’s a creep that comes with this, and there’s an intent to overwhelm that leaves people feeling as if there is simply no option,” Mamdani said.
“Reckless adoption of technology”
Federal regulations on AI are few and far between, and are failing to keep pace with the technology, prompting widespread worry that AI will replace jobs and harm education for both New Yorkers and people around the world.
Mamdani’s comment centers around how AI technology is being relentlessly pushed into products, services, education, and elsewhere with people having very little say in how it is used.
Schools were a particular sticking point for the conversation on AI. Mamdani recently introduced a ban on AI use in elementary and middle schools after the technology began creeping its way into classrooms. Actress and activist Ilana Glazer, interviewing Mamdani, said, “It just makes me nervous. It feels so non-consensual, as though…this has to be in schools. It wasn’t two years ago. Why does it have to be in schools?”
AI is also having an impact on schools in other ways. Speaking on the reckless adoption of AI, Mamdani referenced the US military’s use of an AI targeting tool that was involved in a strike on a school in Iran earlier this year that killed over 150 people including at least 123 children. A subsequent Pentagon investigation found that overreliance on AI tools was a factor in the deadly strike.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
President Trump has pushed forward with an AI at any cost rhetoric framed as an arms race against China, with the President arguing that any attempts to regulate AI could cost the US its lead. “There is this desire to speak about [AI] as if it is infallible, as if it cannot be questioned, as if the only people who can regulate it are the ones who are currently developing it,” Mamdani said.
“What it really is, is an attempt to escape any kind of accountability at any level, without also jeopardizing the potential valuation from an IPO.”
Anthropic is set to enter the public markets before the end of 2026, with OpenAI looking to make the same move in 2027. Both companies have been involved in hacking incidents where AI agents undergoing testing have escaped sandboxes and breached other companies. These incidents have been labelled as ‘rogue’ behavior, despite evidence from investigations suggesting the AI agents were behaving exactly as intended.
The use of the word ‘rogue’ has also been questioned by experts, with Tenable Field CTO Bernard Montel saying the use of the word “muddies the public policy debate by distracting regulators from enforcing strict legal liability for flawed software deployments.”
Despite these events, little movement has been made to introduce regulations, which Mamdani labelled as a “complete abdication of federal law.”
“As we are looking at what comes after this federal administration, there has to be a very different kind of framework in how we think about AI, talk about AI, the accountability we’re willing to bring forward when it comes to that,” he said.

articles.title: Des pirates détournent des NAS D-Link et des enregistreurs Ubiquiti pour gagner de l'argent avec votre connexion Internet
articles.text:
Des cybercriminels exploitent des failles connues pour transformer des équipements connectés en relais Internet rémunérés. Une campagne qui menace aussi la réputation des adresses IP des victimes, susceptibles de servir à d'autres activités malveillantes.
Des pirates ont trouvé un moyen de rentabiliser leurs intrusions sans voler de données ni réclamer de rançon. Leur méthode consiste à détourner des équipements connectés à Internet pour y installer un logiciel de partage de bande passante et tenter d'en tirer des revenus. Une campagne de proxyjacking sur laquelle les chercheurs en cybersécurité de GreyNoise ont enquêté, révélant la compromission d'au moins 143 appareils dans 34 pays, dont des NAS et des systèmes de vidéosurveillance.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Des vulnérabilités connues exploitées pour installer un logiciel légitime
Pour prendre le contrôle des appareils, les pirates se sont appuyés sur plusieurs vulnérabilités déjà documentées. Sur les NAS D-Link ShareCenter, ils ont notamment exploité les failles CVE-2024-3272 et CVE-2024-3273, qui permettent, lorsqu'elles sont combinées, de contourner l'authentification et d'exécuter des commandes à distance.
Les enregistreurs vidéo Ubiquiti UniFi Video ont quant à eux été compromis à travers Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228), une vulnérabilité critique découverte fin 2021. Les chercheurs ont également identifié l'exploitation de la faille CVE-2025-31324 dans SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer, ainsi que des tentatives visant des systèmes de vidéosurveillance Hikvision et Dahua, sans pouvoir préciser les vulnérabilités utilisées dans ces derniers cas.
Une fois les équipements compromis, les attaquants y ont installé Pawns.app, un logiciel légitime conçu pour rémunérer les internautes qui acceptent de partager leur connexion Internet. Le principe repose sur un réseau de proxys résidentiels, dans lequel le trafic de clients tiers transite par les appareils participants. Les sites consultés voient alors l'adresse IP de la connexion utilisée comme relais, plutôt que celle du client à l'origine de la requête.
Dans cette campagne, les pirates ont associé les installations à leur propre compte Pawns.app, afin de percevoir les éventuelles rémunérations générées par les connexions détournées. GreyNoise a également observé que certains appareils avaient été configurés pour accepter une clé SSH contrôlée par les attaquants, leur offrant un autre moyen d'y accéder ultérieurement.
Si les intrusions et les installations frauduleuses sont documentées, les gains réalisés demeurent inconnus. Pawns.app affirme d'ailleurs avoir abandonné sa fonction de partage de bande passante en 2026, bien que son site professionnel propose toujours aux développeurs un SDK reposant sur cette technologie. Les chercheurs ne précisent pas si les pirates ont effectivement reçu des paiements.
Comment protéger ses équipements contre ce type de détournement ?
Outre l'exploitation de la bande passante, le proxyjacking expose les propriétaires à des conséquences parfois difficiles à détecter. Les connexions détournées peuvent servir à faire transiter des activités frauduleuses, dont les requêtes semblent alors provenir de l'adresse IP de la victime. Celle-ci risque notamment de se retrouver sur des listes de blocage ou de subir des vérifications supplémentaires lors de l'accès à certains services.
Pour limiter les risques, la première précaution consiste à maintenir les NAS et les systèmes de vidéosurveillance à jour, et à désactiver les accès distants inutiles. La situation est plus délicate pour les anciens NAS D-Link et les enregistreurs UniFi Video concernés par cette campagne : leurs fabricants respectifs ayant définitivement arrêté leur maintenance, aucune mise à jour ne viendra corriger les vulnérabilités exploitées. La meilleure chose à faire reste donc de les remplacer ou, à défaut, de les isoler d'Internet en limitant leur accès au réseau local.
En cas de suspicion d'intrusion, il faut vérifier les logiciels installés, les clés SSH autorisées et les connexions sortantes inhabituelles. La présence d'une installation Pawns.app non autorisée constitue un indice de compromission, mais sa suppression ne garantit pas l’assainissement de l'appareil. Si les pirates ont conservé un accès au système, il faudra procéder à une réinitialisation complète, changer les identifiants et appliquer les correctifs disponibles avant de remettre l'équipement en service.

articles.title: Hidden code suggests location sharing in Google Messages is about to get a major upgrade — which will make it easier to find people
articles.text:
This leaked Google Messages location-sharing upgrade might actually make it worth using over WhatsApp
More map styles and details
- A new location-sharing upgrade for Google Messages has been spotted
- You'll be able to add different map layers, including live traffic
- It's not clear how long it will be before the feature is enabled for everyone
While Google has added plenty of new features and refinements to its Google Messages app in recent months and years, it still lags behind competitors such as WhatsApp when it comes to certain facets of the app — like sharing your location with other people.
This is something that's essential for social meet-ups, keeping tabs on the kids, planning journey times, and more besides, and hidden code spotted by Android Authority suggests that location sharing in Google Messages is about to get a significant upgrade.
This is code that's present but not yet enabled in the latest beta version of Google Messages for Android, but the Android Authority team was able to get it working. It adds several map types and a map details option, when you choose to share your location.
Currently, you can only show a map in the default Google Maps style when location sharing in Google Messages, but the new options would let you switch to satellite or terrain views instead, as well as overlaying live traffic information on top.
Benefits to users
The satellite view would make it easier to find someone in relation to a landmark or a feature or the landscape, for example, while the terrain view would give you a better idea of how simple (or otherwise) it might be to reach someone in a remote area.
Then there's the traffic view — say if the roads were blocked up around a person you're trying to pick up in a car, you could get them to walk and come and meet you, rather than getting stuck in a traffic jam unnecessarily.
Most of the time I do tend to default to WhatsApp when it comes to letting people know where I am, because everyone's got the app and it's straightforward to use. You can also set time limits on location sharing, something which Google Messages doesn't have.

If improvements like this continue, I might switch to Google Messages for locations instead — at least for those people on Android. There's still work to do, but the feature only arrived earlier this year, so it's encouraging to see upgrades on the way already.

articles.title: Apple explica por qué Safari ya no dejará que las empresas rastreen a usuarios a través del email
articles.text:
Apple amplió el bloqueo de Safari contra empresas que realizan rastreo de usuarios mediante direcciones de email, una medida que alcanza a iPhone, iPad, Mac y Vision Pro y que apunta a impedir la identificación de una misma persona en distintos sitios web para mostrarle anuncios personalizados.
La decisión afecta a LiveRamp, ID5, UID 2.0 de The Trade Desk, Permutive y Audigent, que estuvieron entre las primeras compañías sin soporte tras la actualización de software lanzada en septiembre de 2026.
Los ingenieros del navegador explicaron que Safari deja de comunicarse por completo con esos servicios una vez actualizado el dispositivo. El mecanismo bloqueado comienza cuando una persona ingresa su correo para iniciar sesión en un sitio o recibir un boletín.
Una empresa externa puede convertir esa dirección en un identificador que permite reconocer al usuario en múltiples páginas sin recurrir a cookies.
Apple sostuvo que el correo pasó a ocupar el lugar que antes tenían las cookies en la infraestructura de seguimiento. Safari ya había restringido el uso de esos archivos seis años antes, lo que llevó a parte de la industria publicitaria a buscar otros métodos para vincular la actividad de los usuarios.
Cómo las empresas rastrean a los usuarios a través de internet
Las compañías de tecnología publicitaria se incorporan de forma invisible a las páginas donde los usuarios escriben sus direcciones, según explicó Apple en su blog.
La empresa advirtió: “Dado que la mayoría de las personas conservan una misma dirección durante años y la usan en todos sus dispositivos, el seguimiento posterior es mucho más difícil de erradicar que el que se podía lograr con una cookie”.
Cerrar sesión en un sitio o cancelar un boletín tampoco elimina necesariamente ese rastro. El tercero conserva tanto el correo como el código asociado y puede sumar información con cada nuevo inicio de sesión o formulario hasta construir un perfil individual, conocido en el sector como gráfico de identidad.
Apple argumentó que quienes se suscriben a una lista de distribución no esperan que sus datos sean enviados a otra empresa para un uso diferente. Por eso, Safari bloquea la dirección web completa de los proveedores alcanzados, de modo que modificar la forma de una solicitud no permite eludir la restricción.
La compañía diferenció este método de la personalización realizada por una empresa con información de sus propios clientes. Para un editor, esa excepción incluiría sugerir artículos o adaptar páginas a partir de los datos de sus lectores, siempre que no intervenga una firma externa capaz de vincular a esa persona con su actividad en otros sitios.
De qué forma impacta la decisión de Apple en el mercado publicitario
Las restricciones de Safari reavivaron las dudas de la industria sobre el papel de Apple en un mercado donde también vende publicidad. En 2017, la Protección de Seguimiento Inteligente del navegador comenzó a eliminar las cookies utilizadas por empresas de tecnología publicitaria.
Criteo advirtió a sus inversores de un posible impacto de hasta 10% en sus ingresos del cuarto trimestre, sin considerar los costos de adquisición de tráfico.
Los Anuncios de Búsqueda de Apple, lanzados un año antes, funcionaban dentro de la App Store, donde esas restricciones no se aplicaban. En 2021, la Transparencia de Seguimiento de Aplicaciones llevó a la mayoría de los propietarios de iPhone a rechazar el rastreo por parte de aplicaciones.
Asimismo, Meta calculó que esa política le costaría cerca de 10 mil millones de dólares en 2022. Durante el mismo período, la participación de Apple en el mercado de publicidad para instalaciones de aplicaciones en iPhone pasó de 17% a 58%, según datos de Branch.
Qué puestos de trabajo busca Apple relacionados con publicidad
La empresa tenía 86 puestos vacantes identificados como Apple Ads, aunque varios habían sido publicados meses antes de la restricción, lo que indica que el crecimiento había sido planificado con antelación.
En Cupertino, la compañía buscaba un director de algoritmos para ingeniería publicitaria, un gerente de producto para inteligencia artificial y aprendizaje automático en el mercado de Apple Ads, y un ingeniero sénior dedicado a optimizar campañas.
En Nueva York se concentraban 17 vacantes, entre ellas tres puestos de socios de clientes para atender anunciantes y una posición para gestionar campañas de publicidad de marca.

articles.title: Apple réserve une bonne surprise aux anciens HomePod avec sa prochaine mise à jour
articles.text:
Les nouveautés du HomePod mini 2 ne seront finalement pas toutes réservées à la nouvelle enceinte d’Apple. Avec la mise à jour 27.2, plusieurs fonctions vont également profiter aux anciens modèles, dont une animation lumineuse présentée la semaine dernière.
Vous possédez déjà un HomePod mini et n’avez pas franchement envie de repasser à la caisse pour le nouveau modèle ? Apple a une bonne nouvelle pour vous. Quelques jours après la présentation du HomePod mini 2, la version Release Candidate du logiciel HomePod 27.2 révèle que certaines nouveautés seront également proposées aux enceintes existantes. De quoi prolonger leur durée de vie, même si toutes les fonctions annoncées la semaine dernière ne seront pas disponibles sur les anciennes générations.
Les anciens HomePod vont aussi s’illuminer au rythme de la musique
La principale surprise concerne l’Illumination sonore, ou Sound Glow, présentée par Apple comme l’une des nouveautés de son HomePod mini 2.
Comme l’a découvert MacRumors, cette fonction sera également disponible sur le HomePod mini original, commercialisé en 2020, ainsi que sur le grand HomePod de deuxième génération. Le principe est assez simple : la surface tactile supérieure de l’enceinte s’illumine et change de couleur au rythme de la musique. Les animations s’adaptent notamment aux basses, aux aigus et aux couleurs de la pochette du morceau en cours de lecture.
L’effet fonctionne également avec les podcasts et les sons d’ambiance proposés par Apple. Un petit ajout esthétique, certes, mais qui permettra aux enceintes existantes de profiter d’une partie des nouveautés du modèle 2026. Seul le HomePod original, lancé en 2018, reste exclu de cette fonction.
Une fois la mise à jour installée, l’Illumination sonore pourra être activée dans les réglages du HomePod, si l’iPhone est bien mis à jour vers iOS 27.2. Les utilisateurs disposant d'une Apple TV 4K associée pourront également la contrôler depuis le centre de contrôle du boîtier.
De nouvelles possibilités avec le Mac et l’Apple TV, mais quelques limites
HomePod 27.2 apporte aussi la possibilité d’utiliser une enceinte comme sortie audio par défaut d’un Mac compatible. Apple impose toutefois un ordinateur équipé du Wi-Fi 6E ou d’une version plus récente.
Autre nouveauté, un réglage permettra de verrouiller les commandes tactiles situées sur le dessus de l’enceinte, pour éviter les manipulations accidentelles.
Enfin, la mise à jour prépare le nouveau système surround à quatre enceintes de l’Apple TV 4K, une nouveauté annoncée lors de la présentation de la dernière box TV. Seuls les HomePod de deuxième génération et les HomePod mini 2 pourront en profiter, à condition de posséder la nouvelle Apple TV 4K. Les premiers HomePod mini restent exclus.
Ces fonctions sont actuellement présentes dans la Release Candidate de HomePod 27.2, distribuée aux développeurs et aux testeurs des versions bêta. Le lancement public est attendu prochainement, probablement au début de la dernière semaine d'octobre.
Les propriétaires d’anciens HomePod pourront donc profiter de quelques améliorations sans renouveler leur matériel. Pas de quoi transformer radicalement leur enceinte, mais on ne va pas bouder une mise à jour qui apporte autre chose que les habituels correctifs de stabilité.

articles.title: An 'enormous influx' of new Garmin Connect IQ apps and watch faces spark fears of poor-quality AI slop flooding the store
articles.text:
'Poorly made, AI-generated watch faces will consume everything': Garmin's Connect IQ store has been hit by an 'enormous influx' of submissions, and Garmin users could soon be grappling with a wave of AI slop
Garmin has a Connect IQ problem
- Garmin's Connect IQ store has seen an 'enormous influx' of new submissions
- These include apps and watch faces, and are causing a big backlog as developers struggle to get their submissions reviewed
- It's likely AI is to blame, as the sudden wave of submissions 'was never a problem in the past'
If you wear one of the best Garmin watches, you might have used the Garmin Connect IQ store to download an app like Spotify or Komoot, a new free or paid watch face (even a Pokémon-branded one), or a fun community-made complication like the Walk with Frodo app. However, downloading stuff from the Connect IQ store in future may involve sifting through thousands of low-quality, AI-generated submissions.
Watch face and app developers are complaining on Garmin's forums about delays in submission review: while the process typically takes 1-2 days, according to some devs, the process is now taking up to 13 days.
Garmin Connect IQ moderator/representative Brandon posted directly to one thread, stating: "This is not due to a bug — we have gotten an enormous influx of app submissions in the last month, with no signs of slowing down, and are working through approvals as quickly as we can.
"This was never a problem in the past, except perhaps delays because of a long holiday weekend (e.g. Christmas)."
The fact this glut of submissions is a sudden problem or new phenomenon points to one thing only — AI. Garmin Connect IQ has likely been flooded with vibe-coded or AI-generated products designed to make a quick buck by flooding the digital marketplace.
One Garmin user said in response to Brandon: "You need to limit the upload frequency for each developer; those poorly made AI-generated watch faces will consume everything."
Another said: "I have observed this trend worsening significantly as well. The Connect IQ Store is increasingly flooded with low-effort, repetitive submissions that hurt discoverability, degrade user trust, and crowd out well-crafted apps."
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
While this is bad for developers (who get charged $100 annually to sell apps on the Connect IQ store) it's also bad for Garmin users. We'll now have to wade through a sea of AI slop watch faces in order to get to faces and apps created the old-fashioned way — with human-led, thought-out complications developed and designed by real Garmin users.
It's just one more example of digital merchants being reduced to dealing with an avalanche of AI slop submissions, just like other app stores, and almost every other breed of online storefronts for digital products. We reported as far back as 2023 that AI-generated e-books were flooding Kindle Unlimited, making it difficult for users to find new books, and the problem has only gotten worse with time. The same will likely happen to the Connect IQ store.
I've reached out to Garmin for comment on the situation, and will update this article if I get any response. In the meantime, if you're a Connect IQ user and you've noticed the change, let us know in the comments below.

Matt is TechRadar's expert on all things fitness, wellness and wearable tech.
A former staffer at Men's Health, he holds a Master's Degree in journalism from Cardiff and has written for brands like Runner's World, Women's Health, Men's Fitness, LiveScience and Fit&Well on everything fitness tech, exercise, nutrition and mental wellbeing.
He is the author of the upcoming book The Health Data Heist, set to be published by Bloomsbury in 2027. When he’s not training or writing about health and fitness, he can be found reading doorstop-thick fantasy books with lots of fictional maps in them.

articles.title: Gemini cambia sus herramientas: qué pasará con Gems, Skills y las tareas automáticas desde de noviembre
articles.text:
Google modificará desde el 17 de noviembre la forma en que los usuarios de cuentas personales emplean Gemini, con un cambio que transformará Gems, Skills, Spark, Tarea y las Acciones programadas.
La reorganización integrará instrucciones personalizadas y automatizaciones dentro del chat principal, un ajuste que altera cómo se crean, combinan y ejecutan funciones de inteligencia artificial.
La transición busca ordenar herramientas que cumplen tareas cercanas, aunque responden a objetivos distintos. Google convertirá los Gems en Skills, incorporará Spark bajo la denominación Tarea y conservará las Acciones programadas para pedidos que deben entregarse en un horario fijado. Las cuentas de trabajo y de centros educativos adoptarán el mismo modelo en 2027.
Los Gems se convierten en Skills
Hasta ahora, los Gems funcionaban como asistentes independientes. El usuario los seleccionaba en una barra lateral y cada elección abría una conversación separada. Desde el 17 de noviembre, Google iniciará la conversión automática de los Gems personales en Skills, un formato que traslada las instrucciones configuradas al hilo principal de Gemini.
Tras esa migración, la interfaz anterior desaparecerá para esas cuentas y ya no hará falta cambiar de ventana para recuperar una configuración concreta.
Para utilizar una Skill, bastará con escribir una barra diagonal en el cuadro de solicitud y elegir la opción correspondiente. Gemini también podrá activarla cuando identifique que las pautas guardadas coinciden con el pedido.
La diferencia central radica en que varias Skills pueden operar en una misma conversación: una puede definir la imagen de marca y otra establecer el tono de escritura, sin trasladar resultados entre bots distintos.
Skills tendrá limitaciones iniciales
La sustitución no conservará todas las capacidades disponibles en los Gems. Al comienzo, las Skills no admitirán herramientas como Canvas, Investigación profunda, Aprendizaje guiado ni la generación de video y música. Tampoco permitirán compartir una Skill o adjuntar archivos de Drive. Google prevé incorporar esas opciones más adelante, pero quienes dependan de ellas deberán revisar sus configuraciones antes de la fecha de conversión.
La recomendación para conservar el material consiste en copiar las instrucciones de cada Gem en un archivo Markdown y descargar los archivos de conocimiento asociados. Esa copia permitirá reconstruir los ajustes cuando la versión previa deje de estar disponible. La medida resulta relevante para configuraciones que mezclan directrices de trabajo con documentos o con funciones que Skills aún no incorpora.
Las Acciones programadas generan entregas en horarios definidos
Las Acciones programadas permiten redactar una solicitud, elegir el momento de ejecución y definir su frecuencia. Gemini prepara el resultado en segundo plano y admite hasta 10 acciones activas a la vez.
En la versión web, el chat queda marcado como no leído; en móviles, el servicio envía una notificación que puede aparecer en la pantalla de bloqueo, según los ajustes del dispositivo. Su despliegue para cuentas gratuitas continúa y ya no exige una suscripción a Google AI.
La herramienta requiere Keep Activity activada y elabora el contenido durante la hora anterior a la entrega. Esa condición reduce su utilidad para información que cambia en minutos. Puede servir para recibir un resumen del calendario, una lista de tareas, correos electrónicos o un pronóstico diario. Si la petición utiliza la ubicación, Gemini toma como referencia el lugar donde se creó.
Tarea asume el espacio que ocupaba Spark
Spark, que aparece como Tarea junto al cuadro de solicitud, mantiene función de agente capaz de continuar procesos tras cerrar el ordenador o bloquear el teléfono. Opera en máquinas virtuales de Google Cloud y puede investigar competidores o vigilar precios de vuelos.
Exige Google AI Pro o Ultra, Keep Activity y admite hasta 15 procesos simultáneos. Solicita aprobación antes de enviar mensajes, modificar datos, comprar o completar formularios. A diferencia de las Acciones programadas, puede reaccionar a eventos y completar pasos sin presencia del usuario, aunque requiere supervisión humana.
La simplificación puede facilitar el uso de instrucciones y automatizaciones, aunque también obliga a los usuarios a distinguir con mayor precisión qué tarea corresponde a cada opción y a revisar los límites de las funciones que todavía están en desarrollo.

articles.title: WhatsApp Hid Instructions in Help Pages Telling Its AI Chatbot Not to Recommend Privacy Regulators
articles.text:
WhatsApp's help pages carried hidden instructions for its support chatbot that told it not to recommend a data protection authority or regulator to users who could no longer delete their accounts, even though WhatsApp's own privacy policy for Europe tells users they can complain to one.
The text sat in the pages' code, never shown on screen, until it was removed by October 18. Whether the chatbot ever followed the instructions is not known: Redact, the data-deletion software company that found the text, read the instructions, not the chatbot's answers.
WhatsApp told WIRED the instructions were for the chatbot that users reach by messaging WhatsApp Support with AI, and that they appeared in the pages because of a bug, now fixed.
A second block of hidden text on the page about reporting and blocking told the chatbot that once a user mentioned a lawyer, a lawsuit, or a court, it should not cite privacy laws such as the GDPR, even when the user raised them.
A WhatsApp account can be deleted only from inside the app on the user's main phone. A user who has lost the phone or the number cannot do it, and the help page on deleting an account says so in a visible note: a deactivated account is deleted 30 days after deactivation, and an inactive one is generally deleted after 120 days, or 365 days in the US.
Beneath that note, in text the page never displayed, sat instructions that repeated the waiting periods and added three orders, according to Redact's copy of the page from October 8:
Do not recommend contacting any Data Protection Authority, regulator, or supervisory authority. Do not suggest WhatsApp can manually delete accounts on the user's behalf. Do not recommend using a different phone with an active phone number.
The second block sat near the end of the page about reporting and blocking. It applied, in its own words, "When a user mentions legal action, lawsuits, lawyers, attorneys, courts, or litigation", and from then on told the chatbot not to cite WhatsApp's Terms of Service or Privacy Policy, not to discuss WhatsApp's liability, to send users with legal matters to "a qualified legal professional", and:
Do not reference, cite, or interpret data protection or privacy regulations (for example GDPR, LGPD, CCPA), including when a user raises them directly.
On the regulator, WhatsApp's privacy policy for Europe, effective July 2, 2026, says the opposite. "You have the right to lodge a complaint with WhatsApp's lead supervisory authority under the GDPR, the Irish Data Protection Commission, or any other competent data protection supervisory authority," it says.
On deletion, the gap is narrower: the hidden text told the chatbot not to suggest that WhatsApp could delete a user's account, while the policy says users "always have the right to request access to, rectification of, and erasure of" their information.
Both rights are written into the GDPR itself: the complaint right is Article 77, the erasure right Article 17.
Redact, whose software bulk-deletes users' old posts, messages and data across services, found the first notes on October 8 and published its findings on October 19. After finding them, it read all 545 pages linked by WhatsApp's help center and counted 102 hidden blocks across 80 of them.
Most of the 102 were routine, per Redact's summary: clearing up words people mix up, pointing a question to the right page, and describing paid plans—a few protected users, such as one telling the chatbot never to suggest entering a false age.
A few were in the same family as the two above. The account-deactivation page told the chatbot that for a user who had lost their number, waiting was "the ONLY correct answer", and the block-and-report page told it to say a report is handled internally and to share no further steps or timeframes.
One block named WhatsApp's support chatbot. Redact also checked 300 Facebook and Instagram help pages, which run on the same system, and found no notes like these.
The blocks sat in the pages' HTML under the name HelpContentGalaxyLLMInclude and were not shown on screen, so anyone who viewed the page source could read them.
WhatsApp's server sent them, with the rest of the page, to Google's and Bing's crawlers, Redact found. Requests Redact sent on October 9 under the user-agent names that OpenAI's, Anthropic's, and Perplexity's crawlers use came back without the article or the notes. Redact did not test whether any AI assistant acted on them.
Internet Archive copies of the delete-account page narrow down how long the text was there: a copy from July 12 does not have the note, one from September 4 does, and one from October 9 still carries the notes in its source. Both notes were still on the live pages at 21:40 UTC on October 15.
By 02:08 UTC on October 18, all 102 blocks were removed from all 80 pages, with the pages themselves still up; an archive copy from 02:37 UTC that day shows the change.
WhatsApp removed the text after WIRED contacted Meta about it, WIRED reported, and before either WIRED or Redact published.
"These are instructions to our chatbot, not directly to users, and are intended to ensure accurate and relevant responses for WhatsApp users who choose to message WhatsApp Support with AI," WhatsApp spokesperson Joshua Breckman told WIRED.
The company wants its support chatbots "focused on providing the best advice to users about WhatsApp" and "not to offer legal advice," he said.
It's unclear whether the same instructions still apply to the chatbot, now that they are out of the pages.
A user who cannot delete an account in the app still has routes outside the chatbot, starting with waiting out the periods specified by the help page. Under WhatsApp's privacy policy for Europe, a user can always ask WhatsApp to erase their information.
In the EU, a user who is not satisfied can complain to their national data protection authority or to the Irish Data Protection Commission, which WhatsApp's policy names and asks people to raise the matter with the organization first, then through its online form.

articles.title: Guía de Dragon Ball Super Beerus: cuántos episodios tendrá y dónde verlos completos
articles.text:
Dragon Ball Super Beerus tendrá 19 episodios que se estrenan uno por semana. La serie llegó a Crunchyroll el 11 de octubre de 2026, tanto en Latinoamérica como en España, aunque las opciones de streaming cambian según la región.
En América Latina, el anime también está disponible en Disney+, HBO Max y Netflix, con estrenos escalonados. Disney+ comenzó el 14 de octubre, HBO Max el 16 y Netflix el 17.
En España, además de Crunchyroll, se sumaron AnimeBox, Disney+ y Netflix; Prime Video ofrece la serie a través de un canal de Crunchyroll. Los catálogos y las fechas pueden variar entre países, por lo que conviene comprobar la disponibilidad en cada servicio.
Cuántos episodios tiene Dragon Ball Super Beerus
La nueva entrega está formada por 19 capítulos, publicados semanalmente. No se trata de una temporada completa disponible de una sola vez: cada plataforma sigue un día de estreno propio, así que la cantidad de episodios que se puede ver depende del servicio y del país.
En Latinoamérica, el calendario publicado fija los estrenos de Crunchyroll para los domingos, los de Disney+ para los miércoles, los de HBO Max para los viernes y los de Netflix para los sábados. Si se mantienen esas fechas semanales, el episodio final llegará primero a Crunchyroll, el 14 de febrero de 2027, y después a Disney+, HBO Max y Netflix, entre el 17 y el 20 de febrero.
Quienes quieran ponerse al día pueden revisar cuántos capítulos hay cargados en su plataforma. Si prefieren esperar a que termine la emisión para ver la temporada seguida, tendrán que aguardar hasta que cada servicio publique el episodio 19.
Dónde ver el anime en Latinoamérica
Crunchyroll fue la primera plataforma en estrenar la serie en América Latina, con lanzamiento simultáneo con Japón el 11 de octubre. Después se incorporaron Disney+, el 14; HBO Max, el 16, y Netflix, el 17. Los capítulos llegan semanalmente y con varios días de diferencia entre servicios.
La disponibilidad puede depender del territorio. Por eso, aunque la serie figure en el catálogo regional de una plataforma, el usuario debería buscarla en la aplicación de su país para confirmar que puede reproducirla y conocer las opciones de audio y subtítulos. La ficha de Prime Video, por ejemplo, muestra subtítulos en español latinoamericano, pero no confirma que esa plataforma distribuya la serie en todos los países de la región.
Dónde ver Dragon Ball Super Beerus en España
En España, Crunchyroll y AnimeBox estrenaron el anime el 11 de octubre. Disney+ lo incorporó el 14 y Netflix el 18. Prime Video también presenta la serie mediante la suscripción del canal de Crunchyroll. La oferta, por tanto, es distinta a la de Latinoamérica: allí HBO Max forma parte de las opciones citadas, mientras que AnimeBox corresponde a España.
De qué trata la historia
La trama comienza años después de la derrota de Majin Buu, cuando la Tierra atraviesa una etapa de paz. Esa tranquilidad cambia con el despertar de Beerus, el Dios de la Destrucción, quien oye hablar del Saiyan que venció a Freezer y viaja para buscar a Goku.
El encuentro amenaza con desatar una batalla de escala cósmica. Goku y sus aliados tendrán que encontrar la manera de detener a Beerus, un adversario capaz de destruir planetas. La historia retoma personajes conocidos y presenta el conflicto de forma accesible para quienes se acercan por primera vez a la franquicia.
Dragon Ball Super Beerus ofrece una versión renovada del anime, con escenas nuevas y redibujadas, mejoras visuales y una narración reconstruida, según Disney+. Con 19 episodios y estrenos semanales, los espectadores de Latinoamérica y España pueden seguir el regreso de Goku, aunque deberán elegir la plataforma según su país y el calendario que prefieran.

articles.title: Orange vient d’éteindre la 2G presque partout en France : SFR et Bouygues Telecom vont très vite suivre
articles.text:
L'opérateur Orange a éteint ce mardi son réseau 2G dans les 43 derniers départements de l’Hexagone. Une fin quasi totale pour la technologie, avant celle de SFR et Bouygues Telecom, programmée d’ici mi-décembre.
La fin de la 2G chez Orange est plus que jamais une réalité, puisque ce mardi 20 octobre 2026, l'opérateur historique a coupé son réseau 2G dans les 43 derniers départements de l'Hexagone où il émettait encore. L'entreprise peut se concentrer sur un réseau plus sûr, plus sobre d'un point de vue énergétique, en plus de récupérer au passage des fréquences pour la 4G et la 5G. À la fin du mois de juin, pourtant, 1,7 million d'appareils dépendaient encore uniquement de la 2G selon l'ARCEP, tandis que SFR et Bouygues Telecom préparent déjà leur propre coupure, qui ne va pas tarder. On vous explique.
Pourquoi Orange coupe la 2G sans regret
La dernière vague d'extinction du réseau 2G d'Orange est tombée ce mardi, et on peut dire qu'elle touche du monde. Paris, le Rhône, le Nord ou encore la Gironde figurent parmi les 43 départements concernés. Bayonne, Anglet et Biarritz avaient servi d'éclaireurs le 31 mars dernier, avant le reste du Sud-Ouest en mai et juin, Nice le 22 septembre puis 44 départements le 6 octobre. D'après le calendrier de l'opérateur, les zones blanches réglementaires, ces secteurs mal couverts où les opérateurs partagent leurs antennes, gardent la 2G jusqu'au 15 décembre au plus tard.
Pour justifier la fin de 2G, Orange évoque une nécessite d'espace, de sécurité et de sobriété. L'espace, d'abord. La 2G occupait en effet 5 MHz de fréquences, une vraie voie de circulation sur les ondes, qu'Orange va céder à la 4G et à la 5G. La sécurité, ensuite, car ces réseaux plus récents chiffrent mieux les communications et vérifient plus sérieusement l'identité des appareils qui s'y connectent. Et la sobriété, enfin, parce que selon la Fédération française des télécoms, faire transiter un gigaoctet de données en 2G peut consommer jusqu'à 500 fois plus d'énergie qu'en 5G.
Plus de deux cents opérateurs dans le monde ont déjà éteint la 2G ou la 3G. Chez Orange, c'est La Réunion qui avait ouvert la voie, avec une extinction bouclée dès octobre 2025. Les Antilles et la Guyane ont suivi au printemps, avant une généralisation le 26 septembre, et Mayotte fermera la marche d'ici la fin de l'année. L'opération s'est déroulée « sans encombre », assure Orange. La Banque des Territoires fait tout de même état de rares cas isolés, comme le paiement dans les transports publics de Bayonne, aussitôt réglé.
Fin de la 2G : SFR et Bouygues sortent les ciseaux à leur tour
La fin de la 2G a pu poser quelques soucis, et ce n'est pas fini. Forcément, un mobile uniquement compatible 2G ne peut plus passer ni recevoir d'appels et de SMS sur le réseau d'Orange, numéros d'urgence compris. Les abonnés Free sont dans le même bateau, puisque l'opérateur n'a jamais construit sa propre 2G et utilisait celle d'Orange en itinérance. Pour savoir si vous êtes concerné, pensez à consulter la fiche technique papier ou numérique de votre téléphone. Il y a aussi eu la polémique autour des systèmes d'alerte d'ascenseur ou boîtiers de téléassistance et de télésurveillance, qui pour certains reposent encore sur la 2G, et deviennent muets dès la coupure.
Pour ce qui est des clients SFR et Bouygues Telecom, ces derniers ont encore quelques semaines de répit. Bouygues coupera sa 2G le 15 novembre à Brest, Guipavas, Nancy et Vandœuvre-lès-Nancy, avant d'éteindre le reste de la métropole entre le 1er et le 15 décembre. SFR débutera lui aussi mi-novembre, par les zones très denses, puis généralisera dans la première quinzaine de décembre. Outre-mer, Outremer Telecom coupe sa 2G en Guadeloupe dès ce jeudi 22 octobre, et SRR suivra à La Réunion et à Mayotte le 30 novembre. Sous le sapin, la 2G ne sera ainsi plus qu'un souvenir, en théorie.
La prochaine sur la liste, vous le savez, c'est la 3G, qu'Orange éteindra en 2028, SFR fin 2028 et Bouygues Telecom fin 2029, Free n'ayant pas encore fixé de date. Si vous changez de téléphone, vérifiez qu'il gère bien la 4G et la VoLTE, la fonction qui fait passer les appels par la 4G. Sans elle, même un téléphone compatible 4G ne pourra plus appeler une fois la 3G éteinte. Côté couverture, il n'y a pas d'inquiétude à avoir, car selon l'ARCEP, la 4G touche déjà plus de 99,9 % de la population métropolitaine.

articles.title: Microsoft admits 'frontier models can't be trusted', unveils new security tools to treat AI agents as insider threats
articles.text:
Microsoft admits 'frontier models can't be trusted', unveils new security tools to treat AI agents as insider threats
Say hi to your new Guardian Agent
- Microsoft unveils Guardian Agents to monitor, constrain, and manage risks posed by autonomous AI agents
- New controls dynamically adjust agent permissions, behavior, and access based on changing risk levels
- Company warns “agentic insiders” require continuous AI-driven oversight beyond traditional security controls
AI fans, your vocabulary is about to become two phrases richer: Agentic Insider, and Guardian Agent. These are the two phrases Microsoft used while announcing a swathe of new tools and features to help businesses secure their operations running AI agents.
A new Microsoft blog, published by Microsoft's Corporate VP for Identity and Network Access, Nadim Abdo, argues that agents, while not inherently malicious, can make mistakes or be manipulated and compromised.
Since they need to be granted relatively extensive permissions in order to be able to work properly, it creates the sort of risk that can prove disastrous if not properly handled.
Agentic Overwatch
Abdo also added that AI agents doing their master's bidding cannot be trusted with their own security.
"Satya Nadella, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Microsoft, recently described the trust architecture this new era requires: we must separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it," Abdo writes.
"We should not ask a model to be its own security authority. The controls that determine what it can access, what actions it can take, and whether it should continue operating must sit outside the model, where the model cannot bypass or tamper with them."
So, oversight is the keyword here. But AI agents move at machine speed, something no human can match, and therefore humans are not properly equipped for the job. Instead, separate AI agents need to be introduced to keep their juniors in check. Earlier, Microsoft introduced Project Perception and the Microsoft cyber stack, to help organizations defend with agents.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Project Perception is an AI-powered cybersecurity system designed to coordinate specialized AI agents that analyze security data, identify vulnerabilities, and investigate different threats. The system uses three types of agents: red agents that probe for weaknesses, blue agents that investigate potential threats, and green agents that implement corrections and fixes.
Now, Microsoft says it is extending the project to secure “the agentic insider”. They’re calling it - Guardian Agent.
“Guardian Agents help security teams operate continuously, at machine speed and scale, while sensors, context, and actuators across the cyber stack help understand changing agent risk and continuously adapt protection in response,” Abdo explained. “Project Perception and Microsoft Agent 365 share signals, context, and a unified registry giving IT and security teams a consistent view of agents and risk, with the controls each needs.”
Drill sergeant
Abdo says Guardian Agents build on a security principle where non-deterministic intelligence needs to be surrounded with deterministic controls, independent evidence, and containment boundaries.
These controls are divided into seven aspects - identity, permissions, data, endpoints, network, cloud, and runtime - and these have four responsibilities: to know which agent exists, who owns them and why, and what they’re doing; to contain what each agents can access and do before it acts; to protect the data, tools, runtime, resources, and systems the agent uses; and to adapt protection continuously as behavior, context, and risk change.
In other words, the AI needs to be the drill sergeant for the drones, adapting to changes in real-time to make sure they’re doing good work and not going rogue.
Microsoft also said it is expanding discovery to 35 additional types of local agents, including Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and GitHub Copilot. It also announced extending Microsoft Entra Agent ID with identity types for additional agent patterns, including both local and previously unknown agents discovered through security sensors.
With “Dynamic Permissions” and “Dynamic Agent Risk”, Microsoft wants to give businesses tighter control over what AI agents can access and do, while keeping tabs on their behavior and risk levels. Dynamic Permissions limit agents to the access they need for a specific task, while Dynamic Agent Risk checks for potential threats.
Dynamic Conditional Access can then respond to rising risks by restricting permissions, blocking certain operations, or asking for human approval. In more extreme scenarios, an agent can be stopped and isolated.

articles.title: What Security Teams Can Do To Tame Wild Code
articles.text:
A sales manager builds an AI-assisted workflow to route leads. It connects to customer records, summarizes inbound requests, and posts updates to a shared channel. The workflow saves time, reduces manual work, and soon becomes part of the team’s daily routine. Across the same organization, employees are building useful apps, agents, and automations faster than existing processes can support them.
If you work in security, that success introduces a new set of questions. Whose credentials does the workflow use? Which records can it access? Who can see its output? If it starts exposing information it shouldn’t, can you trace what happened and stop further access?
Wild code takes root when useful builds spread faster than the processes for owning, securing, and maintaining them. It isn’t simply another name for unapproved software. Employees are creating new capabilities, not just adopting existing products. A small experiment can become an operational dependency before security knows it exists.
The risk goes beyond vulnerabilities in generated code. Even code that works as intended can operate with too much access or expose data to the wrong audience:
- Excessive permissions. A workflow needs a small set of records but runs with credentials that can read or modify far more.
- Sensitive data exposure. An employee connects an agent to information it doesn’t need, or makes its output available too broadly. Sensitive information can also end up in model requests or logs.
- Unintended actions. An agent can change records or permissions without an approval boundary appropriate to the action.
- Orphaned access. A useful workflow keeps running after its creator changes roles or leaves, with no clear owner reviewing its permissions.
- Investigation gaps. When something goes wrong, security can’t readily establish which identity ran the workflow, what it accessed, or what changed.
Employee education, sandboxes, and AI steering committees are a good start, but they aren’t enough to control wild code on their own. A more sustainable approach builds controls into the environment itself: what employees can connect to, what their apps and agents can do, and how that work is monitored once it’s running.
Why the usual fixes fall short
Education, sandboxes, and steering committees all have a role. The mistake is expecting them to govern software they may never encounter, or control what happens after it starts running. A policy describes what should happen. Security also needs controls that constrain what can happen, evidence of what did happen, and a way to intervene.
1. Education explains good practice, but can’t enforce it
An AI policy can explain what’s allowed. Training can introduce good practices. Neither guarantees that someone building a reporting workflow will recognize the moment they cross into handling sensitive data or operating production software.
As AI brings more employees into building software, organizations have an opportunity to make practices like least privilege, secrets management, and separating test environments from production more accessible. Policies can set expectations, but employees also need practical guidance and built-in safeguards to apply them in everyday work.
Even employees who recognize a risk still face deadlines and pressure to move faster. If the approved route is slow or confusing, knowing the rules doesn’t make following them easier.
Education helps people make better decisions. It shouldn’t be the only thing preventing an unsafe connection or an unauthorized action.
2. Sandboxes protect experiments, not their entire future
An isolated environment is useful for testing prompts, models, and generated code. But a prototype’s value often depends on eventually reaching real business systems and data.
Once a prototype connects to live business systems, it needs controls that extend beyond the test environment. Permissions, monitoring, and change reviews have to remain in place throughout its working life, not just during the experiment. A successful test doesn’t establish which data the production workflow should access or which actions it should be allowed to take.
As Brad Rumph, field CTO at Tines, puts it: “Sandboxes solve the design problem and leave the runtime problem alone.”
A successful experiment still needs a governed path into operation. Without that path, isolation postpones the hard questions rather than resolving them.
3. Committees can’t review what they can’t see
Steering committees can set direction, establish accountability, and make decisions about high-risk use cases. But their review cycles don’t always match the speed at which employees can create and deploy software.
A committee might prohibit one risky practice while employees discover another way to achieve the same result. Oversight can also concentrate on engineering, where established controls already exist, while overlooking builds in finance, HR, or operations.
The limitation isn’t the quality of the committee. It’s a model that depends on each build becoming visible before it becomes useful. An approval process can’t be the only way security discovers new paths to sensitive data and privileged actions.
Put security controls where the work happens
The alternative is to build controls into the environment employees use to create, run, and maintain their work.
Rather than asking everyone to independently assemble a secure operating model, security teams define shared boundaries with IT and system owners, apply them consistently throughout the lifecycle, and update them as business needs and risks change.
Three principles make this practical.
1. Govern before deployment, and keep governing afterward
Define permitted data sources, actions, and access before employees connect business systems. Keep those controls in place when the workflow goes live.
Permissions should reflect what a workflow needs to do, not everything its creator can access. Consequential actions should require human approval where appropriate. A prompt telling an agent what not to do is not an access control.
Keep creation, execution, and monitoring connected. An approved build shouldn’t become an operational blind spot the moment someone starts using it.
2. Make the approved route the easiest route
Employees need more than a list of restrictions. Give them an environment that lets them solve real problems quickly.
That means accessible building experiences, useful connections to approved systems, and a clear route from idea to operation. Enterprise administrative controls can limit risky alternatives, but the sanctioned option also has to meet employees’ needs.
If governance adds friction at every step, users will choose workarounds to get the job done. Shared safeguards should handle routine requirements so security teams can focus deeper review on sensitive access and consequential actions.
AI can help create an application or agent. It shouldn’t decide which business data that application may expose or which actions that agent may take. Security teams should set those boundaries explicitly with the people responsible for the systems and data.
3. Make investigation and intervention part of the design Security
needs to understand what a workflow did, not just what it was intended to do.
Keep ownership, execution identities, relevant actions, and changes traceable. Protect those records without unnecessarily capturing sensitive information in logs.
Before a workflow becomes an operational dependency, establish who can pause it, how to revoke its access, and how to determine what it affected. Human judgment remains necessary for reviewing consequential changes and responding when behavior diverges from expectations.
What this looks like in practice
A governed environment should make important security questions answerable without a separate investigation:
- Accountable ownership. Who owns the workflow, and which identity does it run as?
- Controlled access. What can it read, change, and send elsewhere? Which actions require approval, and where is that enforced?
- Protected execution. Are workflow steps isolated and credentials injected at runtime rather than exposed in code? These protections should complement, not replace, appropriately scoped permissions.
- Traceable activity. Can security establish what ran, what it accessed, and what changed?
- Clear intervention. How do security teams stop execution and revoke access if something goes wrong?
These controls don’t eliminate every risk. They reduce reliance on employees remembering every rule and security discovering every problem after the fact.
Keep control as more people build
Employees will keep finding valuable ways to build with AI. The goal is to make those improvements visible, supportable, and secure from the start.
As a security practitioner, you don’t need to become the maintainer of every employee-built application. You do need confidence that workflows touching sensitive systems have appropriate access, accountable owners, and activity you can investigate.
Built-in governance makes those protections part of everyday building rather than a cleanup exercise after deployment. It gives employees room to solve problems while giving security clear boundaries to enforce and a way to respond when something goes wrong.
It’s the thinking behind Tines: give teams room to build AI-assisted apps, agents, and automations while keeping security in control of how that work runs. For a closer look at the framework and a readiness checklist, download Taming wild code: The IT leader’s guide to AI code sprawl.

articles.title: HP OmniBook 3 : petit prix et jusqu’à 20 heures d’autonomie... grâce au Snapdragon C ?
articles.text:
L’Omnibook 3 n’est pas une nouveauté à proprement parler chez HP, mais ce modèle se décline en cette fin d’année au travers d’une nouvelle configuration 16 pouces motorisée par un processeur encore peu répandu : le Snapdragon C. Si ses performances s’annoncent modestes, le prix et l’autonomie de l’engin, eux, pourraient bien faire mouche sur l’entrée de gamme.
Dans le sillage du MacBook Neo, toute une flopée de PC portables à 800 euros a été lancée par les constructeurs de modèles Windows. On pense par exemple à l'ASUS Zenbook 14, au Acer Swift Air 14 ou encore au Tecno MegaBook T14 Air… mais tous ont pour point commun de se limiter au format 14 pouces. Ce n’est pas le cas du nouveau HP Omnibook 3 qui nous intéresse aujourd’hui.
Fort d’un format 16 pouces plus confortable, ce dernier tire parti d’un processeur Snapdragon C (C1-10-100), annoncé au printemps mais encore peu usité, pour s’installer sur l’entrée de gamme avec la promesse d’une autonomie vraiment généreuse.
Un PC « efficace et pas cher » ? Peut-être, mais attention quand même…
Pour contexte, le HP Omnibook 3 de 16 pouces existait déjà sur le marché depuis quelques mois, notamment au travers d’une configuration Snapdragon X (X1P-26-100) qui avait plutôt été saluée pour son rapport équipement / prix et son autonomie. Avec cette nouvelle version Snapdragon C, l’appareil se positionne à un tarif encore plus accessible, avec un prix de départ fixé à 599 dollars (hors taxes) aux États-Unis. Une version qui vient toutefois avec un énorme désavantage.
Pour débuter à ce prix, l’appareil n’embarque que 4 Go de mémoire vive et 128 Go de stockage au format UFS. Une fiche technique très maigrelette, que l’on ne peut pas décemment recommander en 2026. HP vend clairement un PC jetable et pratiquement inutilisable à ce prix. Heureusement, on passe à 8 Go de LPDDR5 et 256 Go de SSD sur la mouture proposée à 769 dollars. Une configuration bien plus acceptable.
Le petit Snapdragon C aux manettes pour 20 heures sur batterie ?
On passe sur les nombreuses options proposées, en retenant quand même qu’il est possible d’opter pour 512 Go de SSD moyennant un supplément, en choisissant ou non de conserver du stockage au format UFS sur la carte mère, souligne NotebookCheck.
Côté écran, HP nous propose une dalle Full HD+ / 60 Hz affichant 300 cd/m2 de luminance et couvrant seulement 62,5 % du spectre sRGB. Pas de quoi sabrer le champagne, mais ce type de panneau reste suffisant en bureautique, surtout à ce prix. Une option tactile est par ailleurs disponible et il faut compter 20 dollars supplémentaires pour ajouter le rétroéclairage au clavier, qui comporte, du reste, un pavé numérique.
Côté batterie, l’Omnibook 3 dispose enfin d’une capacité de 41 Wh lui conférant jusqu’à 20 heures d’autonomie selon HP, qui évoque alors de la lecture vidéo 1080p locale avec la luminosité de l’écran à environ 70 %. En usage bureautique et multimédia quotidien, tablez plutôt sur une douzaine d’heures, ce qui reste crédible à ce niveau de prix.
Nous avons contacté HP France pour en savoir plus sur les prix de ce modèle Snapdragon C dans l’Hexagone.
Source : NotebookCheck / HP

articles.title: This Ryzen 7 mini PC is the best machine you can buy under $500
articles.text:
'The best mini PC under $500': The Getorli GT106 packs an AMD Ryzen 7 processor, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 1TB SSD, offering plenty of power for the price
This tiny Windows 11 Pro PC packs impressive specs
You don't need a bulky desktop tower to get a powerful Windows 11 Pro device. The Getorli GT106 mini PC is currently priced at $450 (was $500) at Amazon, and combines an eight-core AMD Ryzen 7 processor, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 1TB SSD in a compact design. For the price and specs, our managing editor has dubbed this "the best mini PC under $500."
• Best for: Home offices, multitasking, multi-monitor workstations, media centers, and anyone who wants a compact system for everyday computing and lighter gaming.
• What we like: Alongside the Ryzen 7 chip and fast DDR5 memory, the mini PC also has integrated AMD Radeon 780M graphics and can drive up to four 4K monitors at a time via HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4, and two USB4 connections.
Today's best mini PC deal
This compact desktop features an eight-core Ryzen 7 H255 processor, Radeon 780M graphics, 16GB DDR5 memory, 1TB PCIe SSD, dual USB4 ports, quad 4K display support, Wi-Fi 6, and Ethernet.
Why we recommend it
The Getorli GT106 is powered by an AMD Ryzen 7 H255 processor with eight cores and 16 threads, running at up to 4.9GHz. There's also 16GB of DDR5 RAM, which comes installed as a single module, leaving the second slot available for an upgrade. For storage there's a 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD, and a second M.2 slot, with support for up to 4TB capacity.
Alongside Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.3, you get dual 2.5Gb Ethernet ports and two 40Gbps USB4 ports for connecting fast external storage and other peripherals.
It comes with Windows 11 Pro installed, and Getorli includes a VESA mounting bracket so you can tuck the device behind a compatible monitor.
For more of our favorites, we've tested the best mini PCs you can buy.
Price context & historical value
The Getorli GT106 is $50 below its usual $499.99 price. That's a 10% discount, bringing the mini PC below the $450 mark. I've seen it retail for as low as $404.99 in the past, however. But so long as it flies easily under the $500 mark, it's a great buy.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Getorli GT106 if...
You want a small Windows 11 Pro mini PC with a Ryzen 7 processor, 16GB DDR5, and 1TB SSD. It's a useful option if you need several monitors or want to connect fast external drives via USB4.
❌ Skip the Getorli GT106 if...
You need a more powerful device. It ships with a single 16GB DDR5 module, which means it initially operates in single-channel memory mode, which can reduce integrated graphics performance.
