articles.title: Hackers vulneraron OpenCode: hicieron compras de hasta USD 1.700 en cuentas de OpenAI, Anthropic y Google
articles.text:
Un ataque informático contra OpenCode, una herramienta de programación con inteligencia artificial de código abierto, dejó expuestas las claves de acceso de un grupo de usuarios y les generó cargos no autorizados de hasta USD 1.700 en sus cuentas de OpenAI, Anthropic y Google.
La compañía confirmó en la red social X que un atacante entró a un sistema antiguo que estaba en proceso de dar de baja y accedió a las claves que el 1,4% de los usuarios de OpenCode Console, su plataforma paga, habían guardado para conectar modelos de otros proveedores.
Esas claves funcionan como una contraseña digital: permiten que una aplicación use los servicios de IA de una empresa en nombre del usuario y le cobre a su cuenta. Según The Hacker News, la primera exposición posible ocurrió la madrugada del 17 de octubre de 2026.
OpenCode, que compite con herramientas como Claude Code y Cursor entre desarrolladores, notificó por correo a los afectados esa misma mañana y aclaró que quienes no recibieron el aviso no fueron alcanzados por la brecha.
Facturas que llegaron antes que el aviso de OpenCode
Varios desarrolladores se enteraron del problema por sus propias facturas antes del comunicado oficial. En Reddit y en X, usuarios publicaron alertas de gasto y cargos que no habían generado.
Uno de ellos, identificado como Colin Parsons, escribió que le cobraron USD 281 en su cuenta de OpenAI y USD 168 en la de Anthropic. Otro usuario, Preston Zeller, calculó sus pérdidas en USD 1.700, mientras que un tercero reportó más de USD 700 en consumo de OpenAI antes de desconectar su clave.
Anthropic revocó las claves de Claude que consideró comprometidas, OpenAI dijo que trabajó con OpenCode para restablecer el acceso de los usuarios y reembolsar los créditos consumidos durante el ataque y Google, suspendió proyectos que detectó con actividad de uso indebido.
Dax Raad, cofundador de OpenCode, aclaró que la brecha afectó únicamente a Console, el servicio alojado en los servidores de la empresa y no a la aplicación de código abierto que se instala en la computadora del usuario: “esas claves nunca nos llegan a nosotros”, escribió.
La compañía vinculó el episodio con un “ataque de destilación a gran escala”: una técnica que consiste en usar las respuestas de un modelo de IA costoso para entrenar, sin autorización, un modelo propio más barato. Algunos especialistas en seguridad cuestionaron esa explicación y plantearon que podría tratarse de una brecha común cuyo destino final todavía no está probado.
Los propios filtros de seguridad frenaron la respuesta
Raad relató que, mientras su equipo investigaba el ataque, los modelos de IA que usaban para analizar el código malicioso se negaban a procesarlo porque activaba sus propios filtros de seguridad. “Fue bastante frustrante”, escribió en X.
El problema se resolvió cuando OpenCode obtuvo acceso al programa Daybreak Blue de OpenAI, que habilita modelos menos restrictivos para tareas defensivas de ciberseguridad a usuarios verificados.
David Sacks, copresidente del Consejo de Asesores en Ciencia y Tecnología del presidente de Estados Unidos, comentó el caso en X: “OpenCode, como antes Hugging Face, chocó con el mismo muro en medio de un ataque: los modelos de IA más avanzados se negaron a analizar los mismos códigos maliciosos que hacían falta para defenderse porque activaban los filtros de seguridad”.
En julio pasado, la plataforma Hugging Face había enfrentado una situación similar cuando los modelos comerciales de IA se negaron a analizar los registros de una intrusión que, luego reveló OpenAI, habían ejecutado sus propios modelos durante una prueba con medidas de seguridad reducidas.
Raad dijo que los atacantes intentaron ingresar a los sistemas de OpenCode de forma ininterrumpida durante 48 horas, lo que obligó al equipo a mantener agentes de IA defensivos activos todo el tiempo. La compañía aún no reveló cómo lograron el acceso inicial ni la extensión total del robo de datos, y pidió a los usuarios afectados revocar y reemplazar sus claves directamente en cada proveedor.

articles.title: Le patron de Rivian en est convaincu : la conduite autonome va transformer radicalement le design des voitures
articles.text:
Et si la conduite autonome changeait la forme même de nos voitures ? RJ Scaringe, le patron de Rivian, assure que l’automobile va subir une profonde mutation.
Le constructeur américain, connu pour ses pick-up et SUV pensés pour l’aventure, a lancé en juin le R2, une voiture plus compacte et plus abordable. Et son modèle commence à porter ses fruits après des années de pertes : Rivian a livré 19 248 véhicules au troisième trimestre, un record, soit environ 46 % de plus qu’un an plus tôt.
RJ Scaringe, son fondateur et P.-D.G de Rivian, s’est justement exprimé il y a quelques jours lors du TechCrunch Disrupt, grande conférence américaine consacrée aux nouvelles technologies. Ses prédictions sont fascinantes.
Des « expériences radicalement différentes »
Il a en effet expliqué à TechCrunch que l’autonomie permettrait à son entreprise de construire des « expériences radicalement différentes ». Le dirigeant se dit « follement enthousiaste « à l’idée de ce que les dix prochaines années vont rendre possible dans le secteur, et il est même prêt à repousser la rentabilité de Rivian pour y parvenir.
L’enjeu dépasse le simple confort de conduite. Si la voiture n’a plus besoin d’être pilotée, ses concepteurs n’ont plus à respecter les codes actuels de l’automobile, « on imagine les formats que l’on veut construire pour un véhicule autonome », étaye-t-il. Selon lui, cela « ouvre toutes sortes d’opportunités de design ».
Et Scaringe s’oppose directement à Tesla : il ne croit pas à un monde où tout le monde laisserait sa voiture au garage pour appeler un robotaxi. Même si les voitures savent un jour conduire seules sur certains trajets, il estime peu probable que les habitudes changent radicalement. Reste à voir à quoi ressembleront ces voitures personnelles et autonomes.
Des concepts, mais c’est tout
Mais ce concept n’est pas nouveau. Il y a dix ans, constructeurs automobiles et spécialistes de la conduite autonome annonçaient que les voitures sans conducteur, associées aux moteurs électriques plus simples et moins encombrants que les moteurs thermiques, feraient naître des formes de véhicules inédites.
Quand Mercedes présentait une cabine en forme de bulle, Toyota imaginait des « salons sur roues » tandis que Hyundai dévoilait une voiture dotée de pattes. Aucun de ces projets n’a dépassé le stade du prototype : l’autonomie a demandé bien plus de temps que prévu, et lancer une toute nouvelle catégorie de véhicule s’est révélé bien plus compliqué. Les robotaxis, eux, sont bien là, même s’ils doivent encore faire face à des défis.
De son côté, le système de conduite autonome de Rivian permet aujourd’hui de lâcher le volant, à condition de continuer à surveiller la route. D’ici à la fin de l’année, il doit être capable de mener une voiture d’un point de départ à une destination sans intervention, toujours sous le contrôle du conducteur. La véritable autonomie devrait arriver en 2028, avec la version robotaxi de la R2.

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Plex2Shell Flaws to Install Crypto Miners and Linux Proxy Backdoor
articles.text:
Threat actors have begun to exploit a chain of vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server to deploy cryptocurrency miners and reverse proxy software, a day after a proof-of-concept (PoC) went public.
According to a researcher who goes by the online alias boredhackerblog, the exploitation activity involves chaining four different vulnerabilities, collectively called Plex2Shell.
The vulnerabilities are below -
- CVE-2026-96652 (CVSS score: 5.3) - An unauthenticated server-side request forgery (SSRF) stemming via the "/player/timeline" endpoint by taking advantage of the fact that the "protocol" parameter is inserted into a programmatically-constructed player URL with no validation, allowing an attacker to force the Plex server to POST to a destination of their choice.
- CVE-2026-96654 (CVSS score: 6.9) - An improper neutralization of URL values included in the "searchOne" endpoint that could allow an attacker to call other plugins' functions and supply their own parameters to obtain the owner's admin token.
- CVE-2026-96655 (CVSS score: 5.3) - An SSRF vulnerability that allows an authenticated user (i.e., the owner token) to request arbitrary internal or external addresses (e.g., an attacker-hosted carrier video carrying the malicious ELF payload) via the '/video/:/transcode/universal' path parameter.
- CVE-2026-96656 (CVSS score: 8.6) - An external control of file name or path vulnerability that writes the ELF shared object to an attacker-chosen path in the Codecs directory and execute it.
Put differently, the vulnerabilities can be combined together in this order to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on susceptible Plex Media Server instances.
The vulnerabilities, along with CVE-2026-96651 (CVSS score: 7.1), were disclosed to Plex on July 27, 2026, by security researcher Zach Main, and were patched in Plex Media Server 1.43.3.10861 released on August 3, 2026.
In-the-wild exploitation attempts targeting the flaws have since been recorded a day after technical details of the Plex2Shell chain went public on October 16, 2026. The attacks make use of a shell script to retrieve and deploy a miner payload ("x12345") hosted on a remote server ("217.60.194[.]116") using wget or curl.
The attack efforts have been observed from the following IP addresses -
- 91.92.40[.]202
- 176.65.139[.]228
- 45.194.92[.]222
- 176.65.139[.]228
| The Plex2Shell chain \| Source: Zach Main | 
Furthermore, the vulnerabilities have been exploited to deliver an artifact named "myawesomeproxy," which, according to VirusTotal, is a stealthy Linux backdoor and reverse proxy. Running the program displays the below message, per boredhackerblog -
Running this software on any of your devices makes you agree to the potential external use of your internet traffic.
Also deployed concurrently is an XMRig miner process identified as "mylovelyminer" with its mining server pointing to "ota.proxystream[.]st." Notably, another subdomain associated with the same domain, "global.relay.proxystream[.]st," was flagged by Bitsight in August 2026 in connection with the AISURU DDoS and proxyware botnet.
Posts on Reddit indicate that multiple Plex users have had their instances compromised with the same "mylovelyminer" payload. That said, it's not known at this stage if it stems from the exploitation of Plex2Shell flaws.
The development comes more than a month after Plex urged users to update their instances to the latest version following the release of an update that addressed multiple unspecified security flaws.
It's unclear if the aforementioned vulnerabilities were part of this alert. The Hacker News has contacted Plex for comment and we will update the story if we hear back. In light of active exploitation, users are advised to keep their Plex installations up-to-date for optimal protection.

articles.title: Halloween : de Netflix à Prime Video, 10 séries flippantes à voir en streaming
articles.text:
Halloween : de Netflix à Prime Video, 10 séries flippantes à voir en streaming
À la recherche d'une ou plusieurs séries effrayantes à regarder en attendant Halloween ? Les Numériques vous a trouvé 10 séries horrifiques à ne pas manquer en streaming.
Halloween approche à grands pas et vous avez peut-être envie de regarder des séries horrifiques en plus de vous faire peur devant des films du même genre. Cela tombe bien car Les Numériques a fait le tour des plateformes de streaming pour vous proposer une sélection de séries d'épouvante parfaites pour la saison qui donne la chair de poule.
De fictions franchement flippantes comme Ça : bienvenue à Derry et From à des séries plus gentillement effrayantes comme Mercredi et Les nouvelles aventures de Sabrina, voici 10 fictions sérielles pour vous préparer à la fête du 31 octobre à retrouver sur Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+, HBO Max et Paramount+ (dont l'offre est accessible via Canal+).
Ça : bienvenue à Derry (HBO Max)
Ça : Bienvenue à Derry
HBO Max
- Date de sortie
- 27/10/2025
- Genre
- Epouvante-horreur
- Durée
- 60 min
- Episodes
- 9
Des événements étranges se déroulent dans la ville de Derry dans les années 1960, liés au clown Grippe-Sou, un personnage mystérieux qui hante les lieux.
Ça : Bienvenue à Derry se base sur le roman Ça de Stephen King pour étendre son univers et la vision mise en place par Andy Muschietti dans ses deux films Ça. Résultat ? Une série absolument terrifiante et magistrale, un petit bijou horrifique du petit écran racontant une histoire captivante, soutenue par des protagonistes attachants, une mythologie fascinante et une mise en scène aussi glaçante que poignante. Tant pis si ça fait peur, on ne veut plus quitter Derry.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
The Haunting of Bly Manor (Netflix)
Dans l'Angleterre des années 1980, après la mort tragique d'une jeune fille au pair, Henry Wingrave engage une gouvernante américaine inexpérimentée pour s'occuper de sa nièce et de son neveu. Ces deux orphelins résident à Bly Manor avec le responsable du domaine Owen, la gardienne Jamie, et l'intendante Mrs Grose. Mais le manoir regorge de faux-semblants, et des siècles de sombres secrets n'attendent que d'être exhumés au fil de cette terrifiante romance gothique sur l'amour et le deuil. Car à Bly Manor, les morts ne sont pas tous des disparus...
Ce drame gothique inspiré de plusieurs histoires surnaturelles emblématiques d'Henry James est le deuxième volet de l'anthologie The Haunting de Mike Flanagan. Portée par une distribution épatante, des décors inquiétants et un récit captivant, cette série sait émouvoir autant que donner la chair de poule.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Widow's Bay (Apple TV)
Le maire d'une ville de Nouvelle-Angleterre souhaite en faire une destination touristique, malgré les avertissements sur le fait qu'elle est maudite.
Vous aimez l'horreur, les intrigues pleines de mystère et l'humour noir ? Alors vous serez comblés par cette série portée par un Matthew Rhys (The Americans) en grande forme. Sur fond de petite île à l'atmosphère inquiétante, Widow's Bay déroule une histoire prenante, soutenue par une mise en scène experte et des performances irréprochables de la part de l'ensemble de la distribution.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Entretien avec un vampire (Paramount+)
En 2022, le vampire Louis de Pointe du Lac raconte son histoire au célèbre journaliste Daniel Molloy. En 1910 à La Nouvelle-Orléans, Louis et Lestat forment une famille vampirique à laquelle vient s'ajouter Claudia, la novice adolescente.
Entretien avec un vampire est l’une des meilleures séries de ces dernières années et a su s’approprier Les Chroniques des vampires d'Anne Rice pour en faire une version plus sensuelle et contemporaine que l'adaptation cinématographique de 1994 avec Tom Cruise et Brad Pitt. De la distribution à l’écriture, en passant par la mise en scène, la cinématographie et les costumes, tout est soigneusement calibré pour proposer au spectateur une histoire gothique délicieusement addictive, portée par les performances impeccables de Sam Reid et Jacob Anderson.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Chair de poule (Disney+)
Cinq lycéens se lancent dans une terrible enquête pleine de rebondissements afin de cerner les circonstances du décès tragique, trente ans plus tôt, d’un adolescent, et découvrent au passage les lourds secrets de leurs parents.
Avec cette série, Disney+ modernise les histoires cultes de R.L. Stine et propose une fiction horrifique à la Stranger Things, avec une bande d'ados confrontée à des forces surnaturelles. Chair de poule mélange humour, drame et épouvante pour donner lieu à une histoire rythmée qui ouvre la porte au genre de l'horreur pour ceux qui ne s'y aventurent pas souvent.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Les nouvelles aventures de Sabrina (Netflix)
La magie se mêle au trouble alors que Sabrina, demi-humaine demi-sorcière, navigue entre deux mondes, sa vie d'ado mortelle et son héritage familial, l'Église de la Nuit.
Cette production Netflix réinvente la sitcom culte des années 1990 pour en faire une série bien plus sombre et tournée vers l'occulte, le macabre et l'épouvante. Sur fond d'histoire sur le passage à l'âge adulte, la série brille par son atmosphère inquiétante, son casting épatant (Kiernan Shipka, Miranda Otto, Lucy Davis...) pour offrir aux spectateurs un mélange de série pour ados, surnaturel et frissons.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Penny Dreadful (Prime Video)
Londres, 1891, une menace quasi invisible massacre la population. Vanessa Ives, une jeune femme aux pouvoirs puissants et hypnotiques, rencontre et propose à Ethan Chandler, un homme rebelle et violent, de s'allier à elle ainsi qu'à Sir Malcolm Murray, un homme riche d'un certain âge aux ressources intarissables, pour combattre cette nouvelle menace.
Laissez-vous séduire par cette série gothique à souhait qui a eu droit à trois saisons entre 2014 et 2016. Portée par Eva Green, Timothy Dalton et Josh Hartnett, cette série entre fantastique, épouvante et drame met en scène des personnages phares de la littérature du 19e siècle pour raconter une histoire aussi macabre que poétique. Des décors aux costumes en passant par la distribution, tout sort son plus grand jeu pour donner vie à une fiction sans pareille.
- Regardez une bande-annonce de la série :
From (Paramount+)
L'histoire d'une ville effrayante au milieu des États-Unis où toute personne qui y entre se retrouve piégée. Les habitants de la bourgade essaient de maintenir les choses aussi normales que possible tout en cherchant un moyen de s'échapper, car la nuit venue ils sont terrorisés par des monstres meurtriers.
Créée par John Griffin (Le Cratère, La Quatrième Dimension) et produite par des anciens de Lost, cette série d'horreur et de science-fiction plaira aux spectateurs qui aiment les personnalités fortes coincées dans une situation impossible. La série captive grâce à une histoire et des personnages fascinants tout en donnant des sueurs froides avec des créatures cauchemardesques.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Mercredi (Netflix)
La série suit les aventures de Mercredi Addams, désormais étudiante à la Nevermore Academy. Alors qu’elle apprend à dompter ses nouveaux pouvoirs psychiques, la jeune fille doit aussi déjouer une série de meurtres monstrueux qui terrorisent la ville et résoudre le mystère auquel ont été mêlés ses parents il y a 25 ans, le tout en tentant péniblement de nouer de nouvelles relations au sein de Nevermore.
Mercredi propose une histoire palpitante et bardée de rebondissements. Une série généreuse et délicieusement macabre qui saura plaire à tout le monde, de l’ado rebelle à ses parents déboussolés, en passant par l’adepte d’énigmes rondement ficelées. Un tour de force pour une famille Addams dont on a définitivement envie de faire partie.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
American Horror Story (Disney+)
Maisons hantées, asiles, sorcières, hôtels maudits ou sectes : la série change d’époque, de décor et de personnages à chaque nouvelle intrigue, tout en conservant certains visages familiers au casting. Les histoires mêlent surnaturel, violence, croyances, crimes et traumatismes profondément ancrés dans la société américaine. Certaines saisons finissent aussi par se répondre ou partager des personnages, dessinant peu à peu un univers commun derrière cette anthologie. Chaque chapitre explore ainsi une nouvelle forme de peur, souvent inspirée autant par les monstres que par les êtres humains.
Créé par Ryan Murphy, le showrunner et scénariste derrière les séries Dahmer, Glee et Ratched, American Horror Story est LE programme parfait pour les fans de frissons et d'horreur. Chacune de ses saisons possède sa thématique propre, de la maison hantée au cirque, en passant par l'apocalypse et l'asile, et joue avec brio de son ambiance glauque et de sa tension pour vous river à votre siège. Une série culte à rattraper ou revoir sans modération.
- Regardez une bande-annonce de la série :

articles.title: Nabta Health advances $3 million pre-Series A with backing from PVP
articles.text: UAE-based healthtech startup Nabta Health has secured a fresh investment from Phoenix Venture Partners (PVP), which led the second close of the company's ongoing $3 million pre-Series A round. PVP's investment includes both primary and secondary capital, while the amount raised in this closing was not disclosed. Founded in 2017 by Sophie Smith, Nabta Health develops AI-powered preventive healthcare solutions, with a focus on women's health, combining early disease detection, digital health services and clinical care. The company offers Aya, an AI-supported care navigation tool, alongside preventive screening and personalised care pathways, connecting patients, employers, insurers and healthcare providers to facilitate earlier intervention and coordinated care. The funding will support Nabta Health's commercial expansion, customer acquisition and strategic partnerships, particularly with employers, insurance companies and healthcare providers. In November 2025, Nabta Health raised $2 million pre-Series A , bringing its total funding to $4.5 million. Press release: Phoenix Venture Partners Limited (“PVP”), a venture capital fund manager domiciled in the Abu Dhabi Global Market (“ADGM”) and regulated by the Financial Services Regulatory Authority (“FSRA”), today announced that it has led the second close of Nabta Health's (“NABTA”) ongoing $3 million Pre-Series A financing. PVP’s investment comprises a blend of primary and secondary capital, further institutionalising a longstanding relationship with NABTA as the company enters its next stage of growth. The Pre-Series A has attracted participation from institutional investors, venture capital firms, family offices and high-net-worth investors. Founded in 2017 by Sophie Smith, NABTA has evolved significantly from its origins as a direct-to-consumer women’s health platform. Following years of investment in technology, clinical infrastructure and R&D, the company is entering a new phase focused on building AI-powered preventive healthcare infrastructure for employers, insurers and healthcare providers. NABTA combines early disease detection, AI-supported care navigation through Aya, and hybrid digital and clinical care, positioning the business as a connecting layer across patients, payors and providers. The company’s model is increasingly focused on enabling earlier intervention, more coordinated care and improved health outcomes, while helping employers and insurers address long-term healthcare costs through prevention and better population health management. NABTA’s clinics and expertise in women’s health remain important enablers of this broader platform. The investment marks the next chapter in PVP's longstanding relationship with NABTA. Dr. Mussaad Al-Razouki, Co-Founder and Non-Executive Director of PVP, who has supported NABTA since its early days as a founding investor and former Executive Chairman, will transition from his position on NABTA's Board, with Steve Khayat joining the Board as PVP's representative. The transition comes as NABTA moves from an extended period of product development and R&D into a phase increasingly focused on commercialisation and scale. Steve Khayat, Founder and CEO of Phoenix Venture Partners, said: “NABTA has done the hard work of building its technology, clinical infrastructure and model, and is already demonstrating strong commercial traction. We believe the company is now at an inflection point where the focus can shift decisively toward go-to-market and sales acceleration. Our role at PVP will be to work alongside Sophie and the team to deepen strategic partnerships, accelerate customer acquisition and help translate that traction into scalable growth.” Sophie Smith, Founder and CEO of Nabta Health, added: “We are delighted to welcome PVP as a shareholder and Steve to our Board at an important stage in NABTA’s journey. PVP brings not only capital, but also the regional relationships and hands-on support that can help us accelerate our next phase of commercial growth and deepen our partnerships with employers, insurers and healthcare providers.” The funding will support NABTA as it accelerates its go-to-market strategy, expands its enterprise proposition and develops new commercial relationships across the employer, insurance and healthcare ecosystems. PVP will work alongside NABTA’s leadership team to support this next stage of growth, leveraging its regional network and value-creation capabilities to help accelerate commercial partnerships and position the company for its next phase of institutional growth.

articles.title: Revolut and Lloyds Bank are down for millions — here's all the latest on the outages
articles.text:
Revolut and Lloyds Bank are down for millions — here's all the latest on the outages
Is Google Cloud to blame?
The online banking services for Revolut and Lloyds Bank are down for many users right now, with Revolut confirming it's been hit by an outage that's affecting "multiple services".
The issues for both Revolut and Lloyds Bank started at the same time at about 6.46am BST / 1.46am ET, with both showing large spikes on Downdetector. At their peak, there were almost 1,500 reports from Revolut customers on Downdetector and arounds 500 for Lloyds Bank.
While the reports have since dropped slightly, the outage appears to be ongoing for many — here's all the latest news, including whether it could potentially be related to confirmed Google Cloud problems...
The latest news
- Revolut and Lloyds Bank have been hit by outages in the UK this morning
- Revolut has confirmed it's experiencing a "service disruption" hitting "multiple services"
- The issues could be related to a Google Cloud outage that's also hitting UK other services, although this hasn't been confirmed
A 'power event' to blame?
The Google Cloud status page now says that "a power event caused an outage" in its europe-west2 region, which is based in London.
We still don't know for sure that it was the cause of today's Revolut and Lloyds Bank issues, but given the timing it certainly seems possible — and the good news is that the event has been "mitigated", with Google Cloud saying it's "seeing the recovery of services".
Google Cloud has "tentatively" promised that "full recovery of existing workloads" should be complete by 2pm BST — so if you're still struggling with your banking apps today, there is hope on the horizon.
Revolut reports remain high
While the likes of Lloyds Bank and HSBC have seen their number of reported issues on Downdetector drop significantly in the last two hours, Revolut has stayed pretty steady — which suggests that it continues to be the worst hit by today's cloud issues.
At 12.49pm BST, there were still almost 600 reports for Revolut — and its warning-splattered status page remains unchanged. Its engineers seemingly haven't yet been able to find a migration fix to get things working.
However, Google Cloud's status page has now "tentatively" promised that "full recovery of existing workloads should be completed" by 2pm BST, which could be promising news — assuming the two are related.
Revolut apologises
The Revolut Support account on X is working overtime to try and placate its many frustrated customers — but there's still no update on a fix for today's problems.
The latest updates from the account say "our team is working to restore service as soon as possible" and points people towards its system status page for more updates.
Right now, that page still looks identical to earlier, with a "partially unavailable" header and warning flags across most of its features, from card payments to ATM withdrawals.
Revolut appears to be the worst hit by today's issues — that could potentially be related to its deep "strategic partnership" with Google Cloud.
Another app bites the dust
The financial budgeting app, Emma, is also reporting being down today — and interestingly it directly blames the Google Cloud issues for the issues.
As far as I'm aware, none of the other banking services experiencing problems today have directly blamed Google Cloud, but Emma just has — and it's confirmed that "this is a technical outage, not a security issue".
We've hit the five-hour mark
Frustration is growing with many Revolut and Lloyds Bank customers, who have now been without important banking services for several hours — and have, in some cases, been left stranded.
Some of the anecdotal reports include people who are stuck at petrol stations being unable to pay, someone who can't pay for their taxi en route to an airport, and another poor soul who seemingly can't exit their train station in Japan.
The first reports started at 6.55am BST, so we're now approaching five hours with no fix in sight. And the frustration is partly stemming from the scale of outage, which is still hitting most parts of Revolut's services from the app to payments and transfers.
Revolut's latest statement continues to be the one it sent to us earlier and also posted on X at 8.54am.
HSBC and Rightmove also hit
While Revolut and Lloyds Bank have the highest number of reported issues this morning on Downdetector, they're far from alone — with HSBC and Rightmove also showing significant spikes.
Just over 400 users are reporting issues with the Rightmove app and also the paid Rightmove Plus service, while HSBC reports have dropped to just over 100 from an earlier high of 266 at 10.16am BST — but seem to be on the rise again.
While we still can't directly confirm all of this to today's Google Cloud incident or the problems affecting Revolut and Lloyds Bank, the simultaneous problems all point to a shared cloud infrastructure outage — and the only major one right now is with Google Cloud.
The case for Google Cloud grows
It's looking increasingly likely that Google Cloud is to blame for this morning's banking app issues.
The incident reported on Google Cloud's service health page is still ongoing, and we're reporting live on that outage separately.
While neither Revolut or Lloyds Bank have directly blamed Google Cloud for their issues today, their report graphs on Downdetector closely match those for Google's cloud infrastructure today (above).
This means both banking services could be somewhat reliant on Google Cloud fixing its issues in the "europe-west2 region" (which is based in London). Google's latest update at 10.24am BST says "our engineering team continues to investigate the issue", and that it'll provide another update at 12pm BST.
A statement from Lloyds Bank
A Lloyds Bank spokesperson has just sent me a statement on the issues it's experiencing this morning.
"Our app is online and customers can log in normally, though we understand some are having issues with certain online services this morning. We are aware of similar issues affecting other organisations and are monitoring the situation closely," they said.
That tallies with our experiences — my colleague Matthew Bolton, for example, says the Lloyds app is working for him, but is very slow. It's also telling that Lloyds says it's aware of "similar issues affecting other organisations", which could again point to that major Google Cloud outage being a potential cause.
Revolut confirms your money is safe
I've reached out to Revolut and Lloyds Bank this morning for their latest statements on this morning's banking problems. But if you're worried about your money in either bank, Revolut did post the message above earlier today at 8.54am BST.
It confirms the service disruption and says "we can confirm that all our customers’ money and data are safe". However, that's scant consolation to those who need to spend their money today – for example, the person who's reported being stuck in Japan train as they can't pay to get out.
Hopefully the "fix" that Revolut is working on will come soon, but reports on Downdetector are continuing to climb...
Is Google Cloud to blame?
While this is just speculation for now, the simultaneous issues affecting both Revolut and Lloyds Bank today point to a shared cloud infrastructure issue — and one of those is also hitting Google Cloud right now.
The Google Cloud status page reports that "Multiple services are experiencing issues in the europe-west2 region", which is located in London.
We don't yet know if there's a connection to the Revolut and Lloyds Bank issues, but that would explain why multiple UK services are experiencing issues right now. We've also seen spikes in reports for the likes of Royal Mail this morning, too.
Reports are on the rise
Reports on Downdetector peaked for Revolut at around 8.10am BST, but they seem to be on the rise again — and that's also the case for Lloyds Bank customers.
Most of the reports for Lloyds Bank are around 'login' issues, while for Revolut it's 'app' and 'funds transfer'.
I'm asking Revolut and Lloyds for an update on the issues, but Revolut's system status page says it's "currently experiencing an incident" that's affecting everything from sign-ins, card payments and topping up via bank card to ATM withdrawals.

articles.title: Una contraseña guardada en un dispositivo personal detonó el masivo hackeo a las licencias de Florida
articles.text:
Una sola contraseña guardada en un dispositivo electrónico personal desató el masivo hackeo a la base de datos de licencias de conducir de Florida (DAVID). La investigación confirmó que un criminal cibernético obtuvo las credenciales que un empleado policial conservaba fuera de los sistemas protegidos de la institución, usándolas para infiltrar los registros de licencias, vehículos e imágenes de documentos de residentes.
Tras el ataque ocurrido el 4 de septiembre, el Departamento de Seguridad Vial y Vehículos Motorizados de Florida (FLHSMV) comenzó a notificar tardíamente a las víctimas con un mes y medio de demora.
Un fallo de seguridad en una sola clave de policía expuso la base de datos de licencias
La investigación del propio FLHSMV determinó que el acceso no autorizado se produjo a través de las credenciales de un solo empleado del Departamento de Policía de Plant City, un suburbio cercano a Tampa. Ese empleado había guardado sus datos de acceso en un dispositivo electrónico personal, fuera de los sistemas protegidos de la policía.
Un criminal consiguió esas credenciales y las utilizó para ingresar a DAVID, la base de datos estatal que reúne licencias de conducir e información de vehículos y que usan agencias autorizadas en todo el país. El organismo atribuyó el ataque a “una organización criminal cibernética internacional”, sin identificarla formalmente.
El medio especializado en ciberseguridad BleepingComputer vinculó el episodio con el grupo ShinyHunters, que semanas atrás había publicado en un foro de la web oscura una captura de una supuesta licencia de conducir de Jeffrey Epstein, el financista fallecido y condenado por delitos sexuales, como prueba del robo. Según Ars Technica, ShinyHunters llegó a exigir un pago para no filtrar la base completa, con un plazo límite fijado para el 11 de septiembre.
Poco después de esa publicación, el grupo eliminó toda mención a Florida de su mensaje original, un movimiento que un investigador de la empresa de monitoreo de amenazas Flashpoint interpretó como un indicio de que el estado negociaba con los atacantes para evitar la difusión de los datos.
Qué información quedó expuesta
Según el propio FLHSMV, los datos que pudieron verse comprometidos incluyen licencias de conducir, información de vehículos, imágenes de documentos y otra información personal. La agencia no precisó cuántos registros fueron afectados en total.
ShinyHunters había reclamado haber sustraído más de 200.000 registros de conductores, de acuerdo con BleepingComputer, aunque el organismo estatal no confirmó esa cifra en ninguna de sus comunicaciones públicas.
El departamento ofrece un año de monitoreo de crédito gratuito a través de Sontiq, una empresa de TransUnion, para quienes reciban la carta de notificación. El problema, admitió la propia agencia, es que no cuenta con datos de contacto actualizados de muchos antiguos residentes de Florida cuya información seguía almacenada en el sistema.
Quienes sospechen que pudieron verse afectados, aunque ya no vivan en el estado, pueden escribir a la casilla customerinquiry@flhsmv.gov (dirección de correo electrónico) para confirmar si sus datos formaron parte del robo. La agencia también recomendó revisar periódicamente los resúmenes bancarios y considerar congelar el acceso al crédito ante las tres principales agencias calificadoras.
Un patrón que se repite
El episodio de Plant City ilustra lo que los especialistas en seguridad informática llaman “TI en la sombra”: el uso de dispositivos personales no autorizados para acceder a sistemas sensibles, fuera del control de los departamentos de tecnología. Un profesor de ciberseguridad consultado por la cadena WCTV explicó que esos equipos son mucho más fáciles de vulnerar que las computadoras institucionales.
FLHSMV aclaró que la investigación continúa junto con el Servicio Digital de Florida y el Departamento de Aplicación de la Ley del estado, y que difundirá nueva información cuando lo considere oportuno. Mientras tanto, las cartas de notificación seguirán llegando a quienes la agencia pueda localizar entre los residentes actuales y pasados del estado.

articles.title: Espressif Debuts ESP-Mosaico Modular Development Platform
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Espressif Debuts ESP-Mosaico Modular Development Platform
Espressif Systems (688018.SH) today announced ESP-Mosaico, a modular development platform designed for AI-assisted hardware creation. ESP-Mosaico allows creators to combine functional modules and multiple devices while enabling Coding Agents to understand the current hardware configuration and participate directly in application development.
ESP-Mosaico supports two complementary development approaches. Chat Coding lets creators start from a natural-language request and quickly build working hardware prototypes without setting up a local development environment. Vibe Coding brings AI Agents deeper into the engineering workflow, including implementation, deployment, testing on physical hardware, and continuous iteration.Software can now be generated and modified rapidly with AI, but hardware is still often constrained by fixed boards, interfaces, and product forms. ESP-Mosaico is designed to make hardware equally extensible: capabilities can be added as ideas evolve, without requiring creators to define the final form of a device from the outset.
The name Mosaico, meaning "mosaic," reflects this concept—individual hardware building blocks can be combined to create something larger and continuously evolving.
Modular Hardware That Grows with the Application
At the center of ESP-Mosaico is a compact standalone host featuring a 480 × 480 OLED touchscreen, haptic feedback, a built-in battery, USB Type-C connectivity, and expansion I/O.
The host is powered by Espressif's ESP32-S31, a RISC-V SoC running at up to 320 MHz, with 512 KB SRAM and support for up to 32 MB of high-speed DDR PSRAM. ESP32-S31 also integrates Wi-Fi 6, dual-mode Bluetooth 5.4, and 802.15.4, and supports interfaces including 1 Gbps Ethernet, USB 2.0 High-Speed OTG, hardware JPEG encoding and decoding, and DVP camera input.ESP-Mosaico extends these capabilities through modular hardware for functions such as cameras, sensors, buttons, lighting, and motors. Supported modules can be automatically identified and integrated by the system, reducing the need to repeatedly handle wiring and low-level driver adaptation.
Composability also extends across devices. Multiple ESP-Mosaico hosts can recognize their relative position and orientation and synchronize application state wirelessly, allowing devices to be joined, separated, or rearranged as part of the application itself. This enables experiences ranging from cross-screen games to modular information displays and other multi-screen applications.
Bringing AI Agents into Real-World Development
Chat Coding: From an Idea to a Working Prototype
For creators new to programming or AI-assisted development, ESP-Mosaico provides Chat Coding through ESP-Claw, the Coding Agent built into the platform.
Creators simply describe what they want to build. ESP-Claw uses the capabilities of the connected ESP-Mosaico hardware to generate, build, and deploy the application. Development does not require a locally configured toolchain, while application interfaces, logic, and peripheral control that do not depend on online services run locally on the device after deployment.
Creators can then continue refining the application conversationally—for example, adding functionality, changing behavior, or improving the user interface—turning an initial idea into an interactive hardware prototype through successive iterations.
ESP-Mosaico also connects to Skills Lab, where device applications can be packaged as reusable Skills containing Lua scripts, assets, and peripheral dependencies. Creators can install existing Skills, customize supported applications, or publish their own Skills for others to use.
Vibe Coding: Iterating Directly on Real Hardware
ESP-Mosaico is supported on ESP ZeroCode AI platform including its complete board and peripheral simulation. You can find various ESP-Mosaico community projects here.
For more advanced development, ESP-Mosaico is designed to bring other coding agents into the complete build-test-debug loop.
The platform provides:
- Specification-driven UI development, giving Agents defined design rules, components, resources, and constraints.
- ESP-GSP, an AI-oriented UI framework, where interfaces can be represented using structured JSON, validated during build, simulated on a PC, and then deployed to ESP32 hardware.
- Closed-loop device debugging, exposing flashing, device control, inputs, UI state, performance data, and fault information through unified interfaces so Agents can analyze results and iterate.
- Agent-ready development resources, including BSPs, SDKs, schematics, reference projects, documentation, and Agent References.
- Together, these capabilities allow an Agent to repeatedly modify code, build and deploy, test on real hardware, analyze feedback, and refine the application, while developers define the goals, constraints, and acceptance criteria.
Built on the Open ESP Development Ecosystem
AI-generated code still depends on a strong engineering foundation to run reliably on physical hardware. ESP-Mosaico builds on Espressif's established development ecosystem, including ESP-IDF, drivers and components, technical documentation, development and debugging tools, ESP Component Registry, and community projects. 
More than 200,000 projects related to ESP32 and ESP8266 are available on GitHub, along with more than 300 books published in over 10 languages. These resources can provide Coding Agents with engineering context, reference implementations, and proven development practices.
By connecting these open engineering resources with direct feedback from physical devices, ESP-Mosaico provides a foundation for AI-assisted hardware development that Agents can not only reference, but also build against and validate on real hardware.
Bring Ideas Beyond the Screen
Whether starting with Chat Coding or using Vibe Coding for deeper product development, ESP-Mosaico enables creators to move from an idea to a working physical device—and continue evolving it through software, hardware, and AI-assisted iteration.
Developers can visit the ESP-Mosaico website to learn more about the product and access development resources, or share applications with other users through Skills Lab.
The ESP-Mosaico development kit is now available for purchase. For additional product information, please contact the Espressif customer support team.
From natural-language creation to Agent-driven development, and from modular hardware to multi-device applications, ESP-Mosaico brings AI coding beyond the screen and into the physical world.
Sources:
				Espressif, 				Mosaico

articles.title: Ils détournent une PS5 pour faire tourner une IA locale et les résultats sont surprenants
articles.text:
Une PlayStation 5 capable de faire tourner des modèles d'intelligence artificielle à plus de 100 tokens par seconde ? C'est ce que démontre PS5LM Plus, un projet open source qui exploite le processeur graphique de la console pour exécuter des IA localement. Une prouesse technique, mais réservée aux PS5 modifiées.
Faire tourner une IA locale exige généralement un ordinateur doté de suffisamment de mémoire et de puissance de calcul. Pourtant, des développeurs ont trouvé un moyen d'exploiter un matériel déjà présent dans des millions de foyers : la PlayStation 5.
Tout commence avec PS5LM, un projet de Mert Cobanov qui adapte le moteur llama.cpp à la console de Sony. En quelques jours, un dérivé baptisé PS5LM Plus, développé par abhi245y, est allé beaucoup plus loin en permettant aux modèles d'utiliser directement le GPU AMD de la machine.
Du processeur au GPU, les performances changent d'échelle
La première approche utilisait uniquement le processeur de la PS5, avec environ 6 Gio de mémoire accessibles au programme. Sur un modèle volumineux, Qwen 3.8 27B, le résultat était extrêmement lent : environ un token généré par minute, les données devant être lues depuis le stockage.
PS5LM Plus contourne ces limitations grâce à une application native exploitant Vulkan et le processeur graphique de la console. Elle peut ainsi utiliser environ 12 Gio de mémoire partagée pour exécuter les modèles.
Le changement est spectaculaire : Qwen 3.8 27B atteint désormais une vingtaine de tokens par seconde, contre un seul par minute auparavant. Le développeur annonce également 61 tokens/s avec Gemma 4 E4B et jusqu'à 124 tokens/s avec Llama 3.2 3B.
Le projet rapporte même une réponse de 7 775 tokens produite à une moyenne de 19,7 tokens/s avec Qwen, signe que le débit peut se maintenir sur une génération relativement longue. Ces résultats restent toutefois ceux du développeur, et non de tests indépendants.
Pour tenir dans la mémoire disponible, le modèle de 27 milliards de paramètres utilise une quantification très poussée : ses paramètres sont compressés avec une précision d'environ 2 bits chacun. Cette méthode réduit considérablement les besoins en mémoire, mais peut dégrader la qualité des réponses.
Un serveur d'IA dans le salon, mais réservé aux bidouilleurs
Alors non, l'intérêt ne se limite pas à discuter avec une IA depuis son téléviseur ! PS5LM Plus propose une interface utilisable à la manette, une bibliothèque de modèles téléchargeables depuis Hugging Face et un serveur accessible aux autres appareils du réseau local.
Un ordinateur ou un smartphone peut ainsi envoyer des requêtes à la console, qui exécute les modèles sans passer par un service d'IA distant. Le serveur propose des interfaces compatibles avec les API OpenAI et Anthropic, permettant notamment à Claude Code, Codex ou OpenCode d'utiliser la PS5 comme moteur d'IA local, sous réserve des capacités du modèle installé.
Mais cette expérimentation exige une PS5 jailbreakée, avec un firmware compatible et plusieurs outils communautaires, notamment kstuff-lite, etaHEN et ShadowMountPlus. L'installation implique des manipulations techniques, avec des risques d'instabilité, de sécurité et d'éventuelles restrictions d'accès aux services Sony.
Il ne s'agit donc pas d'une solution prête à l'emploi, ni d'une raison suffisante pour acheter une PS5 afin d'exécuter des modèles d'IA. Les résultats dépendent aussi du modèle choisi, de sa compression et des ressources disponibles. L'expérience reste révélatrice : en exploitant le GPU d'une console conçue avant tout pour les jeux vidéo, les développeurs montrent qu'un appareil de salon peut aussi devenir un serveur d'intelligence artificielle.
Les projets PS5LM et PS5LM Plus sont disponibles sur GitHub.

articles.title: Popular WordPress SEO Plugin Rank Math PRO Hijacked to Deliver Self-Restoring Backdoor
articles.text:
Copies of Rank Math PRO, the paid version of the Rank Math SEO plugin for WordPress, that were downloaded from rankmath.com or delivered as updates between 20:02 UTC on October 15 and 07:12 UTC on October 16 contained malware, Rank Math said in a security notice published on October 16.
Any site that installed and activated one of those copies should be treated as compromised, and the malware can recreate its hidden backdoor whenever someone visits the site.
Rank Math has removed the affected files and released a clean version, 3.0.124. Installing it replaces the plugin but does not remove files, administrator accounts, or scheduled tasks the malware may already have placed elsewhere on the server, Wordfence said in an advisory on October 17.
Who Is Affected
The version number does not show whether a copy is affected. Rank Math's changelog dates 3.0.123 to October 7, more than a week before the window opened, and the notice limits the incident to copies downloaded or installed through an update during the window.
A copy of 3.0.123 obtained before 20:02 UTC on October 15 is outside it.
The notice sorts sites into three cases:
- You installed and activated 3.0.123 during the window: treat the site as compromised, even if it has since been updated to 3.0.124, and follow the recovery steps below.
- You installed it but never activated it: delete the plugin files, install 3.0.124 from your Rank Math account, and run a security scan.
- You downloaded it but never installed or activated it: nothing in this incident alone indicates the site was compromised.
Rank Math has emailed some users about the incident and told anyone unsure whether the files were installed or activated to contact its support team.
The notice applies only to the PRO plugin, which customers download and update from rankmath.com rather than WordPress.org. The free Rank Math SEO plugin on WordPress.org, which lists more than 4 million active installations and was last updated on October 6, is not named in it.
What the Malware Does
What is known about the malware comes from Rank Math's notice. Neither it nor Wordfence's advisory includes an analysis of the code, and neither names who is behind it.
Deleting suspicious files before stopping what recreates the backdoor may not resolve the problem, which is why the cleanup order below matters. The attacker may also have left PHP backdoor files in other plugins' folders, in theme folders, and in the must-use plugins directory, created administrator accounts, added a fake WordPress core file, changed .htaccess so that .cache files run as PHP, and added scheduled tasks and SSH keys.
Any password, database credential, API key, or other secret the site could reach may have been exposed, and owners should assume it was.
Wordfence assigned the incident CVE-2026-111862 and rates it 9.8 out of 10, with the researcher listed as unknown.
Patchstack classifies it as a backdoor and says that, because the attack was on Rank Math's own systems, "a rule is not possible for mitigation."
How to Recover
Rank Math's preferred recovery is a restore. Where a backup of the site and its database from before 20:02 UTC on October 15 exists, restore it, run a security scan, change every password and credential, and only then install 3.0.124 from your Rank Math account.
Where no clean backup exists, the manual cleanup runs in a fixed order, and three actions come before anything else is touched:
- Delete the entire rank-math-pro plugin folder using the hosting file manager or FTP. "Deactivating the plugin alone is not sufficient," the notice says.
- In the wp_options table, delete any entry whose option_name is _uf6qdn2hmm, t8krdk990phb or _np5pvf754c.
- Block outgoing connections to rank1cdn[.]com if the hosting provider or firewall allows it.
Only then does the search for other changes begin, in these places:
- Files: PHP files in wp-content/mu-plugins/, in other plugins' folders, in the inc/, includes/ and lib/ folders of non-default themes, in Rank Math's own includes/ folder, and in uploads/.
- Code: PHP that uses base64_decode with XOR loops, the key xmmqhn, proc_open, or PHP-FPM socket code.
- File: wp-includes/class-wp-cache-util.php, which is not a WordPress core file.
- Accounts: administrator usernames beginning wpsupport_, or accounts with email addresses ending @wp-mail[.]net.
- Server: .htaccess rules that let .cache files run as PHP, .cache files containing PHP code, entries tagged #ms6v46 in the web server user's crontab, WordPress scheduled events, SSH authorized_keys files, other users' crontabs, running processes, and any location outside the site where the web server can write.
Wordfence adds a caution: "Their absence does not, by itself, prove that a website is clean."
Credentials are changed in every case, even after a restore from backup. The list covers WordPress passwords, the database username and password in wp-config.php, the security keys and salts in the same file, payment gateway, SMTP and other API keys, hosting control panel, FTP, SFTP and SSH access, secrets held in environment variables, and two-factor authentication for administrators.
The cleanup ends with a security scan, wp core verify-checksums for WordPress core, and wp plugin verify-checksums --all, with the caution that checksums may not exist for premium plugins.
WordPress.org publishes none for this one. The Hacker News checked its plugin-checksums service on October 19 and found no file for the PRO plugin under either of its names, while the service does publish one for the free plugin. The fallback notice provides a clean copy from the official source.
The clean 3.0.124 goes on last, downloaded by logging in at rankmath.com directly. Some customers may be unable to log in and may need to reset their account password, the notice says, without saying why, and Rank Math will never send login or download links by email.
What Rank Math Has Not Said
Rank Math, part of the Swedish hosting group group.one, has not said how the malicious files entered its download and update system, how many customers received one, whether automatic updates delivered them, or what the clean and tainted packages' hashes are. Its only statement about the future is that the team is taking steps to reduce the risk of similar incidents.
Registry records show the domain Rank Math tells owners to block, rank1cdn[.]com, was registered at 19:31 UTC on October 14, about a day before the window opened.
A Pattern This Year
This is at least the third time this year that a premium WordPress plugin's vendor-run update channel has delivered backdoored builds. In April, Nextend's update system served a backdoored Smart Slider 3 Pro for about six hours.
In June, ShapedPlugin's Pro plugins were found to have been backdoored in its update channel, and one package that had shipped clean was later "tampered with under the same version number," the trap Rank Math's customers now face.
Attackers also altered scripts served from Awesome Motive's CDN in June and poisoned BdThemes' API feed in August. Nothing published links the attackers behind any of those incidents to this one.

articles.title: Gemini tiene nuevos nombres: así cambian algunas funciones en la IA de Google
articles.text:
Google reorganiza los nombres de varias funciones de Gemini y modifica la forma en que los usuarios acceden a las instrucciones personalizadas de su inteligencia artificial. El cambio alcanza a Gems, Spark y Acciones programadas, con un cronograma que arranca en octubre de 2026 y se extiende hasta 2027 para cuentas corporativas y educativas.
La transición no es solo cosmética. Cada función conserva su propósito, pero cambia el modo en que se activa y, en algunos casos, se integra dentro del chat principal en lugar de abrir una ventana propia.
Cuáles son los cambios en los nombres de Gemini
- De Gems a Skills
Los Gems funcionaban como bots personalizados independientes: cada uno se seleccionaba desde una barra lateral y abría una conversación separada. Esa lógica desaparece con la llegada de las Skills, un sistema que incorpora las instrucciones personalizadas directamente al chat principal de Gemini.
Para activar una Skill, basta con escribir una barra diagonal dentro del cuadro de solicitud y elegir la opción necesaria. Gemini también puede aplicarla de forma automática cuando detecta que las instrucciones coinciden con el pedido del usuario.
La diferencia con el esquema anterior es la posibilidad de combinar varias Skills en una misma conversación: una puede fijar la identidad de marca de una empresa y otra el tono de escritura, sin necesidad de trasladar resultados entre bots distintos.
Las Skills usan el formato abierto SKILL.md, basado en Markdown, lo que permite crear y transferir instrucciones entre herramientas sin depender de una sola plataforma. Están disponibles en la aplicación de Gemini y también en Google Workspace, algo que los Gems nunca permitieron.
No todas las funciones migraron todavía. Canvas, Investigación profunda, Aprendizaje guiado y la generación de vídeo y música siguen sin funcionar dentro de una Skill, como tampoco es posible compartirla ni adjuntar archivos de Drive, opciones que Google prometió incorporar más adelante.
- Spark se convierte en Tarea
Spark es el agente de Gemini que continúa trabajando después de que el usuario cierra la computadora o bloquea el teléfono. Google dejó de destacar ese nombre y ahora lo presenta como Tarea, visible en un selector junto al cuadro de solicitud, mientras que su página de configuración pasó a llamarse Configuración de tareas.
La herramienta opera en máquinas virtuales de Google Cloud y puede ejecutar procesos de varios pasos en aplicaciones y sitios web, como investigar competidores o monitorear precios de vuelos.
Google incorporó puntos de control: la función pide aprobación antes de enviar mensajes, modificar datos, realizar compras o completar formularios, y devuelve el control cuando un sitio solicita contraseñas o datos de pago.
Cuál es la función que no cambia de nombre
A diferencia de Gems y Spark, Acciones programadas mantiene su denominación. Permite escribir una solicitud, definir cuándo debe ejecutarse y establecer la frecuencia, con un límite de 10 acciones activas de forma simultánea.
En la versión web, el chat correspondiente aparece como no leído; en móviles, Gemini envía una notificación que puede mostrarse en la pantalla de bloqueo según la configuración del dispositivo.
Cuándo se realizarán los cambios en Gemini
El despliegue de Skills en Workspace comenzó el 5 de octubre de 2026 para dominios de lanzamiento rápido y se extendió a dominios programados a partir del 19 de octubre, con finalización prevista a mediados de noviembre.
En la aplicación de Gemini, las Skills empezaron a lanzarse el 13 de octubre de 2026 para todos los usuarios, con el mismo cierre estimado a mediados de noviembre. Durante ese período conviven ambos sistemas.
El 17 de noviembre de 2026 es la fecha clave para cuentas personales: Google empezará a convertir de forma automática los Gems en Skills, que quedarán como borradores inactivos hasta que el creador los revise y active.
Para empresas, el cambio definitivo llega el 1 de marzo de 2027, cuando ya no se podrán crear, editar ni usar Gems, y los flujos de Google Workspace Studio con el paso “Pregúntale a una Gem” dejarán de funcionar.
En educación, el mismo cierre se aplicará el 1 de junio de 2027, con la eliminación de Gems en Google Classroom y en los sistemas de gestión de aprendizaje compatibles con Gemini mediante LTI.

articles.title: Aspiration de 8 000 Pa et vidage automatique : le robot Roborock Q7 L5+ est à 179,99 €
articles.text:
Le robot aspirateur laveur Roborock Q7 L5+ avec station est à 179,99 € (-54 %)
Le robot aspirateur laveur Roborock Q7 L5+ combine navigation LiDAR, aspiration de 8 000 Pa et station de vidage automatique pour l’entretien quotidien des sols.
Amazon propose le robot aspirateur laveur Roborock Q7 L5+ blanc à 179,99 €, contre un prix conseillé de 389,99 €, soit une réduction de 54 %. Par rapport au prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours, indiqué à 189,99 €, l’économie atteint 10 €, soit environ 5 %. L’appareil est vendu par Roborock Official EU et expédié par Amazon.
Une aspiration de 8 000 Pa et un parcours guidé par LiDAR
Le robot aspirateur laveur Roborock Q7 L5+ annonce une puissance d’aspiration maximale de 8 000 Pa. Ses brosses principale et latérale sont conçues pour limiter l’enroulement des cheveux et des poils. Cela ne dispense pas de leur entretien, mais vise à réduire les interventions nécessaires.
La navigation LiDAR PreciSense cartographie le logement pour organiser les déplacements. Depuis l’application Roborock, il est possible de programmer les séances, de sélectionner les pièces et de définir des zones interdites. Le fabricant annonce jusqu’à 150 minutes d’autonomie, une durée qui varie selon les réglages et les conditions d’utilisation.
Une station de vidage et une serpillière plate
La station RockDock Plus récupère automatiquement la poussière dans un sac de 2,7 litres. Roborock annonce jusqu’à sept semaines avant son remplacement, selon la fréquence des nettoyages et la quantité de saletés collectées. Elle réduit ainsi le besoin de vider manuellement le bac du robot après chaque passage.
Pour les sols durs, le robot peut aspirer et passer une serpillière avec trois niveaux de débit d’eau. Le lavage repose sur une lingette plate entraînée par les déplacements de l’appareil, sans rotation ni vibration. Le remplissage du réservoir et le nettoyage de la serpillière restent manuels : la station assure le vidage de la poussière et la recharge.

articles.title: Companies are spending nearly a third of IT budgets on software upgrades
articles.text:
Companies are spending nearly a third of IT budgets on software upgrades
'Software tax' is a major ongoing cost
- Enterprises are being forced into software upgrades that they can't really get out of, report finds
- 91% have upgraded hardware in the past three years just to maintain software
- Enterprise protection legislation and software support obligations could be the answer
Legacy tech has become something of a hot topic in recent years with AI, but while hardware and data foundations have been core to the discussion around artificial intelligence, a new Origina report has revealed that around one-third of enterprise IT budgets are being earmarked for software upgrades.
The report found that 28% of large enterprise IT budgets are being spent on vendor-driven changes that they would not have otherwise chosen in a trend the company's calling a 'software tax'.
But more than just consuming budgets, software changes are also impacting worker time and leading to potentially lost productivity as a result.
Software upgrades cost more than you might think
"That's not a one-off cost, it's a recurring drag on capacity, and every year it repeats is a year those people aren't working on the initiatives that actually differentiate the business," former Liberty Mutual CIO James McGlennon and Origina board member James McGlennon explained.
More than four in five (84%) report that senior engineering staff always or often spend time dealing with vendor-driven software changes, taking them away from more meaningful work that they're employed to do. A similar number (80%) also reported that leaving a major software vendor could lead to widespread disruption within their business, ultimately forcing them to stay with that software vendor and enforcing vendor lock-in – with exit costs and migration technicalities to blame.
More than three-quarters now agree their software vendor dictates the timing and terms of changes, not them (78%), and that they have very little negotiating power (76%).
In many instances, enterprise customers don't even feel that an upgrade was totally necessary. Nearly all (91%) had retired fully functional hardware within the past three years just to comply with software vendor support deadlines. While Origina doesn't specifically state it, Windows 10's end of support is likely a large factor in this statistic.

articles.title: Axiomtek Launches MANO330 Compact Thin Mini-ITX Industrial Motherboard
articles.text:
Tuesday, October 20th 2026
Axiomtek Launches MANO330 Compact Thin Mini-ITX Industrial Motherboard
Axiomtek, a world-renowned leader relentlessly devoted to the research, development, and manufacture of innovative, highly efficient, and reliable industrial computer products, proudly introduces the MANO330, a compact Thin Mini-ITX motherboard powered by the Intel Processor N97 or N150 and DDR5 memory. Designed for space-constrained systems that require flexible connectivity and expansion, the MANO330 combines multi-display capability, dual LAN connectivity, versatile M.2 expansion, and industrial I/O in a compact platform. With a wide 12-24 VDC power input, the MANO330 provides system developers with a flexible foundation for smart manufacturing and industrial automation, digital signage, smart retail, and POS applications.
Compact Performance for Space-Constrained Systems
The MANO330 combines a compact Thin Mini-ITX design with Intel Processor N97 or N150 and DDR5-4800 memory support. The N97 supports up to 32 GB of memory, while the N150 supports up to 16 GB. Measuring just 170 x 170 mm, the MANO330 provides the essential computing performance and I/O capabilities needed for embedded systems, helping developers build space-efficient solutions for a wide range of industrial and commercial applications.Rich Visuals and Reliable Network Connectivity
Designed for information-rich applications, the MANO330 supports multiple independent display outputs through HDMI, VGA, LVDS/eDP interface, and USB Type-C with DisplayPort support. This display flexibility allows system developers to configure multiple screens for applications such as digital signage, retail displays, and industrial monitoring. The board also integrates 2.5GbE and GbE LAN, providing reliable network connectivity for connected systems and industrial applications.
Flexible Expansion to Fit Different Applications
The MANO330 provides flexible expansion options for storage and wireless connectivity. Its M.2 Key M 2280 slot supports SATA/NVMe storage, while M.2 Key E 2230 supports wireless connectivity. The M.2 Key B 3042/3052 interface provides an additional expansion option and is paired with a Nano SIM slot for wireless applications. These options allow customers to configure storage and connectivity according to their application requirements, helping simplify system development and integration.
Built-In I/O for Easier System Integration
The MANO330 integrates commonly used industrial interfaces directly on the board, including RS-232, RS-422/485, USB, SATA, and GPIO, helping reduce the need for additional interface hardware. Two RS-232 ports support jumper-selectable RS-422 or RS-485, while four additional RS-232 ports provide further serial connectivity for industrial devices. Combined with the board's 12-24 VDC power input, these built-in interfaces provide system developers with greater flexibility and help simplify system integration.
Tina Tu, Product Manager at Axiomtek"Today's embedded systems need to balance compact design with flexibility for different application requirements. With versatile display, connectivity, expansion, and industrial I/O options, the MANO330 gives system developers greater freedom to configure and integrate solutions for a wide range of industrial and commercial applications"
Advanced Features of MANO330
- Intel Processor N97/N150
- DDR5-4800 SO-DIMM, up to 32 GB with N97 and 16 GB with N150
- Dual LAN ports
- M.2 Key B 3042/3052
- M.2 Key E 2230
- M.2 Key M 2280
The MANO330 is now available.

articles.title: GTA 6 aún no sale, pero ya hay estafadores vendiendo versiones falsas por hasta mil dólares
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 todavía no llega al mercado, pero ya circulan sitios web que prometen copias filtradas, acceso anticipado y versiones de prueba a cambio de hasta USD 1.000. Las falsas ofertas utilizan la expectativa por el estreno previsto para el 19 de noviembre de 2026 para obtener pagos, datos personales o descargas de archivos desconocidos.
El riesgo crece porque muchos jugadores llevan más de una década esperando la nueva entrega de Rockstar Games. La compañía de seguridad digital, Kaspersky, detectó varias páginas dirigidas a los seguidores de GTA VI, con promesas de reservas gratuitas, pruebas beta y criptomonedas vinculadas con el juego. Ninguna de estas alternativas ofrece acceso legítimo antes del lanzamiento oficial.
Ofrecen una supuesta filtración por USD 1.000
Uno de los casos detectados corresponde a una página llamada CyberLeek. El sitio afirma disponer de una versión preliminar de GTA VI y presenta tres formas de obtenerla antes de su salida.
La primera opción promete el “juego completo” por USD 1.000, junto con contenido exclusivo y un enlace de descarga directa. La web asegura que la oferta tiene un límite de una copia por cliente.
También ofrece una prueba de 24 horas por USD 100. La tercera propuesta consiste en una campaña de financiación colectiva. Sus responsables aseguran que reunirán USD 50.000 para liberar el juego, aunque la letra pequeña eleva de forma repentina el objetivo a USD 500.000. Quienes aporten al menos USD 100 recibirían, según el sitio, acceso prioritario.
La página incluso promociona servicios para empresas. Por USD 5.000, propone introducir logotipos, productos o menciones de marca en un supuesto contenido futuro de Grand Theft Auto. La oferta resulta contradictoria con la promesa de una versión completa ya disponible para descargar.
Todos los pagos se realizan con Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT o Litecoin. El sitio indica que las operaciones son definitivas y no admite devoluciones.
CyberLeek fue el apodo del responsable de una intrusión en Rockstar Games y de una filtración de contenido de GTA VI. Después, otros actores comenzaron a utilizar ese nombre para crear webs con diseños distintos, pero con la misma promesa: acceso a una versión filtrada u oficial del juego.
Algunas de esas páginas invitan a descargar un lanzador desconocido o a “desbloquear” la versión completa. Los archivos e instaladores distribuidos desde estas webs pueden representar un riesgo, por lo que no conviene utilizarlos ni ejecutarlos en el ordenador personal.
Las falsas reservas solicitan correos, pagos y datos personales
Otra modalidad se dirige a quienes buscan reservar el juego. Una página ofrece códigos para PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S, y solicita al usuario elegir una consola e introducir su correo electrónico.
Para reforzar la apariencia de legitimidad, el sitio muestra 3.480 usuarios activos y asegura que solo quedan 121 códigos. Tras pulsar “Revelar código”, la página enseña cuatro caracteres y exige una verificación adicional que debe completarse en 15 minutos.
La comprobación lleva a una página en alemán que pide descargar y ejecutar una aplicación de chat con inteligencia artificial, además de aceptar sus condiciones. El objetivo puede ser enviar tráfico a páginas de terceros, algunas de ellas fraudulentas, con GTA VI como señuelo.
También existen páginas que imitan la PlayStation Store. Una de ellas, dirigida a usuarios brasileños, ofrece reservas por 449,9 BRL (cerca de 90 dólares), una cifra similar al precio oficial. El pago se puede efectuar con tarjeta o Pix, pero exige datos personales, incluido el CPF.
Los sitios que aseguran que GTA VI ya está disponible también son una trampa
Otros estafadores simplifican el engaño. Crean páginas con estética de GTA y logotipos de Rockstar Games, donde invitan a “probar GTA 6” o descargarlo para PC, PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S.
El juego no está disponible antes del 19 de noviembre de 2026. Por eso, cualquier descarga previa puede ocultar archivos no deseados. La barra de direcciones suele revelar el fraude: es necesario revisar el dominio y compararlo con la web oficial de Rockstar Games.
Otra web promociona una criptomoneda llamada $GTAVI, diseñada con referencias a Vice City. Sus creadores afirman que quienes posean el token podrían acceder al juego en el futuro, aunque no garantizan una copia.
El sitio declara una capitalización de USD 51.600 y un volumen de negociación diario de USD 7.880, sin explicar el origen ni la precisión de esas cifras. El modelo puede responder a una estrategia de inflar el valor del activo y venderlo después, con pérdidas para quienes lleguen tarde.
La recomendación es instalar juegos solo desde fuentes oficiales, no introducir datos de pago ni información personal en webs sospechosas y evitar lanzadores, archivos comprimidos o programas desconocidos. Ninguna beta, clave o filtración sustituye el lanzamiento oficial de GTA VI.

articles.title: NordVPN patches "clumsy" Windows bug that let attackers disable system services
articles.text:
NordVPN patches "clumsy" Windows bug that let attackers disable system services
The vulnerability allowed low-privileged local attackers to disable unprotected Windows services, but critical antivirus defenses remained completely safe.
- A vulnerability in NordVPN's Windows app allowed local attackers to stop unprotected system services.
- The flaw, officially tracked as CVE-2026-106030, does not affect NordVPN version 8.12.0.0 or later
- Experts label the bug "clumsy," but the actual impact on users is minimal, requiring a device to already be compromised by malware.
Nord Security has rolled out an important security update for its Windows application to address a vulnerability that could allow a hacker to stop unprotected Windows services.
The flaw allowed a local, low-privileged attacker to act as a trusted process. From there, they could potentially stop unprotected Windows services or change their startup types to manual, leading to a denial of service for those specific applications.
When a top-tier provider, frequently ranked as the best VPN on the market, flags a security patch of this nature, it naturally turns heads. However, cybersecurity experts stress that while the coding error shouldn't have happened, the real-world danger to users is incredibly low.
The issue, officially tracked as CVE-2026-106030, was responsibly reported to CERT Polska by IT Security Expert Marcin Ressel. NordVPN appears to have fixed the vulnerability in version 8.12.0.0, and users are simply advised to ensure their app is fully up to date.
How the vulnerability works
To understand the bug, you have to look at how Windows applications talk to each other using a feature called "named pipes."
According to an intelligence brief published by Mallory, the vulnerability allowed an attacker to connect to a specific NordVPN named pipe and invoke methods to stop services or change their start types without proper authorization.
Mike Williams, Technical Editor at TechRadar, explains the core of the issue: "Named pipes are a common means for Windows processes to communicate with each other. One process might send a message to another asking it to carry out some task."
Because this communication channel is incredibly powerful, it is a frequent target for threat actors. "Because named pipes are so sensitive, hackers often try to abuse them, to run these tasks without permission," Williams notes. "That means it's important to secure them, and make sure that only messages from legitimate processes are accepted. Any good developer knows this: it's a fundamental aspect of using named pipes."
Unfortunately, the NordVPN Windows app, specifically versions earlier than 8.12, fell short of this standard. "NordVPN has failed to do that, which makes this a clumsy bug. It should never have happened," Williams adds.
Why the real-world impact is minimal
While the technical details of the flaw, which carries a CVSS v4 base severity score of 6.8, sound alarming, the practical implications for the average user are far less dramatic.
In a LinkedIn post, the researcher who discovered the flaw, Marcin Ressel, described it as "a local privilege escalation with limited impact" that he found while "playing around with NordVPN for Windows."
Crucially, this exploit can't shut down critical, system-protected security services. Built-in defenses like Windows Defender and processes guarded by Windows Tamper Protection are entirely immune to this specific attack.
"But the impact of the bug is very small," Williams clarifies. "All an attacker can do is change the status of non-critical Windows services. That is, it can't turn off Windows Defender, but maybe it could disable something related to media playback. But even if it did that, it's only flipped a Windows setting, and once you understood the cause, you could just flip it back."
Furthermore, this vulnerability cannot be triggered remotely over the internet. An attacker would already need to have a local foothold on your machine to exploit it. There has also been no active exploitation of this flaw reported in the wild.
"In other words, there's no impact on the VPN itself, and you would have to have malware running on your PC to even cause the issue," Williams concludes. "(And if there's malware running on your device then you've much bigger problems than this.)"
If you are running NordVPN on Windows, your best defense is simple: open the app and confirm you are running version 8.12.0.0 or later.
