articles.title: Crean un sistema inalámbrico que brindaría electricidad a implantes médicos blandos aun con el cuerpo en movimiento
articles.text:
Un equipo de investigadores surcoreanos desarrolló un sistema inalámbrico que alimenta implantes médicos blandos mientras se estiran o se mueven dentro del cuerpo, un avance que podría marcar el camino hacia marcapasos y otros dispositivos sin baterías que operen bajo las condiciones dinámicas de un organismo vivo, informó TechXplore, portal de divulgación especializado en ciencia y tecnología.
El sistema, descrito en la revista Nature Electronics, fue desarrollado por un equipo del Instituto de Ciencias Básicas (IBS) y la Universidad Nacional de Seúl (SNU), con la participación de investigadores de la Universidad Nacional de Jeonbuk (JBNU), la Universidad Kyung Hee y el Hospital de la Universidad Nacional de Seúl.
El dispositivo combina un transmisor portátil externo con un receptor implantable fabricado en metal líquido, capaz de deformarse sin perder conductividad eléctrica. El transmisor puede operarse desde un teléfono inteligente a través de una aplicación de Bluetooth Low Energy, con la que un médico o el propio paciente podría ajustar los parámetros del sistema sin necesidad de equipos especializados.
Un sistema que se adapta solo
El principal desafío en la alimentación inalámbrica de implantes blandos es que el movimiento continuo del cuerpo —y en particular el latido del corazón— altera constantemente la posición y la forma del receptor, lo que en los sistemas convencionales provoca una caída abrupta de la eficiencia. Dae-Hyeong Kim, investigador principal del estudio, relató que ese fue el punto de partida del proyecto: “Todo comenzó con una pregunta práctica: ¿cómo podemos alimentar de manera confiable un implante inalámbrico en un cuerpo que está en constante movimiento?”.
Para resolver ese problema, el equipo recurrió a la simetría paridad-tiempo (PT, por sus siglas en inglés), un principio proveniente de la física cuántica que ya se aplica en sistemas ópticos y electrónicos. Aplicado a la transferencia inalámbrica de energía, permite que el transmisor ajuste su frecuencia operativa en tiempo real para seguir al receptor, sin importar cómo se desplace o deforme el implante. “En la transferencia inalámbrica de potencia, este principio permite una transferencia de energía estable al equilibrar la energía suministrada por el transmisor con la que consume el receptor”, describió Kim.
Del lado del implante, el equipo fabricó el receptor con conductores de metal líquido a base de galio, encapsulados en elastómeros blandos y biocompatibles. A diferencia de los metales sólidos —que al estirarse adelgazan y elevan su resistencia eléctrica—, el metal líquido redistribuye su volumen sin perder sección transversal, lo que mantiene la conductividad casi constante durante la deformación. Según los datos publicados en el estudio, la eficiencia de transferencia supera el 50 % incluso cuando el receptor se estira un 30 % respecto de su longitud original, y el sistema permanece estable ante desplazamientos laterales de hasta 30 milímetros.
“Desarrollamos un receptor de metal líquido intrínsecamente elástico que mantiene una alta conductividad eléctrica durante la deformación. Combinado con el transmisor adaptativo, permitió una alimentación inalámbrica confiable incluso cuando el estiramiento y el desalineamiento ocurrían de manera simultánea”, precisó el investigador.
La prueba en el corazón
Para demostrar la viabilidad clínica de la tecnología, el equipo construyó un marcapasos cardíaco sin cables que integra el receptor de metal líquido con circuitos de estimulación y electrodos de nanohilos de plata y oro embebidos en elastómero, un material altamente elástico capaz de estirarse y volver a su forma original. El transmisor portátil —alimentado por una batería de litio de 11 voltios y controlado por un microcontrolador— se montó sobre el exterior del cuerpo en pruebas con animales.
Las pruebas en modelos porcinos confirmaron que el sistema logró estimular el corazón de forma continua y, además, interrumpir episodios de taquiarritmia ventricular, es decir, ritmos cardíacos anormalmente acelerados, mediante estimulación eléctrica controlada. “Confirmamos que el marcapasos funcionó de manera confiable a pesar de la deformación y los cambios en la alineación”, afirmó Kim.
El profesor Junho Moon, de la Facultad de Medicina Veterinaria de la JBNU y responsable de la validación en animales vivos, informó que los dispositivos se implantaron de forma estable bajo la piel y sobre la superficie cardíaca de conejos y cerdos. El monitoreo electrocardiográfico en tiempo real confirmó la estimulación efectiva en múltiples sitios de los ventrículos izquierdo y derecho.
El camino hacia la aplicación clínica
A pesar de los resultados alentadores en animales, el equipo reconoce que el camino hacia la aplicación en entornos de salud reales todavía es largo. Será necesario optimizar la eficiencia de transferencia, miniaturizar los componentes, evaluar la seguridad en tejidos y validar la confiabilidad a largo plazo antes de avanzar hacia ensayos clínicos en humanos.
Kim señaló que el alcance de la tecnología va más allá del marcapasos: “Nuestro enfoque relaja esas restricciones y permite que un transmisor portátil, que podría adoptar la forma de un parche adherible a la piel, alimente de manera confiable un implante blando en condiciones más dinámicas”. La arquitectura podría aplicarse a sistemas de monitoreo fisiológico continuo y de neuroestimulación, entre otros dispositivos blandos que deban operar mientras el cuerpo se mueve.
El próximo objetivo del equipo es extender la funcionalidad del sistema para que, además de recibir energía, el implante pueda enviar datos al dispositivo externo. El investigador describió que trabajan en incorporar la transmisión de señales dentro del mismo marco de simetría PT, con vistas a crear “sistemas de lazo cerrado que ajusten la estimulación en respuesta a las señales que registran”.

articles.title: Fake Web3 Accelerator Uses npm Packages to Spread Malware and Hijack AI Agent Traffic
articles.text:
A fake Web3 accelerator has been observed pushing information stealers and backdoors to Windows and macOS systems using malicious npm packages under the pretext of offering free artificial intelligence (AI) credits for Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini, coding tools, and security audits.
"The tools delivered information-stealing malware and backdoors for macOS and Windows machines," Elastic Security Labs researchers Jia Yu Chan and Daniel Stepanic said. "The operation also repackaged a legitimate coding agent to send model requests through attacker-controlled services, while its audit tools generated fabricated security findings."
The scheme poses as a Web3 venture capital accelerator named Apex Accelerator to target cryptocurrency startups and founders. It's being tracked under the moniker REF8801. The names of the npm packages, each of which targets both Windows and macOS machines, are listed below -
- @apexacc/cli (Apex Copilot CLI — AI advisor for Web3 founders) -
- @apexacc/audit (Web3 Security Scanner — 18 tools for DYOR and smart contract auditing)
While both the packages and their associated GitHub repositories are no longer accessible, "@apexacc/cli" was advertised as an "AI advisor for Web3 founders" that's powered by Claude Fable 5 and Gemini 2.5 Flash.
"@apexacc/audit," on the other hand, claimed to be a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposing 18 security tools for scanning tokens, wallets, and smart contracts. Both packages were published by an npm user named "apexaccelerator" and linked to a GitHub account called "apexaccs" and an entity referred to as the Apex Foundation.
It's unclear who is behind the operation, but Elastic Security Labs said it spotted Russian-language comments in the source code commit history. However, these clues alone are not sufficient to definitively establish their identity or origins.
Interestingly, the campaign itself is not new. In late July 2026, SafeDep detailed three other npm packages linked to the same operation that were found distributing a macOS stealer belonging to the Atomic Stealer (aka AMOS) family -
- @apexfdn/apex
- @copilot-mcp/apex, which features the same package description as "@apexacc/cli"
- @apexfdn/copilot-mcp, which claims to be an Apex Copilot and MCP server for "portfolio diligence and operator tools"
Artifacts captured by Socket show that the Apex Foundation has been linked to at least two distinct domains since April 2026 -
- apexaccs[.]org
- apexfdn[.]xyz
According to Internet Archive snapshots dating back to March 19, 2026, the website claimed that "the Apex Foundation offers $235,000 investments, grants, and partnerships, and connects projects with VCs, angels, and private equity if they don't meet our criteria."
Posts shared on X show the accelerator approaching developers of cryptocurrency wallets and market intelligence tools for traders with offers of direct investment and instructions to run their due diligence tool ("@apexacc/cli"). In the case of the latter, the npm package has been found to drop an encrypted malware loader disguised as an Apple app ("com.apple.system.loader").
"The group also sought to build credibility through its presence at TOKEN2049 in Singapore and other in-person events it has hosted in the past," Elastic said. "The group attempts to manufacture legitimacy by appearing at widely attended conferences, indirectly lending credibility to the project."
Once installed, neither of the npm packages provides the promised functionality. The 18 security tools part of the @apexacc/audit package generate fabricated findings, while @apexacc/cli's scoring test returns an unsupported assessment of a fictitious project.
Instead, their primary responsibility is to propagate a macOS backdoor called CloudSyncD and a custom Windows information stealer that exfiltrates data through Telegram. The platform-specific executables are retrieved from the projects' GitHub releases.
Both packages implement a distinct verification path for Windows and macOS by sending an HTTP POST request containing "win32" or "darwin" to "vrf.apexaccs[.]org/api/v1/vrf" to initiate the appropriate next stage. The Windows and macOS infection chains are as follows -
Windows -
- The malware retrieves a Base64-encoded PowerShell command, which reaches out to another endpoint ("0auth-chromium[.]com/APIService") to fetch a second PowerShell script ("drop.ps1") that downloads an executable ("bludness.exe") from "ehegisnightmare[.]icu" and launches it in a hidden window.
- The PyInstaller executable is a Python loader that checks if it already has administrator privileges and, if so, downloads the next stage from "ehegisnightmare[.]icu," saves it as "%TEMP%\exegis.exe," and launches it. If not, it attempts to bypass User Account Control (UAC) using UACME's ucmDebugObjectMethod().
- The "exegis.exe" binary is another PyInstaller executable that collects system metadata, running processes, and performs anti-virtual-machine (anti-VM) checks before decrypting and launching a bundled loader as "%TEMP%\updater_loader.exe."
- The Golang executable patches Antimalware Scan Interface (AMSI) and Event Tracing for Windows (ETW), unhooks "ntdll.dll" to blind endpoint security tools, and loads the next-stage shellcode into its own memory.
- The shellcode is a native information stealer that examines for signs of a prior infection and then harvests system information, clipboard text, process listings, Wi-Fi profile names, screenshots, and data from wallets, browser extensions, messengers, remote-access and file transfer protocol (FTP) applications, virtual private network (VPN) clients, browsers (Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and Yandex), and game clients. The stealer can also bypass Chrome's app-bound encryption (ABE) protections to extract saved passwords, session cookies, browsing history, download records, and profile metadata. The collected data is exfiltrated through Telegram.
macOS -
- The malware downloads a remotely hosted bash script and executes it on the machine.
- The shell script downloads a GZIP-compressed archive from "verify.apexfdn[.]xyz/unix/," saves it as "package.tar.gz" in a temporary directory, and extracts its contents.
- The archive contains a dropper for CloudSyncD, which first phishes the victim's system login password using a fake authorization prompt and then uses it to launch an embedded payload with sudo privileges. The payload performs host discovery, collects hardware and operating-system details, and then contacts an external server ("ccmihr[.]com") to transmit the data and receive further tasks that allow the malware to download and run additional payloads.
It's worth noting that CloudSyncD was first documented by Jamf Threat Labs late last month, detailing its propagation via a fake Zoom installer. The malware was detected in the wild in mid-September 2026.
"Its behaviors illustrate how macOS malware continues to move toward native implementations, string protection, and execution paths that attempt to avoid writing payloads to disk, while still depending on the oldest technique available: asking the user for their password," Jamf said.
Besides deploying a stealer and backdoor depending upon the infected operating system, the packages are capable of intercepting and redirecting OpenRouter large language model (LLM) traffic, as well as registering an MCP server under their control in the victim's agent configuration.
"These changes allow the attacker-controlled API to receive the prompts, conversation history, code snippets, and tool outputs included in the agent's LLM requests," Elastic researchers explained.
"The attacker's MCP server can also supply instructions that are added to the agent's prompt, along with tool names, descriptions, and accepted inputs that help the model decide which tools to invoke and how to use them. Together, these mechanisms give the attacker visibility into the submitted data and a way to influence the agent's subsequent actions."

articles.title: Exposition aux ondes : le simulateur de l'ANFR ajoute l'intérieur des bâtiments
articles.text:
Exposition aux ondes : le simulateur de l'ANFR ajoute l'intérieur des bâtiments
Si vous vous demandez à quel point l'intérieur de votre domicile ou de votre lieu de travail est exposé aux champs électromagnétiques générés par les antennes de téléphonie mobile, le simulateur de l'ANFR a un début de réponse pour vous.
Depuis le 16 octobre 2026, l’Agence nationale des fréquences (ANFR) met à disposition une version améliorée de son simulateur d’exposition aux champs électromagnétiques. Grâce à de nouvelles cartes, accessibles sur la plateforme Cartoradio.fr et sur l’application mobile OpenBarres, cet outil permet d'obtenir une estimation des niveaux d’exposition générés par les antennes de téléphonie mobile.
L'exposition du public aux réseaux mobiles, y compris chez soi, davantage visible
Depuis avril 2025, il n'était question que de l'exposition en extérieur. Désormais, le simulateur prend aussi en compte l'intérieur des bâtiments. Relevons cependant d'emblée qu'il s'agit bien ici d'une simulation et non d'une mesure réelle, tandis qu'il n'est question que d'une estimation à proximité des fenêtres.
L'objectif de cet outil pédagogique est donc d'apporter "une information complémentaire aux citoyens et aux collectivités", mais aussi "d’orienter la surveillance vers les zones où l’exposition est susceptible d’être plus élevée." Bien entendu, ondes WiFi, Bluetooth et autres ne sont pas concernées ici.
La solution, développée en partenariat avec la Direction Générale de la Prévention des Risques (DGPR) du ministère de la Transition écologique, le Centre scientifique et technique du bâtiment (CSTB) et la société GEOMOD by COEXIA, s'appuie sur des cartes issues de calculs modélisant la propagation des ondes dans un environnement en trois dimensions.
Elles intègrent les données des bases cartographiques de l’IGN (topographie du sol et bâtiments), ainsi que des caractéristiques des stations de téléphonie mobile situées en extérieur et autorisées par l’ANFR. L'estimation des niveaux d’exposition est exprimée en Volt par mètre (V/m), et simule une valeur à 1,5 m au-dessus du sol pour l’extérieur et derrière un double vitrage pour l'intérieur.
	
En France, les valeurs limites réglementaires pour la téléphonie mobile sont comprises entre 36 et 61 V/m, selon les fréquences utilisées. Le respect de ces valeurs limites permet d'assurer une protection contre les effets avérés des champs électromagnétiques radiofréquences.
Les couleurs indiquées permettent de se faire une idée du niveau d'exposition. Pour les couleurs associées aux intérieurs, l'ANFR précise : "Pour 90 % de cette façade, le niveau d’exposition sera inférieur à la valeur associée à la couleur et pour les 10 % restants, il sera supérieur. Le niveau affiché constitue ainsi une haute de l’exposition en intérieur." Ainsi, la réalité peut différer de l'estimation, basée sur une description simplifiée des batîments.
Ces simulations permettent d'ailleurs à l'ANFR de réaliser de vraies mesures sur le terrain dans les zones les plus exposées. Toute personne peut d'ailleurs utiliser un service en ligne dédié pour demander une mesure d'exposition gratuite. L'organisme se veut cependant rassurant : "En France, les niveaux d’exposition simulés, y compris à l‘intérieur des bâtiments, restent très inférieurs aux valeurs limites réglementaires."

articles.title: AWOL Vision Opens Pre-Orders for LuxVision: World's First Optical-Shift 4K 120Hz Projector
articles.text:
Monday, October 19th 2026
AWOL Vision Opens Pre-Orders for LuxVision: World's First Optical-Shift 4K 120Hz Projector
AWOL Vision, a global home entertainment brand delivering immersive audiovisual experiences through large-format displays, home cinema technology, and connected entertainment, announced that the AWOL LuxVision, first unveiled at IFA 2026, is now officially available for pre-order. Customers can reserve LuxVision with a $100 / €100 / £100 deposit to unlock exclusive Super Early Bird Benefits ahead of its official launch.
This world's first UST projector with optional lens shift is designed to adapt to the changing ways people use their big screens, delivering a tailored experience for every scenario. The big screen is no longer just for movie nights. Gaming is moving toward higher frame rates, sports fans are following multiple live events at once, and home theaters are becoming a more integrated part of everyday living spaces.Built for Every Big Screen Moment
Today's gamers expect a big screen to be just as fast and responsive as the games they play. Size alone isn't enough when the experience can't keep pace with the action. LuxVision delivers 4K at 120 Hz from input to output, bringing sharper, smoother motion to the giant screen. With 1 ms input lag at 4K 120 Hz, VRR and ALLM, gameplay stays fast and responsive. 6,000 ISO lumens help maintain vivid images even in real-home lighting, while Dolby Vision Gaming further enhances compatible titles. Together, these features bring the high refresh rates, brightness and low latency of modern gaming to a truly cinematic scale.
Bringing that big screen experience home means making it work with the space you already have. Lens shift has long given long-throw projectors more flexibility in installation, but UST owners haven't had the same option. LuxVision changes that with the industry's first vertical lens shift for UST, allowing users to move the image vertically within a 142-152% offset range without cropping, scaling, or sacrificing true 4K detail. This makes it easier to install, fine-tune, or upgrade a UST setup without having to reposition the screen or replace existing furniture. Combined with its 0.18:1 ultra-short-throw ratio, LuxVision can project a 120-inch image from just 7.5 inches away, bringing a giant screen into the room while taking up remarkably little space.
And all that big screen can do more than show one thing at a time. For sports fans, that means no longer having to choose between games when several big matchups are happening at once. With LuxVision's optional Multiview upgrade, users can connect multiple wired and wireless sources and enjoy up to four views simultaneously on one massive screen. Viewers can keep the main event front and center while following other matchups and key moments at the same time, turning the screen into a complete game-day hub.
Behind all of these experiences is AWOL's flagship imaging platform. LuxVision features an RGB triple-laser light source covering 110% of Rec 2020, along with a 10,000:1 native contrast ratio with IRIS, seven-level Dynamic IRIS and Enhanced Black Level (EBL) technology. It also supports Dolby Vision, HDR10+ and IMAX Enhanced. Anti-RBE Technology II is designed to reduce rainbow artifacts during both 2D and 3D viewing.
Price and Availability
LuxVision is available for reservation from September 14 through November 2 on AWOL's official website. Customers who place a $100, €100, or £100 deposit can lock in the LuxVision Cinema System Launch Offer, which includes the LuxVision Cinema System and one of two eligible screen options: a 100"-150" New Gen Fresnel ALR Screen ($999-$4,999) or a 100"-120" New Gen Floor-Rising ALR Screen ($1,999-$2,999). 
LuxVision will officially launch on November 3, with an MSRP of $5,999 / €5,999 / £4,999. 
LuxVision is offered in three standard finishes: Eclipse Platinum, Boreal Oak, and Champagne Walnut. Customers may also choose a Custom CMF (Color, Material, and Finish) option for an additional $1,000 or add 4-channel HDMI Multiview for an additional $500.

articles.title: Des hackers détournent des serveurs Plex non mis à jour pour miner des cryptos, le vôtre est-il en danger ?
articles.text:
Plus de deux mois après la publication des correctifs, des pirates exploitent plusieurs failles de Plex Media Server. Les machines compromises servent à miner des cryptomonnaies, mais aussi à relayer du trafic Internet à l'insu de leurs propriétaires.
Début septembre, Plex appelait une nouvelle fois ses utilisateurs et utilisatrices à installer une mise à jour de sécurité sur leurs serveurs multimédias. Si l'éditeur se montrait discret sur la nature des vulnérabilités corrigées, il ne faisait alors état d'aucune exploitation active. C'est désormais chose faite depuis la publication, le 16 octobre dernier, d'un code permettant d'exploiter quatre de ces failles pour exécuter du code à distance sur un serveur, sans authentification. Dès le lendemain, un chercheur observait des tentatives d'intrusion sur un serveur leurre, tandis que des propriétaires d'installations non patchées signalaient à leur tour des activités suspectes.
Plex2Shell, quatre vulnérabilités exploitées en chaîne
Baptisée Plex2Shell, cette méthode d'attaque repose sur l'enchaînement de quatre vulnérabilités, référencées CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655 et CVE-2026-96656. Leur exploitation combinée permet de contourner les contrôles d'accès de Plex, de récupérer le jeton d'administration du serveur, puis d'y déposer un fichier malveillant que le logiciel exécutera avec les privilèges du processus Media Server.
Le chercheur Zach Main avait signalé ces failles à Plex dès le 27 juillet, permettant à l'éditeur de les corriger le 4 août dans Media Server 1.43.3.10861. De son côté, l'auteur de BoredHackerBlog avait déployé, en septembre, un serveur Plex volontairement vulnérable et accessible depuis Internet, afin de surveiller d'éventuelles attaques. Pendant plusieurs semaines, il n'y avait relevé que des scans et des tentatives d'exploitation génériques, jusqu'à l'apparition de requêtes correspondant à la méthode Plex2Shell.
Ces tentatives provenaient d'au moins trois adresses IP distinctes. En modifiant la configuration de son serveur leurre pour autoriser les connexions sortantes, le chercheur a également pu observer le téléchargement de fichiers malveillants et récupérer plusieurs échantillons pour les examiner. Le 19 octobre, Plex a confirmé que les vulnérabilités faisaient désormais l'objet d'attaques généralisées contre les installations non corrigées, sans préciser combien de serveurs avaient été compromis.
Des serveurs détournés pour miner des cryptomonnaies et relayer du trafic Internet
Parmi les fichiers récupérés par BoredHackerBlog figure une version de XMRig, un logiciel de minage de cryptomonnaies que les pirates installent sous le nom de mylovelyminer. Une fois lancé, il exploite les ressources du processeur pour générer des revenus à leur profit, au prix d'une dégradation des performances de la machine et d'une hausse de sa consommation électrique. Sur Reddit, plusieurs témoignages abondent dans ce sens, des propriétaires de serveurs Plex rapportant avoir découvert des processus de minage sur leurs installations, parfois après avoir constaté une utilisation anormalement élevée du processeur.
Les investigations ont également révélé la présence d'un second programme, baptisé myawesomeproxy, dont la fonction est bien différente. Associé à des communications vers le domaine proxystream.st, ce logiciel permet de faire transiter le trafic Internet de tiers par le serveur compromis. Les pirates peuvent ainsi utiliser l'adresse IP de leur victime comme relais, et masquer l'origine réelle de leurs connexions. Un détournement particulièrement intéressant lorsque le serveur utilise une adresse IP résidentielle, susceptible d'inspirer davantage confiance à certains services en ligne.
Face à ces compromissions, Plex recommande de vérifier sans attendre la version de Media Server, mais aussi de rechercher d'éventuels processus suspects, des fichiers inconnus dans le répertoire Codecs ou une consommation anormale du processeur. Pour les installations déjà infectées, une simple mise à jour ne suffit pas : l'éditeur préconise de réinstaller le serveur sur un environnement propre, de déconnecter tous les appareils associés au compte Plex et de modifier son mot de passe. Il invite également les personnes qui n'en ont pas l'utilité à désactiver l'accès distant, afin de limiter l'exposition de leur serveur sur Internet.

articles.title: Egyptian proptech Aqar Exit attracts investment at $2 million valuation
articles.text: Egypt-based proptech startup Aqar Exit has secured a $200,000 (EGP 10 million) investment from businessman Ayman Mamdouh Abbas, executive chairman of Intro Holding Group, in exchange for a 10% stake, valuing the company at approximately $2 million (EGP 100 million). Founded in July 2026 by Mahmoud Ammar, Aqar Exit operates a real estate platform that enables property buyers struggling with instalment payments to transfer their purchase contracts to new buyers, allowing sellers to recover payments and buyers to access units at their original contract prices. Since its launch, the company has reported EGP 9 billion in closed listings across 638 transactions, including 404 in its most recent reported month. However, its definition of closed transactions includes listings removed from the platform, rather than necessarily completed sales. The investment will support the launch of new products and expansion into international markets, particularly the Gulf region. Aqar Exit is targeting a $5 million funding round in 2027, with plans to attract local and international investors to support its regional growth. Press release: Egyptian proptech startup Aqar Exit has secured an investment of EGP 10 million (approximately $200,000) from businessman Ayman Mamdouh Abbas, executive chairman of Intro Holding Group, in exchange for a 10% stake in the company. The transaction values Aqar Exit at EGP 100 million (approximately $2 million) on a post-money basis, according to founder and chairman Mahmoud Ammar, who disclosed the investment in an interview with Al Arabiya Business. Founded in July 2026, Aqar Exit operates a platform for transferring property purchase contracts, targeting buyers who are struggling to meet instalment obligations on their real estate units. The platform connects these sellers with prospective buyers seeking properties at their original contract prices, without paying additional premiums, commonly known in Egypt's property market as overprice. Under the company's model, sellers can seek to recover the amounts they have already paid towards their properties without incurring contract assignment fees. The investment follows Aqar Exit's participation in the fifth season of Shark Tank Egypt, where it presented its business model to investors. According to Ammar, the company will use the new capital to develop additional products and support its expansion into international markets, with a particular focus on the Gulf. Aqar Exit has reported EGP 9 billion in closed listings since launching, covering 638 transactions, including 404 in its most recent reported month, compared with 233 in the preceding month. However, the company's definition of a closed transaction includes any listing removed from the platform, meaning the figures do not necessarily represent completed property sales or revenue generated by Aqar Exit. The platform has also registered 14,845 property assignment files submitted by 11,833 sellers, alongside 67,013 purchase requests from 32,870 prospective buyers. Average daily purchase requests increased by 58% to 1,060, from 671 in the preceding period, according to company figures. Looking ahead, Aqar Exit plans to pursue a funding round of approximately $5 million in 2027, targeting participation from Egyptian and international investors, businesspeople and investment funds. The planned financing would support the company's product development and regional expansion as it seeks to establish a broader market for transferring property purchase contracts.

articles.title: Can five degrees decide whether your network survives rising temperatures?
articles.text:
Can five degrees decide whether your network survives rising temperatures?
Rising temperatures are testing the limits of our wireless infrastructure
Five degrees might not sound like much when you look at the weather forecast. But for the networks our everyday lives depend on, it can mean the difference between equipment running reliably and being pushed past the limits it was built for.
That matters more every year as extreme heat becomes more common. Heatwaves, wildfires, severe storms, and prolonged periods of high temperatures are putting IT infrastructure under pressure in places that were never designed for these conditions.
At the same time, the hardware inside our networks is becoming more powerful and densely packed, making it even harder to keep cool.
Director of Wireless Product Management at Extreme Networks.
Traditionally, outdoor wireless equipment has been designed to operate at temperatures of up to 60°C, taking into account both the heat outside the equipment and the heat generated by the hardware itself. But some vendors are now lowering that ceiling to around 55°C.
As temperatures rise and access points generate more heat of their own, that five-degree difference could be critical.
Our networks are getting hotter
The pressure is building as wireless technology evolves. Access points, for example, have gone from housing two radios to three or four, and each extra radio adds more heat that has to be dissipated. As a result, vendors are having to think carefully about how they balance heat and power as they pack in more performance benefits.
Wi-Fi 8 could also raise the stakes even further. Future wireless platforms are expected to incorporate more AI-assisted processing at the edge, increasing demand for compute resources, memory and power. But that extra processing power and memory will also need more power and will generate more heat, creating another challenge for vendors trying to keep their equipment reliable in demanding environments.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Solar load is an increasingly critical factor too. Direct solar exposure can raise equipment temperatures well beyond ambient conditions, making solar load a critical factor in outdoor network design. It’s important to consider both how hot the air around the equipment is becoming and how much additional heat the hardware is absorbing from the sun. Together, this extra heat can push already hot equipment much closer to its limits.
There is a cost to resilience
Designing hardware to operate reliably across a wider temperature range is more complicated than it might seem. Temperatures are rising and are becoming more unpredictable, and the conditions outdoor access points face today could look very different in just a few years.
Every component has its own operating limits, so each part needs to be selected based on the temperatures it’s expected to encounter. However, building access points capable of operating at temperatures closer to 70°C might need industrial or automotive-grade parts. These can be significantly more expensive and aren’t always as widely available globally, creating their own supply chain challenges.
Cooling increasingly powerful access points brings its own trade-offs, too. Fans help dissipate heat, but they add more moving parts and another potential point of failure. Larger heat sinks and liquid cooling can be helpful alternatives, but they also make the equipment bigger, heavier, and more expensive.
At the same time, customers want more powerful and capable equipment at competitive prices. For vendors, however, building more powerful outdoor access points that can withstand higher temperatures increases hardware cost and complexity.
Lowering the maximum operating temperature can therefore help keep costs down. But that five-degree reduction matters, since it can limit the countries, climates and outdoor environments where an access point can be reliably deployed.
Is your network ready for the heat?
As extreme weather becomes more common, organizations need to think carefully about the conditions their network infrastructure may need to operate in over the coming years. That means looking beyond day-one performance specifications and considering how equipment will cope under sustained heat, solar load and other environmental stresses throughout its expected lifespan.
The concern isn’t that an access point will suddenly fail the moment temperatures rise. However, as equipment becomes more powerful and densely packed, thermal management becomes an increasingly important part of maintaining reliable performance over the long term. Designing hardware to operate reliably in demanding conditions can help protect performance, reliability and the lifespan of the investment.
For networking vendors, that means balancing power, performance, cost and thermal design, while ensuring equipment is appropriately designed and tested for the environments in which it will be deployed. For organizations investing in their networks, it means taking a more forward-looking approach and considering not just the conditions equipment faces today, but what it may need to withstand several years from now.
That starts with asking the right questions before deployment. How much environmental headroom does the equipment have? What conditions has it genuinely been designed and tested to withstand? How does it perform under solar load and other real-world stresses? And will that resilience continue to support the network throughout its expected lifespan?
The goal is to build networks for the future, with the resilience to keep performing as both technology and the environment around them change.

articles.title: El nuevo Tesla Roadster se probará en una pista extrema al estilo Hot Wheels en Texas
articles.text:
Tesla prepara una pista de pruebas con loopings al estilo Hot Wheels en su sede de Texas, donde los propietarios del nuevo Roadster podrán experimentar las acrobacias más extremas del vehículo. El anuncio lo hizo Elon Musk a través de su cuenta de X, donde también adelantó que el deportivo eléctrico podrá ejecutar esas maniobras de forma autónoma, sin intervención del conductor al volante.
La novedad surgió el 17 de octubre, durante un intercambio en la red social con el divulgador tecnológico Robert Scoble, quien había señalado el protagonismo de los ordenadores en el funcionamiento del Roadster. Musk aprovechó el comentario para revelar dos planes que, hasta el momento, no tenían fecha ni detalles concretos.
Pista con loopings en Texas: así será la prueba estilo Hot Wheels
El primer anuncio de Musk apunta a la construcción de un circuito con loopings en la sede de Tesla en Texas, pensado para que los clientes pongan a prueba las capacidades del Roadster. El propio Musk estableció la comparación con las pistas de juguete más conocidas del mercado.
“Tendremos una pista de looping salvaje (más loca incluso que Hot Wheels) en nuestra sede de Texas donde podrás probar tu Roadster”, escribió Musk en X.
Por el momento, se trata de un proyecto solo anunciado. No existe fecha de apertura, tampoco se conoce el trazado que tendrá el circuito ni las condiciones de acceso para los propietarios. El magnate no precisó si los clientes recibirán algún tipo de acompañamiento durante las pruebas o qué maniobras concretas podrán realizar en la instalación.
La construcción de este espacio tendría una relevancia particular para la versión Rocket del Roadster. Tesla especifica que esta configuración, la más extrema de todas las disponibles, no está aprobada para circular por vías públicas, lo que convertiría a la futura pista en uno de los pocos entornos habilitados para explotar todo su potencial.
El Roadster podrá ejecutar maniobras sin intervención del conductor
El segundo anuncio de Musk se refiere a la posibilidad de que el Roadster reproduzca de forma autónoma las acrobacias exhibidas durante su presentación. Según explicó, bastaría con que el propietario se lo pidiera al vehículo para que este ejecutara la maniobra sin necesidad de coordinar manualmente cada movimiento.
Un Tesla Roadster que ejecute acrobacias de forma autónoma significa que el vehículo podrá reproducir maniobras complejas (como las mostradas en su presentación) sin que el conductor controle manualmente la dirección, la frenada y la aceleración durante esos instantes, delegando esa coordinación en los sistemas electrónicos del propio coche.
“Podrás pedirle al Roadster que realice cualquiera de los trucos mostrados de forma autónoma, ya que será sensible”, afirmó Musk en la misma conversación con Scoble.
La base técnica para esta función existe en la arquitectura electrónica del vehículo, que ya permite gestionar de manera conjunta los mandos, los ventiladores y los propulsores. Sin embargo, Musk no detalló qué software ejecutaría estas funciones, de qué manera se activarían ni qué tipo de supervisión requerirían por parte del conductor.
Conviene precisar los límites de este anuncio: se circunscribe a maniobras concretas y no implica que el Roadster incorpore capacidades de conducción autónoma general en carretera. Tampoco está confirmado que todas las versiones del vehículo vayan a contar con estas mismas funciones.
Finalmente, este par de anuncios se enmarca en una idea que Musk viene defendiendo: el Roadster podría convertirse en el último modelo de Tesla concebido principalmente para la conducción manual. Bajo ese planteamiento, el disfrute al volante y la automatización de determinadas maniobras no resultarían experiencias contrapuestas, sino complementarias.

articles.title: Unpatched Broadcom Wi-Fi Flaw Lets Attackers in Range Run Code as Root on Routers
articles.text:
A flaw in Broadcom's Wi-Fi setup software lets an attacker within radio range run code as root on Broadcom-based routers, without the network password or any pairing step, security researcher Quentin Kaiser disclosed on October 16.
He showed the attack working against home gateways supplied by three Belgian internet providers, in one case reading the Wi-Fi password off the device and in another opening a remote shell over the air. No CVE has been assigned to the flaw, and no fix has been deployed to the affected routers, Kaiser says.
The flaw is in Broadcom's version of Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS), the feature that lets a device join a Wi-Fi network without the password being typed in. Broadcom's code mishandles the reassembly of fragmented WPS setup messages, so an attacker in range can send crafted messages that corrupt the router's memory. From there, Kaiser built two things: a way to read memory back off the device, and a way to run his own code on it.
Against an Orange Belgium gateway, the Askey TCG3000 read the Wi-Fi password (the PSK) from the router's stored settings, sent it back over the air, and then joined the network with it.
Against a Proximus gateway, the Sagemcom-built BBOX3V+, the exploit opened a reverse shell, a remote command line, carried over Wi-Fi frames, so no outside server was needed.
Both ran without any login, and the attack works at a distance, not only up close, Kaiser says. He reports no real-world attacks using the flaw. The working exploits are his own.
What's Affected
Broadcom's WPS code is embedded in routers and access points from dozens of vendors, and Kaiser estimates that millions of devices worldwide are affected.
The vulnerable chips fall into two families: older eCos-based models (the BCM3380, BCM3383 and BCM33834), where he found no usable fix and calls the bug a permanent "forever day," meaning a flaw that will never be patched on those devices, and newer Linux-based models (the BCM3390, BCM65xx and BCM68xx), which could be fixed if their makers switch Wi-Fi software.
In Belgium, Kaiser found the flaw present and exploitable on gateways from three of the four big providers: Proximus, Orange Belgium and VOO. A fourth, Telenet, may be affected too, but he could not test one.
A wider list he published, ranging from Cisco small-business access points to Huawei and ARRIS routers, mixes confirmed and unconfirmed entries, and some rest on an automated check that only flags a device as "likely vulnerable."
The Belgian per-provider counts, he says, run into the hundreds of thousands of gateways, but are rough estimates.
Why There's No Patch, and No CVE
The flaw is old. Kaiser traces the code back to at least 2010 and says Broadcom shipped an incomplete fix in 2018, then told customers to switch to a different Wi-Fi software package, called hostapd, rather than relying on the fix. On the older eCos chips, he says, no working fix was ever shipped, which is why he calls it a forever day.
No CVE, the tracking identifier that lets defenders and vendors follow a flaw, has been assigned to it. Kaiser says Broadcom told him it has known about the bug since 2018 and had heard about it from others, but would not register a CVE or say anything publicly, which he believes is why so many device makers never patched.
When he took the case to the CERT Coordination Center, it was closed the same day, because Broadcom itself holds the authority to assign CVEs for its products and would not do so. The Hacker News found no CVE for the flaw as of October 19.
What Defenders Can Do
There is no patch to install, and no setting Kaiser points to that blocks the attack over the air. What he provides instead is a way to find affected gear: YARA rules that spot the vulnerable code in extracted firmware, and a script that listens to a live access point and reports whether it looks vulnerable.
Both are triage aids, he notes: a patched device can still match the rules, so a hit is a reason to check further, not a confirmed finding. For gear that will never be fixed, replacement is the practical option.
Kaiser frames the bug as well suited to attackers who reach a target over nearby Wi-Fi rather than the internet, a technique Russian state hackers have used to breach networks from across the street.

articles.title: Les Anneaux de pouvoir : la saison 3 dévoile les serviteurs de Sauron dans des nouvelles affiches
articles.text:
Les Anneaux de pouvoir : la saison 3 dévoile les serviteurs de Sauron dans des nouvelles affiches
Attendue le 11 novembre prochain sur Prime Video, la saison 3 de la série Le Seigneur des anneaux : les anneaux de pouvoir vient de révéler de nouvelles affiches mettant en avant les forces de Sauron.
Fans du Seigneur des anneaux, courage : plus que trois grosses semaines à patienter avant de retourner se balader en Terre du Milieu avec la sortie de la saison 3 de la série Les Anneaux de pouvoir sur la plateforme de streaming Prime Video.
Et comme pour remercier la persévérance de ses fidèles, le show d'Amazon vient d'ailleurs de dévoiler deux affiches particulièrement guerrières et prometteuses, avant l'arrivée imminente d'une nouvelle bande-annonce.
Les Nazgnagôl à l'honneur
La première affiche nous montre ainsi Sauron (Charlie Vickers) tout en armure vêtu, arborant sa couronne de métal sombre (aussi appelée couronne de Morgoth) devant quatre de ses nouveaux serviteurs, les fameux Nazgnagôl qui font leur apparition dans cette troisième saison.
Ces personnages inédits de l'univers de J. R. R. Tolkien, créés par les créateurs du show J.D. Payne et Patrick McKay, sont des sortes de "proto-Nazgûl" : des Nazgûl qui ont encore forme humaine, avant d'être consumés par les anneaux de pouvoir et qu'ils ne deviennent des spectres de l'anneau.
Ce terme a été inventé par les showrunners à partir du “parler noir” (la langue du Mordor), mélange de nazg (anneau) et nagôl (serviteur) et signifiant “serviteur de l'anneau”. Si l'identité de tous les Nazgûl n'a pas été révélée par Tolkien, on sait que l'un d'entre eux sera Khamül l'Oriental.
Ce seigneur de guerre apparaîtra dans la saison 3 sous les traits de Zubin Varla (Andor), et l'acteur a même précisé dans une interview que son personnage suivra “le même chemin que Gollum” : “Le mal engendre le mal, et la violence engendre la violence. Leurs âmes et leurs corps sont corrompus jusqu'à être littéralement évidés, presque dépourvus de toute forme physique”.
Moins impressionnante, la seconde affiche nous montre l'un de ces Nazgnagôl sur son cheval cabré dans les plaines du Mordor, avec la Montagne du destin en arrière-plan. C'est peu, mais cela a de quoi nous faire patienter jusqu'à la sortie imminente d'un nouveau trailer, alors que la dernière bande-annonce date de juillet dernier.
Cette nouvelle saison ne sera d'ailleurs pas uniquement celle des ennemis de la Terre du milieu, et verra aussi l'apparition de l'elfe Celeborn, mari de Galadriel, incarné par Jamie Campbell Bower (Vecna dans Stranger Things). L'acteur rejoint au casting Morfydd Clark, Robert Aramayo, Charlie Vickers, Owain Arthur ou encore Benjamin Walker.
Pour rappel, la troisième saison se déroule cinq ans après les événements de la saison 2, alors que la guerre entre les Elfes et Sauron bat son plein. Le seigneur des ténèbres cherche à forger l'anneau unique, l'arme qui lui donnera l'avantage décisif pour remporter la guerre, asservir tous les peuples à sa volonté et régner enfin sur la Terre du milieu tout entière.

articles.title: GTA 6 reconocerá qué tipo de criminal eres según tus patrones de comportamiento
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 incluirá un perfil criminal que registrará cómo actúan los jugadores durante sus delitos y modificará la respuesta del mundo según sus patrones de comportamiento. Rockstar Games plantea una mecánica que no busca decidir si Jason y Lucia son buenos o malos, sino identificar qué clase de delincuentes construyen los usuarios a lo largo de la partida.
El sistema importa porque afectará una de las bases de la franquicia: las consecuencias de robar, escapar, disparar o llamar la atención de la policía. La forma de completar una misión, la violencia empleada y los rastros que dejen los protagonistas podrán influir en el comportamiento del entorno y en ciertos elementos narrativos de GTA 6.
El perfil criminal analizará cómo se cometen los delitos
Rob Nelson, responsable de desarrollo de Rockstar North, explicó en una entrevista con IGN que el denominado perfil criminal registrará determinados hábitos durante la experiencia. El sistema tendrá en cuenta los delitos cometidos, pero también la forma en que Jason y Lucia los llevan a cabo.
Actuar con precisión, evitar enfrentamientos innecesarios y escapar sin prolongar el conflicto no será equivalente a provocar situaciones violentas de forma constante. Rockstar busca que esas diferencias definan una identidad criminal dentro del mundo de Leonida.
El estudio no ha detallado todas las reglas que determinarán el funcionamiento de esta mecánica. Tampoco se conocen los valores exactos que utilizará para clasificar las acciones ni las herramientas visibles que permitirán consultar la evolución del perfil durante una partida.
En qué se diferenciará con el sistema de honor de Red Dead Redemption 2
La comparación con Red Dead Redemption 2 resulta inevitable. La aventura protagonizada por Arthur Morgan contaba con un sistema de honor que alteraba la reputación del personaje mediante sus decisiones y afectaba distintos aspectos de la experiencia.
GTA 6 utilizará una filosofía relacionada, aunque con otro enfoque. El perfil criminal no establecerá una división tradicional entre comportamientos buenos y malos. La explicación está vinculada con la propia naturaleza de la saga, cuyos protagonistas participan habitualmente en actividades delictivas.
La diferencia estará en la interpretación de las acciones. Completar un robo y escapar sin complicaciones no tendrá el mismo significado que extender un enfrentamiento con violencia innecesaria. Rockstar pretende que esas elecciones formen parte de la identidad de Jason y Lucia.
Los comportamientos repetidos tendrán un peso mayor que una acción aislada. Quienes prefieran actuar de forma controlada podrán hacerlo, mientras que quienes resuelvan cada situación con violencia constante también tendrán esa posibilidad. No existe una única forma correcta de jugar.
Las fugas policiales exigirán borrar rastros
El sistema de búsqueda también dará más importancia a las consecuencias de cada delito. GTA 6 recuperará las seis estrellas de persecución, según la información publicada por Game Informer, con una respuesta policial más difícil de eludir.
Los testigos y las cámaras de seguridad podrán identificar a los responsables y comunicar que la policía busca a dos sospechosos: un hombre y una mujer. Esa información hará que la apariencia, la ropa y el vehículo utilizado durante el crimen se conviertan en elementos relevantes.
Jason Duval y Lucia Caminos deberán eliminar los vínculos visibles con los delitos. Cambiar de ropa, auto y peinado ayudará a reducir las señales que conectan a los protagonistas con una fuga anterior. Mantener la misma imagen facilitará la identificación por parte de los agentes.
Durante el video de gameplay extendido se mostró una acción destinada a ocultar pruebas: los protagonistas abandonan el vehículo empleado en una huida. La escena sugiere que el automóvil puede convertirse en una pista si la policía reconoce el modelo o lo relaciona con el delito.
La posibilidad de separar a Jason y Lucia durante las persecuciones añade una decisión táctica, pero obliga a proteger a ambos, ya que el arresto o la caída de uno terminará la partida. Cuando Grand Theft Auto 6 llegue el 19 de noviembre de 2026 a PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S, los jugadores podrán comprobar cómo el perfil criminal, las fugas y las reacciones de Leonida transforman uno de los títulos más esperados en la historia de los videojuegos.

articles.title: NVIDIA's Faster DLSS 5 Model Gets Extracted From NBA 2K27, Modders Report Up to 90% Gains
articles.text:
Monday, October 19th 2026
NVIDIA's Faster DLSS 5 Model Gets Extracted From NBA 2K27, Modders Report Up to 90% Gains
NVIDIA shipped its faster DLSS 5 Neural Rendering model with NBA 2K27 on October 16, and it didn't take modders long to pull it out and test it elsewhere. Renan Maniero on X extracted the new 310.9.16.0 build of the DLL. That lets people inject it into games that don't officially support DLSS 5 through tools like RenoDX and OptiScaler. The new DLL also keeps the older model around as Preset A, with the new one sitting under Preset B, so comparing the two is as simple as switching presets. Gaming Optimized on X did exactly that, and found the new model running up to 90% faster than the old one in The Witcher 3. The channel points out that the gain varies from game to game, so 90% looks like the best case rather than the norm. 
That roughly aligns with NVIDIA's own claims. The company says the October update shrinks the model by 24% to roughly 118 million parameters, cuts VRAM use at 4K by 20%, and runs the neural rendering workload up to 2x faster than the September version. NVIDIA also quoted up to 40% higher frame rates in NBA 2K27 specifically. Officially, DLSS 5 is still limited to RTX 50-series GPUs and GeForce NOW. NVIDIA plans to bring it to the RTX 40-series, though there's no date yet, and there's no word on RTX 30 or RTX 20 support. Modders, apparently, aren't waiting, since the OptiScaler README notes a modified runtime that gets it running on RTX 20-series cards as well.
Sources:
				Renan Maniero on X, 				Gaming Optimized on X, 				via Tom's Hardware			
	
	
	
		
	
		
10 Comments on NVIDIA's Faster DLSS 5 Model Gets Extracted From NBA 2K27, Modders Report Up to 90% Gains
I also noted that 1% lows dont' seem to have the same performance uplift as averages, particularly on mid-range and lower end cards. There might be some overhead going on here that has to do with the infrastructure of the model that wasn't optimized here.
It requires a lot of attention and optimization from the game developer.
I was convinced DSLSS5 would be terrible, but the fact that the very first iteration already looks decent in some games that were never meant to run with it makes me think that later versions used in game that were designed to use it could actually be pretty good (Also I'm sure if an RTX 6000 ever comes to consumer market, it will run it with less of a performance hit than current gen cards).
In CP2077 maxed with RR and with 6xMFG, all are after SR at Performance 1080P:
Off: ~450 FPS
Preset A: ~340 FPS
Preset B: ~385 FPS

articles.title: Spotify : ce nouveau QR code pourrait sérieusement compliquer le partage de votre abonnement
articles.text:
Spotify renforce la vérification des abonnements Premium Famille avec un QR code à scanner en présence du gestionnaire. Une procédure qui pourrait compliquer le partage entre plusieurs foyers, avec des conséquences importantes pour ceux qui ne respectent pas le délai imposé.
Partager son abonnement Spotify avec cinq proches, c’est pratique pour réduire la facture. Encore faut-il vivre sous le même toit, une condition que la plateforme impose depuis longtemps, mais dont la vérification reposait principalement sur une adresse postale. Spotify semble désormais décidé à aller plus loin. Certains utilisateurs doivent confirmer leur présence physique auprès du titulaire de l’abonnement en scannant un QR code sur son téléphone. Une manipulation assez simple en apparence, mais qui pourrait compliquer les arrangements entre amis ou membres d’une famille vivant à plusieurs adresses.
Un QR code à scanner en personne pour conserver son abonnement
Comme le rapporte 9to5Google, Spotify déploie une nouvelle procédure destinée à vérifier que les membres d’un abonnement Premium Famille résident bien avec le propriétaire du compte.
Le fonctionnement est détaillé dans la documentation officielle française de Spotify. Lorsqu’un membre reçoit une demande de vérification, le gestionnaire doit ouvrir l’application Spotify sur son téléphone, accéder à la rubrique « Votre abonnement Premium », puis sélectionner « Gérer » pour afficher un QR code.
Le membre invité doit ensuite scanner ce code avec son propre smartphone. Les deux personnes sont censées se trouver au même endroit pour effectuer la manipulation.
Spotify précise que le QR code change toutes les quelques secondes, ce qui complique l’utilisation d’une simple capture d’écran envoyée à distance. La vérification s’effectue exclusivement depuis l'application mobile.
Et mieux vaut ne pas laisser traîner la notification. Les membres disposent de sept jours pour effectuer le contrôle. En cas d’échec, ils risquent de perdre leur accès Premium et de revenir à l’offre gratuite. Ils ne pourront pas non plus rejoindre un autre abonnement Famille ou Duo pendant douze mois. Spotify permet toutefois de retrouver le même abonnement partagé, sous réserve de remplir les conditions requises, ou de souscrire une offre individuelle.
Spotify serre la vis sur une règle qui existe depuis longtemps
Cette nouvelle vérification ne change pas les conditions de Premium Famille. L’offre reste réservée à six personnes maximum vivant à la même adresse, chacune disposant de son propre compte.
Jusqu'ici, Spotify vérifiait principalement le domicile déclaré lors de l’inscription ou lorsqu’une nouvelle confirmation était nécessaire. Une procédure que nous évoquions déjà dans notre guide consacré au partage des abonnements, et qui reposait largement sur la bonne foi des utilisateurs.
Avec le QR code dynamique, la plateforme cherche désormais à rendre les contrôles plus contraignants. Cela ne garantit pas pour autant qu’elle puisse établir durablement que deux personnes vivent ensemble : une vérification ponctuelle confirme surtout leur présence au même endroit à un instant donné.
Se pose enfin la question de la disponibilité. La procédure figure déjà dans l’assistance française de Spotify, mais le service ne précise ni les pays concernés par son déploiement actuel, ni le nombre d’abonnés qui recevront cette demande. Rien ne permet donc d’affirmer que tous les comptes Premium Famille français sont déjà soumis à ce contrôle.
Pour les familles qui partagent réellement le même logement, la nouveauté devrait se résumer à quelques manipulations supplémentaires. Pour ceux qui ont pris l’habitude de répartir le prix de l’abonnement entre plusieurs adresses, en revanche, il pourrait devenir plus difficile de conserver leurs habitudes.

articles.title: Popcorn Studio AI secures $1 million to expand AI-powered filmmaking platform
articles.text: UAE-based creative technology startup Popcorn Studio AI has secured a $1 million pre-seed funding package, led by Emirati entrepreneur and investor Mohammed Bin Bouta Alharsoosi, to support product development and international expansion. Founded in 2026 by Egyptian entrepreneurs Shady Essam and Mohamed Hedar, Popcorn Studio AI operates an AI-powered video production platform that enables filmmakers, content creators, agencies and brands to produce cinematic content through an integrated workflow. The platform offers AI tools for scriptwriting, character development, scene generation, voiceovers, lip-syncing and post-production, with a particular focus on Arabic-language content and regional dialects. The funding will support the development of Popcorn's AI technology, expansion of its product suite and growth across the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Egypt, alongside international partnerships. Popcorn Studio AI has also announced an AI filmmaking competition associated with the El Gouna Film Festival, featuring a $70,000 prize pool to support emerging filmmakers. Press release: Popcorn Studio AI, the Dubai-based artificial intelligence platform transforming how films and video content are created, has announced a $1 million funding package, marking a significant milestone in its mission to reshape the future of creative production. The funding, led by Emirati serial entrepreneur and investor Mohammed Bin Bouta Alharsoosi, will support Popcorn's next phase of growth, including continued AI technology development, international expansion, and the evolution of its creative platform. Founded by Egyptian entrepreneurs Shady Essam and Mohamed Hedar, Popcorn Studio AI is challenging one of the creative industry's longest-standing limitations: the belief that producing high-quality cinematic content requires substantial budgets, large production teams, and complex technical workflows. Popcorn is building a future where a compelling idea, rather than access to expensive production infrastructure, determines what can be brought to life. From an Idea to a Film. Without the Traditional Barriers. Unlike conventional AI video generators that require creators to navigate multiple tools, complex prompts, and disconnected production workflows, Popcorn brings the creative process together within one integrated platform. Through its specialised AI studios, creators, filmmakers, agencies, and brands can develop concepts, build characters, generate cinematic scenes, create commercial videos, and produce multilingual content using advanced generative AI models. A defining strength of the platform is its focus on Arabic-language content — including native Arabic lip-sync capabilities and support for regional dialects — addressing a major gap in the global AI video landscape. Built in Dubai with international ambitions, Popcorn combines advanced AI technology with a deep understanding of regional culture, language, and storytelling. Its vision extends beyond making video production faster or more affordable. The company aims to establish an entirely new creative infrastructure where filmmakers can experiment more freely, brands can produce content at scale, and emerging storytellers can bring ambitious ideas to the screen. A New Chapter for AI-Powered Filmmaking Popcorn's growth comes at a time when artificial intelligence is fundamentally changing the economics of the global creative industry. What once required weeks of planning, expensive equipment, physical locations, and large production crews can increasingly be developed through AI-powered creative workflows. Yet the company's founders believe the greatest opportunity is not simply automation but creative empowerment. "Technology has always changed how stories are told. Cinema evolved from silent films to sound, from film reels to digital cameras, and now we're entering the next chapter with artificial intelligence," said Shady Essam, Co-Founder and CEO of Popcorn Studio AI. "Our ambition isn't to replace filmmakers. It's to remove the barriers between imagination and execution. We want to make it possible for anyone with a powerful story to create something extraordinary, regardless of their budget, location, or technical background." The company's momentum has also extended into the filmmaking community, with Popcorn announcing an AI filmmaking competition connected to the El Gouna Film Festival, featuring a $70,000 prize pool. The initiative reflects Popcorn's commitment to supporting emerging filmmakers and accelerating the adoption of AI-powered storytelling across the region. Strategic Investment to Accelerate Global Ambitions For Mohammed Bin Bouta Alharsoosi, the investment reflects a conviction that the MENA region is positioned to lead the next chapter of AI-driven content creation — and that Popcorn has the team and the technology to make that happen. "POPCORN Studio AI represents exactly the kind of bold, regionally rooted technology I look for. The content market across the Middle East and North Africa is enormous, and AI is still in its earliest stages here. Shady and Mohamed have the vision, the execution capability, and a product that's already resonating. I am proud to back them at this stage." — Mohammed Bin Bouta Alharsoosi, Investor With this funding in place, Popcorn Studio AI is focused on expanding its product suite, scaling its user base across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt, and building the partnerships that will bring AI-powered filmmaking to a new generation of creators worldwide.

articles.title: 'We love a good challenge': Logitech head tells us why the AI age could revolutionize collaboration as we know it, as it reveals its biggest product overhaul in years
articles.text:
'We love a good challenge': Logitech head tells us why the AI age could revolutionize collaboration as we know it, as it reveals its biggest product overhaul in years
Simplification can be key to better communication, Logitech believes
As more and more companies press their workers into coming back into the office, even if only for a few days in increasingly popular hybrid working models, the need for effective and reliable communication technology has never been greater.
A common sight in offices and homes across the world, Logitech is ideally placed to monitor trends in what workers at every level require - and at its recent Logi Work 2026 event, it took the opportunity to show off how its latest suite of releases can revolutionize the collaboration experience for all.
To find out more, I spoke to Henry Levak, VP and general manager, Logitech, to see what it sees as the future of meeting rooms, offices, and even the humble home working desk.
Broad portfolio paying off
“We want people to think of us as that simple and flexible partner - the word 'proprietary' and being locked in is luckily something we're moving away from,” Levak tells me.
“The reality is that you will have a world of different configurations,” he notes, highlighting how many of Logitech’s customers are asking workers to come back into the office, meaning the company needs to broaden its offerings even further.
“That's been a huge catalyst for our success,” he notes, “we have an incredibly broad portfolio that covers people working from home, to people working in the boardroom, and everything in between.”
At the event, Levak had spoken about the upcoming launch of Logitech’s new portfolio, which the company had described as its biggest enterprise-focused launch in years.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The new lineup, which includes the Rally Bar 2, Rally System 2 Pro and Sound Shape technology, will revolutionize the way businesses of all sizes collaborate and communicate, with not only more powerful, but more customizable technology being the watchword.
For example, the new Rally Bar 2, the successor to the popular sound bar now seen in boardrooms and meeting spaces across the globe, not only features a Qualcomm Dragonwing chip to allow for better AI processing, but offers a 115 degree POV and much easier wall mounting due to its smaller form factor
The Rally System 2 Pro provides a “modular yet streamlined” offering which looks to simplify complex installs which can be difficult to maintain and manage - making larger rooms better spaces to have these vital meetings in.
In spite of its new range of releases, Logitech had spoken about its goal to “simplify everything” - so I ask Levak how the company can pursue that goal while still offering a range of products attractive to all different kinds of customers.
“It's a big pain point,” he says, “one of the things you can almost always predict is that simplifying will be a request...people want things to be dramatically simpler - but they also want consistency and experience.”
“What they don't want, is that if you walk into a room, like a smaller space with some sort of AI features and capability - and then you walk into a larger room, and for some reason that space doesn't have that feature.”
“The technology should just disappear and blend away into the background, and everyone should just focus on collaboration and creation, not necessarily the technology - and the only way to achieve that is if you have consistent technology.”
Simplify, simplify
Going forward, this will mean that even in a large room or meeting space, customers will only require a small simple device such as a video bar set up, Levak says, removing unnecessary friction and allowing everyone to work effectively.
“The way you simplify it is by dramatically reducing the number of components,” he points out, “what we're doing is something that dramatically simplifies all of that, from installation, provisioning, setup and deployment - it's a reduction in terms of complexity of what's out there today.”
“In terms of what it can bring, it's the first time modern AI is available in much larger rooms - now you have a full ecosystem of components that will deliver that experience.”
Looking forward, Levak is keen to point out the role AI can play in spaces as incongruous as meeting rooms.
With AI agents playing an increasingly important role for many workers, the need for context has never been greater. Such information needs to be collected by a range of sensors, and Logitech feels that products such as microphones and cameras could play a key role in expanding this - as long as effective privacy controls are used - making its equipment the physical layer of a company’s AI ecosystem.
“You can see the power when (an AI agent) has context about you, and the same thing will apply at work,” Levak says, “at a higher level, we’re deploying these sensors in every space, so that the context you need in order to build out a more thoughtful agent for you.”
“We're making sure the products are built for what's coming next,” he concludes, “both from the simplicity and elegance perspective, but also from features and capability.”

articles.title: SmartBear’s BearQ adds Sources to find coverage gaps and Workflows to automate test runs - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
SmartBear’s BearQ adds Sources to find coverage gaps and Workflows to automate test runs
Software testing company SmartBear Software Inc. is pushing its BearQ agentic quality assurance system beyond test automation with two new capabilities released today.
Both additions target the part of quality assurance that artificial intelligence has made more difficult by speeding up coding. SmartBear calls them Sources and Workflows.
Automating individual tests is no longer the bottleneck, in the company’s telling. The tougher job now is working out what still needs testing across sprawling systems, much of it already covered by tests sitting in other tools.
Sources widens BearQ’s view past the application itself. Requirements and bug reports now flow in from Atlassian Corp.’s Jira so the agent knows what ought to be tested. SmartBear’s own Reflect and Zephyr testing tools show what existing tests already cover. BearQ draws on that context to find gaps in coverage before it writes anything new, so teams end up with fewer duplicate tests.
Workflows picks up from there, letting a team chain jobs together behind a single trigger. Once a build lands in the continuous integration and delivery pipeline, for example, BearQ can spin up a test environment and run regression tests against it. Whatever the run turns up goes back into the team’s connected systems, and anyone who would rather not tie testing to builds can put the same sequence on a schedule. How much of a workflow runs without human review is up to the team.
Progressive autonomy is SmartBear’s name for that arrangement. Teams begin with people signing off on what BearQ does, then hand over more of the process as their confidence grows. Trust was the top barrier to adopting or scaling autonomous testing, named by 23% of the 1,436 U.S. and U.K. respondents in a survey SmartBear released Sept. 30.
Bridges Smith, vice president of product management for AI at SmartBear, called autonomous testing “the first step.” By Smith’s account, the bigger opportunity is connecting how an application actually behaves with what a team intends it to do and the test suite it has built up. People would still set the guardrails, Smith said, describing the shift as a move “beyond autonomous testing toward autonomous quality.”
SmartBear has been building BearQ out since it first appeared in March, when the company opened early access for web applications built by midmarket software-as-a-service providers. A September update made it an assignable agent inside Jira. SmartBear’s older lineup includes the Swagger tools for designing application programming interfaces, and about 32,000 organizations use its software, by the company’s count.
More Sources connections are due before the quarter ends. Both features get a public demonstration Thursday in a livestream with “Project Hail Mary” author Andy Weir.
