articles.title: Las entregas del iPhone Duo se extienden hasta 2027: qué otros plegables hay para no esperar
articles.text:
Varias personas tendrán que esperar hasta 2027 para comprar el iPhone Duo, el primer teléfono plegable de Apple. Para aquellos que no quieren esperar existen celulares plegables de otras marcas que se podrían conseguir sin esperar mucho tiempo.
El mercado de los teléfonos plegables ya cuenta con alternativas de fabricantes como Samsung, Google, Motorola, Honor y Oppo. Los modelos disponibles se dividen, en general, entre celulares que se abren como un libro y otros de formato compacto que se pliegan por la mitad.
Entre las opciones figuran el Samsung Galaxy Z Fold y el Galaxy Z Flip, el Google Pixel Fold, el Motorola Razr, el Huawei Mate X y el Honor Magic V.
¿Existe una forma de adelantar la entrega del iPhone Duo?
La respuesta es no. Una vez que Apple asigna una fecha estimada a la reserva, el comprador no cuenta con un mecanismo para adelantarla. Los plazos dependen de la producción, la configuración elegida, el color, la capacidad de almacenamiento y el inventario destinado a cada región.
La compañía sugirió preparar con anticipación el color y la capacidad para agilizar el pedido. Aun así, algunos compradores comentaron en redes sociales que tuvieron problemas para finalizar la compra en la tienda en línea. Esa preparación podía reducir pasos durante la preventa, pero no garantiza una unidad ni modifica una fecha ya asignada.
Cuáles son los riesgos de comprar el teléfono en mercados de reventa
Comprar un iPhone Duo en mercados de reventa puede implicar riesgos. La alta demanda inicial suele derivar en precios por encima del valor oficial, publicaciones sin unidades disponibles y operaciones en las que no es sencillo verificar el origen del dispositivo o las condiciones reales de entrega.
Además, existen riesgos si el vendedor ofrece una reserva en lugar de un dispositivo en su poder. El comprador podría pagar por adelantado y depender de que el revendedor reciba el teléfono en la fecha prometida.
Antes de realizar una operación, que sea desde la página oficial de Apple, la existencia física del producto, el número de serie y las condiciones de devolución.
Qué alternativa hay para quien necesita un teléfono plegable ahora
La única alternativa para evitar la espera consiste en elegir un teléfono plegable de otra marca que tenga disponibilidad inmediata. Esa decisión supone renunciar al modelo de Apple, pero permite acceder antes a un dispositivo con formato plegable sin depender de la lista de pedidos del Duo.
El iPhone Duo llega a una categoría donde otros fabricantes ya tienen presencia, aunque Apple busca diferenciarse mediante su integración con el sistema operativo y su diseño. El modelo cuenta con una pantalla externa de 5,4 pulgadas y un panel interior de 7,6 pulgadas cuando está abierto, con una superficie 80% mayor que la del iPhone 18 Pro.
Cómo es el primer plegable de Apple
El teléfono tiene formato tipo pasaporte, bordes de titanio, dos cámaras traseras y un mecanismo diseñado para que la marca central del pliegue resulte poco visible. Cerrado puede utilizarse con una mano; abierto, permite ejecutar dos aplicaciones lado a lado y ofrece una interfaz orientada a tareas de productividad.
El modelo plegable usa una versión adaptada de iOS 27, incorpora un dock vertical en el borde derecho y habilita modos específicos cuando queda semiplegado. Su batería promete hasta 24 horas de autonomía con el dispositivo cerrado, mientras que la carga rápida recupera el 50% en 20 minutos.
Asimismo, la cámara principal es de 48 megapíxeles, graba video en 4K y ofrece zoom de dos aumentos. El sistema trasero suma una cámara ultra gran angular, sin teleobjetivo dedicado. Apple reemplazó Face ID por Touch ID e integró un chip desarrollado para este dispositivo.
Analistas de Bloomberg estimaron que las ventas del Duo podrían superar los 14 millones de unidades y generar USD 28.000 millones de ingresos durante el año fiscal 2027.

articles.title: NiCE bets the company on AI, data and accountability, and the legacy business buys it time - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
NiCE bets the company on AI, data and accountability, and the legacy business buys it time
Every company in the customer experience ecosystem now claims to be an artificial intelligence company. Last week, at NiCE Ltd.’s annual industry analyst summit, the company demonstrated what happens when an AI strategy shifts the organization’s center of gravity.
A year after closing the Cognigy acquisition, NiCE is no longer a contact center-as-a-service or CCaaS provider with AI bolted on. It’s an AI platform that happens to include the industry’s deepest CCaaS and workforce engagement stack. Even before the Cognigy purchase, I felt NiCE led the CCaaS industry, and the event only reinforced that view.
Cognigy is now the heart of NiCE
During his keynote, Chief Executive Scott Russell (pictured) spoke at length about how the deal transformed the company. “Most acquisitions that companies make expand the portfolio and the capability,” he said. “This one changed where we build from. It changed the nature of who we are as a company.” Jeff Comstock, president of CX product and technology, said Cognigy is “now the underlying substrate for all of our conversational and agentic AI across the entire platform.”
What I found equally interesting is that NiCE isn’t using Cognigy solely to lock in CXone customers. Philipp Heltewig, Cognigy’s co-founder and now NiCE’s chief AI officer, said that the standalone motion of selling Cognigy on top of Genesys, Five9 or Amazon Connect “is equally important to us as the integrated motion.” Russell noted that he has yet to see a rival’s AI running on NiCE, whereas Cognigy runs on theirs.
Cognigy has a large customer base on competitive platforms, and it can be tempting to shut that down and force other vendors to scramble for new partners. It’s the right thing for NiCE to keep selling Cognigy that way because it’s best for customers, and that’s always the best path.
NiCE is becoming a CX data company
NiCE’s real asset is no longer the routing engine or the ability to offer multiple channels. That’s table stakes. NiCE’s strength and competitive moat is its decades of interactions, analytics, and screen recordings originally captured for compliance, which multimodal models can now reason over. Comstock demoed a system that observed a human agent process a refund across voice, screen, and telemetry, then built an AI agent from that observation, including a $250 supervisor-approval guardrail it inferred on its own.
Speaking of the AI startups that partner with NiCE, Russell said, “They need NiCE data. They need our workloads. They need our interactions. They need our intents.” In the Q&A, he added: “There’s no doubt the power of our data is a huge value, not just the interaction data, but the contextual real-time data, the human behavior behind it, the screen record.”
The numbers support that statement. Prospects that get an automated insights readout based on their own data book nine times more AI than those that don’t, and application programming interface volume off the platform is up 7.5 times in two years. Asked whether NiCE would package that intelligence for sales, marketing and the C-suite, Russell said, “Yes, it’s coming, just not right now.” That’s the long-term story. Systems of record capture what happened; NiCE captures how it happened.
Personal agents will break the contact center model
Historically, part of what NiCE did was help customers understand and manage their customers’ journeys. At the event, Russell made an interesting comment, saying, “Companies can no longer own the customer journey.” Consumer AI agents don’t sleep, don’t give up and don’t care about your interactive voice response tree.
Demand, once limited by human patience, is about to surge. Dave Meyer of Hyatt said it’s already happening, starting in Asia. “You have bots talking to bots,” he said, “We don’t have any historical baselines.” His advice is not to “fear the bots,” because “there’s a customer behind every single one of these inquiries.”
Banking isn’t there yet. Mia Carrera, head of customer excellence at Citi, said, “When you’re dealing with your money, there’s no tolerance for error,” though attitudes are shifting.
The race is accountability, not the smartest agent
“The race we are in is not about the smartest agent,” Russell said. “I see some of these announcements about these AI players, and I roll my eyes.” Accountability must shift from design time to runtime, with humans and AI agents held to the same standard.
Heltewig offered an analogy for agent security. Prompt-based guardrails are like telling kids not to touch the cookie jar. “What you got to do is you got to put a padlock on a cookie jar,” he said, meaning permissions enforced by the harness, not the model. Too many vendors still rely on the honor system.
The legacy business is the bridge, not the anchor
From a company perspective, one of the most important points came during the analyst Q&A, when Russell was asked why 50%-plus AI growth isn’t showing up in overall revenue and whether AI expands NiCE’s market or cannibalizes it. Russell said reported revenue blends very different growth profiles: workforce management, analytics, Actimize and public safety don’t grow like CCaaS and AI. “If you look at CXone and NiCE Cognigy, those numbers will blow you away,” he said. “I am obsessed with long-term, durable growth, not with what happened last or this quarter.”
“That 52% year-over-year ARR is not from pilots and POCs,” Russell said. It counts only multiyear commitments, and backlog is growing faster. The bottleneck is deployment, which is why Heltewig’s 30-day time-to-value goal is so important.
This is a point many miss, and it explains why the stock has moved sideways since the Cognigy acquisition. The timing of AI revenue is uncertain because enterprises move slowly. NiCE’s large, sticky installed base gives it time to navigate the transition. Pure-play AI startups lack that cushion, and Russell said customers increasingly realize that many of those startups’ economic models “don’t stack up.”
When I asked about outcome-based deals, Russell said premium customers are defaulting to enterprise license agreements that mix seats, consumption, and outcomes. “Predictability is right now even more important than outcome,” he said. Seats never monetized efficiency; now, “With the AI workloads, we clipped the ticket on everyone.” If seats decline, spend shifts to AI workloads rather than leaving.
That said, investors dislike uncertainty, and anything Russell can do to clarify when AI creates a step function in the company’s growth will help. It’s worth noting that this is an issue not just for NiCE but for the entire CX industry. AI will likely reduce the number of human seats sold, but the revenue upside from AI usage should dwarf that. How and when this happens remain unknown, so many investors sit on the sidelines.
Advice for IT pros
Treat interaction data as a strategic asset. Call recordings, transcripts, quality scores and screen recordings were once compliance artifacts stored until legal needed them. Now they’re the raw material for building, testing, and tuning AI agents, as NiCE’s demos showed. Information technology leaders should inventory where that data lives, how long it’s retained,and who can access it. Every platform contract, NiCE or otherwise, should guarantee that the enterprise can retrieve that data in a usable form. Whoever controls the interaction data will control how fast you can automate, so don’t let it be locked inside a vendor’s walls.
Plan for agent traffic now. Personal agents aren’t a 2028 problem. Hyatt is already seeing them, and the company’s biggest challenge is the lack of a historical baseline to plan against. Start by measuring how much inbound traffic is machine-generated, what those agents are asking for, and when they appear. Then work with security teams to determine how you’ll verify that an agent truly represents a customer and what it’s allowed to do on that customer’s behalf. Capacity planning also needs a rethink, since a single viral post can send millions of agents to your front door at once.
Demand enforcement, not instructions. Heltewig’s cookie-jar analogy should be in every request for proposal. Telling an AI agent in a prompt not to issue refunds above a certain amount is a suggestion, not a control. Ask vendors to show how permissions, spending limits, rate limits and kill switches are enforced in the harness around the model, and how every tool call is logged and auditable. If an agent can grant a 20% discount, someone needs to find out after the first one, not the 500th. If the vendor’s answer to security is a better prompt, keep looking.
Budget for change management. Every customer on stage said the technology was the easy part. Hyatt’s Meyer agreed, favoring a 70/30 split between change management and deployment. Jermain Smith, senior director of customer support at Valvoline, noted that the company more than doubled containment and cut one group’s staff by about 30% through attrition alone. It got there in part by adjusting agent metrics before rollout, so employees weren’t penalized when the AI took over coupon and pricing calls. Citi took a similar approach, making it clear that frontline agents wouldn’t be held responsible when the AI running in the background made a mistake. IT should own the deployment, but it needs human resources, operations and frontline managers in the room from day one.
Get the knowledge base right first. Russell made a point that’s easy to overlook: Human agents can work around inaccurate or outdated knowledge articles through training and experience, but AI agents can’t. They’ll confidently repeat whatever they’re given. Before scaling AI agents, audit the knowledge content they’ll rely on, assign owners and put a process in place to keep it current. This unglamorous work often separates a stalled pilot from a production deployment.
Measure resolution, not containment. Containment is the metric most companies start with, and it’s easy to inflate. A customer who gives up and hangs up counts as “contained.” Hyatt is moving toward measuring whether the customer’s original intent was resolved, along with the accuracy of the information the AI provides. Citi treats accuracy as the metric that matters most. Define what a resolved interaction means for your business before you deploy, and ensure your vendor reports against that definition.
Negotiate for predictability. Outcome-based pricing sounds great until success makes it expensive, and the definition of a completed task can vary widely. Russell said most large customers are choosing predictable models, and that’s the right instinct for now. Look for enterprise license agreements that let spend move across seats, consumption and outcomes as your mix of human and AI agents changes. Also, model token costs before committing, since several customers saw costs balloon and had to switch models mid-deployment.
Final thoughts
NiCE did what it said it would a year ago. The open questions are about execution: how quickly backlog turns into revenue, whether 30-day time to value holds in regulated enterprises, and how aggressively NiCE pushes to monetize its data.
NiCE’s advantage isn’t any single agent. It’s an installed base that funds the transition and a data asset no AI startup can replicate. Many of its traditional peers lack the resources or the data platform to deliver the depth of insight. If personal agents drive the demand surge Russell expects, enterprises will need a platform to absorb, govern, and learn from it. NiCE is betting it’s that platform.
Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

articles.title: OpenAI mise sur deux grands-mères pour faire connaître ChatGPT Voix en France
articles.text:
Monique et Sophie, deux grands-mères, discutent à voix haute avec ChatGPT dans la première campagne publicitaire d'OpenAI en France. Avec trois films diffusés depuis le 19 octobre à la télévision de rattrapage et sur les plateformes de streaming, l'entreprise veut convaincre le public d'essayer le mode vocal de son assistant.
Quatre jours plus tôt, OpenAI avait ajouté à ChatGPT Aube et Rivage, deux voix conçues pour mieux prononcer le français. OpenAI les met en avant dans ses films, avec un argument hérité de l'été. Depuis le déploiement de GPT-Live en juillet, vous pouvez couper la parole à ChatGPT au milieu d'une phrase, car l'assistant continue d'écouter pendant qu'il parle.
Dans la campagne, ChatGPT encaisse les interruptions et traduit en direct. Si vous l'essayez avec l'offre gratuite ou Go, vous tomberez en revanche sur une version allégée de cette voix, avec des publicités dans l'application.
Couper la parole à ChatGPT, un usage mis en scène par OpenAI
Dans le premier film, Monique demande une explication simple, puis Hakim, apprenti comédien, tente d'interrompre l'assistant au milieu de sa réponse. Sophie vérifie ensuite des dates pour une visite du Paris historique et prend rendez-vous chez le coiffeur. Dans le dernier film, Hakim fait traduire en direct sa présentation de comédien, avec une carrière internationale en tête. L'équipe de tournage apparaît à l'image et les personnages s'écartent du texte prévu, de quoi montrer un assistant capable de garder le fil malgré les dérapages.
Au passage, OpenAI cherche à clarifier la différence entre la dictée vocale, qui produit un message écrit à partir de la parole, et ChatGPT Voix, conçu pour discuter à l'oral. Les deux fonctions sont d'ailleurs comptées ensemble dans les chiffres de l'entreprise, qui annonçait en juillet plus de 150 millions de personnes chaque semaine pour la voix et la dictée.
Sur la page de présentation du mode vocal, OpenAI propose même une grand-mère dans ses exemples de requêtes, « Aide-moi à parler à ma grand-mère. Traduis tout ce que nous disons du français à l'anglais ». Trois grands-mères présentaient aussi GPT-Live dans le film américain diffusé en juillet, et Brandon McGraw, directeur marketing grand public par intérim d'OpenAI, résumait alors l'idée de ce film. « Au lieu de mettre en avant l'architecture du modèle, nous montrons ce que cette avancée signifie pour une personne ordinaire, c'est-à-dire parler naturellement et être comprise », expliquait-il.
Sans abonnement Plus, une voix allégée et des publicités
Si la pub vous donne envie d'essayer, regardez d'abord votre formule. OpenAI réserve le modèle GPT-Live-1.1 complet aux abonnés Plus et aux offres supérieures, et les comptes gratuits et Go reçoivent une version plus légère. Vous ne pourrez pas non plus filmer un objet ni partager votre écran en mode Live, car OpenAI garde ces deux fonctions dans l'ancien mode vocal avancé, pour les abonnés payants sur iOS et Android.
OpenAI affiche aussi, depuis le 24 août, des publicités sous les réponses de ChatGPT aux utilisateurs des offres gratuite et Go. L'entreprise est donc à la fois acheteuse d'espaces publicitaires pour sa campagne et vendeuse d'emplacements dans ChatGPT. Son agence média PHD a réservé des espaces sur TF1+, M6+, Canal+, Netflix, Prime Video et Disney+, et une version longue de 2 minutes 20 est disponible sur YouTube. D'après Influencia, OpenAI cherche ainsi à gagner à la fois des utilisateurs et des annonceurs, quelques semaines après l'ouverture de sa régie en France.
« Nous espérons que nos grands-mères donneront à chacun l'envie de découvrir ce qu'il peut accomplir au quotidien avec le mode voix », a déclaré Elke Karskens, directrice du marketing international d'OpenAI. Encore faut-il trouver Aube et Rivage. Dans les paramètres de ChatGPT, les voix proposées varient selon les comptes, et certains spectateurs chercheront ces deux voix en vain.

articles.title: India-New Zealand trade pact kicks in
articles.text:
India-New Zealand trade pact kicks in
The agreement provides duty-free access to a range of Indian goods, including products from labour-intensive sectors such as textiles and leather.
The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA), signed on April 27, came into effect on Tuesday, providing duty-free access to a range of Indian goods, including products from labour-intensive sectors such as textiles and leather.
It is the seventh trade pact to come into force in the last five years. The others are agreements with the UAE, Mauritius, the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) bloc, the UK, Oman and Australia.
Signed on April 27, 2026, the agreement follows negotiations launched in 2010, stalled in 2015 and revived in March 2025. The pact becomes India's 17th operational FTA.
According to experts, the sectors benefiting from the FTA are textiles and apparel, leather and footwear, engineering goods and auto components, gems and jewellery, agriculture and processed foods, pharmaceuticals, and other manufacturing industries.
Gulzar Didwania, Partner, Deloitte India, said the deal is expected to support higher FDI inflows into India, but the scale of any increase remains uncertain and will depend on private-sector investment decisions.
New Zealand has committed FDI worth USD 20 billion in over 15 years.
"The FTA's provisions on duty-free access for certain inputs, bilateral cumulation, customs facilitation, and investment-promotion mechanisms may encourage deeper value-chain integration and improve investment conditions," he said.
He added that the pact has significance beyond trade, strengthening India's strategic position in the Indo-Pacific, expanding its network of FTAs with developed economies.
At a time of growing global trade uncertainty, the India-New Zealand FTA is a strong endorsement of open markets and predictable trade rules. Its target of doubling bilateral trade by 2030 sets an ambitious agenda for both countries.
What makes this FTA particularly valuable is that it goes beyond goods to cover services, investment, skills and mobility, creating fresh opportunities for Indian professionals and businesses.
With 100 per cent of Indian exports gaining duty-free access to New Zealand from day one, the agreement gives Indian exporters a significant competitive advantage. MSMEs in textiles, leather, footwear and engineering goods are particularly well placed to benefit.
Economic think tank Chintan Research Foundation (CRF India) President Shishir Priyadarshi said that at a time of growing global trade uncertainty, the India-New Zealand FTA is a strong endorsement of open markets and predictable trade rules.
"What makes this FTA particularly valuable is that it goes beyond goods to cover services, investment, skills and mobility, creating fresh opportunities for Indian professionals and businesses," he said.
Trade expert and Hi-Tech Gears Chairman Deep Kapuria said the FTA operationalisation with New Zealand completes India's preferential market access in all major countries of the Asia-Pacific region.
"New Zealand is a very open economy; India has very well crafted this trade deal by securing market access for new services such as Ayush, yoga instructors and student mobility, including post-study work visa," he said.
Bilateral trade declined by about 11 per cent to USD 1.15 billion in 2025-26 from USD 1.3 billion in the previous fiscal year. India's exports stood at USD 566.51 million, while imports were USD 589.1 million, resulting in a meagre trade deficit of USD 22.59 million for India.
Rani Singh, Indian-origin New Zealander, said the deal is an important step forward for both countries as it is not just about trade; it is about bringing the two countries closer, creating opportunities for businesses and people, and building a stronger relationship for the future.
"India now has an opportunity to build its own strong partnership with New Zealand. With duty-free access to New Zealand for all Indian export tariff lines from day one, Indian businesses can become more competitive in this market," she said.
Singh added that the benefits are not limited to goods as there is also scope for greater cooperation in education, tourism, technology, professional services and investment.
Greater opportunities for eligible skilled professionals and young people can further strengthen these connections, she said.

articles.title: C'est officiel, Apple va faire de nouvelles annonces très bientôt : enfin les MacBook Pro Oled ?
articles.text:
Après des mois de rumeurs, c’est peut-être enfin la fin de l’histoire : les MacBook avec écran tactile seraient bientôt là. Pour le moment, ce qui est sûr, c’est qu’Apple donne rendez-vous ce mercredi 28 octobre pour un événement avec le plein d’annonces.
Apple va faire une présentation ce mercredi 28 octobre
C’est le vice-président en charge du marketing d’Apple Greg Joswiak, ou « Joz » qui a annoncé la nouvelle sur X ce lundi 19 octobre. Il a retourné l’expression « show and tell » en « pro and tell », référence directe aux produits « Pro » de la marque. De quoi nous donner un indice sur les annonces, qui devraient surtout concerner le MacBook Pro.
Certains journalistes ont officiellement été invités par Apple pour un événement en présentiel à Los Angeles en Californie. Il aura lieu à 10 heures, heure du Pacifique, soit 19 heures en France. On ne s’attend donc pas à une conférence de type keynote comme pour la présentation des iPhone, mais plutôt à des publications de communiqués de presse. Les journalistes présents sur place devraient pouvoir prendre en main les nouveaux produits annoncés.
Exactement comme l’événement de la semaine dernière, dédié à la domotique avec la présentation du HomeView, de la nouvelle Apple TV 4K, du HomePod mini 2 ainsi que des objets connectés développés avec LG.
Ce qu’on attend des nouveaux MacBook Pro M6
Le nouveau MacBook Pro devrait accueillir pour la première fois la puce M6. Il y aurait tout d’abord un modèle « d’entrée de gamme » doté de cette puce gravée en 2 nm, qui vise de meilleures performances ainsi qu’une meilleure efficacité énergétique. Un MacBook Pro qui serait décliné dans une seconde version dotée d’un écran Oled tactile en 14 ou 16 pouces. Ce serait la première fois qu’un ordinateur portable d’Apple serait équipé d’une dalle tactile. Une nouveauté attendue depuis longtemps dans les rumeurs, mais aussi par macOS 27, qui est adapté aux interactions tactiles. Néanmoins, cette version tactile du MacBook Pro embarquerait des puces M5 Pro et M5 Max : la version M6 arriverait fin 2027.
L’encoche en profiterait pour disparaître, remplacée par un poinçon proche de la Dynamic Island qu’on connaît sur les iPhone. Le châssis de l’ordinateur serait repensé pour être plus fin et plus léger, avec une nouvelle charnière et des bordures réduites. Le tout avec un prix plus élevé, à cause de l’inflation et de la crise des composants.
Aux côtés de ce nouveaux MacBook Pro, on s’attend aussi à une mise à jour de l’iMac vers la puce M6. En effet, le dernier iMac remonte à deux ans tout pile ; il avait eu le droit à la puce M4. Enfin, il devrait y avoir le retour de l’iPad mini, pour la première fois avec un écran Oled. La semaine dernière, le site d’Apple avait fait fuité un modèle d’iPad inconnu : il pourrait bien s’agir de lui. Tous ces nouveaux produits pourraient être lancés ce vendredi 6 novembre.

articles.title: Japan launches mission to bring home a piece of the Martian moon Phobos
articles.text:
Japan launched a $578 million mission Monday on a five-year expedition to land on the largest moon of Mars and retrieve samples for return to Earth, a daring international project that could yield new insights into the formation of the Solar System.
The robotic Martian Moons eXploration mission, known as MMX, lifted off at 3:41 pm EDT Monday (4:41 am Japan Standard Time Tuesday) from Tanegashima Space Center in southern Japan.
The MMX spacecraft rode into orbit atop a 207-foot-tall (63-meter) H3 rocket, Japan’s flagship launch vehicle. The rocket assigned to MMX debuted a new souped-up configuration with four strap-on solid rocket boosters, full-throttle main engines, and an extended payload shroud to accommodate the demands of Japan’s heaviest and most ambitious interplanetary mission to date.
The rocket’s upper stage accelerated the MMX spacecraft to a top speed of more than 24,000 mph, fast enough to break free of Earth’s gravitational pull for the 10-month voyage to Mars. The nearly 9,900-pound (4.5-metric ton) spacecraft—two-thirds of its mass comprised of propellant—separated from the H3 rocket about 71 minutes after liftoff.
Hiroshi Yamakawa, president of the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), declared the launch a success. “A long journey of five years has just started,” Yamakawa said.
MMX established contact with ground controllers, unfurled its solar panels, and was in a “very stable condition” soon after separating from the H3 rocket, according to Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, the mission’s project manager at JAXA. “So far, so good.”
“The MMX [mission] we launched today is a challenging mission aiming for the world’s first sample return from the Martian moons,” said Yoshihiro Seki, Japan’s science minister. “We hope that the results obtained through this mission will contribute to the development of our nation’s space science and exploration technology.”
Building on a legacy
The mission to the Martian moons builds on Japan’s success in leading the Hayabusa and Hayabusa 2 missions, the world’s first two spacecraft to bring back pristine specimens from asteroids. Scientists believe Phobos could itself be an asteroid that was captured into orbit around Mars billions of years ago. One of MMX’s science goals is finding out if that theory is correct.

articles.title: Itaú agora permite usar pontos acumulados para pagar Pix • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Itaú agora permite usar pontos acumulados para pagar Pix
Clientes poderão usar o saldo de pontos para pagar transações pelo app, sem cobrança de taxa.
O Itaú Unibanco anunciou nesta segunda-feira (19/10) que os pontos acumulados pelos clientes poderão ser usados para pagamentos via Pix. A novidade permite utilizar o saldo do programa de benefícios em despesas do dia a dia, sem precisar trocá-los por produtos, milhas ou dinheiro antes da operação.
O recurso está sendo liberado gradualmente ao longo de outubro para clientes do programa Pontos Itaú, através do app do banco, e não terá cobrança de taxa sobre as transações, segundo o diretor de Cartões, Contas e Pagamentos do Itaú Unibanco, Felipe Piccoli Aversa. A previsão é ampliar a disponibilidade para todos os participantes até o fim do ano.
Nós perguntamos ao Itaú qual seria a taxa de conversão entre pontos e reais. O banco não quis responder. Disse, porém, que a cotação pode variar ao longo do tempo e que “o cliente sempre vai ver quanto valem seus pontos antes de efetuar a transação”.
Na hora de fazer um Pix, o cliente precisa ter uma quantidade de pontos que cubra 100% do valor da transação, pois não será possível combinar pontos com outra forma de pagamento para completar a quantia.
O aplicativo vai mostrar quantos pontos estão disponíveis e quanto será necessário para concluir a transação, além do valor equivalente em reais, antes da confirmação. O cliente deverá escolher entre o saldo da conta, o cartão de crédito ou os pontos como forma de pagamento.
A novidade estará disponível para pagamentos via Pix por chave, QR Code e aproximação, e não será compatível com o Pix Automático. O uso dos pontos ficará registrado no extrato do programa.
A funcionalidade contempla pontos acumulados no programa Pontos e Cashback do Itaú. Saldos de programas parceiros, como Latam Pass e TudoAzul, não poderão ser utilizados dessa forma.

articles.title: Electronics hobbyist converts $120 DDR5 SODIMM kit into ‘$1000’ desktop kit to fight RAM crisis — ICs from SK hynix DDR5-5600 16GB modules used to create DDR5-7800 desktop sticks
articles.text:
Electronics hobbyist converts $120 DDR5 SODIMM kit into ‘$1000’ desktop kit to fight RAM crisis — ICs from SK hynix DDR5-5600 16GB modules used to create DDR5-7800 desktop sticks
You have to be lucky to find such cheap DDR5 SODIMMs, and specialist equipment and skills are required for success.
What if you could buy a cheap used DDR5 SODIMM (laptop memory) kit and transform it into a super-fast DDR5 desktop kit? That’s what electronics hobbyist Blighted Agent recently did when they succeeded in converting a SK hynix 2x 16GB DDR5-5600 SODIMM kit they got from Facebook Marketplace for $120 into a 2x 16GB DDR5-7800 desktop kit, claimed to be worth around $1,000. They also had to buy some blank DDR5 desktop memory PCBs from AliExpress for around $16 each, and a set of heatsinks for around $18.
In the above video, our hero says they bought the donor laptop 2x 16GB DDR5-5600 sticks for just $120, which is a bargain. With extra bits and pieces from AliExpress (desktop DDR5 PCBs, etc.), the total bill of materials came to $175. Blighted Agent comments that the SODIMMs used what he believed to be SK hynix A-die modules, which are the same as the ICs used in expensive desktop DDR5 modules like the G.Skill Trident Royal line.
The process began with taking the memory ICs from the donor modules using a hot air station. Then they were cleaned and had 0.45mm leaded solder balls added, using a DDR5 stencil, reballing jig, and hot air. Next, the blank desktop DDR5 PCBs were prepared. A little solder was added to the plethora of BGA connectors to be ready for the memory chips to connect to.
The old DDR5 ICs and the new desktop modules could now be mated, using flux, the preheater, hot air, and watching and prodding carefully with a dental pick. Blighted Agent’s experience lets him know when the BGA chips have successfully mated with the PCB. You can eyeball when they pop precisely into place due to surface tension, and offer up a modicum of resistance to pick prodding.
Finally, the enthusiast added the SPD chip and BIOS chip from the SODIMMs to the new desktop DIMMs. These new desktop DIMMs were quickly tested in a PC before they were finished off with carefully applied thermal pads and the fancy-looking heatsinks.
Blighted Agent felt lucky that there were no issues with the newly created desktop modules. There’s a lot of intricate things that can go wrong during such a process. The initial boot verification showed them recognized in his Asus ROG Maximus Z790 Apex Encore motherboard as two “SK hynix 16,384MB 5600MHz” modules, which was correct. Some tuning resulted in rock-steady performance at DDR5-7800 CL38 and 1.40V. This was verified by stress testing for 90 minutes, which the enthusiast reckons was ample for a gaming PC. It is very likely a better result than using those mechanical SODIMM-to-DIMM converters you can buy, which can be problematic.
Blighted Agent seems to specialize in BGA soldering work, and has also successfully upgraded several graphics cards with double the VRAM. Though videos like this are edited to be brief, and they make the process look easy, the TechTuber admits there is a lot that can go wrong during this kind of rework. Moreover, with RAM modules, they lack the testing equipment to locate an issue with any particular IC on the PCB. So, if this module didn’t work, they might have ended up in a world of pain, not knowing which memory chip had an issue due to either an internal fault or a BGA soldering glitch.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Looking around at used DDR5 SODIMMs, it looks like Blighted Agent was very lucky to get a used working 32GB kit for $120. I just checked eBay U.S., and the best deal there was $320. Meanwhile, the best price for a new 32GB DDR5-6000 kit seems to be $449 at the time of writing.
We reported on Russian enthusiast VIK-on succeeding in a similar project earlier this year, but all their costing was in Rubles, and they went the extra mile in flashing custom firmware so the remade modules would be auto-detected with 6400 MT/s XMP support on most motherboards. In late 2026, DDR5 RAM continues to be too expensive.

Also, I much prefer it from the manufacturer, just because it posts now doesn't mean it will in a week or year, Ball Grid Arrays (BGAs) and Chip Scale Packages (CSPs) are notorious for bad joints. Even with the best technology in the world there is a high chance of the joints not being perfect and severely degrees the longevity of the product - that's why these manufactured use XRAY. articles.title: Pennsylvania issues alert on congenital measles—something US hasn't seen for decades
articles.text:
Pennsylvania’s health department issued a health alert Monday as cases of measles in pregnancy and, in turn, cases of congenital measles have continued to increase. Before the current outbreak—which continues to rage across the state—congenital measles cases hadn’t been seen in decades, the department noted in its advisory.
The alert included detailed clinical guidance for managing measles exposures and cases during pregnancy as well as cases in newborns. Many doctors have never seen such cases in their careers given the decades of successful use of the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine. But now, with vaccination rates slipping nationwide, the highly infectious virus is better able to get footholds in communities and spread rapidly through under-vaccinated pockets, as is happening in Pennsylvania.
As of October 19, Pennsylvania had reported 1,286 measles cases this year across 42 counties. Of those, 247 have been hospitalized, and six people have reportedly died (though the latest reported death is still pending an investigation by the state health department before it is added to the state tally).
The Pennsylvania health department did not immediately respond to a request for information from Ars Technica. But reporting from The 19th earlier this month put the number of measles cases during pregnancy at 53. At least one case of congenital measles led to a death; the first death reported in the current outbreak was in a newborn baby boy, who died immediately after birth while his mother was severely ill with measles.
Risky infection
Pregnant people who have not been vaccinated against measles nor previously had the infection are susceptible. A case of measles during pregnancy increases the risk of hospitalization, pneumonia, the need for oxygen support or mechanical ventilation, and death. It also increases the risk of miscarriage, stillbirth, low birth weight, and preterm labor. The MMR vaccine is not recommended during pregnancy because it is a live attenuated vaccine and poses a theoretical risk of causing an infection in a fetus. If a pregnant person is exposed to the virus, they’re recommended to receive intravenous immunoglobulin to help protect against infection—but only if it is given within six days of exposure.

articles.title: Petition launches to can Anthropic Nova Scotia data centre project
articles.text:
A change.org petition has been launched to stop the construction of an AI data centre in Nova Scotia, and it is rapidly gaining support.
The petition, which was posted by resident Kevin Fifield, calls the decision to build the data centre as “a decision that significantly impacts our environment, our power grid, and our community at large.”
According to CBC News, the data centre in question is a proposed data centre just outside Port Hawkesbury in Cape Breton, Nova Scotia. EverWind Fuels, a renewable energy company based in Halifax, will own the facility, and Anthropic will lease it to power Claude.
The company noted it will build the facility in two stages, with the first phase coming online by the end of 2027 and the second in 2028. Both companies say they will pay for any required upgrades to the province’s electricity system, and EverWind has raised $8 billion in private capital.
Currently, the petition has 12,142 shares, 174 comments, and 11,800 signatures.
“This data centre is poised to benefit a select few while the costs are disproportionately shared by Nova Scotians,” writes Fifield. We must scrutinize who truly benefits from such projects and weigh these against long-term impacts on our environment and economy.”
Interestingly, Jacob Glick told Global News during a protest in Halifax against the data centre that “Canadians are using Claude in growing numbers, and we want our infrastructure to be closer to the people who rely on it.”
However, the people don’t exactly want the infrastructure close to them. Beyond these recent protests, the cities of Hamilton, Ontario, and Vancouver, British Columbia both sought a pause on AI data centres, with Hamilton rejecting a proposal for a large-scale project after public outcry.
Image credit: Shutterstock
Source: Kevin Pifield — Change.org

articles.title: Otter.ai raises $320 million from General Catalyst's growth fund for its meeting tool | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Meeting note-taking tool Otter.ai announced on Tuesday that it has raised $320 million from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund (CVF), which provides capital to startups without diluting equity and gets returns on the results of marketing spend.
Otter.ai said that it will use these funds for enterprise growth, go-to-market strategy, international expansion, and product innovation.
The startup, which has been around for nearly a decade, has raised $50 million in total funding with its last round in 2021, according to PitchBook data.
Last year, Otter hit a revenue milestone after crossing $100 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR). The company said it’s now approaching new milestones, but didn’t provide updated figures.
The company said that 40 million users have used its product to date, up from 25 million last year. However, given the crowded space among meeting note-taking products, a pertinent challenge for Otter would be to have its customers stick around. Unfortunately, the startup didn’t provide any numbers around its monthly active users or churn.
“Voice is one of the biggest untapped opportunities in enterprise AI, and Otter is at the forefront of it – a conviction that’s only deepened watching Otter’s growth,” said Pranav Singhvi, Partner and Co-founder of CVF, General Catalyst. “When Otter enables enterprises to capture critical voice data and turns it into actionable business insights, teams move faster, decisions get sharper, and productivity compounds across the organization, and that’s why it’s a strong partner for CVF.”
There is a lot of competition in the market with well-funded meeting notetakers like Fireflies.ai, Granola, and Read AI; new entrants like Calendly, Wispr, and Superhuman, which acquired Fathom; and other notetakers like Circleback, Talat, and Quill.
Most of these notetakers want to connect to enterprise systems and, based on data captured in meetings, automate workflows. Otter is also heading in that direction. In the last few years, it introduced a meeting assistant, a search function that works across apps, and integration with other AI tools.
Otter’s newly appointed CMO, Alex Gay, who comes from Superhuman, told TechCrunch at a sit-down at the HumanX conference last month that the company sees a big opportunity in turning transcripts into an actionable roadmap for people who are in back-to-back meetings.
“When we start thinking about what is actually the bigger problem that people are facing right now, we saw this large pain point in meeting-heavy roles, where people are back-to-back in conversations. These meetings are the work for them. That’s either customer conversations or, from a sales standpoint. That’s where strategies are discussed. But meetings are terribly inefficient because when you come into a meeting, you spend the first twenty minutes recapping what was said before to catch everybody up,” he said.
The company is now experimenting with providing insights before, after, and during meetings. It has been testing a feature to send a pre-brief to users with details and background information, with context from previous conversations across surfaces. Plus, it is also trying out a Live Assist feature to let users ask questions to the AI assistant during the meeting to get knowledge.

articles.title: Attack Shark Launches R5 Turbo Flagship Carbon Fiber Gaming Mouse
articles.text:
Monday, October 19th 2026
Attack Shark Launches R5 Turbo Flagship Carbon Fiber Gaming Mouse
High-performance gaming peripheral brand ATTACK SHARK today announced the upcoming release of the R5 TURBO. This next-generation flagship wireless gaming mouse builds on the R5 ULTRA's success with upgraded hardware, dual 8K connectivity, a design optimized for precision control, and a new Dune colorway, alongside classic black and white options.
Gavin Cheng, CEO and Co-Founder of ATTACK SHARK"Following the strong market response to the R5 ULTRA, we pushed further to deliver even greater precision and speed. The R5 TURBO represents our continued commitment to give competitive players the edge they need to perform at their best."
The R5 TURBO continues ATTACK SHARK's commitment to lightweight, precision-driven design with an injection-molded carbon fiber composite housing. Weighing approximately 43 g (± 3 g), the mouse combines structural strength with everyday durability through a hollowed-out, breathable design philosophy. The exterior features a glass-like cool-touch coating to reduce stickiness from hand sweat, which provides a smooth, responsive feel during extended gaming sessions.
Powered by the PixArt PAW3950MAX optical sensor, the R5 TURBO supports a DPI range of 1,200-60,000 with 50-DPI step adjustments, enabling players to fine-tune sensitivity with exceptional precision. The sensor delivers tracking speeds of up to 750 IPS and 60G acceleration, ensuring smooth and accurate movement across various surfaces. With its three-level LOD (Lift-Off Distance) adjustment system, users can customize tracking height based on personal preference and optimize control for different playstyles.
The R5 TURBO features the new Nordic nRF54LM20 flagship MCU, an upgrade from the previous generation's nRF54L15. This advanced processor enables wired and wireless 8KHz polling rates for responsive gameplay. Internal testing showed wireless click latency as low as 0.168 ms. The chip also supports static scan frame rates exceeding 20,000 FPS in competitive mode, while delivering improved power efficiency and reduced heat generation. Enhanced Bluetooth channel sounding technology further strengthens connection stability and reliability.
Another standout feature of the R5 TURBO is ATTACK SHARK's signature shark-fin-inspired 8K wireless receiver, which incorporates an extended antenna structure for superior signal strength. Three LED indicators provide real-time status updates on connection mode, polling rate, and battery life. The mouse supports triple-mode connectivity, including wired, 2.4 GHz wireless, and Bluetooth, giving players flexibility to choose the optimal setup for their environment.
Inside the lightweight chassis, the R5 TURBO houses a 290 mAh high-density automotive-grade battery. Under standard 1K polling-rate conditions, the mouse delivers up to 300 hours of battery life, supporting both extended gaming marathons and daily productivity use.
The R5 TURBO also brings upgrades to its core interaction components. Omron optical switches, rated for over 100 million clicks, deliver fast, consistent actuation for competitive play. The scroll wheel features a custom electroplated finish and TTC Golden Wheel encoders, providing precise scrolling and enhanced tactile feedback. These refinements help deliver the speed, accuracy, and responsiveness players expect in high-level gaming.
The R5 TURBO also introduces intelligent driver support with cloud-based configuration and standalone download options. The software automatically recognizes connected devices, simplifying customization of DPI, polling rate, and other supported functions to match individual player preferences.
From the R5 ULTRA to the R5 TURBO, ATTACK SHARK continues to explore the intersection of carbon fiber materials, lightweight structures, and high-performance esports technology.
The ATTACK SHARK R5 TURBO will be available starting October 23, 2026.

articles.title: Votre smartphone connecté à un satellite sans passer par Starlink ? Orange et trois géants européens préparent la riposte
articles.text:
Ce n’était encore qu’une rumeur en septembre, comme nous l’expliquions alors. C’est désormais officiel. Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica et Vodafone ont annoncé ce lundi 19 octobre avoir signé une lettre d’intention pour étudier « une éventuelle candidature conjointe » à l’attribution, en Europe, des fréquences réservées aux services mobiles par satellite. Ce sont elles qui permettent à un smartphone classique de se connecter directement à un satellite, sans antenne particulière, là où le réseau terrestre ne passe pas.
Les quatre opérateurs ne construiront pas leurs propres satellites. Ils prévoient de déployer en Europe les infrastructures au sol ainsi que les fonctions de coordination et de supervision du réseau, la constellation étant fournie par « un partenaire satellitaire qui reste à sélectionner ». Ils promettent aussi un accès « ouvert et non discriminatoire » à tous les opérateurs mobiles. Bouygues Telecom, Free ou SFR pourraient donc, en théorie, en profiter eux aussi.
Des fréquences convoitées par SpaceX
Tout se joue sur la bande des 2 GHz, dont les licences actuelles, détenues par Viasat et EchoStar, expirent en mai 2027. Or SpaceX a racheté en 2025 une partie du spectre d’EchoStar, et les licences européennes de ce dernier doivent lui être transférées en 2027, selon le site spécialisé Light Reading. Pour garder la main sur ces fréquences, la Commission européenne a proposé en mai, la Commission européenne a proposé en mai de découper la bande en trois parts égales : une pour les communications gouvernementales, intégrée à la constellation IRIS², une réservée aux nouveaux entrants européens et une ouverte à tous, Starlink compris. C’est la part européenne que vise le quatuor. Le texte doit encore être adopté, et l’attribution des nouveaux droits n’est pas attendue avant 2029.
L’alliance n’est pas dénuée de paradoxes. La lettre d’intention des quatre opérateurs « ne remplace pas les partenariats satellitaires existants », et ils sont nombreux. Deutsche Telekom a signé avec Starlink pour un lancement en 2028, Vodafone partage une coentreprise avec l’américain AST SpaceMobile, et Orange, qui vend déjà son option Message Satellite, travaille aussi avec AST. Seulement, aucun d’eux n’a seul la puissance de feu de SpaceX, qui vient encore de racheter pour près de 8 milliards de dollars de fréquences aux États-Unis. En s’alliant, les opérateurs évitent surtout que Starlink ne vende un jour ses propres forfaits mobiles en se passant d’eux.
Washington brandit la menace
Le projet européen irrite déjà les États-Unis. L’ambassadeur américain auprès de l’Union européenne, Andrew Puzder, a averti dans le Financial Times que les entreprises européennes présentes aux États-Unis pourraient subir des représailles « dévastatrices » si Bruxelles restreignait l’accès de Starlink à ces fréquences. La Commission assure de son côté que son projet reste ouvert aux acteurs non européens.
Pour les abonnés, l’enjeu concerne surtout les zones blanches, la montagne, la mer et les situations où les antennes terrestres tombent en panne. Il faudra toutefois s’armer de patience : trouver un partenaire satellitaire, de préférence européen, ne sera pas simple, alors qu’IRIS² n’est pas attendu avant 2030.

articles.title: Neural Concept launches MCP to help AI agents operate commercial CAD tools - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Neural Concept launches MCP to help AI agents operate commercial CAD tools
Switzerland-based artificial intelligence-native engineering company Neural Concept SA today launched Model Context Protocol Bridge to help AI agents operate commercial computer-aided design and simulation tools.
The capability will also help large engineering organizations automate complex software environments that are fundamental to designing and simulating physical products. This is an important part of manufacturing and proving prototypes before they are prepared for the real world.
In a typical simulation cycle, running solvers is the only step that doesn’t require human engineers. It’s largely already automated through retrieving proper physical geometry, cleaning it up and turning it into a virtual simulated mesh.
Founded in 2019, Neural Concept serves leading original equipment manufacturers and engineering organizations in industries throughout automotive, aerospace, energy, consumer, electronics, semiconductors and defense. It integrates an AI-augmented engineering platform and deep learning directly into computer-aided design and computer-aided engineering workflows.
With the new MCP Bridge, the platform will give AI agents access to the tools that make this happen, as well as the engineering know-how to use them, while companies retain control and ownership of their software and data.
“For the first time, the software that shapes every physical product can be operated by AI at enterprise scale,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Pierre Baqué.
Ideally, Baqué added, the opportunity is to reduce the tedium for engineers, who can then take on harder problems and work faster. This comes at a time when manufacturers are looking to shorten development lifecycles with fewer engineering experts available.
If an agent can handle an approved task in design and simulation software, every hour it takes is an hour handed back to an expert for more critical work. In one customer case, an engineer using MCP Bridge cleaned up the geometry of a wheel rim in three minutes, compared with a day using a manual process. That work is needed to get a physical product from physical to virtual model preparation and into simulation.
Thiat process, virtual model preparation and simulation, shifts engineering from reaction, physical trial-and-error into proactive data-driven digital environments by creating “digital twins.” These digital twins can be simulated in high fidelity, but only if they are “cleaned up” to act, look and react like their real-world counterparts with real-world physics before manufacturing happens.
That preparation works off spec sheets, materials guidelines and vast amounts of data. It can be extremely tedious, long work that requires extensive validation.
Once it’s done, engineers can test thousands of design scenarios simultaneously in virtual labs instead of waiting for real-world physical prototypes. However, getting one set up and into a rough draft an expert can refine can take weeks or more; an AI agent working in computer-aided engineering software can cut that time to hours. An engineer can fine-tune the result.
“AI agents have completely changed the way I work,” said Ciro Alosa, an electromagnetic design engineer at Traton SE, a subsidiary of Volkswagen Group that manages its heavy truck, bus and light commercial vehicle brands. “I can run more work in parallel, and going from a research paper to a validated script in our simulation toolchain now takes a couple of days.”
