articles.title: Apple deve lançar novos Macs em evento de 28 de outubro • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apple deve lançar novos Macs em evento de 28 de outubro
Apresentação pode ter novos MacBooks Pro com tela OLED e touchscreen, além de iPad mini e Macs com chip M6.
A Apple anunciou nesta segunda-feira (19/10) um novo evento marcado para 28 de outubro, em Los Angeles, nos Estados Unidos. A apresentação começa às 14h, no horário de Brasília, e foi divulgada sob o slogan “Pro and tell”.
Ainda não há nenhuma informação oficial sobre quais produtos devem aparecer neste evento, o quarto de lançamento de produtos da empresa no ano. No entanto, o jornalista Mark Gurman, da Bloomberg, adiantou há algumas semanas que uma nova rodada de lançamentos neste mês teria foco em Macs e iPads.
Entre os principais possíveis lançamentos esperados para o evento estão novos MacBook Pro de 14 e 15 polegadas com tela OLED sensível ao toque. Essa seria uma das maiores mudanças na linha desde a reformulação de 2021.
As informações apontam para a substituição do notch por uma Ilha Dinâmica, presente nos iPhones desde a linha 14 Pro, além de uma redução no peso. As versões mais avançadas devem manter os chips M5 Pro e M5 Max, que já apareceram na linha nos lançamentos de março. Porém, a versão de entrada do modelo de 14 polegadas pode avançar para o M6.
À primeira vista a situação parece bastante incomum, mas é importante notar que o chip M6 foi lançado como um modelo de transição pela Apple, tanto que não receberá versões aprimoradas (como Pro e Max). Espera-se que a companhia introduza o chip M7 já no primeiro semestre do ano que vem — esse sim receberia versões aprimoradas para os aparelhos mais potentes.
Com a tela sensível ao toque, a Apple naturalmente também estaria trabalhando em adaptações no macOS para o uso com os dedos, o que devei incluir elementos maiores na interface e suporte a gestos comuns em iPads, por exemplo.
Outros produtos esperados para o evento são:
O lançamento dos novos produtos nas lojas deve ocorrer apenas em novembro, também de acordo com Gurman.
O “Pro and tell” ocorre pouco mais de duas semanas após o evento Welcome Home, em Nova York. Na ocasião, a Apple apresentou produtos para casa, como a tela inteligente HomeView, o HomePod mini 2, uma nova geração da Apple TV 4K e outros acessórios para casa conectada em parceria com a LG.
Aquele foi o terceiro evento da companhia no ano apenas para lançamento de produtos. Considerando também a WWDC, realizada em junho, a Apple já promoveu cinco grandes eventos. É o maior número desde 2021, em que distribuiu lançamentos em três ocasiões, além da conferência sobre as novidades de software.
Essa maior quantidade de eventos de lançamento deve ser um padrão na gestão de John Ternus, que, segundo a Bloomberg, quer lançamentos menos concentrados no grande evento de setembro, geralmente dedicado aos iPhones mais potentes.

articles.title: Motive brings agentic AI to physical operations with agents that act before problems escalate - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Motive brings agentic AI to physical operations with agents that act before problems escalate
Motive Inc., the San Francisco-based artificial intelligence platform provider for physical operations, today announced the launch of Agents, a new capability that automatically responds to safety, maintenance and operational issues before they escalate into accidents, costly breakdowns or business disruptions.
The new Agents platform moves beyond alerts to automatically contact drivers, initiate maintenance and coordinate operational responses. The launch advances Motive’s strategy to bring agentic AI to the physical economy.
Motive’s technology uses operational data already collected through their platform to identify potential problems and initiate corrective actions. Agents can contact drivers, create maintenance work orders, alert managers and coordinate responses across fleet operations without requiring personnel to manually process every notification.
The launch targets one of the biggest challenges facing transportation, logistics, construction and other physical industries: Organizations have more operational data than ever, but acting on that information still requires significant manual coordination.
Motive estimates that companies lose approximately $46 billion to preventable operational problems, including vehicle downtime, compliance violations and unnecessary idling. According to the company’s 2026 ROI Report, 42% of surveyed organizations cite operational inefficiencies, including excessive administrative work, as a leading concern.
“Our customers don’t need another alert. They need action,” said Hemant Banavar, chief product officer at Motive. “The data that prevents collisions and breakdowns already lives in Motive. Agents put it to work the moment it matters, so teams can grow without adding headcount.”
Agents are available now to Motive customers. The company is demonstrating the new capabilities this week at the American Trucking Association’s Management Conference & Exhibition in Charlotte, North Carolina.
Motive plans to expand the technology in early 2027 with natural-language agent creation, allowing customers to describe a workflow in plain English and have AI build the corresponding automation. That future capability represents a progression beyond the rule-based and AI-assisted workflows available today. Motive has not provided independently validated performance results for the newly launched Agents platform.
The announcement builds on technology introduced earlier this year, including the company’s Atlas AI assistant, AI-powered automation tools and expanding edge computing capabilities.
Analysis: Motive’s bigger play is moving physical AI from insights to action
The Motive announcement is a good example of what I see emerging as one of the most important trends in enterprise AI: the transition from systems that generate insights to intelligent systems that actually do work.
For years, enterprise software has focused on collecting information, improving visibility and giving people dashboards to manage their businesses. The cloud era made that data more accessible. Generative AI made it easier to query, summarize and interpret. Agentic AI introduces a different opportunity: closing the gap between understanding what’s happening and taking action. This will be very important in the physical economy.
The deeper opportunity isn’t simply automating individual tasks. It’s eliminating the operational latency between detecting a problem, making a decision and executing a response.
This is where agentic AI could change the unit economics of physical operations. Companies have spent years investing in sensors, cameras, telematics and operational software. Those technologies generate enormous amounts of information, but much of the responsibility for converting that information into action still falls on people.
Agents introduce the possibility of compressing that coordination layer.
When intelligence can initiate an approved operational response instead of simply generating another alert, the economics begin to change. Fleet managers can potentially oversee more vehicles, maintenance teams can respond earlier, and organizations can improve utilization without adding proportional administrative overhead.
The real prize in physical AI may not be automating the workflow. It may be redesigning the operating model around intelligence that continuously turns signals into action.
The roadmap was already visible in our June 2026 interview
During a recent interview on theCUBE’s NYSE Wired: Physical AI & Robotics program, Motive Chief Product Officer Hemant Banavar discussed the company’s evolving architecture. “The next era of AI is about action and not insights,” Banavar said.
He was describing an industry that had spent years deploying telematics, cameras and monitoring devices but had created a new problem in the process: too much data and too little time to respond.
Banavar outlined a real-world scenario involving a fatigued driver. Motive’s computer vision technology could detect signs of fatigue and issue a warning. If the condition persisted, an automated workflow could initiate a conversation with the driver, encourage a safe stop and alert the fleet manager. “Imagine now nobody needs to be watching a dashboard in real time,” he explained.
The technology is designed to turn a sequence of disconnected activities — monitoring, detecting, notifying, communicating and coordinating — into an integrated operational workflow. This matters because the strategic value of agentic AI isn’t simply automating an individual task.
Physical AI requires a different architecture
In our recent interview, Banavar also explained why AI in physical operations has fundamentally different requirements from AI in traditional digital environments. He emphasized that accuracy in physical AI can be a matter of life and death, unlike many digital AI applications where an incorrect response may have limited consequences.
A slightly incorrect email generated by a language model is inconvenient. A safety system that fails to recognize a dangerous operating condition can have serious consequences. That places a premium on real-time processing, reliable models and the integration of intelligence directly into physical environments.
Motive has been investing in edge AI technologies, including its AI Dashcam Plus and AI Omnicam Plus, which extend computer vision and processing capabilities inside and around vehicles.
Banavar discussed the company’s relationship with Qualcomm, whose chips power these devices. He said Motive’s latest hardware can run three times more computer vision models than competing devices in its comparison, increasing the number of conditions the system can detect.
The performance comparison is Motive’s claim, but the architectural implications are meaningful. Motive is combining processing at the edge with cloud-connected operational systems and AI-driven workflows. The edge detects events. The platform provides operational context. Agents initiate approved actions. Atlas enables direct communication with people.
This integrated stack could become an important competitive differentiator as agentic AI moves into industries where reliability, real-time decision-making and safety are critical.
Practical AI: The ROI story is already taking shape
One of my recurring themes on theCUBE is that the real opportunity in AI isn’t just technological innovation. It’s the ability to produce measurable economic value.
During my July 2025 interview with Nyanya Joof, then Motive’s regional vice president for the U.K. market, at the RAISE Summit in Paris, we discussed the economics of physical AI and the opportunity to bring intelligence to industries that have traditionally relied on manual processes.
I characterized the opportunity as practical AI — not another demonstration of a powerful language model, but technology that can deliver measurable operational improvements.
Joof provided several examples. Phoenix Global, a metals and mining company, had reduced safety incidents by 40%, according to Joof, while improving its operational performance.
Ernst Concrete, an 80-year-old construction materials business, had deployed Motive’s AI cameras and video coaching after experiencing costly safety incidents. Joof said the company achieved $6.5 million in savings and a 2,000% return on investment over 13 months.
Motive also reported significant reductions in collisions and accident-related costs among Motive customers, along with improvements in vehicle uptime and administrative productivity.
In the physical economy, companies can measure AI’s value in cost per mile, vehicle uptime, accident rates, fuel consumption, maintenance expenses and labor productivity. Those metrics create a more direct connection between technology investments and business outcomes than many early generative AI productivity applications have demonstrated.
Agents could potentially extend those benefits by reducing the time and human intervention required to resolve problems once detected.
From blue-collar operations to AI-augmented knowledge work
Another important theme from my conversation with Joof was how AI could transform the role of frontline workers.
Much of the AI debate has focused on replacing white-collar jobs. But physical AI offers a different narrative: using intelligence to augment people operating vehicles, machinery and industrial equipment.
A driver who previously had to rely on personal experience or contact a supervisor can now receive contextual guidance from an AI assistant. A fleet manager who previously spent hours reviewing alerts and contacting drivers can increasingly focus on exceptions, higher-value decisions and operational improvements.
This creates an interesting shift in the nature of frontline work. AI can make specialized knowledge more accessible at the point of activity, potentially improving productivity and safety while reducing repetitive administrative demands.
The objective isn’t necessarily removing the human from the process. It’s changing where human judgment is applied. Agents will need clear operating policies, reliable escalation mechanisms, transparency and human accountability. The industry has considerable work ahead in demonstrating how autonomous systems can operate safely and predictably in the physical world.
The bigger industry shift: Systems of intelligence become systems of action
The Motive launch connects to a larger thesis we’ve been developing around the evolution of enterprise computing and systems of intelligence.
Traditional systems of record were designed to capture business information. Systems of engagement improved how people interact with that information. Systems of intelligence introduced AI-powered analysis, context and recommendations.
Now agentic AI is adding an execution layer. Instead of merely showing managers what happened or recommending what they should do, AI systems can initiate the next operational step within defined business policies.
Motive provides a concrete example of this evolution in the physical economy. The company’s early approach is relatively constrained: Customers define triggers and actions, while AI interprets operational conditions and assists in executing the workflow.
The longer-term roadmap moves toward goal-oriented agents that determine how to achieve business outcomes. That’s a much bigger architectural transition, and it introduces important questions about governance, explainability, human oversight and accountability.
But the strategic opportunity is clear. The competitive advantage in enterprise agentic AI may increasingly come from the combination of domain-specific data, real-time context and the ability to execute reliable actions.
Foundation models will continue improving. But the models themselves are only part of the value chain. The systems that understand a business’s unique operating environment and can take appropriate action may ultimately capture more durable value.
For Motive, its integrated hardware, software and AI strategy provides a foundation for pursuing that opportunity. The challenge now is proving that Agents deliver incremental improvements in operational outcomes while maintaining the reliability required for physical-world applications.
Bottom line
The bigger story isn’t another AI agent entering the market. It’s the emergence of a new operating model where intelligence becomes an active participant in how physical businesses function.
For Motive, the opportunity is to turn years of investment in edge computing, computer vision and operational data into a system that not only understands what’s happening but can coordinate what happens next. The competitive test will be whether that integration produces measurable improvements beyond conventional automation — fewer accidents, lower downtime, better asset utilization and greater operating leverage.
My takeaway: The physical economy could become one of the most compelling proving grounds for agentic AI because the outcomes are tangible, the economics are measurable and the consequences of execution are immediate.
The next wave of AI value won’t be measured by how many agents companies deploy, but by how much operational friction they eliminate and how effectively intelligence translates into real-world outcomes.

articles.title: The Commodore C64's spiritual godson surfaces on HP's online store — EliteBoard G2a brings 'Gorgon Point' Ryzen AI 7 Pro APUs to a novel form factor with a battery and an eye-watering $4,200 price tag
articles.text:
The Commodore C64's spiritual godson surfaces on HP's online store — EliteBoard G2a brings 'Gorgon Point' Ryzen AI 7 Pro APUs to a novel form factor with a battery and an eye-watering $4,200 price tag
A Commodore 64 cost $595 in 1982
- HP has quietly listed the EliteBoard G2a keyboard PC in the US and UK, from $3,028 to $4,191 for the Ryzen AI 7 PRO 450 model with a 32Wh battery
- The underlying AMD Gorgon Point refresh adds just 100MHz over the G1a's Ryzen AI 7 PRO 350, with identical cores, cache, Radeon 860M graphics, and a 50 TOPS NPU
- Entry-level pricing has roughly doubled since the G1a's $1,499 debut as DRAM costs soar and HP's PC shipments fall 30.9% year over year
HP has slipped a second-generation keyboard PC onto its web store with remarkably little fanfare.
The EliteBoard G2a appeared on HP's US and UK sites around nine months after the EliteBoard G1a's CES 2026 unveiling, and we couldn't find a press release to go with it.
The top configuration, listed as the E6FY3UA SKU, pairs AMD's Ryzen AI 7 PRO 450 with 32GB of DDR5-5600, a 512GB SSD, a 32Wh battery, and a detachable USB-C cable, and costs $4,191 before discounts, or $4,167 with the cable attached.
A hard-to-resist Commodore comparison for an EliteBoard G1A with slightly better silicon
A Commodore comparison is hard to resist when it comes to the EliteBoard G2a. The C64 also made its debut at CES in Las Vegas in January 1982, packed a whole computer under its keys, and borrowed someone else's screen, usually the family TV. It went on sale that August for $595, roughly $2,000 in today's money, and the Computer History Museum still ranks it as the best-selling computer model of all time.
HP's flagship G2a costs about seven times the C64's launch price, around double its inflation-adjusted price, and carries roughly half a million times its 64KB of RAM and, somewhat unimpressively, on a single stick.
The G2a is essentially the G1a, which TechRadar Pro recently covered, but with one small caveat: it has a slightly faster APU under the hood. The underlying chip is AMD's Gorgon Point silicon, part of the Ryzen AI 400 family AMD launched at CES, and it's a mild upgrade over the G1a's configuration, coming with only a 100 MHz boost.
The chip also supports faster LPDDR5X-8533 memory, but that's moot here, since the EliteBoard uses DDR5-5600 SO-DIMMs in a single-channel configuration.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The keyboard-cum computer also carries over the same fatal memory limitations that the G1a has: a single 32GB SO-DIMM memory stick that limits bandwidth by running in single-channel mode. This would affect on-device AI performance and general compute needs, as the APU's iGPU and NPU use the same memory for localized models.
This hasn't stopped HP from leaning on novelty, however; At CES, the company pitched the G1a as the first complete AI PC ever to live inside a keyboard, with Guayente Sanmartin, president of HP's commercial systems and displays division, promising "next-generation local AI power in a keyboard-sized form factor."
A footnote ironically does the heavy lifting here: the claim covers only keyboard-chassis PCs with an NPU rated at 40 TOPS or more plus enterprise-grade CPU, memory, storage and I/O, a definition that neatly rules out every keyboard computer that came before.
There were plenty of such candidates; beyond the C64 and the Amiga 500, which TechRadar's CES coverage also invoked, Asus announced the Atom-powered Eee Keyboard at CES 2009 and later sold it in the US for $499, a device our coverage once called "one of the most bizarre concepts for a computer we have ever seen."
The G2a also seems to be the victim of a deepening memory crisis that has driven prices up, even as its sibling, the G1a, has a starting price of $1,499 that is no longer in play, with much higher MSRPs being displayed (then cut down by discounts) by HP.
The G2a is a solid computer despite its limitations and eye-watering price tag at the high end. It might, however, see better business discounts than retail pricing that could make it an easier choice for some IT managers.
However, when performance matters and suitable Nvidia RTX Spark, DGX Spark, and AMD Strix Halo alternatives are cheaper and faster for the same money, it may be a hard sell unless the discounts are substantially higher.

articles.title: Apple hosting 'Pro and Tell' event on October 28
articles.text:
Apple announced its new ‘Pro and Tell’ event in LA on October 28 at 10 a.m. PT/1 p.m. ET. The Pro and Tell event takes place one week after the company’s ‘welcome home‘ presentation, where the company announced several smart home products.
We expect to see the new MacBook Pro at the event, which will have the first-ever touchscreen on a MacBook. The touchscreen OLED will reportedly be lighter and sport an iPhone-like Dynamic Island. Reportedly, this will feature an M6 chip introduced in the Mac Mini.
Although this is considered the ‘Pro and Tell’ event, maybe we’ll see a new iPad Pro, which got a revamp this time last year. Or even a new Vision Pro, which also saw a revamp last year. Although that’s just speculation based on the ‘Pro and Tell’ naming.
Other actual rumours also indicate there will be an entry-level MacBook Pro and an M6 iMac. The other product that’s rumoured is the OLED iPad Mini, which will reportedly have a front-facing camera on the landscape side, with a revamped speaker system.
Bloomberg‘s Mark Gurman said that the OLED MacBook Pro could launch as soon as November 6.

articles.title: Mit deutschen Sensoren zum Mars: Was Technik aus Jena zur japanischen Mission beiträgt
articles.text:
Japans Marsmission: So sollen Sensoren aus Deutschland zum Erfolg beitragen
Eine japanische Raumsonde mit dem deutsch-französischen Rover „Idefix“ ist Richtung Mars aufgebrochen – und Sensoren aus Jena helfen ihr beim Navigieren im All. Zwei Stern-Sensoren des Thüringer Raumfahrtunternehmens Jena-Optronik sollen die Raumsonde zu den Marsmonden Phobos und Deimos geleiten. Sie tragen nach Unternehmensangaben zur exakten Ausrichtung und Navigation des Raumschiffs bei.
Jena-Optronik war nach eigenen Angaben ein wichtiger Zulieferer für die Mitsubishi Electric Corporation bei dem Projekt. Die Stern-Sensoren seien Teil des Lage- und Bahnsteuerungssystems. Die Rakete mit der Sonde und den Sensoren aus Jena war in der Nacht erfolgreich von Japans Weltraumbahnhof Tanegashima abgehoben.
Sensoren als „Auge“ beim Navigieren
Die Stern-Sensoren von Jena-Optronik, die Optik mit Bildverarbeitung kombinieren und Sterne zur Orientierung nutzen, gehören zu den grundlegenden optischen Navigationssystemen in der Raumfahrt. Sie dienten quasi als Auges des Lageregulierungssystems der Raumsonde, so das Unternehmen.
Auf dem Marsmond Phobos soll ein vom Deutschen Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt (DLR) und der französischen Raumfahrtbehörde CNES entworfener Rover im Jahr 2029 aufsetzen. 2031 sollen dann mit einem Rückkehrmodul erstmals Proben von Phobos zur Erde gebracht werden.
Die Sensoren, die nur wenig Strom verbrauchten, erfassen nach Angaben von Jena-Optronik das die Sonde umgebende Sternenfeld und vergleichen es augenblicklich mit einem integrierten Sternenkatalog, um die exakte Ausrichtung des Flugkörpers im Raum zu bestimmen. Auch wissenschaftliche Instrumente seien auf eine sehr präzise Ausrichtung angewiesen, um genaue Daten von den Oberflächen der Marsmonde zu erfassen.
Jenaer Technik bei vielen Weltraummissionen dabei
Stern-Sensoren aus Jena hatten in diesem Jahr bereits bei der in den USA gestarteten Artemis-Mission zum Mond eine Rolle gespielt.
Jena-Optronik hat eine lange Tradition bei der Produktion von Systemen zur Lageregulierung von Satelliten, aber auch Raumschiffen. Diese geht bis in die DDR-Zeit zurück. Stern- sowie Rendezvous- und Dockingsensoren aus Jena waren bereits bei einer Vielzahl von Weltraummissionen dabei. Das Unternehmen hat nach eigenen Angaben bisher mehr als 450 Lageregelungssensoren verkauft, die weltweit in nationalen und internationalen Projekten eingesetzt werden. Jena-Optronik ist eine Tochter von Airbus Defence and Space.

articles.title: Walmart's Flipkart is quietly building a food delivery challenger in India | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Flipkart, the Walmart-owned Indian e-commerce giant, is preparing to challenge India’s food-delivery duopoly of Zomato and Swiggy. It is entering a fiercely competitive market that has defeated even previous attempts by Amazon and Google to break in.
The Bengaluru-based company is testing its food-delivery service internally and has expanded the trial from a few hundred employees to upwards of 8,000, according to two people familiar with the matter. It has also deployed a dedicated fleet of riders through its logistics arm, Ekart, separate from the riders who handle its quick-commerce deliveries, as it prepares for a public launch.
The employee-only service appears as a separate tab on Flipkart’s main shopping app, alongside its Minutes quick-commerce offering and travel bookings, TechCrunch has learned. It draws on restaurants listed through ONDC, a government-backed network that connects online buyers and sellers across different platforms, as well as restaurants that Flipkart signed up directly.
Riders wearing jerseys bearing the “Eat-in by Minutes” branding have also begun fulfilling orders on the streets of Bengaluru, the southern Indian city where Flipkart is headquartered.
As Flipkart expands its food-delivery operations, it is entering a market that the brokerage firm Bernstein estimates is growing 18% to 20% a year. Online delivery, though, still accounts for just over 15% of India’s broader food-services industry. Zomato, owned by Eternal, and Swiggy together serve an estimated 85 million to 95 million paying customers a year, per Bernstein. That figure shows how dominant the two are, and how much room newcomers have to grow online food ordering in the world’s most populous country, which has more than a billion internet subscriptions.
Flipkart is not the only company trying to shake up India’s food-delivery market. Ride-hailing company Rapido, which has already given Uber and its Indian rival Ola a tough fight, has been expanding Ownly, its food-delivery service that charges restaurants zero commission. Meanwhile, Swiggy has launched Toing, a separate app aimed at customers looking for cheaper meals. Both moves reflect growing pressure on the industry’s existing pricing model and the commissions that restaurants pay.
“Monopoly is bad, but duopoly is more pathetic,” said Sagar Daryani, president of the New Delhi-headquartered National Restaurant Association of India, which represents over 500,000 restaurants nationwide. “What one does, the other follows suit.”
Daryani argued that restaurants have long needed alternatives to the two dominant platforms.
Flipkart is not the first deep-pocketed company to try breaking into India’s food-delivery market. In 2020, Amazon launched a food-ordering service in Bengaluru, but it shut the service down two years later. Google’s Areo app, which offered food ordering alongside other services, also failed to gain traction. Uber also left the market in 2020, selling its Uber Eats business in India to Zomato.
Daryani sees one important difference between Flipkart and the companies that tried food delivery before it. Zomato and Swiggy built their businesses around delivering meals before expanding into quick commerce. Flipkart is doing the reverse, using its established e-commerce business and growing quick-commerce operations as a springboard into food delivery.
“Flipkart’s quick commerce benefit will get passed on to food delivery, so it will be leaner, more efficient,” Daryani told TechCrunch.
Restaurants are also hoping that new entrants will bring down the cost of selling meals online. Daryani, also co-founder and CEO of the dumpling chain Wow! Momo Foods, said Flipkart has proposed a base commission of about 10%, compared with the 20% to 25% that restaurants typically pay Zomato and Swiggy.
Commissions are only part of the expense, though. Once advertising, discounts, and other promotional costs are factored in, restaurants can end up spending 40% to 50% of an order’s value on the established platforms, Daryani told TechCrunch. He expects Flipkart to keep that total cost closer to 15% to 16%, which could mean restaurants keep more money from each order.
Nonetheless, getting restaurants on board is one thing and winning over customers is another. Bernstein estimates that new entrants could save customers just ₹20 to ₹30 (around 20–30 cents) per order by operating more efficiently, which may not be enough to draw customers away from Zomato and Swiggy. The two incumbents could also offer deeper discounts to keep them.
Flipkart is not planning to stay in Bengaluru for long. The company has told restaurants that it expects to launch its food-delivery service publicly by the end of October and to expand to five or six cities by the end of this year, Daryani told TechCrunch.
The food-delivery push also comes as Flipkart’s long-awaited stock-market listing remains uncertain. Chief Executive Kalyan Krishnamurthy (pictured above) recently declined to give a timetable for an IPO, even as the company continues to expand into businesses that could bring customers back to its app more frequently.
Flipkart’s expansion comes as competition in India’s e-commerce market intensifies. Quick-commerce platforms that started by delivering groceries in minutes now sell even the latest iPhones and other discretionary purchases, putting them in more direct competition with Flipkart and Amazon.
Flipkart did not respond to a request for comments.

articles.title: Accused OpenAI spy had folder called “Saudi Gov Docs,” FBI says
articles.text:
On Monday, a court granted the US government’s request to deny release of a former OpenAI engineer accused of bugging a top-secret conference room to steal the frontier lab’s secrets.
In a court filing Sunday, US attorney Craig Missakian argued that Abdulrahman Alfozan must continue to be detained while the US makes its case that Alfozan brazenly spied on OpenAI, either for his own personal business gain or to benefit the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
Evidence showed that Alfozan had been chatting with a member of the KSA royal family on WhatsApp, while pursuing opportunities to permanently move back to Saudi Arabia during the country’s biggest AI push yet, the government argued. Shortly before his arrest, the FBI found he accessed a folder called “Saudi Gov Docs” on his iPhone, where he also allegedly stored photos of a second bug he planted in the offices.
With so much evidence against him, Alfozan—a Saudi national and US permanent legal resident—is a flight risk with seemingly endless support from the Saudi government, Missakian alleged.
The FBI arrested Alfozan days before he could hop a plane, Missakian said. The US attorney noted that Alfozan had already booked a one-way ticket for him, his wife, and their baby to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia’s capital. That ticket was allegedly “paid for by the Saudi government.” Following his arrest, his wife and son booked a sooner flight and immediately left the US without him. Once again, the US found “a member of the Saudi military booked and paid for yet another one-way ticket for the defendant’s wife and son, this one business class to Doha, Qatar.”
After receiving “significant compensation from a decade of high-tech employment in the Bay Area,” Alfozan has “ample resources” to run away to Saudi Arabia, the US government alleged. He also has “at least two bank accounts in Saudi Arabia,” the government said.
To support their request to detain Alfozan, the government pointed to a case where former Twitter employees were charged with spying for the Saudi government. Charges are still pending against one of the ex-Twitter staffers, Ali Alzabarah, the US said, partly because “a Saudi foreign official” helped “coordinate a next-day flight to Saudi Arabia” shortly after Twitter confronted him.

articles.title: TP-Link and Key Tronic Sign Letter of Intent to Bring Router Assembly to the United States
articles.text:
Monday, October 19th 2026
TP-Link and Key Tronic Sign Letter of Intent to Bring Router Assembly to the United States
TP-Link Systems Inc., a global leader in networking and smart home solutions, today announced that it has entered into a Letter of Intent (LOI) with Key Tronic Corp., a premier U.S.-based electronics manufacturer, to bring next-generation product assembly to the United States. The LOI is a significant step in California-based TP-Link's long-term commitment to expand domestic manufacturing and strengthen supply chain resilience within the U.S.
Under the LOI, the parties intend for Key Tronic to become a primary domestic manufacturing partner for TP-Link, supporting assembly of the company's advanced networking portfolio in Corinth, Mississippi. Pending U.S. regulatory approval, TP-Link expects domestic assembly of its groundbreaking Wi-Fi 8 home networking product line to begin as early as next year. The partnership is part of TP-Link's long-term effort to accelerate U.S. investment in high-tech manufacturing and job creation, designing and assembling next-generation products for American consumers here on American soil."This LOI with Key Tronic demonstrates our firm commitment to expanding domestic advanced manufacturing, and establishing America as our base for delivering secure, reliable connectivity solutions to households and businesses around the world," said Jeffrey Chao, Chief Executive Officer of TP-Link Systems Inc. "By choosing to assemble cutting-edge products here at home, we are thrilled to support U.S. high-tech job growth and empower a new generation of American innovation and innovators."
"Key Tronic is proud to partner with TP-Link as it expands its commitment to domestic manufacturing and works to bring high-tech networking assembly back to American soil," said Brett Larsen, President and Chief Executive Officer of Key Tronic. "Our production footprint will give TP-Link a strong domestic foundation, and our experience in high-reliability electronics manufacturing will help support the company's new generation of Wi-Fi 8 technologies."
The LOI with Key Tronic represents an important milestone in TP-Link's U.S. investment roadmap and its commitment to building a resilient and secure domestic manufacturing operation. This is the beginning of TP-Link's next chapter, one defined by American investment, jobs, and innovation.
Source:
				TP-Link

articles.title: Face à Starlink, Orange et les géants européens s’allient pour connecter directement nos smartphones par satellite
articles.text:
L’heure est aux grandes manœuvres dans les télécoms en Europe. Dans un communiqué commun publié ce lundi 19 octobre 2026, les quatre plus gros opérateurs de téléphonie mobile du Vieux Continent s’associent pour aller chercher des fréquences satellite : l’Allemand Deutsche Telekom, le Français Orange, l’Espagnol Telefónica et le Britannique Vodafone.
En l’espèce, ils annoncent avoir signé une lettre d’intention pour étudier une candidature commune dans le cadre de « l’attribution de fréquences destinées aux services mobiles par satellite et accélérer les services Direct-to-Device » (D2D). On parle donc ici de la connexion directe d’un téléphone mobile à un satellite, sans appareil intermédiaire.
Pour un abonné, cela voudrait dire que son smartphone accrocherait encore du réseau dans une vallée sans antenne-relais à proximité, ou après le passage d’une tempête ayant détruit les installations au sol. Le Direct-to-Cell est d’ailleurs une déclinaison du D2D, pour connecter des smartphones 4G/5G sans passer par des infrastructures terrestres.
Comme toute liaison sans fil, elle passe par des ondes radio : il faut donc lui réserver des fréquences bien précises. En l’espèce, les fréquences en jeu se trouvent dans la bande des 2 GHz, la même dans toute l’Union européenne. Une bande décrite comme « idéale » par la Commission européenne.
Deux entreprises américaines, Viasat et EchoStar, détiennent les droits d’exploitation de cette bande depuis 2009 (initialement, c’était la société britannique Inmarsat qui en possédait une partie, mais elle a été rachetée en 2023 par Viasat). Ces autorisations expirent en mai 2027, dans sept mois.
En amont de cette remise en jeu, Bruxelles a proposé en mai 2026 de revoir le découpage de cette bande. Son projet actuel est de couper la bande en trois parts égales : la première reviendrait aux usages gouvernementaux et militaires, la deuxième serait réservée aux nouveaux entrants européens tandis que la troisième serait ouverte à tous (européens ou non).
Dans cette configuration, le premier bloc permettrait à la future constellation IRIS² (Infrastructure for Resilience, Interconnectivity and Security by Satellite) d’avoir ses fréquences réservées, afin de favoriser l’émergence d’un réseau satellitaire souverain, pour ne pas dépendre d’un Starlink. Les premiers satellites sont attendus en 2029.
Des antennes au sol, des satellites loués
Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica et Vodafone ne prévoient pas de lancer leur propre constellation. Les satellites viendraient d’un partenaire tiers qu’il faudra encore choisir. Les quatre opérateurs construiraient en Europe les infrastructures au sol, puis coordonneraient et superviseraient le réseau.
Le communiqué précise que le service serait ensuite vendu en gros à tous les opérateurs mobiles, de manière « ouverte et non discriminatoire ». En France, cela veut dire que Bouygues Telecom ou Free pourraient donc, en théorie, le proposer à leurs propres abonnés. SFR aussi, sur le papier, mais il doit être vendu à la découpe prochainement.
L’annonce des quatre opérateurs ne mentionne pas Starlink, qui est à la tête d’une immense constellation satellitaire et qui procède à des achats de fréquences. Starlink a d’ailleurs lancé sa propre offre, Starlink Mobile, qui permet une liaison téléphonique via l’espace.
Selon le Financial Times, c’est pourtant bien pour faire face à Starlink que les quatre groupes se sont rapprochés. Il faut en effet relever que SpaceX a racheté les droits d’EchoStar sur cette bande. Or, selon Light Reading, le projet européen l’obligerait à refaire une demande de licence, sur la seule part ouverte aux acteurs non européens.
S’il est question de renforcer « la souveraineté, la sécurité et la résilience de l’Europe » dans le communiqué des opérateurs, ils défendent aussi leur relation avec leurs clients. Un SpaceX vendant une connexion satellite directement aux possesseurs de smartphones, c’est un Orange qui ne contrôlerait plus tout à fait la couverture de ses abonnés dans les zones sans réseau.
En pleine crise Starlink en Ukraine
Mais ce n’est pas tout : le Financial Times évoque aussi des « menaces » américaines à l’endroit de l’Europe en cas de « restrictions sur Starlink ».
Selon le correspondant du FT en Ukraine, les entreprises européennes risquent des représailles « dévastatrices » de Washington si Bruxelles persiste dans ses projets de restreindre l’accès de rivaux américains tels que SpaceX à certaines parties du marché européen. L’avertissement est venu de l’ambassadeur des États-Unis auprès de l’UE.
Difficile à ce stade de savoir si cela aura un effet sur les plans bruxellois en matière de réorganisation du spectre. La séquence arrive cependant pile au moment où l’Europe voit à quel point elle dépend de SpaceX. Les bridages de connectivité observés ces derniers jours en Ukraine ne plaident pas en faveur de Starlink.
Mi-octobre, des responsables ukrainiens ont accusé l’entreprise d’avoir bridé sans prévenir Starshield, la version militaire de Starlink. Selon eux, cela a gêné l’interception de drones russes. Elon Musk a rejeté la responsabilité sur le gouvernement américain, ce que Donald Trump a démenti le 16 octobre. Depuis, une certaine confusion règne.
Sur Telegram, ce 20 octobre, Volodymyr Zelensky a indiqué avoir échangé avec le secrétaire d’État américain Marco Rubio sur Starlink, notamment, en vue de son plein rétablissement. La veille, le président ukrainien indiquait que le réseau satellitaire était toujours bridé dans plusieurs zones du front. Selon lui, ce bridage viserait à lui mettre la pression.
Le 16 octobre, le quotidien britannique The Telegraph a affirmé que c’est bien Elon Musk, patron de SpaceX, qui a proposé ces limitations à Donald Trump, selon quatre sources proches de ces sujets. D’après l’une d’elles, le président américain a bien donné son accord, ce qui a abouti à la mise en œuvre de ces restrictions par le Pentagone.
L’utilisation politique de Starlink, qui a été dénoncée en Europe, repose la question de la place de ce réseau dans les communications de certains pays. Au Canada, en froid avec les États-Unis, le Premier ministre Mark Carney veut ainsi détacher son pays de ce réseau américain.
En Europe, rien ne se jouera avant plusieurs années. À ce stade, la lettre d’intention n’engage pas encore les quatre groupes. Elle ne remplace pas non plus les accords déjà signés, comme celui de Vodafone avec l’Américain AST SpaceMobile. Si le règlement européen passe tel quel, les fréquences seront attribuées en 2029.

articles.title: OVHcloud : un pirate a glissé un logiciel espion dans plusieurs versions de son outil en ligne de commande officiel
articles.text:
Hier, si vous avez installé l’outil en ligne de commande d’OVHcloud depuis GitHub entre 14h47 et 16h21, alors vous avez récupéré un programme conçu pour fouiller votre disque à la recherche de secrets. Et effacer l’exécutable ne vous protège pas, il faut changer toutes les clés stockées sur la machine.
Six semaines après avoir décroché la qualification SecNumCloud pour son cloud public, OVHcloud a subi une attaque par la chaîne d’approvisionnement. Le pirate n’est jamais entré dans ses centres de données. Il a piégé ovhcloud, l’outil avec lequel développeurs et administrateurs pilotent leurs serveurs depuis un terminal, et les utilisateurs ont récupéré le fichier vérolé sur les pages officielles du projet. « La version CLI de 14h47 a été compromise par un hacker », a prévenu Octave Klaba, fondateur d’OVHcloud, sur son compte X. Cinq versions, de la 0.11.0 à la 0.15.0, sont concernées, mais la méthode d’installation compte davantage que le numéro de version pour savoir si vous êtes exposé.
Des fichiers remplacés des semaines après leur publication
Le pirate n’a touché ni au code source ni à la chaîne de compilation. Octave Klaba évoque le compte GitHub « d’un des développeurs ». D’après la chronologie reconstituée par OpenSourceMalware, ce compte appartient à un contributeur de la documentation d’OVHcloud, doté des droits d’écriture sur le dépôt de l’outil. En 25 minutes, le pirate a supprimé puis remplacé les archives de cinq versions publiées entre avril et septembre. Il a ensuite changé le fichier checksums.txt, avec lequel l’utilisateur contrôle l’intégrité d’un téléchargement, pour que les empreintes collent aux binaires piégés. L’attaquant a profité de deux faiblesses. Tout compte doté des droits d’écriture pouvait modifier les fichiers d’une version publiée, et aucune empreinte n’était contrôlée lors de l’installation par le script officiel.
Un client d’OVHcloud avait heureusement fixé, dans sa chaîne d’intégration, l’empreinte SHA-256 de l’archive Linux pour processeurs ARM, et il a vu ses compilations échouer dès le remplacement du fichier. Il a alerté OVHcloud par un signalement public sur le dépôt. Les équipes d’OVHcloud ont effacé les fichiers à 16h21, puis publié une version 0.16.0 signée, dont les fichiers ne peuvent plus être modifiés. « Cette version est immuable, donc les fichiers qui y sont attachés sont fiables », a écrit l’un des mainteneurs de l’outil dans la discussion.
Selon OpenSourceMalware, le pirate contrôlait le compte du contributeur depuis au moins le 5 mars. Ce jour-là, quatre de ses dépôts personnels ont reçu un chargeur écrit en caractères Unicode invisibles. Le portefeuille Solana qui le pilote apparaît dans les listes d’indicateurs de GlassWorm. Repérés en octobre 2025 dans des extensions de l’éditeur VS Code, ces pirates volent les identifiants des développeurs puis réutilisent ces accès pour piéger d’autres logiciels. Les auteurs du ver Miasma, dont l’arsenal complet traîne en libre accès sur GitHub depuis juin, avaient rebondi vers d’autres projets avec les identifiants volés après avoir infecté des paquets npm publiés sous le compte de Red Hat. Les chercheurs ne peuvent toutefois pas prouver que le pirate de mars a lui aussi remplacé les fichiers en octobre.
- money_offRemboursement 30 jours
- securityCertificat SSL inclus
- install_desktopCompatible WordPress
Les installations concernées et les clés à changer
Si vous avez installé ou mis à jour l’outil entre 14h47 et 16h21 avec le script officiel ou avec Homebrew, vous êtes concerné. Vous êtes tout autant exposé si vous avez récupéré l’archive à la main sur GitHub à ces horaires, ou si vos chaînes d’intégration l’ont fait à votre place. D’après OpenSourceMalware, les développeurs qui ont compilé l’outil à partir du code source ou avec la commande go install n’ont rien à craindre, et l’image Docker d’OVHcloud, fabriquée en interne, n’a pas été touchée. Une installation antérieure à 14h47, sans mise à jour l’après-midi, ne pose pas de problème.
Un doute sur l’exécutable installé sur votre machine ? La commande ovhcloud version affiche le numéro de la version, par exemple v0.15.0, sur un fichier officiel, contrairement au fichier vérolé. Si Go est installé sur votre poste, la commande go version -m appliquée au fichier fait apparaître la mention « dirty » sur la copie piégée.
« La qualité du binaire est médiocre mais il peut aller jusqu’au bout », a averti Octave Klaba, qui demande aux personnes concernées de changer tous les secrets stockés sur leur disque. OpenSourceMalware cite en particulier vos clés d’API OVHcloud, le fichier de configuration ovh.conf, vos clés SSH et vos accès Kubernetes. Changez-les depuis un autre ordinateur, avant de supprimer l’exécutable et d’installer la version 0.16.0. Dans une PME, un développeur garde parfois sur son ordinateur les clés de tous les serveurs de production, et le pirate qui les a copiées peut encore s’en servir tant que vous ne les avez pas révoquées.
OVHcloud a promis un post-mortem détaillé sous quelques jours. Le client à l’origine de l’alerte attend de savoir si le compte piraté pouvait aussi pousser du code ou créer des étiquettes de version sur le dépôt.

articles.title: 5 Quotes from the book It Matters a Lot by Shubhra Saxena
articles.text:
5 Quotes from the book It Matters a Lot by Shubhra Saxena
Explore five thought-provoking quotes from Shubhra Saxena’s It Matters A Lot on success, happiness, ambition and finding meaning in life.
We spend much of our lives working towards milestones that society considers important. Degrees, careers, financial security, relationships and recognition often become measures of success.
But what happens when we achieve these goals and still feel that something is missing? This is one of the central questions explored in It Matters A Lot by Shubhra Saxena, an IAS officer and author. Published by Rupa Publications, the book examines identity, ambition, happiness, relationships, failure and the experiences that shape how we understand ourselves.
Rather than prescribing a universal formula for a meaningful life, Saxena encourages readers to question their assumptions and reflect on what genuinely matters to them.
5 Thought-provoking quotes from the book
1. “Because you can tick every box and still miss your own life.”
This line captures the central message of It Matters A Lot. We often follow a familiar checklist for success, pursuing educational qualifications, professional achievements, financial stability and personal milestones without stopping to question whether these goals reflect our own desires.
The problem is not ambition itself. Working towards something meaningful can bring satisfaction and purpose. However, when our goals are shaped entirely by external expectations, we may lose sight of what makes us happy.
Saxena invites readers to consider whether they are building a life that feels right to them or simply one that looks successful to everyone else.
The lesson: Achievement and fulfilment are not always the same. A meaningful life begins with understanding what success means to you.
2. “You can tick every box and still feel like something is missing.”
This line explores the gap between outward success and inner contentment. A person may have a stable career, a comfortable lifestyle and relationships that appear ideal, yet still struggle to understand why they feel unfulfilled.
Such feelings can arise when we pursue goals without examining the reasons behind them. We may believe that the next promotion, purchase or milestone will finally bring happiness, only to discover that the feeling does not last.
It Matters A Lot encourages readers to look beyond achievements and examine their emotional needs, values and expectations.
The lesson: Before chasing another milestone, pause and ask yourself what you hope it will bring into your life. Sometimes, understanding that desire matters more than achieving the goal.
3. “What happens when everything looks right and still doesn't feel enough?”
This question reflects a familiar struggle in a world that encourages constant comparison. Social media, professional competition and cultural expectations can make us feel that we are falling behind, even when we have made meaningful progress.
The difficulty is that there is always another achievement to pursue and another person against whom to measure ourselves. If our satisfaction depends entirely on reaching the next milestone, contentment can remain perpetually out of reach.
Saxena's book encourages readers to reconsider these expectations and develop a more personal understanding of happiness and fulfilment.
The lesson: You do not have to keep pursuing every goal that society celebrates. Learning to recognise what is enough for you can be just as important as striving for more.
4. “Why do we seek approval?”
The desire for approval can influence our decisions more than we realise. From choosing a career to navigating relationships, we may find ourselves prioritising other people's opinions over our own judgement.
Seeking acceptance is a natural human experience. Problems arise when external validation becomes the primary measure of our worth. We may begin making decisions to avoid criticism rather than to pursue what genuinely matters to us.
By encouraging readers to examine their beliefs and motivations, It Matters A Lot opens the door to greater self-awareness and more conscious choices.
The lesson: Other people's opinions can offer useful perspectives, but they do not have to determine the direction of your life. Understanding your values can help you make decisions with greater confidence.
5. “What are we really looking for in love, ambition, happiness, and success?”
These questions bring together several of the themes explored throughout It Matters A Lot. We often pursue different things without examining what we expect them to provide.
We may seek success because we want security, relationships because we want connection, or recognition because we want to feel valued. Yet the things we pursue and the needs we hope to fulfil are not always the same.
Taking time to understand these motivations can help us recognise unhelpful patterns and make choices that better reflect our priorities.
The lesson: Self-awareness begins when we become curious about our own desires. Asking honest questions can help us understand not only what we want, but why we want it.
Final thoughts
It Matters A Lot by Shubhra Saxena invites readers to reconsider the assumptions that shape their understanding of a successful and meaningful life. Its central message is that achievements alone cannot determine whether we feel fulfilled.
Through questions about identity, ambition, relationships and happiness, the book encourages readers to pause and reflect on the lives they are building.
Perhaps the most important question is not whether we have achieved everything we once wanted, but whether the life we are living reflects what truly matters to us.

Points forts
- Écran bien calibré et très lumineux.
- Présence du Snapdragon 8 Elite.
- Volet photo complet.
- Excellente autonomie.
- Expérience One UI 7.
Points faibles
- Design déjà vu.
- Téléobjectif assez décevant.
- Charge limitée à 25 W en 2025 !?
Alors oui, ce Galaxy S25 a tout d’un S24 amélioré, mais le résultat est là : le millésime 2025 surpasse le précédent. Son format compact, son écran réussi et sa puce surpuissante et économe en énergie en font un modèle aussi fluide qu’endurant. L’expérience photo gagne en précision, même si tout n’est pas parfait, notamment du côté du téléobjectif. On peut aussi regretter une puissance de charge encore limitée par rapport à la concurrence. Cependant, l’expérience offerte par One UI 7 et les nombreuses fonctions d’IA apportent un vent de modernité. À moins de posséder le modèle de 2024, cette itération est donc hautement recommandable. Samsung prouve ici que dans la tech comme en amour, il ne faut pas se fier aux apparences, et que l’important, c’est ce qu’il y a à l’intérieur.

articles.title: 1 169 ch et une recharge en 12 minutes : Mercedes dévoile l'AMG GT SUV, un monstre prêt à atomiser les supercars
articles.text:
La branche sportive AMG de Mercedes continue à explorer des territoires inédits. Un an après avoir présenté son tout premier modèle électrique, l’AMG GT Coupé 4 Portes Électrique, elle enchaîne avec son premier SUV à batterie, l’AMG GT SUV. Si ce dernier se veut infiniment plus familial que la berline, il en conserve les principales caractéristiques, comme une recharge explosive et un surpuissant triplé de moteurs à flux axial.
Sur la version haute GT63, deux de ces machines électriques prennent ainsi place sur le train arrière alors que la troisième s’invite sur le train avant. En fonctionnant de concert, le trio développe 1 169 ch et 2 000 Nm de couple. C’est franchement beaucoup, et suffisant déjà pour abattre le 0 à 100 km/h en 2,7 secondes avant d’atteindre les 270 km/h en pointe. Est-ce bien raisonnable ? Le modèle intermédiaire GT55 tient lui aussi la dragée haute.
Jusqu’à 710 kW : la recharge la plus rapide du marché ?
Avec 816 ch, 1 860 Nm de couple et un 0 à 100 km/h enrhumé en 3,1 secondes, c’est tout aussi appréciable. Dans les deux cas, l’autonomie atteint les 700 km sur le cycle WLTP grâce à un pack de 128 kWh. L’entrée de gamme GT53 se limite pour sa part à deux machines électriques développant 544 ch et 800 Nm de couple pour un 0 à 100 km/h en 4,2 secondes. Toujours très bien, même si l’autonomie flanche à 668 km avec une batterie de 106 kWh.
La recharge est expéditive avec 600 kW en courant continu DC pour l’accumulateur de 106 kWh et 710 kW pour le pack de 128 kWh. De quoi gratter 380 km d’autonomie en 10 minutes dans le premier cas et 450 km dans le second. Notons que le chargeur embarqué bascule automatiquement entre les modes 800 V et 400 V selon les bornes. Commode pour sûr, mais pas réellement impressionnant.
Une suspension ultra-technologique qui se passe de barres antiroulis
Ce qui l’est davantage est l’inédit système de suspension nommé Active Ride Control+ associant des ressorts pneumatiques à trois niveaux à un réservoir de pression de 8,2 litres. Une interconnexion hydraulique se joint à l’ensemble, qui permet de se passer des traditionnelles barres antiroulis contrôlant habituellement le tangage et le roulis. On passera sur le style très particulier de l’engin de 5,08 mètres pour se focaliser sur l’aérodynamisme.
L’aileron de toit présent en série sur les GT55 et GT63 adapte sa position pour réduire la traînée au-delà de 150 km/h alors que des ailettes présentes sous la calandre s’ouvrent ou se ferment en fonction des besoins de refroidissement. Côté équipement, l’AMG GT SUV retient une sonorisation Burmester 4D, un toit panoramique opacifiant, des roues arrière directrices, des freins en céramique, un assistant vocal avec ChatGPT et plus encore.
Prix et disponibilité : à partir de quel tarif est-il proposé ?
La planche de bord est identique à celle de l’AMG GT 4 Portes Électrique avec une instrumentation numérique de 10,2 pouces, un écran multimédia central de 14 pouces et une troisième dalle côté passager de 14 pouces. Mercedes promet avoir particulièrement travaillé la position de conduite pour retranscrire les sensations d’une vraie voiture de sport. L’AMG GT SUV débute à 112 350 € en Allemagne.

La TCL 65C6K Pro de 65 pulgadas combina panel QD-MiniLED, tasa de refresco nativa de 144 Hz y sonido firmado por Onkyo. Ahora puedes conseguirla por 599 euros.
TV QD-Mini LED 65" - TCL 65C6K Pro, UHD 4K, TCL AiPQ Processor, Smart TV con Google TV, Dolby Vision-Atmos
Una tele de grandes dimensiones a precio reducido
Con un precio anterior de casi 800 euros, este modelo, que ahora cuesta 599 euros es una buena opción en relación calidad-precio dentro de su categoría. Esta tele destaca por su pantalla con tecnología QD-MiniLED (Quantum Dot + MiniLED) con resolución 4K UHD.
Gracias al asistente de atenuación local (Full Array Local Dimming), ofrece unos negros mucho más profundos, un contraste superior y un brillo pico excelente en comparación con los paneles LED tradicionales.
Es compatible con los principales formatos de rango dinámico, incluidos Dolby Vision IQ, HDR10+ y HLG, garantizando una calidad visual óptima tanto en películas como en series. En su interior alberga el procesador AiPQ Pro Processor, encargado de escalar contenidos de menor resolución mediante inteligencia artificial.
Para los aficionados a los videojuegos o al deporte en directo, equipa un panel con 144 Hz nativos e integra la suite de tecnologías Game Master Pro, con compatibilidad con HDMI 2.1, VRR (tasa de refresco variable) y ALLM (modo de baja latencia), ideal para exprimir al máximo consolas de última generación como Xbox Series X o PS5.
En el apartado sonoro, incluye un sistema 2.1 firmado por Onkyo y compatible con Dolby Atmos y DTS Virtual:X, ofreciendo una potencia y nitidez superiores a la media sin necesidad de añadir obligatoriamente una barra de sonido. articles.title: Fortanix extends Confidential AI to Kubernetes workloads through Confidential Containers - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Fortanix extends Confidential AI to Kubernetes workloads through Confidential Containers
Data security company Fortanix Inc. today extended its Fortanix Confidential AI platform to support the Cloud Native Computing Foundation’s Confidential Containers project, so enterprises can run artificial intelligence workloads on Kubernetes inside hardware-based trusted execution environments.
The release goes after the exposure that comes during inference, when model weights and the data fed to them have to be decrypted in processor memory. Privileged administrators and cloud operators with access to the infrastructure can potentially reach them at that point.
Fortanix published survey figures last week on how AI leaders view that risk. Atomik Research polled 300 of them at large U.S. companies on Fortanix’s behalf, and 93% said traditional encryption does not protect data while AI is processing it. Security concerns had led 41% to block a deployment completely.
Fortanix’s answer builds on Confidential Containers, which reached incubating status at the CNCF in July. The open-source plugins the company is writing for the project verify that a container is genuine before it gets anywhere near an encryption key. That check runs through Fortanix Confidential Computing Manager, which attests the CPU and GPU together so an inference job spanning both is covered in full.
The company’s Data Security Manager hands over the keys only if the result satisfies the customer’s security policy. They go nowhere but the protected environment.
Co-founder and Chief Executive Anand Kashyap said moving AI into containers “doesn’t change the threat,” since models and agents still touch a company’s most sensitive data while they run. With the plugins in place, deploying a container into a confidential computing environment takes one click on supported hardware and Kubernetes platforms.
Fortanix is pitching the update at regulated industries that need confidential AI to hold up in production. Key release runs on a cluster, so losing one server does not block it. Customers with sovereignty requirements can run the platform on-premises or fully air-gapped, and the company says that also lets an enterprise host a frontier lab’s proprietary model next to its own data without putting the lab’s intellectual property at risk.
“Attestation is a protocol. Trust is an operation,” said Anuj Jaiswal, Fortanix’s chief product officer. Having attestation and key management on one platform spares enterprises from building the trust layer themselves when they adopt standard Confidential Containers, he said.
Advanced Micro Devices Inc., Intel Corp. and CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. are among more than a dozen companies Fortanix lists as supporting the work. John Fanelli, vice president of enterprise software at Nvidia Corp., said Fortanix is building on open standards for attestation and secure key release “at production scale.” Nvidia and Fortanix launched a joint on-premises confidential AI platform last October.
Fortanix Confidential AI for Confidential Containers is available now. The company plans to demonstrate it on Nvidia GPUs with confidential computing enabled at Nvidia GTC Berlin, which runs Oct. 20-22.

articles.title: GitHub Actions Runner Controller 0.15.0 Targets Reliability at Scale
articles.text:
GitHub has released Actions Runner Controller (ARC) 0.15.0, introducing reliability, scalability, and observability improvements for organisations running self-hosted GitHub Actions runners on Kubernetes. The October 1 release focuses on reducing unnecessary Kubernetes API requests, improving controller throughput and making upgrades and shutdowns more predictable, particularly for environments managing large numbers of runner scale sets.
ARC is a Kubernetes operator that automatically scales self-hosted runners in response to workflow demand. It allows organisations to run their own execution infrastructure while creating and removing runner instances as jobs arrive and finish. This is particularly useful for enterprises that need control over build environments, network access, compute resources, or workload isolation without maintaining a permanently provisioned pool of runners.
One of the main themes in version 0.15.0 is reducing the work the controller performs to keep runner resources in sync. Controller updates now use Kubernetes patch requests instead of full update requests, reducing the size of API payloads. Runner status aggregation has also moved to metrics for EphemeralRunnerSet and AutoscalingRunnerSet, reducing the number of status updates sent to the Kubernetes API.
The controllers now filter incoming events to avoid unnecessary reconciliation, while listener API client rate limits can be configured through queries-per-second and burst settings. Teams can also configure reconciliation concurrency globally or for individual controllers using max-concurrent-reconciles flags. Together, these changes give platform teams more control over how ARC behaves under load and should help reduce avoidable processing and API traffic in larger deployments.
The release also addresses lifecycle management. Patch-version upgrades now update resources in place, maintaining a one-to-one mapping between autoscaling runner sets and ephemeral runner sets and reducing disruption during upgrades.
Controller shutdown behaviour has also been improved. The terminationGracePeriodSeconds setting is now configurable and aligned with the controller manager's graceful-shutdown timeout, allowing operators to better control how the controller exits during restarts or upgrades.
ARC can also re-register a runner scale set when its recorded counterpart no longer exists in the GitHub Actions service. This helps the controller recover from a mismatch between its local Kubernetes state and the scale-set state maintained by GitHub.
Finally, ephemeral runners can be deleted faster when their runner pods exit successfully because ARC skips an additional server-side check for runner removal. While individually small, these changes address the operational details that become increasingly important when runner environments are created and destroyed continuously.
Moving runner status aggregation into metrics is particularly relevant to teams operating ARC as shared CI infrastructure. Large runner fleets generate frequent lifecycle events as jobs are queued, runners are provisioned, workloads execute, and ephemeral environments are removed. Reducing status patches can ease pressure on the Kubernetes API, while metrics provide a more suitable basis for monitoring aggregate controller and runner behaviour.
Configurable reconciliation concurrency and listener rate limits also help operators tune the balance between throughput and API pressure. However, these settings are not simply performance switches: increasing concurrency can increase the rate at which the controller interacts with Kubernetes and GitHub services. Teams should therefore validate changes against their workload patterns and cluster capacity rather than assuming higher concurrency is always better.
ARC is part of a broader move towards dynamically managed CI execution infrastructure. CircleCI's Machine Runner Orchestrator, for example, focuses on scaling machine-based runners and supports different resource classes, including CPU, GPU, and ARM workloads. ARC instead integrates directly with Kubernetes to manage GitHub Actions runner scale sets, commonly using ephemeral runner environments. The two approaches address the same broad challenge, matching execution capacity to CI demand, but differ in their platform integration and runner execution models
For organisations already standardised on GitHub Actions and Kubernetes, ARC provides a native way to manage runner capacity alongside other cluster resources. Its trade-off is that platform teams must also operate the controller, manage Kubernetes capacity and understand how runner scaling interacts with cluster scheduling, API limits and workflow demand.
ARC 0.15.0 is an incremental release, but its emphasis reflects a significant engineering concern: once CI infrastructure serves many repositories and teams, controller efficiency and lifecycle reliability become delivery concerns in their own right.

articles.title: Criptomonedas: el precio de Bitcoin para este lunes
articles.text:
El bitcoin fue la primera criptomoneda que salió al mercado. Ideada por Satoshi Nakamoto en 2008, esta divisa digital promovía un ideal libertario y buscaba poner en jaque a las instituciones monetarias y financieras tradicionales luego de la crisis financiera mundial que se vivió ese año.
La victoria electoral de Donald Trump significó un movimiento positivo para las principales criptomonedas del mercado. A finales de 2024, bitcoin registró un nuevo máximo histórico que logró superar los 107.000 dólares por unidad, después de que el presidente estadounidense reiteró su idea de crear una reserva estratégica de la criptodivisa en Estados Unidos.
Las divisas digitales serán un foco de atención durante este año, las iniciativas del presidente de Estados Unidos y el desarrollo de nuevos modelos de inteligencia artificial fungirán un papel importante en la cotización de estos activos. Después del lanzamiento del nuevo modelo de IA chino DeepSeek, BTC y otras criptos cayeron en la mayoría de los mercados de valores.
Valor de la criptomoneda Bitcoin
El precio de la criptomoneda bitcoin para este día a las 14:00 horas (UTC) es de 82505.77 dólares. Esto quiere decir que el activo digital registró un cambio de 0.88% en el último día, así como un movimiento de 0.0% en la última hora.
Por su nivel de capitalización, esta moneda digital ocupa la posición #1 entre las más populares.
Bitcoin alcanza un nuevo récord y lidera el auge en el mercado de las criptomonedas
En marzo del año pasado el bitcoin ha logrado un nuevo máximo histórico, superando los valores anteriores y reafirmándose como la criptomoneda más importante en el mercado, acercándose a los 73 mil dólares. Este récord se obtuvo en medio de un flujo sin precedentes de inversiones hacia las criptomonedas, un acontecimiento notable para el sector financiero digital.
El aumento en el valor de bitcoin ocurre en un contexto donde hay un entrante masivo de capital hacia las criptomonedas, lo que indica un creciente interés y confianza de los inversores en estos activos. La subida del precio beneficia no solo a bitcoin sino que también tiene un impacto positivo en el mercado de las criptomonedas en general, favoreciendo una mayor estabilidad y visibilidad, de acuerdo a un análisis de Bloomberg.
Expertos financiaron este aumento a diferentes factores, como la adopción institucional de las criptomonedas, la búsqueda de alternativas de inversión debido a la incertidumbre económica mundial y la innovación continua en la tecnología blockchain que respalda a bitcoin y otras divisas digitales. Esta combinación de factores ha creado un entorno propicio para el crecimiento continuo en el valor de Bitcoin.
Cómo adquirir criptomonedas
Para comprarlas e intercambiarlas se utilizan portales especializados. Su valor varía en función de la oferta, de la demanda y del compromiso de los usuarios, por lo que puede cambiar más rápido que el dinero tradicional, pero mientras más gente esté interesada y quiera comprar determinada divisa, mayor será su valor.
No obstante, quien invierte en este tipo de monedas digitales debe tener muy claro que esta forma trae consigo un elevado riesgo al capital, pues, así como puede haber un incremento, también puede tener inesperadamente un desplome y acabar con los ahorros de sus usuarios.
Para almacenarlas, los usuarios deben contar con un monedero digital o wallet, que en realidad es un software a través del cual es posible guardar, enviar y hacer transacciones de las criptomonedas. En realidad, este tipo de monederos sólo guarda las claves que marcan la propiedad y el derecho de una persona sobre cierta criptomoneda, por lo que estos códigos son los que en realidad se deben proteger.
