articles.title: Even Realities G2s are my new daily smartglasses; the R1 ring is clutch
articles.text:
I’ve really been on a smart glasses kick, but of the many I’ve tried out, the Even Realities’ Even G2 is among the best. These camera-less smart glasses keep privacy in mind and offer two displays on each lens. The Even G2 paired with the R1 smart ring makes for a pair that I really enjoy, as it keeps my interactions with the smart glasses very discreet. Though the pair aren’t without some faults, the Even G2 and R1 ring are honestly great.
One Ring
The Even G2s look stylish; you can barely tell there’s anything different about them. The temple tips by your ear are a bit thicker than usual, but that’s pretty much the only indicator they might be smart glasses. The glasses are slim and light, weighing only 36g; you’d forget they’re smart glasses if not for the displays. Seriously, I’ve had people be shocked to know I’m wearing smart glasses. And if these had cameras, maybe that’d be a problem, but they don’t, so no issue here.
I could see the Even R1 smart ring being too thick for some women. It’s a pretty thick ring, but I didn’t mind it at all. There’s a flat part of the ring with an ‘E,’ and my finger naturally gravitates towards it, playing with the ring all the time. The flat part doesn’t control the ring or anything, but indicates the correct placement of the ring on the charging stand and helps you dive into the R1 a little more. The smart ring is able to navigate your smart glasses with different gestures. Below the E on the ring, you’ll see dots indicating where you’re supposed to touch. The different gestures include a single tap, a double tap, and a double tap that you hold on the second tap, and you’ll swipe up and down.
Discreet
The screens on the lenses aren’t very evident; people can’t ever tell I’m reading my HUD. Well, until they realize I’m not making eye contact because I’m reading a lengthy text message — or a literal book. Often, people can’t even tell I’m wearing smart glasses; even other journalists and creators in tech who have used the glasses themselves take a moment or two to realize I’m wearing the G2 glasses. Even I don’t always clock when people are wearing the glasses; like in this picture of George Clooney at the Venice International Film Festival, it took me a moment to realize that the star was wearing the smart glasses.
The Even Realities G2 two panels can do a variety of things. Whenever I put on my smart glasses in the morning, I’m greeted by my dashboard that offers the time, date, and the battery percentage of the smart ring and glasses in the top left corner. The bottom left corner shows the temperature, sunset, and the forecast for the following day. The right side shows my calendar for the day, but by swiping on the ring or the temple tips, I can see upcoming tasks and my steps, calories, sleep score, heart rate (beats per minute), and my O2 — based on data provided by the smart ring. Of course, this is all customizable and based on what you want to see. Other widgets include the news, stocks and quick notes.
A double tap — one short, one long — opens a menu which shows notifications, conversate, teleprompter, translate, Even AI, photos and books. This menu can also be customized, and you can add a lot more plugins as well, including one for navigation, one to play chess, and even add the Bible. Books and Photos weren’t there by default either; I added them.
Conversate
While checking your notifications is always useful, my favourite feature is ‘Conversate.’ Conversate writes down all the words being said, kind of like subtitles. I always feel like I have difficulty hearing people around me, so giving everyone subtitles helps. And Conversate offers insight into what’s being said; for instance, the first time I used the feature, I had a family member in the hospital and while Conversate offered subtitles, when I asked my cousin why she needed her sodium up before surgery, a pop-up indicator appeared. To my surprise, the indicator explained why someone would need more sodium in their blood before surgery. It offers a lot of details, pretty much about anything anyone is talking about. I had someone sort of give me an astronomy lesson, and it was able to correct some of the information he was talking about — a single year on Venus is 29.5 Earth years, not 33 years — and even while at church, when the preacher said a bible scripture, the smart glasses showed the verses.
Other cool features include a teleprompter; I haven’t needed to use it yet, but I’ve tried it out, and I can see how it’s very helpful, especially if I’m saying lines in front of the camera. And I had my partner speak with me in Spanish, and I could understand clearly what he was saying. Even Realities’ Even AI can answer any and every question; you can even set it for continuous listening, so it can listen for follow-up questions. You can summon the AI with the phrase “Hey Even,” and it works in English and French, among other languages.
Some of the downsides
The Even Realities G2s aren’t perfect, though. Sometimes, I find the R1 ring a little finicky, and it takes a few swipes before it registers. I’ve had issues with the ring connecting a couple of times, but it’s not a constant problem. Randomly, I’ve seen “ring disconnected”; check it, and it’s already connected again.
This one is a me-thing, but even though the G2s are IP65 water-resistant, I’m always worried about the smart glasses getting wet in the rain or if I’m going to sweat too much and damage them. Another me-thing, but I needed to remind myself to silence my smart glasses before playing badminton because I got a shuttlecock to the forehead when I looked up, saw my dashboard and couldn’t see the birdie anymore.
And unfortunately, the price tag is a bit of a con. The Even Realities G2s are US$599 (C$846) and the R1 smart ring is US$249 (C$352), and this is before including your prescription lenses.

articles.title: Trade Republic geht unter die Versicherer: Das steckt dahinter
articles.text:
Trade Republic geht unter die Versicherer: Das steckt dahinter
Gerade erst ist Trade Republic mit einem kostenlosen Angebot in den Wettbewerb um das kommende Altersvorsorgedepot eingestiegen, da zeigt sich: Das Fintech hat für den staatlich geförderten Riester-Nachfolger wohl noch weitere Pläne.
Wie der Branchendienst “Versicherungsmonitor” als erster berichtete, hat der Berliner Neobroker unter dem Namen „Justinian Versicherungs AG“ einen eigenen Lebensversicherer gegründet. Damit wäre Trade Republic künftig auch in der Lage, eine Variante des Altersvorsorgedepots anzubieten, die eine Garantie-Komponente enthält.
Kampf um die besten Konditionen
Derzeit tobt ein Preiskampf um die Konditionen für die neue private Rentenvorsorge. Das Altersvorsorgedepot ist als Nachfolger der Riester-Rente geplant und soll Anfang 2027 starten. Der Staat steuert dann bis zu 540 Euro jährlich bei, wenn Sparer über Fonds, ETFs oder Anleihen fürs Alter vorsorgen.
Anbieter eines geförderten Altersvorsorgedepots müssen ein sogenanntes Standarddepot bereitstellen, bei dem die Effektivkosten maximal ein Prozent betragen dürfen. Das Geld wird dabei nach gesetzlichen Vorgaben auf einen Aktien- und einen Anleihen-Fonds verteilt.
Daneben bieten viele Broker auch eine günstige Variante für Selbstentscheider, bei der Kunden die Anlagen selbst aus einem Bündel von Aktien-, Anleihen- und Rohstoff-ETFs, Fonds oder ELTIFs auswählen können.
Einen gesetzlichen Kostendeckel gibt es hierfür nicht, aber aktuell werben viele Anbieter auch bei dieser Variante mit günstigen Einstiegsprodukten, in der Hoffnung, die neuen Kunden dann langfristig an sich zu binden. Insbesondere Neobroker unterbieten sich gerade mit dem Versprechen, beide Varianten weit unter dem vorgesehenen 1-Prozent-Deckel für das Standarddepot anbieten zu wollen.
Erst in der vergangenen Woche kündigte Trade Republic an, das Altersvorsorgedepot sogar komplett kostenlos anzubieten. Dazu verzichtet der Neobroker ähnlich wie Konkurrenten auf Depot- und Ausführungskosten. Darüber hinaus werden bei ausgewählten ETFs aber auch keine laufenden Verwaltungsgebühren fällig, die normalerweise bei bis zu 0,2 Prozent liegen. Bei diesen ausgewählten Fonds werden die Gebühren sogar reinvestiert, ähnlich wie es Trade Republic bei den Kinderdepots macht.
Was der Einstieg ins Versicherungsgeschäft bedeutet
Die Gründung eines eigenen Versicherers deutet darauf hin, dass Trade Republic bald ein Altersvorsorgedepot mit Beitragsgarantie anbieten könnte. Solchen Produkten zahlen Kunden im Rentenalter mindestens 80 oder 100 Prozent des investierten Geldes aus, selbst wenn es gerade einen Börsencrash gab. Diese Sicherheit geht jedoch zulasten der Rendite, da ein großer Teil des Geldes in sichere, niedrig verzinste Anlagen fließt, um die Garantie zu finanzieren.
Vor allem Kunden, die bisher einen Riester-Vertrag bespart haben, könnten auf ein Depot mit Beitragsgarantie umsteigen, da sie diese Absicherung bereits gewohnt sind. Auch ältere Sparer, die kurz vor der Rente stehen, oder sicherheitsorientierte Anleger, die Börsenturbulenzen schlecht aushalten, könnten so ein Produkt bevorzugen.
Für Trade Republic eröffnet sich damit ein neuer Kundenkreis, der bisher von klassischen Versicherern bedient wurde. Zu welchen Konditionen der Neobroker diese Variante des Altersvorsorgedepots anbieten wird, ist jedoch noch nicht bekannt.

articles.title: Operadoras europeias se unem para enfrentar a Starlink • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Operadoras europeias se unem para enfrentar a Starlink
Iniciativa reúne Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Vodafone e Telefónica, dona da Vivo no Brasil.
As operadoras Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Vodafone e Telefónica, dona da Vivo no Brasil, assinaram uma carta de intenções para estudar uma candidatura conjunta a frequências de comunicação por satélite na Europa.
A iniciativa foi anunciada nesta segunda-feira (19/10) e pode criar uma alternativa aos serviços de conexão direta com celulares oferecidos pela Starlink, de Elon Musk. A medida, no entanto, ainda não tem parceiro definido para fornecer os satélites nem previsão de lançamento, preços ou lista de aparelhos compatíveis.
A tecnologia direct-to-device (D2D) permite que aparelhos compatíveis se comuniquem diretamente com satélites, sem uma antena externa dedicada. Os satélites funcionam como torres de telefonia no espaço.
A proposta é complementar a cobertura das redes convencionais, especialmente em regiões com pouca infraestrutura terrestre. As quatro operadoras planejam estabelecer infraestrutura terrestre, coordenação e monitoramento na Europa, mas não pretendem investir diretamente em uma constelação.
O modelo também prevê acesso aberto a outras operadoras. Entre os objetivos estão proteger comunicações críticas e aumentar a resistência das redes a falhas. A compatibilidade dos celulares depende da solução adotada e das frequências utilizadas.
Por enquanto, a carta representa uma etapa de estudo. O The Verge apresenta o projeto como uma alternativa europeia à conectividade direta para celulares da Starlink, operada pela SpaceX. A iniciativa das operadoras busca fortalecer a governança europeia sobre infraestrutura crítica de conectividade.
Em paralelo, há uma discussão regulatória na União Europeia. Em maio, a Comissão Europeia apresentou uma proposta para selecionar prestadores de serviços móveis por satélite na faixa de 2 GHz. Pelo plano, um terço do espectro seria reservado a comunicações governamentais, de segurança e militares. O restante seria dividido igualmente entre novos fornecedores da UE e uma parcela aberta também a empresas de fora do bloco.
Por aqui, há projetos separados de conexão direta entre satélites e celulares. A Anatel prorrogou até abril de 2029 a autorização experimental da Telefônica Brasil para a tecnologia. O Tecnoblog também revelou testes com a identificação de rede “Vivo Starlink” e negociações com a empresa de Elon Musk.
A Claro, por sua vez, realizou testes com a Lynk Global na faixa de 850 MHz em São Luís (MA), incluindo envio de SMS e uma chamada de voz. O experimento usou aparelhos sem modificações: um Moto G4 Plus, um Galaxy S22 e um iPhone 13.

articles.title: Startup taps underwater volcano as energy source in "proof point" test
articles.text:
The world’s first demonstration of a subsea geothermal power plant has taken place near an active underwater volcano almost a mile below the ocean surface. It generated less than 10 seconds of net-positive electricity but showed the technical feasibility of tapping another form of renewable energy underwater.
The three-week test deployment of the 3-ton prototype power plant took place at the Axial Seamount in the northeast Pacific Ocean in September. Endurance Energy, the Seattle-based startup behind the effort, aims to eventually commercialize subsea geothermal power for Pacific island nations and other customers looking for alternatives to importing expensive fossil fuels.
“The deep ocean gives us unlimited cold seawater for cooling, and its weight keeps the system and the well pressurized, so our plants can be compact,” said Andrew Redd, founder and CEO of Endurance Energy, in an email to Ars.
But efforts to tap geothermal power on the seafloor face many different challenges from land-based geothermal projects, which can also add up to higher installation and operational costs. So Endurance Energy must demonstrate consistent underwater operations as well as prove the approach can be cost-effective.
“It’s probably technically feasible, but it would undoubtedly be more expensive than to do it on land,” said Roland Horne, professor of energy science & engineering at Stanford University, in an emailed response to Ars.
Deep sea drilling
Endurance Energy’s deployment required a subsea lander drill to deploy from the ship Ocean Guardian—operated by Stabbert Maritime—and drill two holes in the seafloor at a depth of about 5,000 feet (1,524 meters). That means the test took place at a depth exceeding 2.5 times the height of the One World Trade Center building in New York City, which is the tallest building in the United States.
Both the drilled holes started venting hot hydrothermal fluid measured at a temperature of about 500° F (260° C). The Endurance Energy team proceeded to case and cement the second hole before installing a valve to create a well.
Next up, the company deployed its 100-kilowatt power plant, named Adélie, that is designed to vaporize incoming hydrothermal fluid to spin a turbine and drive an electric generator. It used the assistance of Canada’s remotely operated submersible ROPOS to help connect the power plant to the newly drilled well.
Adélie also connected to Endurance Energy’s Seattle command center by plugging into the Regional Cabled Array, a 559-mile (900-kilometer) network of undersea fiber-optic and electric cables that provides both power and connectivity to scientific sensors on the seafloor. The undersea network is funded by the US National Science Foundation and is operated by the University of Washington.
That all set the stage for the Adélie power test. But a major hitch soon arose—the drilled well extending 52 feet (16 meters) down into the seafloor was not delivering enough of the hydrothermal fluid to run the power plant.
“For our first well, the goal was to show we could drill, case, cement, and cap a well on the seafloor, so we kept it small and shallow,” Redd explained. “That limited how much fluid it could deliver, and deeper wells should change that.”
The test well was also just 2 inches (5 centimeters) wide, compared to oil, gas, and onshore geothermal wells that typically have casings 20 to 36 inches (51 to 91 centimeters) across.
Endurance Energy plans to avoid this issue in the future by drilling deeper wells to access more fluid. The company’s current lander drill can reach about 260 feet (80 meters), which would be five times deeper than the initial test well.
Powering on
To try running the Adélie power plant anyway, the team redeployed it to a nearby natural vent where hydrothermal fluid was already flowing out at about 538° F (281° C). On September 27, they gave it a try.
Over nearly half a minute, the power plant turbine reached about 26,000 rpm and enabled the generator to produce 60 watt-hours of electricity.
The power plant also became net-positive by producing more electricity than it consumed for about 8.7 seconds. It produced a median of about 2 kilowatts of net power and peaked at 16.5 kilowatts of net power.
“It’s the proof point,” Redd told Ars. “Net-positive is the threshold that matters: the plant made more power than it took to run itself on the seafloor, which no one had done before.”
The 100-kilowatt power plant named Adélie was designed to tap geothermal energy from the seafloor.
Credit:
Endurance Energy
The 100-kilowatt power plant named Adélie was designed to tap geothermal energy from the seafloor.
Credit:
Endurance Energy
But then a software issue brought the power run to a halt. Before the generator takes over, Adélie first relies on a battery to run its pumps, thrusters, and controls, along with spinning the turbine to get it up to speed, Redd explained. A battery module recorded a brief spike in current during the spin-up process and then stopped reporting.
That prompted Adélie’s software to automatically stop the power plant as a safety precaution, because it kept relying on the old reading from the battery module.
When the team was restarting the power plant, a power cable feeding the refrigerant pump also failed when an imperfection in the cable casing allowed seawater to seep in and short two of the electrical conductors. That ended the trial run, although Endurance Energy already plans to use the experience to improve how it builds and tests subsea cables.
Future deployments
Placing the geothermal plant on top of a natural hydrothermal vent was a one-time test for purely research and demonstration purposes, Redd said. His company still plans to rely on drilled wells in future deployments.
Endurance Energy also described taking steps to reduce potential environmental impacts on the seafloor and marine life. The team described choosing the “least disruptive” site for the test run and continuously monitored the process by sampling the water and recording the seafloor array of tubeworms, snails, crabs, and bacterial mats. It also checked findings against scientific sensors run by independent researchers and sent water, rock, and mineral samples for independent lab analysis.
The company’s next trial run planned for the winter of 2026—2027 will involve a refurbished and upgraded Adélie—renamed Gentoo in keeping with the penguin-inspired naming—that will aim to sustain higher power generation.
The company is also developing a larger 2-megawatt commercial generator for its first planned commercial deployment with the Kingdom of Tonga in 2027. The Polynesian island nation in the South Pacific Ocean runs its power grid primarily on imported diesel fuel, which has significantly increased in price since the United States and Israel launched their war with Iran.
“The 2 MW commercial generators will be about the size of a shipping container, and we are deploying up to six of these generators [to] offshore Tonga,” Redd told Ars. “The physical footprint of this project will be relatively small.”
Geothermal energy projects are already cost-effective on land but “on the edge of competitive pricewise,” said Horne at Stanford University. So he cautioned that any factors making geothermal more expensive would “push it to the noncompetitive side.”
Still, other customers may consider Endurance Energy’s approach if the company can demonstrate reliable operations over time with the Kingdom of Tonga. The skyrocketing cost of imported fossil fuels is a huge factor that has already spurred multiple governments to invest in more renewable energy alternatives.
“Large markets with ample offshore geothermal resources include the United States—Pacific Northwest and Alaska—Taiwan, and Japan,” Redd said. “As the technology matures, we expect to compete on cost and deliver continuous, weather-independent power to utilities and large energy users.”
Jeremy Hsu is a reporter exploring a wide range of topics across deep tech and AI. He has previously written for New Scientist, Scientific American, IEEE Spectrum, Wired, Undark Magazine and MIT Tech Review, among many other publications, about topics such as deepfakes, data centers, drones, battery tech, robotics, and GPS jamming. He also has a Master of Arts in Journalism from NYU, and a bachelor's degree from University of Pennsylvania in History and Sociology of Science, with a minor in English.

articles.title: "I have to stop this": Retired professor arrested for blocking delivery robots she says are taking human jobs
articles.text:
A hot potato: A lot of people are angry at the sight of robots carrying out deliveries, seeing it as another sign that machines are making more human jobs obsolete. One such person, a 78-year-old retired professor, made her displeasure known last week by repeatedly standing in front of a delivery robot, blocking its path. The situation ended with her being handcuffed and arrested, but it hasn't deterred her from staging more protests.
Carolyn Marvin, a professor emeritus at the University of Pennsylvania's Annenberg School of Communication, decided to take a literal stand against an oncoming Avride delivery robot from Uber Eats in Philadelphia's Center City. She repeatedly stood in its path so it couldn't move.
Marvin's actions drew a small crowd, and Philadelphia police eventually responded after witnesses reported a disturbance near Reading Terminal Market.
ABC13 reports that Marvin repeatedly ignored officers' requests to allow the robot to pass. She was arrested and charged with disorderly conduct.
Marvin later said she was protesting the use of delivery robots because she believes they are replacing human workers.
"I know they're taking the jobs of human delivery workers and so, I have been protesting them whenever I saw them by standing in front of them and preventing them from going forward," Marvin said, adding that she considers her action as protected speech.
She also confirmed that she had confronted delivery robots on multiple occasions. One witness to a previous encounter thought the machine had hit Marvin. When asked if she was okay, Marvin replied, "No, I have to stop this. They're taking over the world."
When asked if she plans to continue her protests following her arrest, Marvin said, "I do. Why not? I think it's my First Amendment right to publicly demonstrate on a sidewalk to protest against delivery robots."
In a different interview with KYW Newsradio, Marvin went into more detail about why she was interfering with the robots. She called it a protest against the "ruthless way that rich corporations are casting aside human workers – and here, we're talking about the humble delivery folks – in order to enrich their bottom lines."
Marvin added that she hopes the attention her protests receive will encourage more discussion about delivery robots, artificial intelligence and their growing role in everyday life.
Earlier this year, it was reported that as the number of delivery robots on the streets increases, so too does the number of social media clips showing people kicking, grabbing, and even attempting to destroy the machines. While some incidents involve attempted theft, many appear to be expressions of anger at the bots, which symbolize the automation of a job once performed exclusively by humans.

articles.title: Embedded AI evaluators won't be an easy solution, Hugging Face's policy chief says | TechCrunch
articles.text:
AI labs have staked their reputations on model benchmarking — the supposedly neutral and accurate system of evaluations that are designed to measure whether one AI product is better than another.
However, the methods behind these evaluations are complicated and still maturing, said Irene Solaiman, Hugging Face’s chief policy officer, during a discussion at TechCrunch Disrupt last week. Testing needs to come together into a more consistent science if the industry is to rely on them in the future.
With that in mind, can we trust the current tests that are being released?
“Trust is such a weighted term,” said Solaiman. “In terms of whether we can trust results, one big part [of that] is can you reproduce the results of an evaluation? Do you have the level of access that you need to the model itself — this is where open weights come in in a big way,” she added.
Reproducibility in model evaluations has long remained one of the stickier aspects of benchmarking — and remains a topic of significant debate in the industry.
Outside of an individual test’s validity, there’s also the added question of how that test compares to other evaluations.
“They are an evolving science — where we don’t know how to meaningfully compare them to each other,” Solaiman said.
“They start to get ineffective relatively quickly, and we don’t have as much of a thriving ecosystem as we need,” she added. “There’s this hunger for an embedded evaluator ecosystem now, but the qualifications that determine who is an effective evaluator across what tasks need a lot more standardization.”
The idea of embedded evaluators — in which supposedly “neutral” third-party observers are placed inside AI organizations — has been popularized over the last several months, as AI labs grapple with a rash of safety incidents that have spurred concerns over the potential harms of their technology. Hugging Face was famously the target of one of those incidents.
Instead of active government regulation to identify and mitigate model safety concerns, labs have pushed for the third-party solution. However, doubts remain over how neutral or effective those evaluators will actually be. Anthropic’s decision to hire Accenture as its first evaluator spurred a good amount of backlash, with some critics mocking the idea that the consulting firm was qualified to do the task at hand.
Evaluations are now moving from merely a test of the model itself to a test of the entire system around the model — including the harness and agent. The harness — or the tool the user is using to access the model — specifically, has a lot to do with a model’s performance, and a weaker model with a better harness could easily outperform a frontier model, Solaiman shared.
“Agentic evals are really hard and really expensive,” said Solaiman. “We have just more evaluations for models. … We don’t have as many evaluations for harnesses, and we are developing better evaluations for the holistic agent — because that’s what a lot of folks are getting value out of,” she added.
In other words, the evaluation space is a bit of a free-for-all at the moment, and if benchmarking is going to continue to be seen as a useful tool for industry leaders, a more uniform, industry-wide approach — where everyone is on the same page — may be necessary.

articles.title: Google DeepMind says four AI agents beat Minecraft in 27 hours by writing 2,783 programs of their own — AI team died 605 times on Easy difficulty and ran up an estimated $520 in tokens
articles.text:
Google DeepMind says four AI agents beat Minecraft in 27 hours by writing 2,783 programs of their own — AI team died 605 times on Easy difficulty and ran up an estimated $520 in tokens
About half the run was spent fighting the dragon, solved by stacking dirt to reach its crystals.
The game of Minecraft is no match for a team of four Gemini 4 Argon agents, as they were able to defeat it in 27 hours with 2,783 self-written programs, a paper from Google DeepMind reveals. The agents did die 605 times, even on Easy, and about half the run was spent fighting the Ender Dragon, the final boss of the game. The run finally came to completion when the End was solved by stacking dirt to reach the boss’s crystals, at an estimated cost of around $520 in tokens.
The experimental run was designed from the get-go with one goal: kill the Ender Dragon. The playthrough involved a random, shared survival world on Easy with four agents — a fifth agent existed only for reporting — from Gemini 4 Argon, Google’s latest frontier model. Each agent had its own player through the open-source Mineflayer JavaScript library for Minecraft bots, but they were able to coordinate through in-game chat and shared notes. Every program used in the run was written by the agents themselves, and the emphasis is on coding and teamwork rather than game-playing.
The authors say this is the “first end-to-end autonomous completion of Minecraft by AI agents,” at least “to our knowledge,” qualified by the use of Mineflayer “without pre-scouted seeds or other game-specific tools written by humans.” Mineflayer tells the agents where blocks and creatures are, with a pathfinding plugin to plan routes. There was “no human input during the run” and “no one assigned roles or wrote game logic.” The run, starting with the first program and ending with the dragon's death, took 27 hours and 14 minutes.
Although the agents were not given roles, within about 10 minutes a division of labor was proposed in chat by bot janesick. Bot Auratian offered an alternative plan while Bot Gyldenia acknowledged it. The roles ended up being: Gyldenia for food, beds, and flint; Bulicame for diamonds; Janesick for iron and tools; Auratian for the Nether portal. Moments of losses, such as a Ghast fireball destroying dropped items, led the team to diagnose the cause and write rules to prevent it in the future.
Finding the stronghold involved janesick, who threw two Eyes of Ender from different spots and sampled each eye’s flight once every 50 ms, triangulating the location. Carrying the eyes involved its own dire moment when Auratian drowned during the task, but the spot was noted, and the eyes were rescued.
The eventual fight with the dragon led to 69 deaths, and the ten crystals kept regenerating the boss until Auratian discovered they could use dirt pillars to reach the crystals. Four hours and 40 minutes later, all ten crystals were downed, and the dragon was dead 39 minutes after that.
The agents operated by writing short JavaScript programs, almost 2,800 in total, with 42 helper functions kept alive between programs, while a Mineflayer bot ran them in the shared world. Text was returned with status data, not pictures. This is a shared approach to the non-screenshot GPT-6 Astra clear of the Orc starting zone in World of Warcraft earlier this month. AI agents playing games is an ongoing trend, with Pokémon Red probably being the most popular, a game defeated in multiple ways, including with a Jev decision model layer.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Minecraft has also been a popular target, and the authors admit this, highlighting two earlier community dragon kills: a planner with an action-selection model on a fixed speedrun seed in Peaceful mode, and a single Claude Opus 5 agent that used 37 ready-made, high-level tools on Normal, versus Mineflayer alone for the Gemini team. AI Bengineering’s Claude run, relying mostly on Opus 5 at high effort, took 3 hours and 56 minutes from start — “no human input after the prompt” — to kill with 388 tool calls and only one death. The cost in that case, at API-equivalent rates, was about $93.
Google’s Minecraft run, using Gemini 4 Argon’s 50% introductory pricing, which runs from initial API access that followed the model announcement through Nov. 30, cost more than half a grand; at normal pricing, that’s more than a grand. A GPT-6 Astra Portal run last month, which took about 24 hours, came in at $571 in tokens.
Google’s run took about 1.35 billion input tokens with 91% served from cache. About 24,000 model calls involved around 16 million output tokens, a quarter of them thinking. In total, if we’re also including the observer agent, the session would be estimated at $810, or $1,620 after the promotion, at list prices.
Each player is driven by a “general-purpose Gemini 4 Argon coding agent,” which is a fancy way of saying that it’s not specialized for Minecraft. Gemini 4 Argon itself is a frontier model for “real-world software engineering, enterprise knowledge work like legal and finance, and cybersecurity defense,” according to a company blog. With Minecraft, 22% of the agents’ programs ended in an error, with more than 600 deaths.
Although the model was used for a game here, the run was designed to show that Argon is capable of “complex, long-horizon workflows” for complex real-world tasks and agent coordination. Such long projects can involve decompiling a game back into source code, as we covered recently with a Modern Warfare 2 rebuild that now has 83% of its functions matching the original byte for byte.

Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: Chip legend Jim Keller's Tenstorrent raises $1.5B to expand its open compute ecosystem - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Chip legend Jim Keller’s Tenstorrent raises $1.5B to expand its open compute ecosystem
Artificial intelligence computing hardware startup Tenstorrent Inc. is pushing hard to position itself as an alternative to Nvidia Corp.’s graphics processing units after raising a massive $1.5 billion in a late-stage funding round today.
The Series E round was jointly led by Trace Capital and Innovation X and saw participation from new and existing backers including Protagonist, Morgan Stanley, Fidelity Management & Research Co., ARK Invest and T. Rowe Price. It brings the startup’s valuation to $6.2 billion.
Toronto-based Tenstorrent is led by its Chief Executive Jim Keller (pictured), who is widely regarded as a legend in the semiconductor industry, having previously helped to design a number of groundbreaking processors for the likes of Intel Corp., Advanced Micro Devices Inc., Apple Inc. and Tesla Inc.
The startup originally set out as a chip designer but quickly pivoted to offer more than just the bare silicon. Today, it sells a complete portfolio of AI compute platforms, ranging from its Galaxy servers, TT-QuietBox workstations and its Blackhole cards for laptops.
Those platforms are powered by its specialized Tensix Neo accelerators and its Ascalon central processing units, which are both based on the open-standard RISC-V instruction set. They’re designed to be extremely scalable and energy-efficient, capable of producing top-tier performance for AI workloads without runaway power consumption, ensuring costs remain low.
Its best-selling products are the Galaxy Tenstorrent servers, which are enterprise-class systems that can work in coordination with others to create massive superclusters for training and running advanced frontier models. According to Tenstorrent, the Galaxy servers are already being used by companies such as Virtu Financial Inc. to power on-premises AI trading agents, while the data center colocation provider Equinix Inc. also makes them available to enterprises.
Developers who need immense compute locally may be more interested in Tenstorrent’s TT-QuietBox (below), which is a liquid-cooled desktop AI workstation that has enough power to test and run cutting-edge models right out of the box, with minimal setup. These systems are powered by Tenstorrent’s Blackhole cards, which are infinitely scalable PCIe boards packed with massive RISC-V cores and GDDR6 memory to enable high-performance AI processing in a very small package. For larger workloads, it’s possible to network multiple Blackhole cards and TT-QuietBoxes to pool their memory and compute.
Hardware is one thing, but where Tenstorrent really sets itself apart is that it also develops all of the software needed to make its platforms usable. It has also developed an open-source software stack that gives developers the ability to bring any AI workload to its hardware.
This stack consists of TT-Forge, a compiler that bridges machine learning frameworks like PyTorch to its RISC-V chips; TT-Metalium, which is a software development kit for hardware optimization and custom kernel development; and TT-LLK, for low-level kernel optimizations. These three components combine to enable developers to compile, fine-tune and then execute AI models on its custom silicon.
Keller said Tenstorrent’s platform approach allows it to scale from a single workstation to massive cloud-based clusters. “We’ve built one architecture and we sell it at every size,” He explained. “The future of compute is open, scalable and owned by the people building on it.”
Constellation Research analyst Holger Mueller told SiliconANGLE that Tenstorrent is one of a growing number of innovative startups trying to build more efficient computing platforms for AI, and the pedigree track record of its CEO Keller means it’s also one of the most promising. “Tenstorrent gets the funding it needs to keep innovating, and this is good news for enterprises,” the analyst said. “Nvidia is not the only option anymore. More competition and deployment options for AI compute can only be beneficial for enterprises, making AI workloads cheaper and more flexible.”
The funds from today’s round mean that Tenstorrent now has the muscle to ramp up production of its Galaxy servers, which will be deployed globally to support developers running massive large language models and video generation workloads. Some of the money will be given to its research team, which will look to advance innovation in the RISC-V ecosystem. Finally, Tenstorrent plans to expand its workforce globally.
Protagonist co-founder and Managing Partner George Bousis said Tenstorrent’s full platform approach sets it apart from the legions of startups scrambling to provide a viable alternative to Nvidia’s GPU ecosystem. “Few companies design the chip and the software that runs on it, but Tenstorrent does both, and its video generation results beat industry benchmarks ahead of our expectations,” he said.

articles.title: Amazon baisse le prix de ce radiateur connecté Dreo de 2000 W au bon moment
articles.text:
Un radiateur d’appoint est surtout utile dans plusieurs situations : lorsque le chauffage principal n’est pas encore allumé, lorsqu’une pièce peine à atteindre une température confortable ou encore quand la salle de bains est glaciale au moment de sortir de la douche. À la fin du mois d’octobre, ces situations deviennent courantes dans de nombreux logements. Mieux vaut donc s’équiper avant les premières grosses vagues de froid, lorsque tout le monde se met à chercher la même chose au même moment.
Amazon propose justement le radiateur Convection Heater 711S à convection connecté de Dreo à 129,99 € au lieu de 149,99 €. La remise atteint donc 20 €, soit environ 13 %. C’est toujours ça de pris sur un appareil qui tournera tout l’hiver. L’offre se termine le 31 octobre 2026.
Ce modèle, présenté au salon IFA de Berlin début septembre, est en vente depuis le 10 septembre. Cette remise arrive donc à peine plus d’un mois après sa sortie.
Comment fonctionne ce radiateur Dreo à convection ?
La convection est le principe le plus simple du chauffage électrique. Une résistance chauffe l’air à son contact, cet air chaud monte, et l’air plus frais du bas de la pièce vient prendre sa place. La circulation se fait toute seule, sans ventilateur. Le Dreo n’émet donc ni souffle d’air ni ronronnement de moteur, un atout dans une chambre ou un bureau. Son élément chauffant en forme de X développe 2 000 watts, une puissance que le fabricant destine aux grandes pièces.
Le radiateur embarque un thermostat avec affichage numérique, une minuterie jusqu’à 24 heures, une télécommande et un verrouillage pour les enfants. Une protection contre la surchauffe coupe l’appareil en cas de problème. Le Dreo se pilote aussi à distance depuis l’application mobile de la marque, disponible sur iOS et Android. Celle-ci permet de régler la température, de modifier le mode de chauffage ou encore de programmer des plages de fonctionnement pour adapter le chauffage à ses habitudes. L’appareil peut également être associé à des assistants vocaux comme Amazon Alexa et Google Assistant, afin de le commander à la voix.
Le chauffage dispose d’une certification IP24. Cet indice de protection signifie que l’appareil empêche l’accès des doigts à ses parties électriques et qu’il résiste aux projections d’eau venues de toutes les directions. Il peut donc servir dans une salle de bains. Il mesure 78,3 cm de large, 48,4 cm de haut et 24 cm de profondeur. Monté sur roulettes, il se déplace facilement d’une pièce à l’autre, et une barre lumineuse indique aussi la température de la pièce.
À ce prix, le radiateur Dreo est-il une bonne affaire ?
À 129,99 €, ce Dreo coche beaucoup de cases pour un radiateur d’appoint : grande puissance, fonctionnement silencieux, programmation sur 24 heures et usage possible dans une salle de bains. Il faut toutefois connaître les limites de la convection. Elle chauffe la pièce de façon plus douce et plus progressive qu’un chauffage soufflant, qui envoie immédiatement de l’air chaud vers vous. Cela suffit pour maintenir une température agréable dans une pièce au quotidien, notamment si vous l’utilisez en complément du chauffage principal ou pour réchauffer une pièce un peu fraîche en intersaison.
À pleine puissance, un radiateur de 2 000 watts consomme 2 kWh par heure, soit environ 40 centimes au tarif réglementé (0,2001 € le kWh en option Base depuis le 1er août 2026). Le thermostat et la minuterie servent justement à limiter son usage aux heures où vous en avez besoin. Ce modèle a surtout du sens dans une chambre ou une salle de bains, là où son silence et son indice IP24 comptent.

articles.title: OWC Announces General Availability of Dock Ejector 2.1
articles.text:
Monday, October 19th 2026
OWC Announces General Availability of Dock Ejector 2.1
Other World Computing (OWC), a trusted leader in high-performance storage, memory, connectivity, software, and accessories that empower creative and business professionals to maximize performance, enhance reliability, and streamline workflows, today announced the general availability (GA) launch of OWC Dock Ejector 2.1 software that adds one-click safe ejection for connected data volumes, for Mac and PC. In addition, on Mac, OWC Dock Ejector 2.1 now provides seamless high-power USB port enablement.While OWC docks are fully functional without OWC Dock Ejector, the v2.1 software adds another layer of convenience, data protection, and capability. With OWC Dock Ejector 2.1, users can:
- Safely eject all detected connected data volumes with a single click on Mac or PC, protecting against data corruption or loss before disconnecting from a dock.
- Safely eject SoftRAID, AppleRAID, and other connected non-raid volumes, including camera cards, without having to locate and eject each volume individually.
- Reduce the risk associated with improperly unmounting volumes, particularly ExFAT and FAT32 media commonly used with camera cards and in cross-platform creative workflows.
- On Mac, automatically enable supported OWC dock USB ports for higher-power operation recognized by macOS, allowing compatible devices to access the additional power they require without changing macOS security settings.
- Support devices such as Apple SuperDrive and mobile devices that may require macOS to recognize a USB port as high-power enabled for proper operation or faster charging.
- Download Dock Ejector 2.1 free from OWC.com or, for the first time, through the Apple App Store.
"OWC Dock Ejector takes something that can be a tedious manual process and turns it into one-click assurance for your data," said Larry O'Connor, Founder and CEO, Other World Computing (OWC). "Whether you're on a Mac or PC, it detects and safely ejects connected data volumes so you can disconnect your dock without worrying that you missed a drive. That's especially important for creators working with camera media and ExFAT or FAT32 volumes, where an improper disconnect can result in data loss or corruption. OWC docks stand on their own - OWC Dock Ejector simply makes the experience safer, easier, and better."
"On the Mac, OWC Dock Ejector goes even further by enabling macOS to recognize the higher-power capability already built into supported OWC dock USB ports, so devices that require additional power can operate or fast charge as intended," O'Connor continued. "It does that without requiring users to dig into messy security settings. Bringing together one-click drive safety and high-power port enablement in a free, integrated software experience is another OWC difference - adding even more capability, convenience, and value to an OWC dock."

articles.title: Kaspersky's VPN and password manager went dark for days worldwide — and the timing has raised awkward questions about Russia's drone-hit data centers
articles.text:
Kaspersky's VPN and password manager went dark for days worldwide — and the timing has raised awkward questions about Russia's drone-hit data centers
Kaspersky blamed technical issues for a multi-day outage
- Kaspersky's VPN, Password Manager, Safe Kids, and My Kaspersky portal failed worldwide from October 11 to roughly October 14
- The outage began hours after Ukrainian drones shut down Yandex's Vladimir data center, but no technical link has been shown between the two
- A viral post calling Kaspersky "practically dead" was wrong on database updates, lost passwords, and its Europe-only framing - the effect was global and temporary
Kaspersky customers worldwide recently spent several days unable to use the company's VPN, Password Manager, Safe Kids parental controls, or My Kaspersky account portal, after an outage began within hours of Ukrainian drones forcing a third Yandex data center offline.
The company has blamed technical issues and has not named an underlying cause - but the overlap with the strikes on Russia's biggest tech firm has been hard for users to ignore.
On October 15 2026, Riga-based commentator Professor Talk (@SergejTalk) told his followers that European users were finding Kaspersky's antivirus "practically dead," with database updates failing, the password manager gone along with its contents, and the VPN wiped out.
Many of those claims don't hold up to the record; the outage itself, however, was real, global, and lasted the better part of four days, but it did point to a potential connection to Russian hosting for many of Kaspersky's key services.
Locked out on four continents: Bad timing or something more?
The first complaints landed on Kaspersky's support forum early on Sunday, October 11, when a user reported the VPN refusing to connect on both PC and phone. Within a day, the thread had drawn reports from Malaysia, Brazil, Italy, Vietnam, Spain, Germany, Iraq, the UK, and Australia, while users in Japan described failed activations and an unreachable VPN on X.
As a result, on October 12, Kaspersky employee and forum moderator Danila T. confirmed that some features in Kaspersky products and on My Kaspersky were temporarily unavailable, naming VPN, Safe Kids, and Password Manager, and said protection and user data were unaffected.
A later notice, relayed in French by moderator Berny, said the VPN problems hit the app on every supported operating system, and that licenses bought from October 10 onward could face activation delays. Kaspersky said it would extend affected subscriptions automatically to cover the lost time.
The staff, while in damage-control mode, also told users not to uninstall or reinstall applications, noting that the activation service issues would essentially lock them out of the applications altogether.
Service came back in stages. Berny reported My Kaspersky was reachable again on the evening of October 13; users said the VPN was connecting by the morning of October 14, and Danila T. posted that day that "the VPN issue should now be resolved."
The timing is what has people talking. Drones struck Yandex's Sasovo data center in the Ryazan region overnight on October 7 to 8, partially disabled its Kaluga site on October 9, and forced the complete shutdown of its Vladimir facility overnight into October 11.
Yandex Cloud was placed into emergency mode, and customers were advised to activate their own disaster recovery plans. We reported Yandex search traffic collapsing as the company's central Russian cloud zones went dark.
Correlation, not proven causation
A detailed incident timeline published on Habr puts the Vladimir power failure between 04:00 and 06:08 Moscow time on October 11, close to when Kaspersky VPN users began reporting problems. Kaspersky's own notice flagging licenses bought on October 10 also falls within a window when two Yandex sites were already damaged.
This is correlation, not causation, and Kaspersky has not said any consumer service runs on Yandex Cloud; none of the reporting to date, including Günter Born's blog and WinFuture, has produced technical evidence that one does.
WinFuture has noted that it remains unclear whether Kaspersky still depends on Russian data centers. Yandex's collapse also knocked over more than a dozen unrelated third-party services, according to The Record, from retailers to the Russian arm of TikTok, so a coincidental fault elsewhere would struggle to stand out.
The same week also reminded everyone how quickly such links harden online often without actual grounding in facts. Viral claims that the strikes had silenced Russian troll farms drew a rebuttal from OCCRP senior editor Ilya Lozovsky, who said they have "no basis in fact", noting the Cloudflare data in question measured automated crawlers rather than social media bots.
Irrespective of what is true here, the timing of Kaspersky's services going offline coinciding with Russian data centers going offline is a worrying one for an EU that is already looking to develop its own data security infrastructure and is trying to wean its users off 3rd-party services of what could in the future be an adversary.
The wider data center war shows no sign of easing. Russian strikes damaged at least six Ukrainian data centers in late September, and Ukraine's current strikes are seen as a tit-for-tat measure rather than an escalation.
For retail customers of Kaspersky's services inside or outside the EU, the practical lesson is narrower: Local protection kept working, which matters most for antivirus software.
But anyone leaning on the company's VPN or cloud-synced password manager has just seen how a disruption far from their own machine can take those tools away for days. Those who want a reliable plan B can find alternatives in our guide to the best antivirus software or the best VPN solutions for their specific use cases.

articles.title: Wisst ihr noch? Als Tester versehentlich das erste Samsung Galaxy Fold zerstörten
articles.text:
Folie abgezogen, Display tot: Als Tester versehentlich das erste Samsung Galaxy Fold zerstörten
Am 23. Oktober kommt das iPhone Duo in den Handel. Zwar ist es Apples erstes Foldable, ein Pionier ist das Unternehmen damit aber nicht. Samsung stellte sein erstes faltbares Smartphone, das Samsung Galaxy Fold, bereits Anfang 2019 vor. Schon damals war die Technik nicht günstig. 2.000 Euro sollte das Telefon kosten. Dass das Unternehmen damit dennoch groß auftrumpfen wollte, war klar. Vor dem Markstart produzierte das Unternehmen einen Werbefilm mit bekannten Größen wie dem Fußballstar Mario Götze oder dem Youtube-Influencer Casey Neistat.
Schon längst ist dieses Video auf Samsungs eigenen Kanälen aber nicht mehr auffindbar. Denn das Gerät hatte gleich mehrere Probleme mit der Stabilität, wie unter anderem The Verge 2019 berichtete. Dieter Bohn, damals Redakteur bei dem Medium, bemerkte nach einem Tag der Nutzung, dass etwas unterhalb der Displayfalte gegen den Bildschirm drückte. „Meine Vermutung ist, dass es sich um einen Fremdkörper handelt, auf jeden Fall um etwas, das härter ist als Flusen“, schrieb er damals. Kurze Zeit später habe das Display nicht mehr funktioniert. Auch CNBC berichtete zeitgleich von einem ausgefallenen Bildschirm.
Displayschicht wird zur Falle für Tester
Weitere Stimmen, die über Probleme mit dem Bildschirm klagten, waren daran zumindest nicht ganz unschuldig. Youtuber Marques Brownlee entfernte eine Schutzfolie vom Bildschirm, die er besser an Ort und Stelle gelassen hatte. Wie Samsung später in einem Statement mitteilte, war diese Folie „Teil der Bildschirmstruktur“. Sie sollte das Display vor Kratzern schützen, durfte aber nicht entfernt werden.
Brownlee war damit nicht allein. Auch der vor allem für seine Apple-Berichterstattung bekannte Mark Gurman von Bloomberg entfernte den wichtigen Film vom Bildschirm. Beide hielten das Cover für einen normalen Schutzfilm, wie er üblicherweise aufs Smartphone angebracht ist und nach dem Auspacken entfernt wird. In beiden Fällen trug das Display allerdings Schäden davon.
Zum Verhängnis wurde den Testern, dass die Bildschirmschicht so aufgebracht war, dass sie den Anschein erweckte, man könnte sie leicht abziehen. Brownlee bemängelte in einem Video, dass entsprechende Hinweise nicht auf das Verpackungsmaterial gedruckt waren. Joanna Stern, damals noch beim Wall Street Journal, begann ebenfalls, die Displayfolie abzuziehen, ließ dann aber doch auf dem Gerät. Samsung tauschte es nach ihren Angaben, wie auch bei den anderen Testern, aus.
Nur bei Einheiten, die Mobilfunkprovidern vorlagen, war offenbar schon vorab eine Warnung aufgedruckt, wie Des Smith, damals Senior Product Manager bei T-Mobile US, auf X postete. Smith betrieb naher einen Youtube-Kanal und war und ist auch in anderen sozialen Netzwerken aktiv. Erst mit dem Statement erklärte Samsung: „Wir werden sicherstellen, dass wir unseren Kunden diese Information deutlich vermitteln.“
Start verschoben, Smartphone verbessert
Trotz der negativen Berichte der Tester wollte Samsung zum nächsten am geplanten Starttermin (dem 26. April 2019 in den USA und dem 3. Mai in Europa) festhalten, entschloss sich kurzfristig aber doch um und kündigte an, den Verkaufsstart zu verschieben. „Erste Ergebnisse aus den Auswertungen der gemeldeten Display-Probleme zeigen, dass die Ursache am Scharnier liegen kann. Es gab auch einen Fall, in dem Stoffe, die sich im Inneren des Geräts befanden, die Display Leistung beeinträchtigten“, verkündete das Unternehmen in einem weiteren Statement.
Der Start folgte dann im September 2019. Diesmal stellte Samsung sicher, dass Nutzer die Schutzfolie nicht mehr entfernen konnten. Neue Abdeckungen sorgten zudem dafür, dass sich keine Fremdkörper mehr unters Display verirren konnten.
Längst bereiten die Samsung-Geräte Testern keine Probleme mehr. Im Jahr 2025 war Samsung mit 40 Prozent Marktanteil laut Counterpoint Research sogar Marktführer bei den Foldables. Ob das Unternehmen die Poleposition auch 2026 behält, bleibt abzuwarten. Da kommt ja schließlich noch was von Apple.

Low Power-High Performance
                        WHITEPAPERS
		
Opimizing embedded memory IP for RibbonFET and PowerVia.
								October 19th, 2026 - 
								By: Synopsys
								
							
Embedded memory, not compute, has become the limiting factor in AI and HPC SoCs, consuming more than half of total die area while constraining bandwidth, latency, and energy efficiency. As the industry transitions to gate-all-around (GAA) devices and backside power delivery network (BSPDN) technology, embedded memory architectures must evolve to keep pace.
This white paper examines how these shifts redefine embedded memory requirements and how Synopsys Embedded Memory IP addresses them through device-aware architectures, power-optimized designs, and highly configurable compilers. It also presents silicon results from SRAM and Register File test chips on the Intel 18A process node, including density improvements in the 5–10% range and ISO-power performance gains of up to approximately 4%.
Read the paper to discover how RibbonFET and PowerVia enable PPA improvements and reduce advanced-node integration risk.
What you’ll learn:
- Why embedded memory, not compute, is limiting AI and HPC SoC performance
- How GAA devices and BSPDN technology reshape advanced-node embedded memory
- The critical PPA, power-delivery, and configurability requirements for embedded memory IP
- How RibbonFET and PowerVia enable measurable PPA improvements
- What silicon-proven SRAM and Register File results show on Intel 18A

articles.title: Foxconn's latest EV push is a $727 million bet for half of Mitsubishi Electric's car parts business
articles.text:
What just happened? Foxconn has agreed to pay $727 million for a 50% stake in Mitsubishi Electric's automotive equipment business, gaining access to vehicle-control technology and software expertise for its push to develop electric vehicles for other manufacturers. The deal gives Foxconn a broader engineering base, but much of the business it is buying still serves conventional vehicles. Its success will depend on turning that expertise into products automakers want to buy.
The companies plan to combine Mitsubishi Electric's powertrain, autonomous-driving and in-car computing technology with Foxconn's manufacturing operations. They want to build EV platforms in Japan, sell them first to Japanese automakers and then seek customers overseas.
"What attracted us most was the electronic-control technology – and the substantial software resources behind them," Jun Seki, Foxconn's chief strategy officer for EVs, said at a news conference in Tokyo.
Mitsubishi Electric Mobility's products include alternators, starters, ignition coils, radar sensors and electric powertrain equipment. Its established automaker relationships also give Foxconn a route to potential customers.
But Foxconn is not buying into all of Mitsubishi Electric's EV technology. The Japanese company's power-semiconductor business is outside the agreement. That includes silicon-carbide and insulated-gate bipolar transistor power modules used in EV inverters.
The automotive deal instead covers the equipment business that Mitsubishi Electric spun off into Mitsubishi Electric Mobility in April 2024. Before closing, Mitsubishi Electric will move its remaining automotive operations, including those held by overseas subsidiaries, into that company.
Foxconn's investment arm, Lin Yin International Investment, will acquire half of the combined business. The partners expect the deal to close in October 2027, following antitrust reviews and other required approvals.
Mitsubishi Electric has been reshaping its portfolio, exiting car multimedia and fuel injectors and transferring its lighting business to Stanley Electric.
An earlier electric-powertrain partnership changed course. In May 2024, Mitsubishi Electric Mobility and Aisin agreed to establish a joint venture for traction motors, inverters and control software. Five months later, they dropped the joint-venture plan and opted for a business alliance.
The purchase gives Foxconn another way into the car industry after several years of prototypes, partnerships and setbacks.
Foxconn had planned to build Fisker's Pear EV at its Lordstown, Ohio, factory, but the vehicle never reached production. Fisker went bankrupt in 2024, and Foxconn sold the factory last year.
Foxconn has made progress elsewhere. Mitsubishi Motors, which is separate from Mitsubishi Electric, is putting its badge on the Foxtron-developed ASX VR-e for Australia and New Zealand. Foxconn also has a bus joint venture with Mitsubishi Fuso and is a partner in Saudi Arabia's Ceer EV brand.
The Mitsubishi Electric agreement adds an established automotive supplier to Foxconn's network, alongside its existing vehicle-development and manufacturing partnerships.

articles.title: Free en panne ? Les signalements s’envolent en même temps que Google et YouTube — Frandroid
articles.text:
Il y a des jours où la page d’accueil de Downdetector ressemble à un sapin de Noël. Ce mardi, quatre services y figurent en tête : Revolut, dont la courbe redescend après une matinée chaotique sans revenir à zéro, puis Free, Google et YouTube, qui décollent tous les trois en même temps depuis le début de l’après-midi. Chez Free, la majorité des signalements porte sur l’accès à Internet.
L’opérateur n’avait pas communiqué sur un incident au moment où nous écrivons ces lignes. Des signalements localisés remontaient déjà depuis la matinée dans plusieurs communes des Bouches-du-Rhône, de Salon-de-Provence à Miramas, mais la hausse visible en début d’après-midi touche désormais tout le pays, de Paris à Lyon en passant par Mulhouse.
- Débit jusqu’à 2 Gb/s
- Sans Player TV
- Wi-Fi 7
- Débit jusqu’à 1 Gb/s
- Sans Player TV
- Wi-Fi 5
- Débit jusqu’à 5 Gb/s
- Sans Player TV
- Wi-Fi 7
Google Cloud, suspect idéal mais pas prouvé
On connaît désormais la cause de la panne du matin. Google évoque un incident d’alimentation électrique dans la zone europe-west2-b, l’un de ses centres de données de Londres, qui a rendu ses services cloud indisponibles dans cette zone et perturbé le reste de la région. Revolut, Lloyds ou HSBC en ont fait les frais.
    Pour aller plus loin
Panne Revolut : Google Cloud et son centre de données de Londres pointés du doigt
            
Free exploite en revanche son propre réseau, et rien ne le relie pour l’instant à l’incident londonien. Il faut aussi garder en tête la façon dont fonctionne Downdetector, qui compile des signalements d’internautes et ne mesure rien lui-même. Quand YouTube ou Google ne répondent plus, beaucoup accusent d’abord leur box et signalent leur opérateur. L’inverse est vrai aussi : une coupure chez un fournisseur d’accès fait grimper mécaniquement les signalements des sites que ses abonnés n’arrivent plus à charger.

Cartes refusées, application bloquée : Revolut reconnaît une panne sans donner de cause

articles.title: How a FD calculator helps investors plan savings with ease
articles.text:
How a FD calculator helps investors plan savings with ease
Saving for life’s big goals? Start with an FD calculator: Bajaj Finance’s online tool lets you compare amounts, tenures, and payout options instantly, turning guesswork into clear savings plans.
Establishing a financial goal makes the process of saving a lot easier. If you plan to save well, you need to know the total amount you plan to save as well as the time frame for saving. Whether you want to save for a family event, pay for tuition, or renovate your home, you should be aware of the amount of money you want to save and the time frame.
A fixed deposit is a type of investment that guarantees you a fixed amount of return during the investment period. However, calculating returns manually can be a hassle. So, using Bajaj Finance's FD Calculator saves a lot of time and energy as it allows you to know your estimated returns in seconds based on your inputs. You can explore options before making the final investment.
Define your savings goal
The first crucial step in investing is to find out your investment's purpose. Knowing why you are making the investment will give you the desired amount you need to save and the time of retrieval for the money.
For example, if the amount required for a particular instance is Rs 3 lakh in three years, you can use the calculator
See how much your deposit may earn
The Bajaj Finance FD Calculator estimates your return after you provide the required inputs. These generally include the investment amount, investor category, tenure, and interest payout option.
The result shows the estimated interest earned and the expected maturity amount. This allows you to see how much of the final value comes from your original deposit and how much may come from interest.
The calculation also makes percentage rates easier to understand. An annual interest rate may appear attractive, but the calculator translates it into an estimated rupee value. This provides a more practical picture of how the investment could contribute towards your savings goal.
Choose an amount without affecting your budget
A larger amount will yield a higher maturity value, but putting in too much money could create issues when it's time to pay the bills. The right figure would give you the money you need to achieve your future goal.
Before making a fixed deposit, be sure to think about rent, bills, school tuition, medical expenses, and anything else that you must pay for in the near future.
The calculator allows you to compare various amounts almost instantly. Enter Rs 50,000, Rs 1 lakh, or any other amount and watch the maturity figure change accordingly.
Match the tenure with your goal date
Bajaj Finance’s fixed deposit scheme has time frames that range from 12 to 60 months. The applicable interest rate differs based on the time chosen, meaning changing the time can result in varied rates of return.
A longer period gives the deposit a longer opportunity to earn interest through the compound option, but maturity needs to happen close to the time of using the funds.
Suppose your goal is due after two years. Selecting a five-year deposit merely because it shows a larger maturity value could leave the funds unavailable at the required time. The FD interest Calculator lets you compare eligible tenures and select one that balances potential earnings with timely access.
How to use the FD calculator
The Bajaj Finance online calculator is designed to provide estimates quickly. You can repeat the calculation with different inputs and compare the results before starting the investment process.
- Choose the investor category: Select the relevant option for a customer below 60 or a senior citizen.
- Enter the deposit amount: Add the amount you are considering investing.
- Select the tenure: Choose an available period between 12 and 60 months.
- Pick the payout option: Select interest at maturity or a periodic payout frequency.
- Review the estimate: Check the estimated interest earnings and maturity amount.
- Try another combination: Change the amount, tenure, or payout option to compare the result.
Consider safety and access to your money
Return is only one aspect of FD planning. Credit ratings of the institution, conditions for early withdrawal, nomination facility, maturity instructions, and renewal options are some other aspects that must be evaluated as well.
Bajaj Finance Fixed Deposit comes with guaranteed returns and good credit safety ratings, with CRISIL AAA/STABLE and ICRA AAA (Stable). Minimum investment starts at Rs 15,000, making it possible to experiment with various amounts via the calculator before finalizing the exact amount.
Early withdrawals are allowed but require certain conditions to be met, which could lead to lower interest. Therefore, it is wise to select an amount and tenure you are fairly certain you will not deviate from.
Conclusion
Choosing the appropriate amount and period for a fixed deposit account can help you achieve short-term and medium-term savings objectives. The Bajaj Finance FD Calculator lets you know the returns that different fixed deposit accounts can bring.
It is useful to compare various investment scenarios involving the fixed deposit calculator and check information about current FD interest rates, tax rates, credit ratings, and penalties for early withdrawal of a fixed deposit.

articles.title: 250 000 dollars d'acompte et zéro garantie : la folle condition imposée par Tesla pour le nouveau Roadster
articles.text:
On oublierait presque qu’il puisse aussi rouler au sol comme une voiture ordinaire. Capable des galipettes les plus impressionnantes qui soient, le nouveau Tesla Roadster tient véritablement de la science-fiction. La pirouette au-dessus d’un Semi ? Check. La promenade au plafond ? Check. Le 0 à 100 km/h sous la seconde ? Check. La livraison dans les temps ? Houlà, ça reste à prouver, d’autant plus que la livraison « tout court » n’est même pas garantie…
On pourrait en effet penser qu’après 9 ans d’attente, les commandes du Roadster seront enfin honorées. Quelle erreur ! Le loup se cache au paragraphe numéro 4 du contrat de réservation de la supercar volante : « vous comprenez que le Roadster est encore en phase de développement au moment de signer ce contrat et que, par conséquent, nous ne pouvons garantir ni la date de livraison de votre véhicule, ni même s’il sera livré ».
À lire aussi : le Tesla Roadster pourra-t-il rouler (et voler) en France ?
Un chèque de 250 000 $ versé… sans même connaître le prix final
En sachant qu’il faut débourser jusqu’à 250 000 $ pour effectuer la réservation, il y a de quoi l’avoir en travers de la gorge. Surtout que vous serez juste placé en liste d’attente lorsque Tesla sera enfin prêt à mettre les véhicules en production. Inutile donc d’espérer avoir l’engin dans votre garage à ce stade. D’ailleurs, le prix du nouveau Roadster n’a même pas été communiqué, ce qui n’est guère rassurant quant à l’attente se profilant.
Le même contrat stipule en effet que « le prix d’achat estimatif du véhicule, s’il est indiqué, n’est qu’une estimation. Tesla travaille encore sur les options, les fonctionnalités et les équipements du véhicule et ne peut donc pas encore confirmer le prix exact. Le prix définitif sera indiqué une fois que vous aurez configuré votre véhicule ». Le chemin est donc encore très long avant le lancement, normalement prévu pour 2028.
Pas d’interdiction de revente, mais des conditions très particulières
L’accord a beau poser des conditions assez inédites, il n’avance en revanche aucune interdiction de revente. C’est pourtant chose fréquente chez les marques lançant des modèles exclusifs imposant une attente importante. Pour éviter que le véhicule ne soit revendu uniquement pour faire de la spéculation et briser les délais aux acheteurs les plus pressés, remettre immédiatement la voiture sur le marché est alors interdit.
Ce n’est pas le cas pour le Roadster, alors même que les Cybertruck Founders Series et Model S Signature Edition ont bien été concernés par cette interdiction. Une bonne chose, même si les réservations du Roadster ne sont pas transférables. L’autre bonne nouvelle, c’est que l’acompte versé pour la réservation est entièrement remboursable si vous changez d’avis ou que Tesla soit effectivement dans l’impossibilité de livrer le véhicule. C’est bien le minimum…

articles.title: Apple rachète Samplab, l'app d'édition audio dopée à l'IA
articles.text:
Apple a repris en juin une partie des actifs de Samplab, une start-up suisse spécialisée dans l'édition audio par IA, et propose un poste à une partie de ses salariés. L'accord n'a été rendu public que lundi, via la liste des acquisitions de la Commission européenne.
Samplab proposait une application et des plug-ins pour retoucher un morceau note par note. Son service a fermé mi-septembre et son site redirige désormais vers Apple.com.
Samplab transformait un fichier audio en partition modifiable
Dans son avis, la Commission indique qu'Apple reprend, par l'intermédiaire d'une filiale, une partie des actifs de Samplab GmbH et propose un emploi à une partie de ses salariés. L'accord date du 17 juin. Samplab, fondée à Zurich en 2020 par Manuel Fritsche et Gian-Marco Hutter, compterait dix employés au maximum, et peut-être seulement ses deux fondateurs d'après LinkedIn. La start-up avait annoncé sa fermeture fin juin et prévoyait de rembourser le solde des abonnements annuels. C'est le DMA qui force APple a rendre cet accord public. L'entreprise est classée contrôleur d'accès (gatekeeper) et doit informer Bruxelles de ses opérations touchant aux services de plateforme, aux services numériques ou à la collecte de données.
Concrètement, Samplab convertissait un enregistrement audio en MIDI. Ce format ne contient pas le son, mais une sorte de partition numérique. Il indique quelles notes sont jouées, à quel moment et pendant combien de temps. Une fois l'audio converti, il est possible de modifier une note ou un accord sans réenregistrer. L'outil détectait les accords, calait le tempo et la tonalité de plusieurs échantillons pour obtenir un ensemble harmonieux, et séparait les "stems", c'est-à-dire les pistes d'un morceau (voix, guitare, batterie par exemple). Il permettait aussi de retoucher des notes dans un audio polyphonique, où plusieurs notes sonnent en même temps, sans toucher au timbre.
Apple n'a pas commenté l'opération. La firme de Cupertino pourrait intégrer la technologies dans ses applications, qu'il s'agisse de Logic Pro, GaraBand, ou Final Cut Pro. Souligons que les plug-ins de Samplab fonctionnaient déjà avec Logic Pro.
Cet accord arrive une semaine après celui de Huxe, une start-up fondée par d'anciens ingénieurs de NotebookLM, spécialisée dans les briefings audio et les contenus de type podcast générés par IA. Nous rapportions en janvier qu'Apple avait déboursé près de 2 milliards de dollars pour s'offrir Q.ai, une jeune pousse israélienne dont l'IA interprète les micro-mouvements du visage. Pour Samplab, le texte publié ne mentionne aucun montant.
Sources : AppleInsider

Para escolher a melhor TV de 50″, verifique especificações que vão fazer a diferença na exibição de conteúdos, como tipo do painel e tecnologias de otimização. Fique de olho em:
Não existe unanimidade, já que a escolha varia com base no portfólio e experiências individuais. Mas um levantamento da Counterpoint indica que Samsung, TCL, Hisense e LG (nessa ordem) dominaram o envio global de TVs no primeiro semestre de 2026.
Sim. TVs de 50 polegadas têm telas relativamente grandes para mais imersão durante as jogatinas. Esses televisores também costumam oferecer imagens em 4K — resolução compatível com consoles de última geração. No entanto, se a taxa de atualização é um fator decisivo para sua gameplay, é importante ficar atento, já que muitos modelos de TVs de 50″ (geralmente mais baratos) se limitam a 60 Hz.
A distância entre o sofá e a TV deve ser de no mínimo 1,5 metro para um televisor de 50 polegadas. A metragem tem como base uma das referências usadas pela indústria, que define o tamanho de tela ideal ao usar a distância entre sofá e TV (em centímetros) e dividir o valor por três.
No entanto, o gosto pessoal do usuário também interfere nessa escolha e, por isso, as distâncias podem variar.
Uma TV de 50 polegadas tem diagonal de 127 cm, considerando que cada polegada equivale a 2,54 cm. E também costuma ter entre 110 cm e 115 cm de largura, e cerca de 65 cm de altura, com variações de modelo para modelo.
Depende das suas preferências de usabilidade. O Tizen se destaca pela integração com aparelhos Samsung e vários anos de atualizações, enquanto o webOS da LG é conhecido pela interface intuitiva. Já o Google TV é baseado no Android TV e costuma oferecer recomendações de conteúdo mais personalizadas.
QLED e QNED são tecnologias de telas similares baseadas em displays LCD retroiluminados por LEDs (ou MiniLEDs) com filtro de pontos quânticos para melhorar a reprodução de cores.
Essas Smart TVs ocupam o segmento intermediário premium, abaixo de TVs OLED. O termo QNED é proprietário da LG, enquanto marcas como Samsung e TCL adotam o QLED.
Já UHD é a sigla de “Ultra High Definition” (ou “Ultra Alta Definição”, em tradução livre). O termo se refere à resolução de 3840 x 2160 pixels, conhecida como 4K, e geralmente acompanha modelos com painéis mais simples, como a linha Crystal UHD da Samsung ou a série LG UHD 4K.

articles.title: Ahold Delhaize: Cyberattack affects services across US and Europe
articles.text:
Ahold Delhaize, one of the world's largest food retail chains, confirmed that last week's cyberattack disrupted services at stores across Europe and the United States.
Right before the cyberattack was disclosed, customers couldn't use websites, apps, and customer service platforms at Albert Heijn, Etos, and Gall & Gall stores in the Netherlands, and Delhaize in Belgium, while employees at the Stop & Shop American regional supermarket chain reported having trouble accessing their schedules and pay stubs.
When BleepingComputer asked right after the incident whether it also affected both corporate and store systems and whether any devices were encrypted during the attack, an Ahold Delhaize spokesperson redirected us to the company's statement.
In a Monday update, Ahold Delhaize said the cybersecurity incident announced last week forced it to take some systems offline, including its brands' websites and apps, causing service issues, although stores remained open to serve customers.
While most store websites and apps in Central and Southeastern Europe (CSE) are now online, the company says it's still working to restore some systems and services for European and US brands that remain down.
"Albert Heijn's website and app are back online, with home deliveries expected to resume from Friday, October 23. The Etos and Gall & Gall websites are also available for customers. E-commerce services at our Ahold Delhaize USA brands are expected to come back in the coming days. In Belgium, e-commerce is now fully operational," Ahold Delhaize said.
"As part of our response, we notified the Dutch National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) within 24 hours of discovering the malicious activity and have continued to provide timely updates to the NCSC, law enforcement and other relevant regulatory authorities. Today, Ahold Delhaize has filed a formal police report with the Dutch police.
The retail giant did not share further details that could interfere with response efforts or compromise security measures protecting its systems, but noted that an ongoing investigation has not yet found evidence that sensitive customer, associate, or partner data was stolen in the incident.
"Although this incident was caused by the malicious actions of others, we apologize for the inconvenience this has caused - especially to our customers," said Frans Muller, President and CEO of Ahold Delhaize.
This is the second major cyberattack to affect Ahold Delhaize's systems in recent years, after the personal, financial, and health information of over 2.2 million individuals was stolen in a November 2024 attack that impacted the company's U.S. systems and was claimed by the ransomware group INC Ransom.
The multinational retailer employs more than 384,000 people and operates 9,551 stores serving 77 million customers each week across the United States, Europe, and Indonesia.
