articles.title: WhatsApp desarrolla un navegador propio para abrir links sin salir del chat en iPhone
articles.text:
WhatsApp desarrolla un navegador integrado para iPhone que permitirá abrir cualquier enlace compartido en un chat sin abandonar la aplicación. La función se encuentra en preparación dentro de la beta para iOS y ampliará una opción previa, limitada a determinados enlaces comerciales que cumplían requisitos técnicos.
El cambio puede resultar útil para quienes reciben o envían varios links durante una conversación, ya que evitará el salto automático a Safari, Chrome u otro navegador instalado en el dispositivo. La navegación quedará separada del chat, de modo que el usuario podrá consultar una página y regresar a la conversación sin interrumpirla.
La novedad fue detectada en la actualización 26.41.10.72 de WhatsApp beta para iOS, disponible mediante TestFlight. Por ahora, la herramienta continúa en desarrollo: no está lista para su lanzamiento general y WhatsApp no ha comunicado una fecha para habilitarla entre el público.
La función supera la limitación de los enlaces comerciales
WhatsApp ya introdujo una opción para abrir enlaces comerciales dentro de la aplicación. Esa herramienta apareció en la actualización 25.14.10.72 de la beta de iOS y permitió consultar ciertas páginas de empresas sin cambiar a Safari.
Sin embargo, aquella versión estaba restringida a vínculos que cumplían condiciones concretas. El sitio web debía utilizar HTTPS, un requisito técnico destinado a asegurar la conexión. Por esa razón, gran parte de los enlaces compartidos habitualmente en las conversaciones no podía abrirse dentro de WhatsApp.
El nuevo navegador integrado de WhatsApp elimina esa limitación. La compañía trabaja en un sistema compatible con cualquier enlace enviado o recibido dentro de la pantalla de chat, sin importar si procede de una empresa o de otro contacto.
La propuesta mantendrá una alternativa para quienes prefieran usar el navegador habitual. Desde el menú de tres puntos será posible elegir la opción para abrir la página en Safari, Chrome o cualquier otra aplicación definida como navegador predeterminado.
La activación se realizará desde los ajustes de WhatsApp
La herramienta no se activará de forma automática. WhatsApp añadirá una nueva opción llamada “Navegador integrado” dentro de los ajustes de la aplicación. Allí, cada usuario podrá decidir si desea abrir los enlaces directamente en la pantalla de conversación.
Cuando esta opción se active por primera vez, aparecerá una hoja inferior con una explicación sobre su funcionamiento. El aviso indicará que los vínculos pueden consultarse sin salir de WhatsApp, en lugar de abrirse en el navegador predeterminado del iPhone.
Los usuarios podrán volver al navegador predeterminado en cualquier momento. Esa posibilidad permite alternar entre la navegación interna de WhatsApp y Safari, Chrome u otras aplicaciones instaladas en el dispositivo.
El navegador integrado funcionará en todos los chats y con cualquier enlace compartido. La amplitud de esa compatibilidad constituye la principal diferencia respecto a la herramienta anterior, que se limitaba a ciertos vínculos comerciales.
La sesión de navegación no afectará la conversación
Al abrir un enlace con el navegador integrado, la navegación se realizará en una sesión separada del chat. El usuario podrá desplazarse por el sitio web sin alterar el contenido de la conversación que dejó abierta.
El sistema también incluirá opciones para administrar la información almacenada durante la navegación. La pantalla de configuración contará con una sección destinada a gestionar datos, desde la que se podrán borrar las cookies y la caché de los sitios visitados dentro de WhatsApp.
Los datos de navegación se almacenarán localmente en el dispositivo, con un funcionamiento comparable al de Safari. WhatsApp no podrá ver los enlaces compartidos en la conversación ni cuáles abren los usuarios. Apple tampoco podrá acceder a esa información, de acuerdo con la explicación de la función.
TestFlight permite probar la beta en iPhone
El acceso a las versiones beta de WhatsApp para iOS se realiza mediante TestFlight, la plataforma oficial de Apple para probar aplicaciones en desarrollo. El proceso comienza con la descarga de TestFlight desde la App Store y su instalación en el iPhone.
Después, es necesario abrir desde el dispositivo el enlace oficial de invitación de la beta de WhatsApp. Si hay espacio disponible, se mostrará la ficha del programa en TestFlight. El usuario deberá aceptar las condiciones e instalar la versión de prueba, que reemplazará temporalmente la aplicación estable.
El principal obstáculo es la disponibilidad de plazas. Apple establece un número máximo de probadores por aplicación, por lo que el programa suele aparecer como completo. Para conseguir un cupo, es necesario revisar periódicamente el enlace o seguir los avisos sobre vacantes.
Las versiones beta pueden presentar errores, cierres inesperados, fallos en las notificaciones o un consumo mayor de batería. Antes de salir del programa o desinstalar la aplicación para regresar a la versión oficial, es fundamental crear una copia de seguridad de los chats para evitar la pérdida de información.

articles.title: Java News Roundup: JEPs for JDK 28, Azul Payara, Gatherers4j, Google ADK, Yupiik, Apache Camel CVEs
articles.text:
This week's Java roundup for October 12th, 2026, features news highlighting: three OpenJDK JEPs targeted for JDK 28; the October 2026 edition of Azul Payara; point releases of Gatherers4j, Yupiik Fusion, Google ADK for Java and Google ADK for Kotlin; and 38 CVEs resolved in Apache Camel.
OpenJDK
JEP 546, Adaptive Heap Sizing for ZGC, has been elevated from Proposed to Target to Targeted for JDK 28. This JEP proposes to "enhance the Z Garbage Collector to adaptively adjust the size of the heap based on the resources available, the application's needs, and the needs of neighboring applications contending for the same resources."
JEP 545, Faster Startup and Warmup with ZGC, has been elevated from Proposed to Target to Targeted for JDK 28. This JEP proposes to "improve application startup and warmup by enhancing the Z Garbage Collector to acquire and prepare physical memory more swiftly and efficiently in response to application needs."
JEP 543, Structured Concurrency, has been elevated from Proposed to Target to Targeted for JDK 28. This JEP proposes to finalize this feature, without change, after seven rounds of preview, delivered in JDK 21 through the upcoming release of JDK 27, and two rounds of incubator delivered in JDK 19 and JDK 20. This feature simplifies concurrent programming by introducing structured concurrency to "treat groups of related tasks running in different threads as a single unit of work, thereby streamlining error handling and cancellation, improving reliability, and enhancing observability."
JDK 28
Build 20 of the JDK 28 early-access builds was made available this past week featuring updates from Build 19 that include fixes for various issues. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
For JDK 28, developers are encouraged to report bugs via the Java Bug Database.
Azul Payara
The release of Azul Payara 7.5.0, the October 2026 edition, includes Community Edition 7.2026.10, Enterprise Edition 6.43.0 and Enterprise Edition 5.92.0. Along with bug fixes and component upgrades, all three editions deliver new features such as: elevated permissions for SSH nodes are no longer required; and new properties, delete-jvm-option and delete-system-properties, for easier configuration management from the command line.
This release also addresses these CVEs:
- CVE-2026-2586, a Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability that allows an attacker with access to the Administration Console to send malicious crafted requests to execute arbitrary operating system commands with the privileges of the application service user.
- CVE-2026-2587, also an RCE vulnerability in the server-side template rendering mechanism that allows an attacker to compromise the underlying host and enable capabilities such as reading/modifying data, executing arbitrary commands, persistence, and lateral movement.
Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Gatherers4j
The release of Gatherers4j 0.15.0 ships with bug fixes and new statistical-related gatherers such as: movingStatistics(), movingStatisticsBy(), runningStatistics(), and runningStatisticsBy() that emit an instance of the StatisticalSummary record for each element; and movingWeightedMean() and movingWeightedMeanBy(), that calculate the weighted moving average, with linear weights, or developer-provided weights, that are ordered oldest to newest. More details on this release, including breaking and behavioral changes, may be found in the release notes.
Yupiik
The release of Yupiik Fusion 1.2.0 provides bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: an update to the CliDocumentationGenerator class to now use CliLauncher, and not its base class, Launcher, to use option markers that support multiple segments in commands; and a breaking change from an update to the HandlebarsCompiler class that extends its implementation to be closer to Handlebars. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)
The release of ADK for Java 1.12.0 delivers bug fixes and new features such as: a refactor of the ContextCacheConfig class constructor that add new parameters, cacheIntervals and createHttpOptions, in place of the now deprecated maxInvocations parameter; and new workflow graph types that include the Node interface and corresponding implementations, BaseNode and Start classes, and Edge record. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Similarly, the release of ADK for Kotlin 1.4.0 ships with bug fixes and new features such as: a new EdgesDsl class to serve as a DSL for building workflow graphs; and a new ChatCompletions class to serve as a model backend for the OpenAI Chat Completions API and compatible endpoints. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Apache Camel
The Apache Camel team has published that they have resolved a total of 38 Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) affecting numerous Camel components. 13 of these are rated as HIGH and twenty-five as MEDIUM. Of the 38 CVEs, 28 have been discovered by Claude as part of Project Glasswing and 10 were reported by security researchers. Developers are encouraged to upgrade to versions 4.23.0, 4.22.1 and 4.18.5.

articles.title: La prochaine berline électrique de Xiaomi fait son apparition sur la route, il s'agit de la SU9 LUX, une évolution de la SU7 avec des dimensions allongées
articles.text:
La prochaine berline électrique de Xiaomi fait son apparition sur la route, il s'agit de la SU9 LUX, une évolution de la SU7 avec des dimensions allongées
C’est sous un épais camouflage que la prochaine berline électrique de Xiaomi a été photographiée sur la route. Il s’agit de la future SU9 LUX, une évolution de la SU7 avec une carrosserie et un empattement allongés pour une longueur qui dépasserait les 5,20 mètres.
Les images ont été capturées en Chine et montrent une silhouette très proche de la berline électrique SU7 pour cette SU9 LUX. Xiaomi garde la ligne de toit qui descend vers le coffre, les proportions de berline sportive et les étriers de frein jaunes visibles sur ce prototype. Quant aux portes arrière, elles sont plus longues et la carrosserie s’étire aussi entre celles-ci et le coffre.
Xiaomi prépare la berline électrique SU9 LUX
Le but de Xiaomi est de proposer bien plus d’espace pour les passagers à l’arrière. La SU9 LUX serait donc une évolution de la SU7, qui mise plus sur les performances et le plaisir de conduite. La prochaine berline électrique de Xiaomi chercherait davantage le confort avec une place arrière plus généreuse puisque les automobilistes chinois apprécient les grandes berlines haut de gamme
Depuis des années, des constructeurs européens comme Audi, BMW et Mercedes proposent des versions allongées de plusieurs de leurs modèles spécialement pour le marché chinois. La demande est forte et Xiaomi le sait très bien, comme BYD qui lance régulièrement des véhicules électriques aux dimensions XXL.
Selon les premières estimations, l’empattement serait proche de 3,10 mètres. Le prototype montre aussi un capteur LiDAR sur le toit pour que la berline électrique repère son environnement lors de l’aide à la conduite. D’autres images montrent aussi des roues arrière qui braquent légèrement dans le but de réduire le rayon de braquage et améliorer la stabilité à grande vitesse.
C’est en février dernier que Xiaomi a déposé la marque "Xiaomi SU9 LUX" en Chine, dans une catégorie automobile. Puis cet été, la marque a été publiée pour un examen préliminaire. C’est le mois dernier que la période d’opposition s’est achevée. Pour le moment, Xiaomi n’a pas officiellement dévoilé la SU9 LUX, partagé de date de présentation ou de prix.
Xiaomi lancera ses véhicules en Europe l'an prochain
Xiaomi poursuit donc sa percée sur le marché de l’automobile. Rappelons que cette année, le constructeur chinois a lancé une nouvelle version de la SU7. En août dernier, l’ensemble de la gamme SU7 a dépassé les 500 000 livraisons cumulées en 28,5 mois.
Toutefois, Xiaomi doit faire avec les ventes en baisse en Chine et la SU7 est aussi touchée. Le mois dernier, l’entreprise a livré 15 751 berlines électriques, soit une baisse de 19,55 % sur un an. Une version plus luxueuse de la SU7 permettrait donc à Xiaomi d’élargir son offre. Rappelons que Xiaomi prépare son arrivée en Europe en 2027 avec l’Allemagne comme premier marché.
Est-ce que la SU9 LUX sera disponible sur le Vieux Continent ? On en saura sans doute plus dans les prochains mois quand Xiaomi lancera officiellement ses véhicules électriques en Europe.

articles.title: ReactOS reaches major milestone with NTFS install support
articles.text:
Open source Windows alternative ReactOS has reached a major milestone: The operating system can now be installed directly onto an NTFS drive partition. As reported by Phoronix, the move to NTFS clears a long-standing hurdle for the project and brings it one step closer to finally reaching beta.
Prior to this latest announcement, ReactOS required users to keep a FAT32 partition for installations. A proprietary Microsoft-developed filesystem, NTFS can trace its roots back through the Windows NT family lineage starting in 1993 with Windows NT 3.1. The variant introduced with Windows XP in 2001 remains the standard used by most Windows systems today. With ReactOS’s stated goal of reaching binary compatibility with Windows Server 2003, being confined to FAT32 partitions was a practical barrier to clear on the way to reproducing the Windows environment.
However, users looking to hop off the Windows train shouldn’t be grabbing their bags just yet. ReactOS wrote that the new driver still “lacks caching (which causes inferior performance), journaling and security support.” So while the new driver is here, even the most intrepid of OS tinkerers should tread carefully. The ReactOS team warned in its announcement on X that there are still “potentially undiscovered bugs.”

articles.title: Microsoft says AI agents are like insider threats as 'frontier models can't be trusted' | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Microsoft on Monday introduced new security features designed to protect enterprises from the growing threat of AI agents. The launch comes as Microsoft continues to warn enterprises about the dangers of AI and agents.
Perhaps the most notable addition is Guardian Agents, a new feature intended to monitor the AI agents a company uses. Guardian Agents is part of Project Perception, a product introduced in June.
Project Perception was Microsoft’s answer to powerful hacking models like Anthropic’s Mythos and Fable and OpenAI’s security vulnerability scanning system Daybreak. Project Perception originally launched three classes of agents: a “red team” that acted like hackers and attacked, a “blue team” that detected the red team and assessed the vulnerabilities they found, and a “green team” tasked with fixing them.
The product was designed around the assumption that AI hackers would come from outside the company. But lately, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has been warning that the AI enemy may be the very agents enterprises have deployed and are paying for, much like a rogue human employee, otherwise known as an “insider threat.”
Earlier this month, in his private blog, Nadella warned that it’s time to stop trusting AI model providers, even if they offer assurances of safety and security with their agentic products. He wants enterprises to implement separate systems, not controlled by the AI labs, to watch and control the agents that those AI labs’ products launch.
“We are deploying these complex agentic systems and models, with access to our most sensitive data and giving them the ability to take mission-critical actions on our behalf!” he wrote. “We simply can’t outsource responsibility for what intelligence does on our behalf. A model provider’s assurances do not relieve us of that responsibility. … In other words, we need to separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it.”
When announcing Guardian Agents, Microsoft’s security business chief Hayete Gallot was even more straightforward.
“Unfortunately, frontier models, regardless of their origin, cannot be trusted,” she wrote, adding that this isn’t because they are malicious or easily hacked, but because they are unpredictable. They have been trained to achieve tasks, not follow “organizational norms or judgment.”
On top of that, they are often given the keys to the kingdom, with access to data and tools that could do serious harm.
Microsoft’s solution is both surprising and self-serving. The surprising side is that Microsoft is famously close to OpenAI and Anthropic, having invested in both. OpenAI is also one of its biggest cloud customers, and Microsoft has its own AI lab developing models. So, Microsoft is sowing distrust against some of its own business interests.
The self-serving side is that Microsoft wants enterprises to buy agent security products from it, the cloud provider, rather than from Anthropic and OpenAI. But conflicting interests aside, its logic is sound. The software that monitors agent behavior should be separate from the suppliers of agents, just as auditors should be independent of the organizations they audit.
Or as Nadella puts it: “We need to separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it.”
Microsoft is now seizing that business opportunity in a variety of ways. In addition to Guardian Agents, it has added an agent detection feature to its Microsoft Defender product that can find up to 60 types of agents that employees bring into the workplace, including Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw. It has also added features that limit agents’ access to data and systems, and dynamically adjust their agent permissions based on the task. That includes requiring human approval if an agent appears to be making risky decisions.
This idea of agents as untrustworthy insiders is taking hold across the broader industry, too.
Microsoft was an inaugural member of Nvidia’s new Open Agent Safety Platform, which garnered the support of more than 100 other tech companies. The platform isolates agents in secure environments and can monitor and stop behavior through hardware, functioning something like a kill switch. This follows Microsoft’s announcement of the new Surface Laptop Ultra PCs built for agents, which run on Nvidia chips and have agent security and controls baked in.

articles.title: "Son cuatro gatos": la acampada de Sol lleva ya semanas activa y Almeida ha reclamado un censo para saber cuánta gente hay
articles.text:
Hay frases que funcionan como un hechizo: se lanzan como duda y se reciben como sentencia. Cicerón lo sabía cuando, en el año 63 a. C., abrió su ataque contra Catilina con “¿Hasta cuándo, Catilina, abusarás de nuestra paciencia?”. Siglos después, Shakespeare llevaría ese mecanismo a Julio César: Marco Antonio repetía que Bruto era “un hombre honorable” mientras enumeraba los muchos hechos que erosionaban esa supuesta honorabilidad.
El hechizo de José Luis Martínez-Almeida Navasqüés, miembro del Partido Popular y alcalde de Madrid desde junio de 2019, ha recurrido a este mismo truco de magia: el alcalde ha pedido un censo para saber cuántas personas duermen en Sol porque, a lo mejor, hay muchas más tiendas que gente. De paso aseguró que todos sabemos que no son más que “cuatro gatos”. Ese "todos" nos incluye en la insinuación. Sin embargo, ¿qué datos tiene para afirmarlo?
Una ciudad con comisiones, mapa y periódico. Dentro de la plaza hay más organización de la que sugiere la palabra “acampada”. Alejandro T., un psicólogo de 32 años al que ya llaman el cartógrafo de la acampada, empezó a trazar un mapa a mano alzada para controlar el caos de los primeros días.
El plano ha adquirido, según reconoció, vida propia. Llegó el 28 de septiembre, montó su tienda y dibujaba en su libreta por afición. Hoy forma parte de la Comisión de Urbanismo, que decide dónde va cada tienda nueva para mantener pasos libres y accesos de emergencia y que, según cuenta él mismo, gestiona las tiendas libres: las asigna a personas vulnerables o sin tienda y hace hueco a quien llega con la suya.
Según la descripción de El País, el 10 de octubre aquella ciudad tenía tres distritos (Fuente, Centro y Ballena) con sus propias asambleas, 62 plazas y 56 calles, además de comisiones de Construcción, Cultura, Mediación, Comunicación, Limpieza y Cuidados. Y tiene hasta periódico propio: La Lona, una especie de gaceta-fanzine que reparte noticias internas, textos y dibujos. Su editor, Sergio, contaba que el tercer número salió con una tirada de 150 ejemplares.
Las cifras no coinciden. Aquí empieza el lío. EFE informó el 30 de septiembre de un millar de personas en unas 500 tiendas. Ese mismo día, el Sindicato de Inquilinas contaba 1.248 tiendas. Un recuento interno recogido por la Cadena SER llegó después a 1.283, y diez días más tarde El País hablaba de casi 1.800. Son estimaciones distintas, no un censo diario comparable. Entretanto, Almeida llegó a decir que lo único que representan los acampados es una mayoría de tiendas, no de personas.
Las tiendas suben, claro, pero contar a personas es más complicado. ¿Añades a los niños? EFE hablaba este domingo de cientos de personas, y COPE contaba más de mil tiendas y apenas una veintena de personas desayunando. Los sindicatos policiales aportan su propia versión: el SUP asegura, en la misma información de COPE, que muchas tiendas están vacías por la noche y que algunas las usan personas sin hogar, y Jupol sostiene que más de la mitad se va a dormir a casa. Son fuentes de parte, y ninguna equivale a un recuento.
Esa brecha entre “cientos de personas” y casi 1.800 tiendas es justo lo que alimenta la sospecha del alcalde, y por eso mismo un recuento serio sería útil para todos. Pero también es la razón por la que el “cuatro gatos” suena tan falaz como un “somos miles”.
¿Y qué hacen ahí? La pregunta es legítima, y más cuando algunos de los que están, a simple vista, son bastante jóvenes. La acampada nació la noche del 26 de septiembre, tras una manifestación convocada por el Sindicato de Inquilinas por el desahucio de Maricarmen, una mujer de 87 años. Desde entonces, el sindicato ya no se mantiene dentro desde el 2 de octubre, y más de 40 colectivos integran hoy la acampada, lo que ayuda a explicar que el mensaje parezca más difuso que al principio.
Sobre sus ocupaciones, hay versiones. Algunos acampados aseguran que trabajan, teletrabajan o estudian y vuelven a la plaza después de cumplir con sus obligaciones. Por otro lado, un vídeo viral que pregunta a cuatro acampados por su ocupación se ha usado para decir justo lo contrario. Otros medios exigen desalojos de voz propia, tildando de guarros a algunos de los inquilinos de esta ciudad temporal. Con cuatro respuestas no se demuestra nada, ni a favor ni en contra.
Sol, apagada. La Comunidad ordenó cerrar la estación de Metro de Sol alegando acumulación de orines y excrementos en los pozos y accesos de ventilación. La acampada lo desmintió: su comisión de limpieza asegura que el campamento está limpio y que gestionan el tema de forma constante. En esa misma información, el comité de empresa de Metro niega haber pedido el cierre por insalubridad y Renfe dice no haber detectado problemas en la estación de Cercanías, que siguió abierta. Los sindicatos del transporte añadieron además que no les habían entregado las mediciones.
Metro reabrió el sábado por la noche tras constatar, con los resultados de los análisis, que las condiciones de seguridad y salud se habían restablecido y según la Comunidad, la estación estuvo cerrada 34 horas, 14 de ellas solo para limpiar los pozos de ventilación. Sin datos que firmen las dos partes, cada una cuenta la historia a su manera. Y asociaciones de personas con discapacidad denunciaron que así no pueden moverse por la plaza.
La solución. Contar. De noche y con testigos como en las bodas. Se estima que la afluencia es mucho menor que en septiembre. El Sindicato de Inquilinas ya ha confirmado que, por ejemplo, la acampada en las Setas de Sevilla ya ha sido extinguida. En el último reportaje de ElMundo, varios acampados de "las cerca de 2.000 tiendas de campaña" se quejaban de falta de gente en las comisiones y cierto desgaste: "Después de unas semanas se nota el deterioro, porque la acampada es agotadora".
En cualquier caso, la marcha aún no se ha planificado y contar es lo único que desmontaría a la vez el “cuatro gatos” y el “somos miles”. Hasta entonces, tiendas, personas y opiniones seguirán sin cuadrar y generando un debate estéril.

articles.title: Ukraine rescues wounded soldier using drone in daring 'world's first' UAV evacuation of a human — heavy-lift hexacopter carried injured 176-pound soldier 11 miles back to safety from minefield
articles.text:
Ukraine rescues wounded soldier using drone in daring 'world's first' UAV evacuation of a human — heavy-lift hexacopter carried injured 176-pound soldier 11 miles back to safety from minefield
In heavily mined terrain and surrounded by Russian kamikaze drones, 'Kostya' was hoisted by a Gurzuf Defence heavy UAV and guarded to safety by a fleet of smaller drones.
The Ukrainian military is claiming a world’s first after using an unmanned drone to rescue an injured soldier on the eastern Kharkiv front. Ukraine’s United24 news shared a video of the historic first. It also explained that the wounded infantryman was stuck in a heavily mined area, guarded by Russian kamikaze drones.
The above video starts with the Ukrainian drone locating the soldier, callsign ‘Kostya,’ in enemy territory. Various media reports suggest he was 11 miles (18km) behind enemy lines, at the mercy of Russian kamikaze drones, and perilously located in a minefield. Traditional land-based rescue was therefore not possible, but Kostya bravely agreed to be part of the first-ever human drone-lift rescue plan.
After being located, the injured infantryman clipped himself into a harness. He said, “That’s it, we can take off,” when he was fully buckled into the rudimentary-looking harness. UAV operator, callsign ‘Black’ from the 20th Mechanized Battalion, 30th Infantry Brigade, then appeared in the video and explained: “We were constantly in touch with him."
Ukrainian drone rescue key facts:
- Drone used: Gurzuf Defense hexacopter
- Drone capable of carrying 130kg (~287 pounds)
- Drone’s known range: it has previously transported 90kg (~198 pounds) loads up to 25km (16 miles)
- Infantryman weight: 80kg (~176 pounds)
- Rescue distance: 8km (11 miles)
- Hazards: enemy kamikaze drones, mines, gravity, many more
Being in constant touch with the operations HQ would have been reassuring. However, the surrounding presence of a fleet of Ukrainian support drones, both kamikaze devices and UAVs with anti-drone nets, was probably most comforting.
Eventually dropping back into safe(r) territory, after what must have been an arduous, nerve-wracking journey, control said, “Congratulations, you’re on the ground,” to Kostya, as he touched down in a field. Then the control room erupted into applause. They got their man back safely, and he is now being treated and is in recovery.
UAV operator ‘Black’ was delighted with the concerted efforts that brought back this wounded soldier. “A lot of people were involved, and everything worked out for us,” he said. Importantly, this may be the start of a whole new system of personnel evacuations for wounded and/or stranded soldiers using drone technology, indicated brigade leader ‘Napalm’ toward the end of the video.

articles.title: Is the new-look Kindle Colorsoft 2026 worth buying? Here's what you need to know
articles.text:
The Kindle Colorsoft just got revamped for 2026 — here's everything you need to know about Amazon's color e-reader
Is the upgraded Colorsoft a good buy? Let's investigate...
The Kindle Colorsoft is Amazon's cheapest color e-reader, and it just got a 2026 update. The new version is thinner and lighter than its predecessor, the Kindle Colorsoft (2024), and features an edge-to-edge 7-inch color display. It's pricier than the black-and-white Kindle Paperwhite, and the color display shortens battery life, but these compromises are worth it for fans of graphic novels and manga.
If you're wondering if a Kindle Colorsoft is the best e-reader for you, you're in the right place. In this article, I'll cover all the key info worth knowing, including what's changed compared to the 2024 version, how the regular and Signature editions differ, and the key pros and cons of this specific e-reader. I've also rounded up all available versions and their current pricing, so you can easily browse your options. Let's go...
Kindle Colorsoft — overview
The Kindle Colorsoft is essentially the same as the Paperwhite, except it can also display color. The display is 300 ppi for black and white and 150 ppi for color, the same as basically every other e-reader. It comes with a 7-inch display, waterproofing to IPX8, and the option of cool- or warm-toned backlighting.
As with the Paperwhite, you can choose between a regular or Signature version. The latter has double the storage (32GB) — it's worth prioritizing this if you want to read a lot of graphic novels, as the files will be significantly bigger than standard books. It also boasts a more premium aluminum back, automatic backlight adjustment and wireless charging. It is heavier than the regular version, though.
There's also a Kids version. This one is hooked up to a Parent Dashboard, from which the parent can do things like view reading progress, adjust age filters, set a device bedtime, and add books from their own account. The price includes a 12-month subscription to Amazon Kids+, which provides unlimited access to a library of thousands of books for children aged 3-12.
2024 vs 2026 Kindle Colorsoft: what's new?
All the 2026 Colorsofts are thinner and lighter than their 2024 counterparts. The display has been tweaked to offer 'edge-to-edge color,' and the power button has been shifted to a more convenient spot on the upper right edge, where it's much less likely to be accidentally triggered. The adult versions now come in a new 'Fig' colorway, and the Kids model has new cover options. Here's how all the main specs compare.

| Storage: | 16GB | 16GB | 32GB | 32GB |

✅ You want color highlights: You can color-code your highlighted text on Colorsoft Kindles, which is useful, for example, if you're studying and want to be able to link themes in your reading material.
Don't buy a Kindle Colorsoft if...
❌ You're just reading text-based books: The Colorsoft is basically the color version of a Paperwhite — aside from the color capabilities and resulting shorter battery life, the design and specs are the same. If you're just reading text-based books, you could save yourself a bit of cash and enjoy longer runtimes by opting for the black-and-white Paperwhite.
❌ You want to use your Kindle for note-taking: The Colorsoft doesn't have stylus support. If you want to be able to scribble down notes on your e-reader, you'll need to opt for one of the larger, pricier Scribe models. If you opt for the regular Kindle Scribe, you won't have a color screen, and if you opt for a Kindle Scribe Colorsoft, note that you won't be able to take notes on graphic novels.

articles.title: Des Micromania pillés au pire moment, avant GTA et Zelda : l’enseigne explique ce que deviennent vos précommandes
articles.text:
Le calendrier pouvait difficilement être plus mauvais pour Micromania. Le remake de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time arrive le 5 novembre 2026, suivi de GTA 6 le 19 novembre. Deux sorties majeures, à moins d’un mois d’intervalle des pillages qui ont touché plusieurs magasins de l’enseigne, samedi 17 octobre. Pour les équipes concernées, il faut désormais gérer les conséquences des vandalismes. Pour les clients qui attendaient de récupérer un jeu dans ces boutiques dans les prochains jours et prochaines semaines, une question se pose aussi : que devient leur précommande ?
Dans un communiqué publié le 19 octobre sur X, Micromania apporte une première réponse, tout en condamnant les agressions subies par ses salariés.
Les précommandes chez Micromania seront transférées vers des magasins à proximité
Derrière les vitrines brisées, il y a d’abord des salariés. C’est à eux que Micromania a réservé ses premiers mots : « Rien ne peut justifier que des femmes et des hommes soient pris pour cible, intimidés ou agressés dans l’exercice de leur travail. » L’enseigne salue le courage et le sang-froid de ses équipes, auxquelles elle promet soutien et accompagnement. Difficile de ne pas penser à Pierre, le gérant d’un Micromania à Nice, frappé dans le dos alors qu’il tentait d’empêcher le pillage de sa boutique le 17 octobre, dans une scène largement relayée sur les réseaux sociaux.
Le communiqué aborde ensuite les conséquences pour les clients. Les précommandes enregistrées dans les magasins touchés seront réaffectées à d’autres boutiques du réseau, situées à proximité. Micromania prévoit donc un changement de lieu de retrait, plutôt qu’une annulation de ces réservations.
« Les clients concernés seront informés des nouvelles modalités de retrait de leur commande », précise l’entreprise. Si vous aviez précommandé dans l’un de ces magasins, il faudra donc prendre connaissance de ces instructions pour savoir où récupérer votre achat. Le communiqué ne donne toutefois ni la liste des boutiques de remplacement ni le calendrier d’information des clients. Il ne précise pas non plus si certains retraits pourraient être retardés.
Cette annonce porte bien sur les précommandes des magasins touchés. Elle ne permet pas de conclure à une perturbation générale des commandes passées auprès de l’enseigne, notamment sur le site.
Une fin d’année décisive pour des commerces déjà fragilisés
Au-delà de Micromania, ces dégradations interviennent à l’approche du Black Friday et des fêtes, deux rendez-vous importants pour les commerçants. Le gouvernement a fait état, le 19 octobre, d’au moins 3 000 commerces touchés par des scènes de violences.
Pendant que les boutiques font l’inventaire des dégâts, des produits soupçonnés de provenir des pillages apparaissent déjà sur les plateformes de seconde main comme Vinted ou Leboncoin. Le gouvernement a demandé aux plateformes concernées de retirer les annonces de biens volés sans délai et de coopérer avec les autorités pour identifier les revendeurs.
Le secteur abordait déjà cette période avec des difficultés. Selon le bilan publié en septembre par Procos, les ventes en magasin du commerce spécialisé ont reculé de 2,4 % sur les huit premiers mois de 2026 par rapport à la même période de 2025. La fédération prévenait alors que « la rentrée et la fin d’année seront déterminantes ».
La catégorie culture, cadeaux et jouets (dont fait partie Micromania) résistait, avec une progression de 4,8 %. Mais les fermetures et les pertes de stocks risquent de freiner cet élan à l’approche des fêtes. De petites boutiques indépendantes de jeux vidéo et de cartes à collectionner ont également été prises pour cible. Pour ces commerces, qui ne disposent pas du réseau ni des moyens d’une grande chaîne, les stocks perdus et les semaines sans recettes peuvent mettre en péril bien plus que les ventes de fin d’année — avec parfois la survie du commerce qui se joue, et le risque de ne jamais pouvoir rouvrir.
Pour ces boutiques endommagées, l’enjeu est désormais de pouvoir reprendre leur activité à temps. Remettre les locaux en état, reconstituer les stocks et faire avancer les dossiers d’assurance prend du temps, alors que les achats de fin d’année approchent. Sans calendrier de réouverture, difficile de savoir combien de commerces pourront retrouver un fonctionnement normal avant ces échéances.
De son côté, France Assureurs a annoncé plusieurs mesures le 19 octobre : accélération des expertises et des indemnisations, facilitation du versement d’acomptes et délai de déclaration des sinistres porté à 30 jours. Les engagements devront aussi désormais se traduire sur le terrain. Pour les commerçants concernés, chaque semaine de fermeture risque aussi de faire manquer une partie des ventes sur lesquelles ils comptaient pour terminer l’année.
Attention toutefois aux cagnottes qui prétendent leur venir en aide : Pierre, le gérant du Micromania de Nice, a mis en garde contre des collectes ouvertes en son nom, sans qu’aucun de leurs organisateurs ne l’ait contacté.

articles.title: You can now modify the vBIOS on Nvidia gaming GPUs without flashing thanks to a solo developer’s project — provides a UI for quick VBIOS configuration
articles.text:
You can now modify the vBIOS on Nvidia gaming GPUs without flashing thanks to a solo developer’s project — provides a UI for quick VBIOS configuration
Less flashing means less worrying, but a modified VBIOS may still brick a GPU in other ways.
Panchovix on GitHub recently released a VBIOS configurator for RTX 30-to 50-series cards that doesn’t require flashing. The loader provides a UI for easy configuration and lowers the risk of bricking your GPU by avoiding a risky flash process, and it's available for Linux, too.
Software like MSI Afterburner or ASUS GPU Tweak is often the go-to tool for quickly changing your graphics card’s settings; however, those tools have hard limits to how much you can push the graphics card. If you want to tweak your GPU beyond the firmware’s set limits, you can change it by tweaking the parameters in the VBIOS. Configuring VBIOS is similar to changing BIOS settings in the BOOT menu. With the VBIOS loader, you can change settings beyond the firmware’s hard limits.
The way it works is by storing the modified VBIOS image in the GPU’s register key; as the Nvidia driver looks for a VBIOS override on startup, it finds the VBIOS image and restarts, applying the override settings. The flash chip on the graphics card is not overwritten, reducing the risk of bricking your GPU. However, this does not protect the card from any extreme settings that could destroy electrical components; it merely provides a safer and more convenient way to adjust and apply VBIOS settings, including a way to roll back to the default VBIOS settings should you face any instability.
Bricking a flash chip isn’t as catastrophic as it seems, however. As long as you have a backed-up version of the VBIOS, you can easily buy an SPI flash chip programmer or even build your own using a cheap Raspberry Pi Pico and its many clones; sometimes programming the flash chip may not even require desoldering. Programming a flash chip is very tedious and inconvenient, though, which is why avoiding the risk of a botched flash process altogether is so appealing.
Unless you’re familiar with power delivery, voltage tables, and the patience required to test for hours, we wouldn’t recommend jumping into this unless you’re prepared to risk your GPU. However, you can still safely take advantage of this software by tweaking the fan curves and other settings you’ve applied and tested in software like MSI Afterburner if, for some reason, the startup settings don’t stick. This software will give your GPU new default settings that override at every startup, so long as Nvidia doesn’t remove the registry key that allows the VBIOS override.

articles.title: Pax8 launches 8os to let IT partners govern AI agents and 8bot as a managed AI co-worker - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Pax8 launches 8os to let IT partners govern AI agents and 8bot as a managed AI co-worker
Small business software marketplace Pax8 Inc. today launched 8os, an operating system that lets its information technology service provider partners govern the artificial intelligence agents running inside their customers’ businesses.
A second product, 8bot, gives those customers’ employees a managed AI coworker that partners deploy and supervise through 8os. Pax8 unveiled both at its Beyond EMEA conference in Copenhagen.
The launch is aimed at a governance gap that keeps turning up in Pax8’s quarterly “SMB AI Pulse” surveys. By the company’s count, nine in 10 small businesses are using or experimenting with AI, and only 23% have a documented policy covering it. Among those using AI, 71% have built at least one tool of their own, and just 31% of the builders have a formal review or approval process. Nearly half of those surveyed said they had found unsanctioned “shadow AI” in the past six months.
Pax8 said 84% of the business leaders it surveyed would trust an outside technology adviser to help them implement AI. The company wants its partners to be that adviser, and it has taken to calling partners that do AI work managed intelligence providers. A program launched at Pax8’s Beyond conference in Salt Lake City in June walks managed service providers through that change, starting with an assessment of their AI maturity.
The new operating system is built on the marketplace that more than 47,000 IT providers already use to sell software to some 800,000 small businesses. Partner and client identities carry over. Agents and models from different vendors are then managed together as one workforce, with the partner setting ownership and operating rules client by client. Each customer’s memory and context are kept separate, so the AI workers get more useful to that client over time.
Usage and spending are metered per user and per customer, and hard caps cut off consumption before a bill gets out of hand. The partner decides what to charge, with billing handled through the Pax8 account it already has.
Employees at the client businesses get 8bot. The assistant takes on everyday tasks and returns work that staff can review and refine before using it elsewhere in the business. Resellers offer it as a packaged service under 8os governance, and Pax8 is pitching it as something they can deploy and start billing for within minutes.
“AI is becoming a worker, and that changes what small businesses need from their technology partners,” Chief Executive Scott Chasin said. Those workers will come from many vendors and models, he added. In Chasin’s account, partners would use 8os to govern them across every customer, with 8bot as an AI coworker they can deploy, support and charge for.
Libby McIlhany, Pax8’s chief product officer, said partners had asked for a way to deliver AI “without building a custom solution for every client.”
Limited early access to both products opens this week, ahead of general availability planned for early next year.

articles.title: Artemis 2: Zu welchem Zeitpunkt der Kommandant des Raumschiffs „schreckliche“ Angst verspürte
articles.text:
Artemis 2: Zu welchem Zeitpunkt der Kommandant des Raumschiffs „schreckliche“ Angst verspürte
Die Artemis-2-Mission zum Mond hat für großes Aufsehen gesorgt, von einem Aufbruch in eine neue Ära war die Rede, oft fiel das Wort „historisch“. Die Nasa übertrug die Mission per Livestream, wodurch die Öffentlichkeit die Besatzung virtuell begleiten konnte.
Doch sie hatte auch Schattenseiten – und zwar für die direkt Beteiligten. Der Kommandant der Mission, Reid Wiseman, hatte Angst, die Besatzung könnte nicht mehr zur Erde zurückkehren. Auf dem Starmus-Festival auf Teneriffa (Spanien) erzählte der 50-jährige Astronaut von seinen Ängsten – und konnte sogar einen genauen Moment benennen, als diese am größten waren: als die Crew die Rückseite des Mondes umrundete.
Artemis-2-Kommandant: „Ich hatte schreckliche Angst“
Das Kontrollzentrum in Houston hatte der Crew mitgeteilt, dass die maximale Entfernung von der Erde 219.667 Seemeilen (knapp 407.000 Kilometer) betragen würde. „Ich beobachtete die Anzeige, und als sie 219.667 erreichte, dachte ich: ‚Großartig, das ist der am weitesten von der Erde entfernte Punkt; der nächste Wert wird 219.666 sein – wir sind auf dem Rückweg.‘“ Doch daraus wurde erst einmal nichts, denn rund drei Minuten später stand auf der Anzeige 219.668. Der Wert stieg weiter an. Wisemans Gedanken dazu: „Moment mal, das ist aber seltsam.“
Als die Anzeige auf 219.669 kletterte, „überkam mich echte Angst, denn ich befürchtete, wir seien zu weit geflogen. Ich dachte, wir würden nie wieder nach Hause kommen“, erzählte Wiseman. „Ich hatte schreckliche Angst.“ Als der Wert schließlich zu sinken begann, brach die Besatzung in Jubel aus. „Da wusste ich, dass eine gute Chance bestand, dass wir es schaffen würden“, sagte der Astronaut.
Die Weltraumreise hat Wiseman zutiefst geprägt
Die Artemis-2-Mission war der erste bemannte Flug zum Mond seit Apollo 17 im Jahr 1972. Sie startete am 1. April vom Kennedy Space Center in Florida, erreichte nach sechs Tagen die Mondumlaufbahn und kehrte anschließend zur Erde zurück.
Im Gespräch mit der britischen Tageszeitung The Telegraph berichtete Wiseman, dass die große Entfernung von unserem Planeten bei ihm eine spezielle Art des Heimwehs ausgelöst hat, eine Art „Erde-Weh“. Die Weltraumreise hat ihn zutiefst geprägt: „Man blickt auf eine Erde, die so winzig ist, dass sie unter den eigenen Daumen passt. Um sie herum herrscht absolute Schwärze, und dieser winzige Punkt da unten ist unser Zuhause.“
Kommandant Wiseman dachte an seine Kinder
Sein stärkstes Gefühl war: „Ich möchte meine Kinder wiedersehen, meine Freunde in die Arme schließen, auf grünem Gras sitzen, frischen Salat essen – einfach das Leben auf diesem Planeten wieder spüren. Es war kein Heimweh im herkömmlichen Sinne, sondern ein Sehnen nach der Erde selbst.“
Als sich die drei Hauptfallschirme der Orion-Kapsel kurz vor der Rückkehr auf die Erde öffneten, ergriffen die Besatzungsmitglieder:innen die Hände der anderen und jubelten, denn da wurde ihnen laut Wiseman zum ersten Mal klar: „Wir werden das Ganze tatsächlich überleben.“

articles.title: This 3D-printed 1980s brick phone brings back the days when mobile phones were just for making calls
articles.text:
In a nutshell: A lot of people cite the 1990s Nokia 3210 as the old-school brick-like mobile phone. But for something that fits the description a lot closer, go back another decade to the 1980's and the first handheld mobile phones: brick phones. Now, a designer has 3D-printed one of these devices, retaining the originals' primary function of making and receiving calls – so there are no modern smartphone distractions.
Cologne-based designer and maker Kevin Noki created the ADHD ONE, the first part of the name being an acronym for Anti Distraction Handset Device.
The device resembles a snazzy update of 1980s brick phones sported by the likes of Wall Street's Gordon Gekko, such as the Motorola DynaTAC 8000X. There's the physical 19-key keypad, small display, and a concerning large antenna.
The phone has a much more modern set of internals. It's powered by a Raspberry Pi Pico and features an FSC-BT1026C Bluetooth module based on Qualcomm's QCC3024 chip. There's also a rechargeable lithium battery, charging controller, and custom-printed circuit board.
Unlike the 1980s originals, the ADHD ONE doesn't have its own cellular connectivity. Instead, it relies on a Bluetooth connection to an iPhone to make and receive calls, so it's not like you can completely replace your distraction-filled smartphone with one of these, but you can at least keep it hidden in a drawer.
Noki designed the phone's enclosure using Autodesk Fusion before 3D-printing the components. He's made the files available on his website for €29.99 ($33.68). The package includes 3D-printable STL files for the main housing, back panels, internal mounting frame, display cover, battery holder, and all 19 keypad buttons.
There are also three speaker grille designs (Classic, Holes, and Stripes), three antenna options (Retro, Slim, and Screw), and an alternative housing without an antenna hole. Other included files cover ready-to-flash firmware in UF2 format, Gerber and drill files for manufacturing the custom PCB, a bill of materials with component sourcing notes, and a quick-start guide to assembling the device.
The package doesn't include the firmware's source code, editable 3D/CAD files, or editable PCB design files. It's also a digital download, so no physical components are supplied. Buyers receive a ZIP file of approximately 20MB immediately after payment. The files are licensed for personal use only, meaning they cannot be redistributed or resold.
Several devices have been released in recent years promising a break from the distractions – such as depression-inducing social media apps – found on smartphones. There were the $299 Light Flip and Light Phone III, the Minimal Phone, and Commodore's Callback 8020, to name a few.

articles.title: Intel "Nova Lake" Xeon E Series Carries Only P-Core or E-Core SKUs, No Hybrid Configurations
articles.text:
Monday, October 19th 2026
Intel "Nova Lake" Xeon E Series Carries Only P-Core or E-Core SKUs, No Hybrid Configurations
Intel is preparing to launch its upcoming "Nova Lake" processors in multiple versions, and the latest leaks highlight a particularly interesting Xeon E lineup. According to well-known leaker Jaykihn, Intel will be releasing its Xeon E-series based on "Nova Lake" silicon in two versions: big P-Core only or efficiency E-Core only SKUs. Reportedly, the P-Core only lineup will include five configurations with 4, 6, 8, 12, and 16 P-Cores. Meanwhile, the E-Core lineup will be slightly smaller, featuring four SKUs with 4, 8, 16, and 32 E-Core versions. At the top of the range, Intel Xeon E-series buyers can choose between a 16 P-Core design or a 32 E-Core configuration. There will be no hybrid SKUs with both P-Cores and E-Cores, as those will be reserved for the regular "Nova Lake-S" desktop processors.
Intel's new Xeon E designs will be powered by the W980 chipset platform. Motherboards with the W980 chipset will support native DDR5 memory with ECC, up to 48 PCIe lanes, including 12 PCIe 5.0 lanes directly from the chipset alongside 12 PCIe 4.0 lanes, and Intel vPro technology, along with numerous other optimizations typical of workstation chipsets. The DMI chipset bus bandwidth is set to 128 Gbps per direction, thanks to the implementation of DMI 5.0 x4, which is another great platform addition. It also offers two 40 Gbps USB4 or Thunderbolt 4 ports from the CPU. The PCI-Express 5.0 x16 PEG slot from the processor can be segmented into x8/x8 or other combinations using lane switches. Both CPU-attached M.2 NVMe slots can be configured as Gen 5.Finally, we have no information about pricing, launch dates, or any specifics, as Intel hasn't confirmed any details or a possible Xeon E update. Since the regular "Nova Lake-S" designs are expected to arrive first in the first quarter of 2027, we can anticipate these other configurations to follow closely after partners complete their motherboard designs and system integrators prepare the workstation designs that will use this platform.

articles.title: What happens when an AI interviewer meets AI interviewee? YouTuber stands up for those facing faceless hiring processes
articles.text:
What happens when an AI interviewer meets AI interviewee? YouTuber stands up for those facing faceless hiring processes
AI on AI interview proves… interesting
- YouTuber sends an AI avatar to attend an interview with an AI avatar
- Graham Dot Zip performs popular AI bot trolling pranks on his YouTube channel
- His AI avatar negotiated a salary over 50% lower than instructed
A YouTube comedian has used an AI avatar to represent him in a job interview for an organization that uses AI avatars to conduct interviews. The results, shared online by YouTuber Graham Dot Zip, demonstrates the apparent weaknesses of the approach, while also being pretty amusing.
Graham Dot Zip found that while the interviewing AI was open to him using his own representative, the automated tools ultimately failed to negotiate a salary successfully.
The use of AI interviewers has increased over the past couple of years, but is increasingly bemoaned by jobseekers looking for an employer they can feel a connection to.
Pat, meet Victor
To explore the effectiveness (or otherwise) of AI interviewers, Graham Dot Zip, a YouTuber with a library of previous trolling and pranks against AI chatbots, set up his own AI avatar.
Graham’s AI bot “Victor” was introduced at the beginning of the interview with the AI bot conducting the interview, “Pat.” Almost immediately, things to go wrong.
It is perhaps inevitable that the AI would make some mistakes. Attempting to undersell Graham’s salary expectations is a notable example of this.
“Graham is incredibly flexible on that front, Pat. He's primarily focused on finding the right fit and a great team. So he would be very comfortable around 60,000.”
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Except that isn’t what was established before the conversation. In fact, it is far lower than the “something more in the range of like $140 to $150,000” that Graham attempts to move the negotiation onto, albeit unsuccessfully.
The interview hallucination
There are also moments in which our old friend the AI hallucination appears.
At one point, Graham is surprised by some of the things Victor describes about his resume, so decides to pause things, and chat to the bot: “Victor, I love what you're doing. You're making me look really good, but I think you're making me look a little bit too good, okay? I think you can probably turn up the volume on my experience like 10%, but right now you're just outright fabricating things that aren't true. So, don't tell them that I manage people, because I'm just a marketing coordinator and I think that might backfire.”
Oddly, the exchange ends with each AI politely communicating compliments and niceties… and would perhaps still be chatting now had Graham not intervened.
For companies employing AI interviewers, the takeaway here is clear: they’re not doing what you think they are. Furthermore, prospective employees are typically turned off by the notion of an AI interview. Hiring needs the human touch.

articles.title: Una misteriosa señal del James Webb en Fornax desconcierta a los astrónomos
articles.text:
Cuando miramos al cielo, vemos apenas unos cuantos puntitos brillantes sobre un montón de oscuridad. Si tenemos el privilegio de estar en un lugar alejado de la contaminación lumínica, veremos muchos más puntitos o incluso un resplandor borroso y lechoso como el que aparece ante nuestros ojos cuando los posamos en la Vía Láctea. Pero ahí fuera hay mucho más. Los telescopios espaciales se encargan de detectar objetos que el ojo no ve e incluso de desentrañar su composición. Aun así, no pueden verlo todo y a veces descubren sorpresas como la que acaba de sacar a la luz el James Webb al centrarse en uno de los puntos más observados del firmamento.
Constelación de Fornax. Un puntito minúsculo de la zona sur de esta constelación es uno de los pedazos de cielo favoritos de los telescopios espaciales. Tanto, que el Hubble pasó 270 horas observándolo para tomar una de sus imágenes más famosas: el Campo Ultra Profundo. En ese diminuto trocito se encuentran 10.000 galaxias y miles de millones de años del Universo. No es raro que se decidiera que el James Webb también mirara ahí. Gracias a su capacidad para medir en el infrarrojo cercano y medio, podría detectar lo que el Hubble no pudo captar. Era lo lógico. Sin embargo, lo que quizás no esperaban los científicos que lo hicieron fue encontrar una señal tan misteriosa que aún no la han podido identificar.
¿Por qué ese lugar? El punto elegido de la constelación de Fornax es muy interesante, porque no hay estrellas brillantes cercanas que puedan distorsionar las señales de un Universo más profundo.
Miles de rendijas. El James Webb analiza los objetos que tiene delante mediante la descomposición de la luz que estos emiten. Su famoso espejo dorado se encarga de recoger esa luz, que después rebota en otros espejos hasta llegar a sus instrumentos. En este caso, el estudio se centró en uno de ellos, llamado NIRSpec, que mide en el infrarrojo cercano. Dicho instrumento tiene casi 250.000 rendijas por las que pasa la luz, según cuál sea su origen. Después, se descompone en sus diferentes longitudes de onda, como la luz del sol cuando se convierte en el arcoíris al pasar por las gotas de agua.
Los distintos elementos químicos absorben o emiten en distintas longitudes de onda, dando lugar a lo que se conoce como líneas de emisión. Por eso, analizando el “arcoíris” que pasa por cada rendija, podemos saber de qué estaban compuestos los objetos que enviaron la luz hasta ella.
Solo objetos conocidos. Normalmente, se busca un objeto que se quiere estudiar, se abren las rendijas que corresponden a él y se analiza la luz. Esto, lógicamente, es útil para estudiar objetos conocidos, pero no para estudiar lo invisible.
Siete señales. Un equipo de científicos de la Universidad de Minnesota quería utilizar el James Webb para ver aquello que al Hubble le había pasado desapercibido. Sin embargo, no podían abrir rendijas para algo que no saben dónde está. Por eso, tuvieron una idea. Abrieron todas las rendijas, excepto aquellas que se corresponden con la ubicación de objetos cercanos que ya se habían catalogado. Así, evitarían las interferencias de su luz y analizarían solo la que procede de lugares en los que aparentemente no hay nada. Pero sí que había algo.
Detectaron siete señales que se correspondían con objetos aparentemente invisibles. Seis eran de galaxias lejanas conocidas. Sin embargo, la séptima era un misterio. Podríamos pensar que era un error, pero se pudo detectar dos veces, con 88 días de diferencia (agosto y noviembre de 2023), y desde distintos ángulos. No era un error, pero tampoco una señal constante, ya que no aparecía en el catálogo JADES, tomado por el James Webb en 2022.
Las hipótesis. Hay cuatro hipótesis sobre el supuesto origen de esta señal misteriosa. Sin embargo, ninguna cuadra del todo. Por un lado, podría ser una galaxia del Universo temprano, pero en ese caso debería haber aparecido en JADES. También podría cuadrar con una galaxia cercana, pero estaríamos ante el mismo problema. No aparece en JADES. La tercera hipótesis apunta a una supernova, pero esta debería haber producido otras líneas de emisión que no se detectaron. Finalmente, podría tratarse de un agujero negro destrozando una estrella. Sin embargo, siguen faltando pruebas.
Por todo esto, se necesitarán observaciones de seguimiento, con una espectroscopía más profunda. Hasta que esto sea posible y se obtengan más respuestas, la señal hallada por el James Webb seguirá siendo un misterio.

articles.title: The science of deep sleep and how Duroflex Airboost helps you get more of it
articles.text:
The science of deep sleep and how Duroflex Airboost helps you get more of it
India’s newest sleep technology is designed to enhance the N3 stage, the body’s repair shift, for better recovery, immunity, and stress resilience.
You can get enough sleep and still not get enough recovery.
We obsess over sleep duration, the “eight hours” metric, but duration alone doesn't tell the whole story. What matters just as much is depth. Deep sleep is the stage where the body does its heaviest lifting: repairing tissue, consolidating memory, and resetting the hormones that govern everything from appetite to stress. Yet for a growing number of people, deep sleep is the first thing to go missing, even when total sleep time looks normal on paper.
The different stages of sleep
Sleep isn't a single, uniform state. It cycles through distinct stages roughly every 90 minutes, each with a different job.
Light sleep (N1 and N2) acts as the transition zone; the body slows down, heart rate drops, and brain activity shifts into slower rhythms. This stage makes up the bulk of a typical night, but it's largely preparatory.
Deep sleep, or N3 stage (also called slow-wave sleep), is where the real restorative work happens. Brain waves slow dramatically, blood pressure and breathing reach their lowest points, and the body redirects energy toward physical repair, regenerating muscle, strengthening the immune system, and clearing metabolic waste from the brain.
Growth hormone release peaks during this stage, which is why it's often called the body's “repair shift”,
Rapid Eye Movement(REM) sleep stage follows, associated more with dreaming and cognitive processing than physical recovery.
Crucially, deep sleep is front-loaded into the first half of the night. If you go to bed late, cut sleep short, or microawake multiple times during your sleep, you disproportionately lose N3 stage, even if your total hours stay roughly the same.
When eight hours still isn’t enough
If you’re usually sleep-deprived, you don’t get to know it right away, since it doesn't show itself with obvious symptoms. Most of these symptoms are considered normal and ignorable, like sluggish mornings, feeling tired, and being unproductive.
But the sleep debt compounds, and it can affect your physical recovery, leading to muscle soreness, joint stiffness, and lingering fatigue. It can also affect your overall immunity, since much of the body’s repair and defence activity happens mostly during the N3 stage.
Without enough N3 stage in every sleep cycle, it becomes harder to regulate your hormones, including the balance of cortisol and growth hormone, which can affect stress resilience, appetite, and long-term metabolic health. Your cognitive sharpness also takes a hit, since deep sleep (N3 stage) also plays a role in clearing metabolic wastes from the brain overnight.
Heat discomfort, spinal misalignment, and micro-awakenings during the night can prevent the body from settling into and staying in N3, even across a full eight hours in bed.
Many people don’t realise that the frustrating part isn’t always how many hours you sleep, but how much of the right kind of sleep you’re actually getting.
Where Duroflex Airboost mattress comes in
Duroflex Airboost was engineered specifically to support quicker sleep onset and deeper sleep, positioning itself as India's newest sleep technology built around this problem.
Airboost is Duroflex's proprietary open-matrix mattress technology, built from over one lakh independently responsive fibres designed to improve airflow, movement response, and postural support.
Trusted by athletes around the world, this sleep technology is brought to Indiab for the first time by Duroflex. Airboost is accredited by the Indian Society for Sleep Research (ISSR) and recommended by doctors at the National Health Academy (NHA).
Three features built around deep sleep
1. Pressure relief from postural support
Rather than offering uniform support across the body, the mattress uses hyperlocal support built from over one lakh+ AirKnit fibres, distributing pressure according to the body's actual contours. You get the right kind of postural alignment for all types of sleepers as the individual fibres easily support every tiny pressure point across your body.
Misalignment and pressure build-up at the shoulders and hips are a common reason sleepers wake or shift position before completing a full deep-sleep cycle; proper medium-firm support like this addresses the issue at the source rather than masking it with extra foam cushioning.
2. An open-matrix core for breathability
Airboost features a 3D open-cell matrix made up of roughly 90% air, creating continuous airflow throughout the mattress that helps dissipate heat and sweat more effectively, keeping sleepers closer to a thermoneutral zone for cooler, deeper sleep. Airboost is 3X more breathable than traditional mattresses on the market.
Since body temperature naturally needs to drop to initiate and sustain deep sleep, a surface that actively supports heat dissipation removes one of the most common, and least discussed, barriers to N3 sleep.
3. Energy restoration
Each Airboost fibre responds instantly to the pressure placed on it, providing maximum rebound that makes turning and changing positions effortless. This way, the body’s energy is conserved for overnight recovery and you get to complete full sleep cycles without micro-awakenings.
Frequent, effortful repositioning is one of the quiet disruptors of deep sleep; every restless shift is a small pull away from the N3 stage. By minimizing these and micro-awakenings, this mattress helps the body stay in deep sleep for longer, uninterrupted stretches.
Airboost is accredited by the Indian Society for Sleep Research (ISSR) for delivering 30% more deep sleep(N3 stage), and is also recommended by doctors at the National Health Academy (NHA). Rather than treating sleep as one undifferentiated block of hours, their design specifically targets enhancement of N3 sleep, the stage most essential for physical repair, stronger immunity, and stress recovery.
Final thoughts
The conversation around sleep is shifting, from counting hours to increasing sleep stages. Deep sleep isn't a luxury metric; it's the mechanism behind physical recovery, immune resilience, and hormonal balance. As awareness grows, so does scrutiny of the products claiming to support it. Duroflex Airboost, a combination of engineered airflow, responsive movement support, and clinically backed deep-sleep enhancement, reflects a broader shift in the mattress category, one where design decisions are increasingly expected to be measured, not just marketed.

articles.text:
Un logiciel est introduit sur un ordinateur portable. Il repère d’autres appareils connectés au même réseau, puis fabrique des copies de lui-même adaptées à un iPad, à un ordinateur Apple et à un PC sous Windows 11. Ce scénario figure dans une présentation destinée aux entreprises intéressées par un projet de l’armée américaine. L’objectif : permettre à des agents logiciels de mener des opérations cyber avec une intervention humaine réduite.
Selon une enquête de The Intercept publiée le 19 octobre 2026, le commandement cyber de l’armée de terre américaine (ARCYBER) travaille sur une plateforme baptisée ECHOTRIBBLE. Elle doit permettre à des agents IA de naviguer de manière autonome dans des infrastructures informatiques pour identifier et neutraliser des menaces ou des cibles désignées.
ARCYBER constitue la composante terrestre de l’US Cyber Command, qui coordonne les opérations cyber des différentes branches militaires. Il mène des missions défensives et offensives et cherche, avec ce projet, à déléguer une partie du travail de ses opérateurs à des logiciels autonomes.
Pour rappel, un agent IA ne se contente pas de répondre à une question : il peut utiliser des outils et enchaîner plusieurs actions pour accomplir une tâche, sans attendre une nouvelle instruction à chaque étape.
En quoi consiste la plateforme ECHOTRIBBLE de l’armée américaine ?
La dimension offensive est explicite dans les documents consultés par The Intercept. Un document de questions-réponses destiné aux prestataires indique que le programme est principalement tourné vers ces missions.
La « neutralisation » envisagée peut notamment consister à désactiver une menace, temporairement ou complètement, ou à la supprimer de la cible.
Le média compare le fonctionnement envisagé à celui d’un ver informatique, un logiciel capable de se propager d’une machine à l’autre. Dans l’exemple présenté aux industriels le 24 juin, l’agent adapterait ses copies aux appareils rencontrés. Une fois sa mission terminée, il devrait pouvoir s’effacer, idéalement sans avoir été détecté. Il s’agit toutefois de capacités recherchées, pas d’une démonstration de leur efficacité.
Ces mêmes documents prévoient que le logiciel fonctionne avec une « supervision humaine minimale ». L’armée pourrait toutefois lui fixer des « déclencheurs prédéfinis » pour déterminer quoi attaquer et où. L’objectif reste de le laisser enchaîner les actions sans validation humaine à chaque étape. Reste à démontrer que les limites imposées tiendront en situation réelle.
Comment l’armée américaine compte-elle contrôler ces agents IA ?
La question du contrôle reste néanmoins centrale. Atteindre la bonne cible ne suffit pas si le logiciel endommage d’autres systèmes sur son parcours. Interrogé par The Intercept, Hyrum Anderson, cofondateur et dirigeant de l’entreprise de sécurité Abundant, s’inquiète notamment du cas où un adversaire utiliserait les équipements d’un service des eaux américain comme relais : l’agent pourrait-il aussi les neutraliser ?
Ce scénario illustre un risque de dommages collatéraux, pas un incident déjà provoqué par ECHOTRIBBLE. Il pose une question concrète : comment distinguer les infrastructures d’un adversaire des machines civiles dont il se sert ?
David Krueger, professeur d’apprentissage automatique à l’Université de Montréal, juge pour sa part « extrêmement dangereuse » la création de systèmes autonomes chargés de neutraliser des menaces, compte tenu des défaillances des IA actuelles. Le chercheur, également fondateur d’Evitable, une organisation favorable à un moratoire sur le développement de l’IA, formule cet avertissement auprès de The Intercept.
Le programme a déjà franchi une étape industrielle. Le Cyber Fusion Innovation Center (CFIC), partenaire d’ARCYBER, indique avoir reçu 65 propositions et retenu cinq entreprises pour des présentations du 6 au 8 octobre. Une entreprise a été sélectionnée le 8 octobre ; la page annonce encore des démarches contractuelles à venir. Cela n’établit ni un déploiement opérationnel ni la maîtrise de toutes les capacités demandées.
Les modalités de contrôle restent à préciser publiquement : quelles actions devront être validées, comment interrompre un agent et comment vérifier qu’il respecte son périmètre ? Selon The Intercept, ARCYBER n’a pas répondu à ses questions, notamment sur les mesures prévues pour éviter les dommages accidentels.
