articles.title: Can a Simple App Really Fix PC Game Stutters?
articles.text:
Shader compilation stutter has plagued PC gaming for years, and a new application called Shader Compilation Stutter Killer, or SCSKiller for short, promises to do something about it. The idea is simple enough: compile shaders before launching a game rather than waiting for them to be compiled during gameplay. But does it actually work?
That's what we set out to find out, testing the application across several notoriously stutter-prone games. Along the way, we also discovered something rather interesting about shader compilation on Radeon GPUs. Something that could be a pretty big deal, and that we hadn't heard about before.
What's SCSKiller?
SCSKiller is a free and open-source application, so if you're interested, we recommend downloading it and giving it a shot for yourself. For those unfamiliar with shader compilation stutter, it's a common issue in modern PC gaming where a game briefly freezes or hitches the first time a new visual effect appears.
Some games attempt to address this by precompiling shaders before gameplay begins. The Last of Us Part I, for example, is famous for its lengthy shader compilation process.
Unfortunately, even games that precompile shaders can still suffer from horrific shader compilation stutter, while others don't bother precompiling much of anything, which can also lead to a poor experience.
Rather than relying on a game to compile shaders, either beforehand or on the fly, SCSKiller attempts to do the work before you launch it. The application scans game files, extracts the necessary shader code, and compiles as many shader pipelines as possible into the GPU driver's cache. The idea is that when you launch the game, those shaders are already compiled, so the driver doesn't have to interrupt gameplay to process new visual effects.
SCSKiller doesn't rely on a whitelist of specific games. Instead, it works at the engine level, with support for games built using Unreal Engine 4 and 5, Unity, RE Engine, and FromSoftware's engines, alongside a more generic approach for other DirectX 12 titles. It also supports DirectX 11 games on Nvidia GPUs.
For games where shader pipelines can't easily be extracted from the game files, SCSKiller includes an optional recorder. This allows you to play for a few minutes with recording enabled, after which the application can use the collected data to compile additional shaders.
It's important to understand that SCSKiller doesn't solve all forms of stuttering, because not every stutter you encounter is related to shader compilation. One of the biggest issues, particularly with Unreal Engine 5 games, has been traversal stutter, and SCSKiller can't address that.
In our opinion, traversal stuttering is generally more disruptive, as it can result in longer pauses when new environmental assets are loaded from local storage. This typically happens as you cross an invisible boundary within the game world, triggering the loading of additional assets. Perhaps we'll get a Shader Traversal Stutter Killer, or STSKiller, in the future. Fingers crossed.
The Drawbacks: Compilation Time, Storage, and Memory
There are some drawbacks to SCSKiller, though they're largely unavoidable consequences of how the application works. For starters, brute-forcing thousands of shader pipelines can take considerable time, depending on how many shaders need compiling and the performance of your CPU.
Of course, the advantage is that you can run the compilation process when you're not actively using your PC. Just be aware that it can pin CPU usage at 100% for extended periods, though with a properly configured system, that shouldn't be an issue.
SCSKiller also consumes additional storage space, and with SSDs at a premium right now, that's something worth considering. Compiling thousands of shaders increases the size of the GPU driver's shader cache. As a result, you may need to increase the cache size to prevent older compiled shaders from being removed.
Nvidia users can adjust this through the driver settings. The standard limit is typically 10 GB, but you can increase it to 100 GB or even set it to unlimited, preventing older shaders from being deleted as new ones are added.
Unfortunately, things are more restrictive for Radeon users. According to SCSKiller, AMD's driver has a fixed shader cache limit of 16 GB. We haven't independently confirmed that limit with AMD, but if accurate, it means Radeon owners can't simply increase the cache size. Once the cache reaches its limit, older entries are removed to make room for new ones. SCSKiller will then identify previously optimized games as needing to be compiled again.
This potentially limits the usefulness of SCSKiller on Radeon GPUs, particularly if you're trying to optimize a large library of games. That said, there's no need to panic. As we discovered during testing, AMD has some pretty interesting shader compilation behavior of its own, and we'll explore that shortly.
Test System and Methodology
For all of this initial testing, we used our Ryzen 7 9800X3D test system with 32 GB of RAM, initially paired with the GeForce RTX 5090. Later, we also tested the Radeon RX 9070 XT and GeForce RTX 5070 to investigate some interesting differences in shader compilation behavior.
We may explore additional hardware configurations in the future, particularly slower CPUs. For now, though, the goal was simply to determine whether SCSKiller actually works. As it turns out, we were able to demonstrate that quite clearly using the 9800X3D. So, let's get into the results.
Test System Specs
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D | 
| Motherboard | MSI MPG X870E Carbon WiFi [BIOS 7E49v1AA7] | 
| Memory | G.Skill Trident Z5 RGB DDR5-6000 32GB CL30 [CL30-38-38-96] | 
| Graphics Card | GeForce RTX 5090, GeForce RTX 5070, Radeon RX 9070 XT | 
| ATX Case | MSI Prospect 700R | 
| Power Supply | Kolink Regulator Gold ATX 3.0 1200W | 
| Storage | TeamGroup T-Force Cardea A440 M.2 PCIe Gen4 NVMe SSD 4TB | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 25H2 | 
| Display Driver | AMD Radeon Adrenalin 26.9.2 Nvidia GeForce Game Ready Driver 617.42 | 
Gaming Benchmarks
Star Wars Jedi: Survivor
We'll start with Star Wars Jedi: Survivor, a game famous for its numerous stuttering issues. Jedi: Survivor precompiles shaders when loading for the first time. For this initial test, both configurations were running the game for the first time immediately after completing that initial shader compilation process.
There are quite a few interesting things to note here. First, performance was substantially better with SCSKiller enabled, boosting the average frame rate by 25%, with a similar improvement to the 1% lows. However, you might have also noticed that the standard configuration was consuming around 60% more GPU power, at least at the beginning of the test. That difference gradually decreased to just under 40% by the end of our run.
Despite the game precompiling shaders when initially loading, there appears to be considerable additional shader compilation work taking place during gameplay, particularly in the early stages. This can reduce frame rates and increase the processing overhead associated with rendering new effects.
Something else worth noting is that SCSKiller increased system memory usage. We're looking at around 7% more RAM consumption in this example, apparently due to the additional precompiled shader data being buffered into system memory.
For our second Jedi: Survivor test, we loaded an earlier section of the game immediately after completing the first run. By this point, the game had already been running for quite some time. In terms of performance, the SCSKiller configuration was around 14% faster, though neither configuration suffered from what we'd consider shader compilation stutter.
Interestingly, SCSKiller was now consuming around 30% more system memory, representing almost 7 GB of additional RAM usage. That wasn't a problem for our 32 GB configuration, but it's certainly something to consider if you have less than 32 GB of system memory.
GPU power consumption also increased with SCSKiller this time, which makes sense given that we were rendering more frames. It also suggests the RTX 5090 was spending less time dealing with shader compilation work during gameplay. Although SCSKiller wasn't solving any noticeable shader compilation stutter in this particular example, since the standard configuration wasn't stuttering to begin with, it still managed to improve performance substantially.
It's possible that slower hardware would have exhibited more obvious stuttering with the standard configuration, but that's something we'll need to explore in future testing. It's also worth noting that despite consuming more system memory, SCSKiller didn't always improve frame rates. In another section of the game, performance was much the same between the two configurations. And as we mentioned earlier, SCSKiller can't fix traversal stutter, which remained clearly visible at several points throughout our testing.
Grounded 2
Another game reportedly affected by shader compilation stutter is Grounded 2, so we decided to take a look. However, with the hardware configuration we were testing, we didn't encounter any significant stuttering issues, at least in the sections of the game we examined.
Despite SCSKiller increasing system memory usage by around 5 to 6 GB, there were no measurable performance improvements. In this case, the application simply didn't provide any meaningful benefit.
Hogwarts Legacy
Another game we were particularly keen to investigate was Hogwarts Legacy, especially since the developer of SCSKiller specifically highlights performance improvements in this title. Unfortunately, we couldn't reproduce those improvements in our testing. Initially, we tested using the Ultra quality preset at 4K with Performance upscaling and ray tracing enabled.
Performance remained pretty poor even after running SCSKiller, particularly the 1% lows, and we couldn't identify any meaningful improvements to frame times. What we did see, however, was a substantial increase in system memory usage of over 20%, effectively maxing out our 32 GB capacity.
Concerned that the additional memory consumption might be preventing SCSKiller from delivering an improvement, we decided to retest with ray tracing disabled, which reduced overall memory usage. Unfortunately, that didn't change much. Performance was virtually identical between the two configurations. If anything, the standard configuration was slightly faster, while SCSKiller was now consuming over 50% more system memory without providing any measurable advantage.
Frame pacing was also largely unchanged. In a final attempt to reduce system memory usage, we dropped to the Medium quality preset, again with ray tracing disabled. But once again, frame rates and frame pacing were essentially identical between the two configurations. This time, SCSKiller increased system memory usage by around 25%, still without delivering any meaningful improvement.
So, what's going on here?
It's possible that our hardware configuration was influencing the results, though the SCSKiller developer also reported improvements using an RTX 5090. Alternatively, it could simply be that the section of the game we tested wasn't particularly affected by shader compilation stutter. Either way, we weren't able to reproduce the improvements claimed by the developer, despite testing several graphics configurations.
The Blood of Dawnwalker
The Blood of Dawnwalker is another game we've heard suffers from shader compilation stutter, though in our testing, the issue didn't seem particularly problematic. That said, SCSKiller did manage to deliver a reasonable performance improvement, presumably by making additional compiled shader data available in system memory.
By the end of our test, the 1% lows had improved by 15%, accompanied by a 6% increase in the average frame rate. That's a pretty decent improvement considering the application is free, assuming you have enough storage space and system memory available.
In this example, system memory usage increased by 33%, with SCSKiller consuming approximately 5 GB of additional RAM.
Silent Hill: Townfall
Another relatively new game we decided to examine was Silent Hill: Townfall. Unfortunately, performance was much the same between the two configurations, and SCSKiller wasn't able to eliminate the stuttering we encountered.
In fact, we observed more stuttering with SCSKiller enabled, though it's important to note that this was based on a single pass through the game. That's one limitation of this type of side-by-side testing, as stuttering behavior can vary between runs, so we wouldn't read too much into that particular result. Still, there was no evidence of a meaningful improvement in the section we tested.
Tiny Tina's Wonderlands: A Dramatic Improvement
Now, here's a game we know stutters like absolute buggery. Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is an Unreal Engine 4 title with so much shader compilation stutter that it's almost unplayable at times. And keep in mind, we're testing with a Ryzen 7 9800X3D and GeForce RTX 5090 here. The average frame rate looks pretty impressive, but the 1% lows tell a very different story. They're absolutely horrid.
The game does precompile shaders before you start playing, and while things improve as you spend more time in the same area, moving somewhere new often means it's Stutter City all over again. For example, we left our initial test area for a few minutes before returning. Despite having already explored that section of the game, it didn't take long for the shader compilation stutters to return.
Admittedly, they weren't quite as severe as before, but they remained pretty annoying, especially considering the hardware we were using. This is where SCSKiller really comes into its own. It transformed Tiny Tina's Wonderlands from a stuttery mess into an exceptionally smooth experience, eliminating the constant hitching we had been experiencing.
By the end of our test, the 1% lows had improved from just 45 fps to an incredible 147 fps. More importantly, the constant stuttering and hitching were completely gone in the section we tested. This was one of the most impressive results we'd seen so far, demonstrating SCSKiller can be effective when shader compilation is responsible for poor performance.
However, what happened next was arguably even more interesting.
AMD's Background Shader Compilation: An Unexpected Discovery
Having seen how dramatically SCSKiller improved performance on the RTX 5090 in Tiny Tina's Wonderlands, we decided to swap out the GeForce GPU for a Radeon RX 9070 XT. And we're glad we did, because the results were rather puzzling, but in a good way. What we observed was the first few seconds of gameplay after freshly installing the RX 9070 XT along with AMD's latest display driver. SCSKiller hadn't been used at all.
We simply allowed the game to perform its usual shader precompilation process before loading our save file. Yet, despite everything we'd just seen with the RTX 5090, the game ran perfectly smoothly. There was no noticeable stuttering whatsoever. We couldn't quite believe what we were seeing, especially after spending so much time testing the GeForce GPU, where the experience had been a complete mess.
We continued playing, exploring several new areas, but at no point did the game exhibit the same stuttering problems. This left us looking for answers. That's when we came across an extremely brief article on AMD's website titled AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition 26.9.2 Background Shader Compilation. This was the exact driver we were using for our testing. The article explains that AMD has expanded its DirectX 12 background shader processing support to Unreal Engine 5 games.
According to AMD, the functionality was already enabled for Unreal Engine 4 titles, along with several specifically named games, including Borderlands 3, Dirt 5, Cyberpunk 2077, Guardians of the Galaxy, Halo Infinite, and Tiny Tina's Wonderlands. AMD also notes that background shader compilation can reduce initial game loading times, though performance may be temporarily reduced while compilation is taking place. Because shader compilation is CPU-intensive, the time required to complete the process depends on the processor and overall system load.
For benchmarking purposes, AMD recommends allowing approximately 15 minutes of gameplay for background compilation to finish before recording performance measurements. The company also recommends excluding the first run of each new session when using an in-game benchmark. Based on that explanation, AMD appears to be saying that background shader compilation has already been supported in Unreal Engine 4 titles for some time, with Unreal Engine 5 support arriving more recently.
So the bigger news for Radeon owners is that AMD has been working on background shader compilation at the driver level, and its latest update expands that functionality to Unreal Engine 5 games. This was news to us. Admittedly, shader compilation performance isn't something we've investigated in detail for quite some time. There didn't appear to be much progress on the issue, so it had become one of those unfortunate realities of PC gaming that we'd more or less accepted.
But based on what we're seeing in Tiny Tina's Wonderlands, AMD appears to have effectively solved shader compilation stutter in this particular game. And what's particularly impressive is how quickly it happens. After a brief shader preparation process, we could simply load into the game and start playing without encountering any noticeable stutters. Meanwhile, the same game remained a complete mess on our GeForce GPUs without SCSKiller.
Tiny Tina's Wonderlands: Radeon vs. GeForce
Despite Tiny Tina's Wonderlands already running perfectly smoothly on the RX 9070 XT, we still wanted to see what would happen if we used SCSKiller. This was also when we discovered the apparent 16 GB shader cache limitation on Radeon GPUs. After precompiling the game's shaders using SCSKiller, we ran the test again and found virtually identical performance. SCSKiller increased system memory usage by approximately 2 GB, but this had no measurable effect on frame rates or frame pacing. In other words, AMD's standard driver configuration was already doing everything we needed.
For a better representation of image quality comparisons, check out the HUB video below:
For comparison, we also tested the GeForce RTX 5070 under identical conditions, both with the standard driver configuration and after using SCSKiller. As expected, the RTX 5070 suffered from severe shader compilation stutter when running the game normally. However, after using SCSKiller, those issues were completely eliminated in our test. The application also increased VRAM usage by around 4 GB, bringing it roughly in line with what we observed on the Radeon RX 9070 XT.
Comparing the two GPUs with their standard driver configurations reveals how significant AMD's advantage was in this particular game. Although average frame rates were similar, the 1% and 0.1% lows were substantially better on the Radeon GPU, with AMD's background shader compilation apparently doing an excellent job of preventing the constant interruptions we encountered on GeForce.
For a better representation of image quality comparisons, check out the HUB video below:
Now, compare the standard RX 9070 XT configuration against the RTX 5070 after using SCSKiller. Both GPUs delivered exceptionally smooth performance at roughly the same frame rates, with the GeForce GPU actually coming out ever so slightly ahead. That's a good result for SCSKiller, but it's also a demonstration of what AMD's driver is already doing.
What makes this particularly interesting is the amount of preparation required. For the RX 9070 XT, we literally installed the driver, restarted the system, loaded into Windows, and immediately launched Tiny Tina's Wonderlands. After the game's brief initial shader preparation process, we were playing without any issues.
For the RTX 5070 to deliver the same kind of smooth performance, we first had to install SCSKiller and then spend around 30 minutes precompiling shaders. Only after completing that process were we able to achieve the results shown here. So, at least in Tiny Tina's Wonderlands, AMD's driver implementation appears considerably more efficient at preparing shaders and avoiding compilation stutter. Very impressive stuff.
Final Fantasy VII Rebirth: Another Stutter-Filled Experience
Finally, we wanted to compare the RTX 5070 and RX 9070 XT in Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, another game we've heard suffers from severe shader compilation stutter. And unfortunately, those reports appear to be accurate. Starting with the RX 9070 XT, we compared the standard driver configuration against SCSKiller. Neither configuration was flawless.
It's worth noting that Final Fantasy VII Rebirth has a hard 120 fps frame rate cap, which is a little annoying for this type of testing. However, we're primarily interested in the 1% and 0.1% lows anyway, so the cap isn't a major concern. With the standard Radeon driver configuration, 1% lows remained above 60 fps, but there were still noticeable stutters, reflected in the 0.1% low results. SCSKiller certainly helped, though it wasn't able to eliminate every stuttering issue in this particular title.
While the RX 9070 XT wasn't perfect, its performance was considerably better than what we observed with the RTX 5070. In fact, the situation was remarkably similar to Tiny Tina's Wonderlands. With the standard GeForce driver configuration, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth was a stuttery mess. Whereas the Radeon GPU managed to keep its 1% lows above 60 fps, the RTX 5070 suffered from severe performance drops, with its 1% lows falling into single digits. Average frame rates were very similar between the two GPUs, but the 1% and 0.1% lows on the GeForce GPU were terrible.
Then we enabled SCSKiller. After precompiling shaders, the RTX 5070's performance problems were essentially eliminated. The jarring stutters disappeared, 1% lows remained well above 60 fps throughout our testing, and even the 0.1% lows were very good. Frame pacing was excellent, resulting in a completely transformed gaming experience.
We initially captured several minutes of gameplay, but continued playing beyond that and didn't encounter any further issues in the areas we explored. Comparing the RX 9070 XT and RTX 5070 with SCSKiller enabled on both GPUs produced very similar results. Interestingly, SCSKiller consumed more system memory with the RTX 5070 than with the RX 9070 XT. It's possible that this relates to the Radeon driver's more restrictive on-disk shader cache capacity.
Overall, SCSKiller helped improve performance on both GPUs, though the most dramatic improvement was clearly seen on the GeForce side.
Conclusion: Does SCSKiller Actually Work?
SCSKiller certainly took us down a rabbit hole we weren't expecting. At some point, we might conduct a more extensive investigation comparing Radeon and GeForce GPUs across a broader range of hardware configurations and games. For now, though, we can conclude that SCSKiller is genuinely useful and it can improve performance in games affected by shader compilation stutter.
That doesn't mean it's a universal solution. It doesn't address traversal stutter, and even in games where shader compilation is an issue, the benefits can vary significantly depending on the hardware and the sections being tested. In some titles, such as Hogwarts Legacy, we couldn't reproduce the developer's claimed improvements at all. In others, such as Star Wars Jedi: Survivor and The Blood of Dawnwalker, we observed respectable performance gains, even when the standard configuration wasn't exhibiting particularly severe stuttering.
Then there are games like Tiny Tina's Wonderlands and Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, where SCSKiller completely transformed the experience on our GeForce GPUs.
Of course, there are some practical considerations. Compiling shaders can take considerable time, particularly when dealing with thousands of pipelines. You may also need to repeat the process after driver or game updates, and the resulting shader cache can consume a substantial amount of local storage. SCSKiller can also increase system memory consumption considerably, which may or may not be a problem depending on your PC's configuration.
But the good news is that the application itself is free, and there's little downside to trying it in a game you're already having trouble with, provided you're mindful of storage requirements and anti-cheat compatibility. It's straightforward to download and use, and based on our results, certainly worth experimenting with if you're experiencing shader-related stutters.
The Radeon results, however, are a different story, and potentially the more interesting discovery to come out of this testing. Initially, the inability to increase AMD's on-disk shader cache size seemed like a bit of a Radeon fail. And while we'd still like to see AMD provide more control over that limit, if the company continues improving background shader compilation, perhaps it won't be such a significant limitation after all.
We actually spoke with AMD about this, and the company said that while it appreciates third-party applications such as SCSKiller, it also considers itself an industry leader in supporting DirectX 12 Advanced Shader Delivery, which aims to address the same underlying problems through an officially supported approach.
Advanced Shader Delivery is a separate technology developed by Microsoft for Windows 11 and DirectX 12. It allows supported games to download precompiled shaders, reducing the need for compilation on the player's PC and helping prevent stuttering. AMD has been an early supporter of this technology, though its benefits depend on game and platform support.
In any case, there's clearly more testing to be done. We're particularly interested in seeing how AMD's background shader compilation performs across more games, different CPU configurations, and older Radeon hardware. Likewise, SCSKiller deserves a closer look with slower processors, where shader compilation stutter may be even more disruptive. For now, though, we've learned two things: SCSKiller really can work, and AMD's shader compilation improvements might be a bigger deal than we initially realized.

articles.title: AI game clones are making indie developers afraid to show their work
articles.text:
Since its earliest days, the video game industry has been built on developers creating clones of competing games, with varying levels of originality and varying levels of enforcement from game platforms. Now, though, AI coding tools are making that cloning process so efficient that many developers are getting extremely cautious about sharing their early work too widely.
Developer Alliance Arts highlighted this trend over the weekend, delaying the launch of a planned public demo for its demon-themed Russian Roulette drinking game Drunken Goddess Reflux, which had been set to go live with today’s launch of Steam Next Fest.
In a post on social media Friday evening, the Alliance Arts team wrote that, in addition to concerns about managing streaming restrictions, “we’re concerned that the demo’s content could be used to quickly imitate or replicate the game’s presentation and gameplay with AI or other tools and that such works could be released before our launch.”
Instead, the developer now plans to share the demo only in “closed sessions” with those who agree to rules regarding posting and streaming gameplay.
Alliance Arts isn’t alone in taking a more defensive stance toward sharing ideas. Papers, Please developer Lucas Pope said on an April podcast that, in general, “you don’t really talk about stuff when you’re working on it because I don’t know it’s going to get slurped up by AI or people are going to copy it or something else like that… I just didn’t feel as comfortable talking about the stuff I was working on again.”
Whose game is it, anyway?
Concerns about ideas getting “slurped by AI” have been more than theoretical for a number of indie developers in recent months. In March, developer Freya Holmér attracted some viral social media attention after sharing a video of a prototype of a Tetris-style game played on a central rotating pivot point. Days later, Holmér was confronted with a number of vibe-coded copies that made the basic concept widely playable before Holmér could release her own version.
My only option to compete is to play the same spamming game which I've never wanted to do, much easier to let it die and accept it was fun whilst it lasted.

articles.title: Iqunix Prepares EV63 EDG Edition Keyboard
articles.text:
Monday, October 19th 2026
Iqunix Prepares EV63 EDG Edition Keyboard
Keyboard maker Iqunix has confirmed that the company is preparing a special EV63 EDG Edition to celebrate one of the most successful esports teams focused on Valorant. The EDG team features a signature black and gold aesthetic, which Iqunix claims underwent five rounds of joint fine-tuning for the EV63 EDG Edition color accents before the final release. This time, the company is introducing Timing Synchronization System (TSS) technology, which will align the keyboard's input processing with the PC's USB polling cycle for more consistent responses, lower latency, and more predictable input. To test this, Iqunix used its HyperCore v3.1 firmware to measure actuation latency and release latency.
According to internal testing, actuation latency is between 0.29-0.30 ms, while release latency hovers in an even tighter range of only 0.26-0.27 ms. In addition to low latency, the EV63 also offers traditional hardware enhancements like 8,000 Hz polling, 16,000 Hz scanning, and 0.01 mm Rapid Trigger Smart Switch Adaptation. Finally, the company leaves room for experimentation with different switches. Smart Switch Adaptation automatically recognizes 99% of mainstream Hall Effect switches, simplifying compatibility and making switch replacement more convenient. Combined with Magnetic X Ultra switches, designed for stronger magnetic flux and improved signal stability, the EV63 is built to deliver responsive input with dependable control.The Iqunix EV63 EDG Edition keyboard will join the existing lineup as the sixth option among the company's EV63 keyboards. We've already seen colorways like EV63 Violet, EV63 Silver Knight, EV63 Dark Knight, EV63 Ghost in the Shell Core, and EV63 Ghost in the Shell Cyber Blue. The MSRP of the EDG Edition keyboard is currently unknown, but we can expect the pricing to be anywhere from $169 to $249, similar to the prices of most EV63 keyboards.

articles.title: A Chinese hacker used AI agents to break into more than 100 company websites — Deere and SharkNinja among websites hit by open-source AI-powered problem-solving platform demo
articles.text:
A Chinese hacker used AI agents to break into more than 100 company websites — Deere and SharkNinja among websites hit by open-source AI-powered problem-solving platform demo
Why break into websites yourself when you can task AI bots to do it for you?
A Chinese-speaking hacker has been observed using artificial intelligence (AI) agents to probe and then gain unauthorized access to more than 100 websites belonging to some extremely well-known companies. From Deere, the farming equipment manufacturer, to SharkNinja, the company behind beloved kitchen appliances, the agents were able to leverage exposed instances of Carin, an open-source AI-powered problem-solving platform that has proven popular among hackers, a Reuters report explains.
This is just the latest example of hackers turning to AI agents in an attempt to level up their attacks on unsuspecting companies and services. Snorre Fagerland, principal threat researcher at the cybersecurity company NorForge, spotted the hacker's antics when observing Carin instances that had been inadvertently exposed.
Fagerland was able to watch multiple hackers go about their business, but the Chinese-speaking hacker was the most prolific, the report says. They targeted businesses based in the United States, Canada, Australia, and Japanese e-commerce sites. Notably, the hacker didn't get into detail when commanding their legion of AI agents. Fewer than 100 Chinese characters were used, yet the agents had attempted ot break into more than 1,200 different websites as of the week ending October 18, 2026.
These agents weren't simply throwing everything at a wall and hoping it stuck, either. Security researcher Fagerland was "impressed" by some of the tactics that had been used. In one case, the AI agents scoured digital records to find infrastructure associated with their target, located a public-facing control panel, identified a weakness, and then leveraged it to force the execution of malicious commands, the Reuters report detailed. "It's not straightforward to come up with solutions like that," Fagerland told Reuters. "It's not script kiddie stuff."
Vitally, the approach of using AI agents in this way means that they can be given instructions and then left to their own devices. With no supervision required, those commanding the agents are free to turn their attention elsewhere. While SharkNinja told Reuters that the attack only impacted a site used for product support information, the rest of the AI-aided hackers had more luck. One of the hackers monitored by Gargerland stole credit card data, while another tried to steal from a cryptocurrency exchange — although it isn't clear whether they were successful.

articles.title: DirectX, Vulkan 1.3, Snapshots, l'outil de virtualisation UTM fait le plein de nouveautés
articles.text:
UTM, l'outil libre qui fait tourner Windows ou Linux dans une fenêtre sur Mac, iPhone et iPad, gère maintenant DirectX pour Windows 11 sur macOS et Vulkan 1.3 pour Linux. Il ajoute aussi un onglet Snapshots pour sauvegarder l'état d'une machine virtuelle.
Les notes de la version 5.0.8, publiées sur GitHub, rassemblent les changements de la branche 5.0. Plusieurs nouveautés dépendent de la version de macOS ou d'iOS installée.
DirectX, Vulkan, sauvegardes : les nouveautés et les précautions à prendre
Pour afficher de la 3D, une machine virtuelle (VM) passe par des interfaces comme DirectX (Windows) ou Vulkan et OpenGL (Linux). UTM sait désormais gérer DirectX pour Windows 11 sur macOS. Le pilote reste expérimental et la compatibilité avec les jeux est limitée, d'où la recommandation de repartir d'une installation neuve pour éviter les instabilités. le pilote doit être choisi pendant l'installation des "guest tools", les outils à installer dans Windows. Si l'ancien pilote, limité à l'affichage, est déjà en place, il faut d'abord lancer le script de désinstallation fourni avec ces outils. Nous rapportions dans un article sur Windows 11 et les Mac M3 que Windows passait sur ces machines par sa version ARM, la seule gérée par Parallels Desktop, et que celle-ci pouvait d'ailleurs rencontrer quelques problèmes avec les logiciels conçus pour les processeurs Intel. Avec DirectX, UTM s’attaque à un autre point faible de Windows sur Mac : l’affichage 3D, et donc les jeux et les applications graphiques.
Côté Linux, UTM gère désormais Vulkan 1.3, grâce aux pilotes VirtIO Venus de Mesa (la bibliothèque graphique de Linux). Pour l'interface OpenGL 4.1, il s’appuie sur un nouveau moteur, Apple Core OpenGL. Celui-ci est réservé à macOS et ne prend en charge ni Vulkan ni DirectX. Attention, l’affichage du bureau Linux lui-même ne fonctionne pas avec Vulkan, car certaines commandes de dessin 3D ne sont pas gérées. Il faut alors régler le Linux installé dans la machine virtuelle pour qu’il utilise l’ancien pilote VirGL.
Le nouvel onglet Snapshots fonctionne comme un point de restauration. Il est possible de figer l'état d'une VM pour y revenir plus tard. Il s'applique aux VM QEMU sur macOS et iOS 26, et aux VM Apple Virtualization (la technologie d'Apple) sur macOS 27. Sous macOS 27, ces dernières acceptent aussi les périphériques USB, le Secure Boot pour Linux (qui vérifie le démarrage) et l'exécution sans enregistrer les modifications. De nouveaux modes réseau permettent également aux VM de communiquer entre elles. Sur iOS, les gestes tactiles répondent immédiatement, avec clic central, glisser-clic droit et un mode de défilement par glissement. Sur l'iPhone Duo, plié comme un ordinateur portable, la moitié basse sert de clavier ou de pavé tactile.
Avant de mettre à jour, les développeurs recommandent d'éteindre toutes les VM. Celles qui sont suspendues risquent de ne pas reprendre correctement ensuite. UTM nécessite désormais macOS 12 ou iOS 15 au minimum, contre macOS 11.3 et iOS 14 auparavant.
Quelle différence avec CrossOver ?
Du côté de CrossOver, de l’éditeur CodeWeavers, les choses sont différentes. Le logiciel n’est pas un émulateur. Il traduit les appels des programmes Windows en appels macOS, sans machine virtuelle. Nous rapportions en mars 2025 que CrossOver 25 permettait alors de jouer à Red Dead Redemption 2 sur Mac. La version 26, publiée le 10 février dernier, repose sur Wine 11 et sur D3DMetal 3.0, la couche qui traduit DirectX vers Metal, l’interface graphique du Mac. UTM, lui, fait tourner un Windows 11 complet dans une machine virtuelle et s’appuie aussi sur D3DMetal pour DirectX 12, quand il est disponible. CrossOver fait usage de Rosetta 2, la couche d’Apple qui traduit les programmes Intel pour les puces Apple Silicon. Rosetta 2 doit disparaitre avec macOS 28 en 2027. CodeWeavers a donc présenté cet été une préversion de CrossOver 27 native pour Apple Silicon, laquelle abandonne les Mac Intel. Cette version de test n’inclut pas encore D3DMetal et de nombreux lanceurs de jeux n’y fonctionnent pas. La version finale est attendue début 2027.
- Une solution de virtualisation compatible avec les Mac M1
- De nombreux profils pour les différentes machines virtuelles
- Un design récent

articles.title: Angel One, Zerodha expand US stock investing access for Indian investors
articles.text:
Angel One, Zerodha expand US stock investing access for Indian investors
This reflects a broader push by Indian investment platforms to expand beyond domestic equities as retail investors seek exposure to global markets.
Angel One and Zerodha are expanding access to the US stock markets for Indian investors, as domestic brokerages look to tap into the growing demand for international equities and portfolio diversification.
Angel One has begun rolling out US stock investing on its app, allowing users to invest in US-listed stocks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) alongside their Indian portfolios. The facility is currently available to a limited group of users, with a wider rollout expected by mid-November.
Investors will be able to buy shares of companies such as Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Nvidia, Netflix, Spotify and Toyota. The platform will also support fractional investing, allowing users to purchase a portion of a share rather than an entire unit.
Meanwhile, Zerodha has also launched US stock investing in beta, offering access to around 2,000 US-listed stocks and 1,000 ETFs through its platform. The move gives Indian investors another avenue to access global businesses, particularly in sectors such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and semiconductors.
The expansion follows regulatory approval from the International Financial Services Centres Authority for brokers to offer international investing through GIFT City in Gujarat.
Angel One will waive brokerage charges until December 2026. From January 2027, it will charge 0.1% per trade, subject to a minimum brokerage of $0.99. Account opening, maintenance, deposits, and withdrawals will be free, although regulatory charges, GST, and foreign-exchange conversion costs will apply.
Zerodha's offering is being introduced in beta, with brokerage and other applicable charges governed by its published pricing structure.
Investments through these platforms are subject to the Reserve Bank of India's Liberalised Remittance Scheme and applicable regulatory requirements. Angel One has also said eligible US securities will carry Securities Investor Protection Corporation protection of up to $500,000, subject to applicable conditions.
The launches reflect a broader push by Indian investment platforms to expand beyond domestic equities as retail investors seek exposure to global markets. Platforms including Groww, Upstox and INDmoney also offer routes to international investing, intensifying competition in the segment.

articles.title: Revolut outage disrupts online banking operations worldwide
articles.text:
Fintech company Revolut is working to resolve a massive outage that disrupted most of its services worldwide earlier today.
Since the incident began, thousands of users on the Downdetector outage tracking platform have reported issues with the Revolut app, mobile banking services, and transferring funds between accounts.
In a statement today, the company said the outage has affected its services since Tuesday morning and added that customers' data and funds are safe.
"We are currently experiencing a service disruption affecting multiple services. We can confirm that all our customers' money and data are safe," Revolut said.
"We've been working to fix the issue since it was identified this morning and apologise to anyone affected and for any inconvenience caused."
On its official status page, the company says the outage affects 28 services, including sign-ins, card payments, transfers, currency exchange, stock trading, and live support chat, which are now flagged as partially unavailable.
According to Reuters, the Revolut outage is reportedly linked to ongoing service disruptions affecting Google Cloud's London-based europe-west2 data center after a "power event."
A Revolut spokesperson was not immediately available when BleepingComputer reached out earlier about the root cause of today's outage.
Last month, Revolut also disclosed a data breach after it shared personally identifiable information (PII) from an undisclosed number of customers with a threat actor who was impersonating a government agency.
Four years ago, Revolut disclosed another data breach after threat actors stole the personal, contact, and financial information of more than 50,000 customers in September 2022.
Revolut provides banking, money management, and investment services to more than 80 million customers across 160+ countries and regions, including 800,000 business customers.

articles.title: Waymo llega a Madrid. Lo tiene todo planificado salvo lo que le pasó a Uber: el taxi
articles.text:
Waymo ha anunciado que llevará sus robotaxis a la Comunidad de Madrid, con la intención de abrir el servicio a los primeros usuarios en 2027. Sus Jaguar I-PACE blancos empezarán a circular en los próximos días: primero conducidos a mano y después en modo autónomo con un especialista sentado al volante.
Es un movimiento que veíamos venir desde julio por su documentación europea.
Por qué es importante. Es la primera vez que la empresa con más kilómetros reales sin conductor pisa España. Hasta ahora, la conducción autónoma en nuestro país ha sido cosa de lanzaderas en campus, autobuses en polígonos y fabricantes probando sistemas supervisados.
Waymo llega con más de 4.000 coches que ya trabajan sin nadie al volante en quince ciudades de Estados Unidos y más de 500.000 viajes de pago a la semana.
- Madrid se suma a Londres y Múnich en su lista europea, aunque ninguna de las tres tiene todavía servicio comercial.
En detalle. Waymo ya tiene el permiso de la DGT para hacer pruebas en vías públicas, bajo la Instrucción VEH 2025/07. El plan es el mismo que ha repetido en cada ciudad: mapear las calles conduciendo de forma manual, validar el sistema con conductores de seguridad y, solo después, retirar a la persona del asiento.
Preguntada por Xataka, la empresa nos ha dado algunos detalles adicionales sobre este despliegue inicial:
- Zona. Las pruebas serán en entornos urbanos de Madrid capital, Alcobendas y Getafe, de día y de noche. No cubren toda la Comunidad pero tampoco se limitan al interior de la M-30.
- Flota. Será “pequeña” en esta primera fase, sin cifras concretas.
- App. Para 2027 trabaja con “socios operativos locales”, sin detalles sobre integraciones con plataformas concretas. En Londres, ese papel lo hace Moove, una gestora de flotas participada por Uber.
- Coche. Aunque se trata de un modelo que se dejó de fabricar hace dos años, usará el I-PACE con la quinta generación de Waymo Driver, de 2020 y anterior a la que ya monta en Estados Unidos en la furgoneta Ojai de la china Zeekr y en el Hyundai Ioniq 5. Evaluará otros vehículos a medida que crezca la flota.
El contraste. Waymo no es la primera en Madrid. La DGT ya ha concedido el primer permiso nacional para vehículos autónomos de pasajeros de nivel 4 a WeRide, Uber y Avomo, con una fase inicial de 20 vehículos GXR con un especialista a bordo en zonas de alta demanda de Madrid.
Uber ha confirmado su intención de desplegar ese robotaxi en Madrid antes de que termine 2026. Y 19 Teslas tienen autorización desde hace casi un año para probar su conducción autónoma por carreteras españolas hasta noviembre de 2027, siempre con alguien supervisando desde el asiento del conductor.
Al otro lado. El taxi madrileño ya ha demostrado hasta dónde puede llegar. En enero de 2019 mantuvo una huelga de 16 días contra Uber y Cabify, con la Castellana cortada en hora punta y Fitur en marcha. En Barcelona, la presión consiguió que la Generalitat obligase a contratar las VTC con 15 minutos de antelación, y Uber y Cabify se marcharon de la ciudad.
Entre líneas. Waymo vende, ante todo, seguridad: en su recorrido hasta ahora ha tenido un 95% menos de siniestros con heridos graves o muertos que los conductores humanos.
Para el contexto español ha escogido los 1.119 fallecidos de 2025 en vías interurbanas, la mayoría en salidas de vía y choques frontales. Son carreteras secundarias, así que es justo donde un robotaxi urbano no va a circular.
¿Qué falta? El permiso de la DGT cubre las pruebas, pero cobrar por un viaje sin conductor exige una autorización de transporte de viajeros, el terreno donde el taxi y los VTC llevan más de diez años enfrentados en media España. Waymo habla de “primeros usuarios en 2027” aunque sin aclarar si viajarán con el asiento delantero vacío u ocupado, y la propia DGT ha advertido que la conducción sin supervisión no llegará ni a corto ni a medio plazo.

articles.title: Vinted et Leboncoin envahis par des annonces de produits volés pendant les manifestations
articles.text:
Ces 17 et 18 octobre, un nombre conséquent de magasins ont été pillés à travers la France. Certaines enseignes, grandes et petites, ont été vandalisées, parfois durant plusieurs heures. Et après les pillages, arrive maintenant l’heure de la revente. À ce titre, Vinted a enregistré une hausse soudaine d’annonces suspectes à la suite du 17 octobre.
Les produits volés se revendent maintenant sur Vinted et Leboincoin
Sur les sites de revente en ligne, comme Vinted et Leboncoin, les annonces suspectes se multiplient. Dans certains cas, des produits présentant toujours une étiquette et un antivol sont mis en vente. Dans d’autres cas, les vendeurs indiquent explicitement qu’il s’agit de produits volés durant les événements du 17 octobre.
Seulement voilà, ne pas avoir été pris la main dans le sac au moment des faits n’implique pas d’être sorti d’affaire. Pour cause, la plupart des plateformes en ligne obligent les revendeurs à fournir un certain nombre de données confidentielles afin de pouvoir poster des annonces, comme un nom, un prénom, une adresse postale, un IBAN, voire dans certains cas une copie de la carte d’identité. C’est pourquoi certains candidats à la présidentielle, ont apelé les plateformes de revente en ligne à coopérer avec l’État afin d’identifier certains pilleurs.
Vinted annonce collaborer d’ores et déjà avec les autorités françaises
L’appel semble avoir été entendu de la part des plateformes. Un porte-parole de Vinted a déclaré dans un communiqué que l’entreprise « a immédiatement pris des mesures pour identifier et supprimer les annonces liées au pillage » et a « renforcé la surveillance des annonces suspectes ». Il précise qu’ « En cas d’infraction à notre règlement, nous prenons des mesures contre les comptes concernés, pouvant aller jusqu’à la suspension définitive ». Enfin, notons que Vinted annonce collaborer « activement avec les forces de l’ordre et les autorités françaises ».
Il reste maintenant à déterminer comment vérifier avec précision si un article revendu en ligne provient bel et bien d’un pillage survenu le 17 octobre. Si certains articles intègrent une puce ou un numéro de série, ce n’est pas le cas de tous les produits mis sur le marché. Dans tous les cas, rappelons que le recel, qui consiste notamment à détenir ou à revendre un bien en sachant qu’il a été volé, est passible de cinq ans d’emprisonnement et de 375 000 euros d’amende en France.

articles.title: Inside Gabon’s first angel investor network
articles.text:
20 octobre 2026
Hello 👋,
Welcome back to Francophone Weekly by TechCabal, your weekly deep dive into the tech ecosystem across French-speaking Africa. For readers who want to understand Francophone Africa beyond headlines—through markets, startups, and systems. New editions of the newsletter will land directly in your inbox every Tuesday at 12 PM WAT.
By default, this newsletter is in French. If you’re reading this in your email inbox, click the “Read in English” button below to switch to the English version. If you’re reading on our website, you can either click the button below or toggle the language selector at the top right-hand side of the page to view the English edition.
Le premier réseau structuré d’investisseurs providentiels du Gabon a déployé 67,3 millions de FCFA (118 000 dollars) dans quatre entreprises. La façon dont il y est parvenu en dit plus long sur les écosystèmes naissants que le chiffre lui-même.
En 2025, le Gabon a enregistré une seule opération de capital-risque, d’une valeur d’environ 1 million de dollars, selon l’Association africaine du capital-investissement et du capital-risque (AVCA). Le Cameroun, son voisin au sein du même bloc économique, a comptabilisé huit opérations pour 26 millions de dollars. L’Afrique centrale dans son ensemble n’a concentré que 10 opérations et 27 millions de dollars, faisant de cette région le plus petit marché de capital-risque du continent.
C’est dans ce contexte qu’est né le Gabon Angel Investor Network (GAIN), premier réseau structuré de business angels du pays. Cinq fondateurs l’ont lancé en 2021. Le réseau a réalisé son premier investissement en 2022. Depuis, il a injecté 67 345 000 FCFA (118 000 dollars) dans quatre entreprises, et son ticket moyen est passé de 11,5 millions de FCFA (19 000 dollars) à 25 millions de FCFA (43 000 dollars).
Ces chiffres paraissent modestes au regard des standards du marché du capital-risque nigérian — et c’est précisément là l’enjeu. Le GAIN construit simultanément une base d’investisseurs et un pipeline de startups, dans un marché où moins de 10 % des startups accèdent au crédit bancaire à un stade précoce.
Selon des données de la Banque des États de l’Afrique Centrale (BEAC) citées par le GAIN, le Gabon a capté 18,25 % des nouveaux crédits de la Communauté Économique et Monétaire de l’Afrique Centrale (CEMAC) au quatrième trimestre 2025, contre 63,93 % pour le Cameroun.
Des échanges avec Fabrice Nze Bekale, président du réseau, et Vanessa Adande, membre fondatrice et trésorière, en marge du sommet Africa’s Early Stage Investor Summit (AESIS) 2026 organisé par le GAIN à Libreville, la capitale gabonaise, ce mois-ci, révèlent que construire depuis zéro exige une flexibilité sur presque toutes les variables qu’un investisseur tient ordinairement pour fixes.
1. Recruter des investisseurs, une affaire de confiance
            Participants à une rencontre du GAIN au Gabon, où le réseau tisse des liens entre entrepreneurs et investisseurs potentiels. Source de l’image : GAIN/LinkedIn.
       
        
    
Le GAIN a d’abord recruté dans l’entourage de ses fondateurs. Des cinq membres fondateurs, seuls Fabrice Nze Bekale et Vanessa Adande sont restés. Le déclic est venu en 2024, avec une première sortie (le remboursement intégral d’une facilité accordée à un entrepreneur) et la première édition de l’AESIS au Gabon. Cette visibilité a presque doublé le nombre de membres en 18 mois. Le GAIN en compte aujourd’hui 36.
La moitié sont des femmes, et ce résultat n’a rien d’un hasard. Adande a constaté que le rôle d’investisseur paraissait trop risqué aux femmes, vu de l’extérieur. Elle a donc appelé celles qu’elle connaissait pour leur expliquer le fonctionnement du GAIN au quotidien, et les a rassurées : investir dans un dossier identifié n’est jamais obligatoire.
Elle a aussi avancé un argument de pipeline : une entrepreneure a plus de chances d’être financée si d’autres femmes font partie du groupe d’investisseurs.
« Les hommes de l’association étaient d’ailleurs étonnés que ça demande autant d’effort. Pas moi », confie-t-elle. « Tout ce qui concerne l’argent demande de la confiance. On a confiance dans ce qu’on connaît. »
Le point dépasse largement le cas gabonais. L’AVCA classe l’Afrique centrale parmi les régions où les fondatrices ont levé la plus faible part du capital en 2025 : 8 %.
Dit Adande, l’intérêt des membres féminines s’est ravivé depuis la masterclass d’octobre, plusieurs d’entre elles ayant demandé comment fonctionnent les opérations en pratique. Le GAIN prévoit également un événement plus large dédié à l’investissement providentiel en 2027, afin d’élargir son vivier de cibles d’investissement.
La sortie de 2024 était un remboursement de prêt. Pour un réseau jeune, démontrer que les investisseurs ont récupéré leur mise fait davantage pour attirer de nouveaux membres qu’une valorisation sur le papier.
La spécialisation sectorielle est un luxe
Les réseaux d’angels matures se spécialisent. Le GAIN ne le peut pas encore.
« Dans nos pays, c’est toujours très nouveau, en particulier au Gabon, explique Fabrice Nze Bekale. On est encore à un stade où on fait des réseaux de business angels multisectoriels. On ne peut pas trop se spécialiser, un peu comme DNA [le Dakar Network of Angels] l’a fait au Sénégal, parce que ça reflète l’état de développement et de sophistication de l’écosystème entrepreneurial. »
Au Sénégal, le DNA se concentre sur les startups technologiques. Les quatre investissements du GAIN couvrent l’import-export, une marketplace, la santé et l’agro-industrie, et un dossier dans la santé est en due diligence.
Avec environ 150 startups actives au Gabon, selon la société d’incubation numérique SING, un mandat limité à la tech laisserait les membres avec presque rien à examiner. Le GAIN investit dans des startups tech et non-tech, et peut également considérer des petites et moyennes entreprises (PME) à fort potentiel de croissance. Chaque candidat doit être légalement constitué, avoir au moins un an d’existence, démontrer une traction réelle et présenter un plan d’affaires structuré.
Attendre des entreprises logicielles à l’échelle du capital-risque dans un marché de 150 startups, c’est s’exposer à des années de réunions sans jamais sortir un seul chèque. Le revers de la médaille, c’est qu’un petit groupe doit alors évaluer des profils de risque très hétérogènes — ce qui renvoie directement au problème de due diligence du GAIN.
La newsletter continue après cette publicité.
Fondateurs. Investisseurs. Décideurs politiques. Leaders d’entreprise. Moonshot 2026 rassemble les personnes qui façonnent l’écosystème technologique africain en matière d’IA, de commerce, de climat, d’entreprise et de culture. Mettez votre marque en avant dès aujourd’hui.
2. Moins de fonds propres, plus de dette
            Le Gabon Angel Investor Network (GAIN) s’emploie à connecter les entrepreneurs locaux avec des investisseurs capables d’apporter des financements, une expertise et des contacts d’affaires. Source de l’image : GAIN/LinkedIn.
       
        
    
« L’idéal, c’est toujours de faire des investissements en equity,” Nze Bekale dit. « Mais on est souvent contraints de prendre un peu d’equity pour mettre beaucoup de dette, ou bien de faire de la dette convertible dès le départ, parce que les entrepreneurs ne veulent pas ouvrir leur capital. »
La réticence à la dilution est profonde en Afrique francophone, où beaucoup d’entreprises sont familiales. Le GAIN calibre chaque opération selon la maturité de l’entreprise et sa capacité de remboursement : fonds propres, dette ou financement hybride.
Le continent évolue dans le même sens : la dette a représenté 41 % des 4,1 milliards de dollars levés par les startups africaines en 2025, un record, selon le rapport Partech 2025 Africa Tech Venture Capital.
Cette flexibilité exige une rédaction rigoureuse, car les obligations convertibles échouent en silence. Dans un cas anonymisé présenté lors de la masterclass de l’AESIS, un BSA AIR — l’équivalent français du SAFE (Simple Agreement for Future Equity) — est arrivé à échéance sans avoir converti, et la cession de l’entreprise s’est transformée en une longue négociation sur les droits des investisseurs.
Un convertible doit prévoir dès la signature son échéance, son taux, ses déclencheurs de conversion et le cas de cession. Des angels qui détiennent surtout de la dette doivent aussi évaluer la capacité de remboursement réelle d’aujourd’hui, pas celle des projections.
Expliquer ce qu’est un business angel
Un autre front se situe hors de la salle de négociation.
« On doit faire de la sensibilisation auprès des investisseurs potentiels, auprès des entrepreneurs, et surtout faire de l’advocacy auprès des autorités pour leur expliquer notre rôle, qui n’est pas celui d’une banque et qui n’est pas celui d’un incubateur, » insiste Nze Bekale.
Les autorités ont encore tendance à assimiler les business angels à des financeurs d’activités génératrices de revenus : un plombier ou un chauffeur de taxi qui s’installe à son compte, avec des budgets de 500 000 à 1 million de FCFA (900 à 1 750 dollars).
« On se regroupe pour financer des projets pour lesquels on a besoin de se regrouper, et pas des projets à 500 000 ou un million de francs CFA », précise-t-il.
Si l’État classe l’investissement providentiel dans l’appui à la micro-entreprise, il concevra ses incitations pour le mauvais segment. Le GAIN, qui travaille déjà avec le Centre gabonais de l’innovation (CGI) et le ministère des PME et des PMI, a besoin que l’investissement providentiel soit reconnu comme une catégorie à part entière.
La due diligence, goulot d’étranglement caché
Le GAIN veut augmenter ses financements cette année. C’est la due diligence qui le freine. Pour son premier deal, le réseau a rémunéré un consultant externe à hauteur de 1 à 2 % du montant levé. Pour les suivants, Nze Bekale a mené les DD lui-même.
« Comme ça a commencé à trop peser sur moi, cette année on a décidé de tester un autre modèle », raconte-t-il. Des volontaires parmi les investisseurs potentiels forment désormais une équipe et conduisent le processus.
Pourtant, cela n’a pas bien fonctionné.
« Tout le monde a des activités professionnelles principales, et donc ils ont très peu de temps à consacrer aux DD. Ce n’est même pas secondaire, c’est peut-être tertiaire ou quaternaire, » Nze Bekale dit.
Sur le dossier en cours dans la santé, l’équipe travaille depuis six ou sept mois. Un processus early-stage classique prend deux à quatre mois entre le premier rendez-vous et le décaissement.
Le GAIN envisage de revenir au consultant rémunéré. En attendant, les analystes d’ACT Afrique, le cabinet de conseil de Nze Bekale, portent une grande partie du travail.
« Je n’ai pas de problème à le faire parce que je suis le président, mais si je n’étais pas le président, la question se poserait autrement. »
Il a raison de s’inquiéter. Une due diligence qui repose sur le cabinet d’un seul membre crée un point de défaillance unique et un conflit d’intérêts latent. Le modèle de frais a son propre défaut : 2 % d’une levée de 25 millions de FCFA (43 000 dollars), c’est 500 000 FCFA (860 dollars), tout au plus quelques jours de travail d’analyste.
Deux correctifs seraient utiles. D’abord, standardiser les modèles et les listes de vérification pour réduire le nombre d’heures par opération. Ensuite, traiter la due diligence comme une infrastructure d’écosystème : les institutions de financement du développement financent déjà l’incubation, et un pool d’analystes mutualisé entre les réseaux de business angels de la CEMAC ne coûterait pas grand-chose.
L’épreuve de 2027
Le GAIN a démontré sa capacité à recruter des investisseurs, et la moitié de ses membres sont des femmes. Son prochain défi est de professionnaliser la due diligence sans s’appuyer sur le cabinet de son président. S’il y parvient, ses 36 membres pourront commencer à signer des chèques de 50 millions de FCFA (86 000 dollars) — le plafond que leur mandat autorise.

articles.title: Garmin Edge 1060 : un nouveau compteur GPS avec micro pour parler à son vélo — Frandroid
articles.text:
Deux ans après l’Edge 1050, Garmin renouvelle son compteur GPS le plus haut de gamme. Ce mardi 20 octobre, la marque américaine a présenté le Garmin Edge 1060. Sa principale nouveauté est un micro intégré, qui permet de commander le compteur à la voix sans lâcher le cintre. Le reste de la fiche technique change peu.
    Pour aller plus loin
Quels sont les meilleurs compteurs GPS pour vélo ? Notre sélection
            
Le Garmin Edge 1060 est le premier compteur de la marque à embarquer la reconnaissance vocale et l’assistant Garmin. En prononçant « Okay, Garmin », il permet de demander sa fréquence cardiaque, sa vitesse ou un itinéraire vers le café le plus proche. Le compteur répond en changeant d’écran ou en lisant l’information à voix haute. Avec un smartphone connecté et l’application Garmin Messenger, il peut aussi envoyer des messages vocaux et lire à voix haute ceux qu’on reçoit.
Le haut-parleur existait déjà, présent sur l’Edge 1050, mais servait uniquement aux consignes de navigation et de sonnette numérique.
Même écran, même autonomie
D’après la fiche technique, l’Edge 1060 garde un écran tactile couleur LCD de 3,5 pouces affichant 480 pixels par 800, soit la même taille et la même définition que l’Edge 1050. L’autonomie annoncée ne change pas non plus. Garmin promet toujours 20 heures en usage intensif et 60 heures en mode économie. Le boîtier pèse 142 grammes et reste certifié IPX7, c’est-à-dire qu’il supporte une immersion temporaire.
On retrouve aussi 64 Go de stockage pour les cartes et un GNSS multibande. La face avant devient plate, et Garmin a conservé des boutons physiques pour rouler sous la pluie ou avec des gants. Enfin, la recharge inversée permet de dépanner un éclairage Varia ou un téléphone avec un câble USB-C.
Concernant les nouveautés logicielles, le Garmin Edge 1060 propose plusieurs itinéraires selon la durée, le dénivelé ou le type de vélo, avec un aperçu du trafic et des dangers signalés. Il affiche aussi les routes fermées signalées par d’autres cyclistes Garmin. Un mode Free Flow Routing cherche les parcours avec le moins d’arrêts et de carrefours. Pour l’entraînement, il reprend l’estimation Stamina déjà présente sur l’Edge 1050, et propose les plans Garmin Cycling Coach ainsi que la synchronisation automatique des séances TrainingPeaks, une plateforme de suivi d’entraînement rachetée récemment par la marque.
Prix et disponibilité du Garmin Edge 1060
Le Garmin Edge 1060 est proposé en France au prix de 799,99 euros, et les commandes ouvriront ce vendredi 23 octobre sur la boutique en ligne de Garmin. À titre de comparaison, l’ancien compteur haut de gamme du constructeur, l’Edge 1050, était affiché à 749,99 euros.

articles.title: Pinterest Uses Event Time Watermarks to Finalize Petabyte Scale Data Partitions
articles.text:
Pinterest has introduced an event time-based partition finalization mechanism for its next-generation database ingestion framework, allowing downstream jobs to determine when streaming data is sufficiently complete to consume. The approach uses Apache Flink to measure event time progress and Apache Iceberg metadata to publish a non-regressing finalization watermark, addressing a challenge in continuous Change Data Capture (CDC) ingestion where data can arrive after a partition’s wall clock interval has ended.
Pinterest’s ingestion framework uses CDC, Kafka, Flink, Spark and Iceberg to move database changes from MySQL, TiDB and KVStore into analytical tables. Pinterest says the platform supports petabyte-scale data and thousands of pipelines, with online changes typically available within 15 minutes to an hour. Unlike the previous batch-based approach, where job completion indicated that a partition was ready, streaming ingestion continuously commits changes without an equivalent completion point.
Pinterest architecture showing Kafka CDC events flowing through Flink into a CDC Iceberg table (Source: Pinterest Blog Post)
Nitesh Singhal, Architect at Google, highlighted the design in a LinkedIn post, writing,
The non-regressing safe-to-read watermark is the elegant bit here.
The new mechanism runs inside the Flink to Iceberg sink. For each CDC record, the system extracts a configured event time. During Flink checkpoints, it collects minimum, maximum, and percentile event time statistics. These are stored in the Iceberg snapshot summary, with a t-digest representing the distribution in a few hundred bytes.
After an Iceberg commit, the system calculates a partition finalization watermark from recent checkpoint statistics. The default policy uses the minimum event time across a configurable number of recent commits and rounds it down to the relevant hour. The watermark is monotonic, preventing late-arriving records from moving an already published value backward. Percentile-based policies can trade some completeness for fresher data.
Pinterest describes the change by noting the watermark is stored as an Iceberg table property, allowing downstream sensors to read it without a separate coordination service. Spark also propagates the metadata to the base table during its CDC upsert commit and emphasizes
Finalization is no longer a byproduct of a job finishing.
The design builds on existing Flink and Iceberg capabilities. Flink watermarks track event time progress in out-of-order streams, while Iceberg snapshots provide persistent table metadata. Pinterest uses these capabilities together to derive a table-specific completeness signal and store it alongside the data.
Timeline showing late-arriving CDC events, Flink checkpoints, event time progress and the monotonically increasing finalization watermark. (Source: Pinterest Blog Post)
Tharun Kumar Reddy Polu, Engineer at Salesforce, identified the streaming and batch tradeoff in a LinkedIn comment, writing,
The streaming vs batch tradeoff framing is what makes this land. Getting freshness without losing the guarantees batch gave us is the core challenge.
Pinterest implemented the mechanism using extensibility points in its Flink-to-Iceberg sink. Accumulators collect record statistics, while commit processors execute finalization logic around Iceberg commits. Separately, an Apache Iceberg issue discusses extending IcebergSink for downstream integrations, including custom committable metadata such as watermark information.

articles.title: Pasos para canjear los códigos de Free Fire este 19 de octubre de 2026: gana diamantes gratis
articles.text:
Garena habilitó una nueva ronda de códigos de Free Fire para este lunes 19 de octubre de 2026. Las combinaciones permiten a los jugadores con cuentas registradas intentar reclamar premios dentro del videojuego, entre ellos diamantes, trajes, skins de armas, cajas y otros objetos de disponibilidad limitada.
El acceso a cada beneficio depende de la región de la cuenta, la vigencia de la clave y los cupos de canje disponibles. Por ese motivo, conviene ingresar los códigos cuanto antes y utilizar únicamente el portal oficial de recompensas de Garena, que evita problemas de validación y riesgos de seguridad.
Cuáles son los códigos de Free Fire disponibles este 19 de octubre de 2026
La lista para la jornada incluye más de 15 combinaciones. Cada una debe copiarse como aparece, en mayúsculas y sin espacios antes o después de la secuencia. Un carácter incorrecto puede impedir que el sistema acepte el código.
- H8YC4TN6VKQ9.
- FP9O1I5U3Y2T.
- 6KWMFJVMQQYG.
- FE2R8T6Y4U1I.
- B1RK7C5ZL8YT.
- FQ9W2E1R7T5Y.
- FU1I5O3P7A9S.
- FT4E9Y5U1I3O.
- FFR4G3HM5YJN.
- F7F9A3B2K6G8.
- FA3S7D5F1G9H.
- FM6N1B8V3C4X.
- UPQ7X5NMJ64V.
- 4ST1ZTBZBRP9.
- BR43FMAPYEZZ.
- FF6YH3BFD7VT.
- FK3J9H5G1F7D.
- S9QK2L6VP3MR.
- FZ5X1C7V9B2N.
Las claves pueden tener restricciones territoriales y un número limitado de usos. Por esa razón, que una combinación figure en la lista no garantiza que funcione para todas las cuentas ni que entregue el mismo objeto a todos los usuarios.
Dónde se ingresan los códigos de recompensa de Free Fire
El canje se realiza en el sitio oficial reward.ff.garena.com. El jugador debe acceder desde un navegador, iniciar sesión y seleccionar el método de vinculación que corresponda a la cuenta utilizada habitualmente en Free Fire.
El portal admite perfiles asociados con Google, Facebook, Apple, Huawei o VK. La vinculación previa es necesaria para que el premio llegue al perfil correcto. Las cuentas de invitado no pueden utilizar el sistema hasta que queden enlazadas con una de las plataformas habilitadas.
Cuál es el proceso para reclamar diamantes y otros premios
Después de iniciar sesión, el usuario debe localizar el campo de canje, pegar o escribir una de las claves y confirmar la solicitud. Si el código continúa activo, tiene cupos disponibles y es válido en la región de la cuenta, la página mostrará un mensaje de confirmación.
Las recompensas pueden tardar hasta 24 horas en aparecer en el buzón interno del juego. Para comprobar la acreditación, el jugador debe abrir Free Fire con el mismo perfil que vinculó en el portal. Si el objeto no aparece de inmediato, conviene esperar ese plazo antes de repetir la operación con otra clave.
Qué significa el mensaje de código de Free Fire es inválido o expirado
El aviso “código inválido o expirado” indica que la combinación ya no puede utilizarse. Puede ser porque venció el período de activación, se agotaron los canjes disponibles o la clave no está habilitada para la región desde la cual se intentó validarla.
Además, puede tratarse de un error de escritura. Los códigos combinan letras y números que pueden parecerse entre sí, como la letra O y el número 0, o la letra I y el número 1. Antes de realizar un segundo intento, es clave revisar cada carácter y eliminar posibles espacios añadidos al copiar la secuencia.
Cuáles recompensas pueden otorgar los códigos de Garena en el juego
Los diamantes gratis se encuentran entre los beneficios más buscados porque permiten adquirir artículos en la tienda virtual de Free Fire. Con esta moneda, los jugadores pueden acceder a elementos estéticos, pases, accesorios y otros contenidos que forman parte de las campañas disponibles dentro del juego.
Asimismo, las claves pueden habilitar trajes, skins de armas, personajes, emotes, cajas y objetos coleccionables. El premio final depende de cada código y de la campaña activa, así que no todas las combinaciones otorgan diamantes ni entregan el mismo contenido a todos los perfiles.
En aniversarios, fechas conmemorativas y eventos especiales, Garena suele incorporar artículos temáticos que no forman parte del catálogo habitual. En esos casos, los códigos incluyen prendas, accesorios y otros objetos vinculados con una campaña puntual.

articles.title: Dieses Tool vergleicht hunderte KI-Modelle – und zeigt, welches auf deiner Hardware am besten läuft
articles.text:
KI ohne Cloud-Zwang: So ermittelst du in Sekunden das passende Modell für dein Setup
Es gibt viele gute Gründe, ein KI-Modell lokal zu verwenden. Vor allem bei wiederkehrenden, klar umrissenen Aufgaben und beim Umgang mit sensiblen Daten profitieren Nutzer:innen von mehr Datenschutz und Unabhängigkeit. Allerdings lässt sich nicht jedes Modell ohne Weiteres auf dem eigenen PC betreiben. Anstatt lange zu recherchieren oder selbst auszuprobieren, bietet die Website Whatmodel.sh eine schnellere Lösung: Nutzer:innen können dort mit wenigen Klicks passende Modelle filtern und vergleichen.
Warum sich eine lokale KI-Nutzung lohnt
Je nach Einsatzbereich eignet sich ein anderes KI-Modell. Bei Anthropic gilt Claude Haiku beispielsweise als die beste und günstigste Wahl für schnelle Klassifizierungen und Zusammenfassungen. Claude Fable bietet dagegen tiefes Reasoning für komplexe Aufgaben, langfristige Planungen und KI-Agenten, die über mehrere Phasen hinweg arbeiten. Wer solche Modelle in der App oder im Browser nutzt, schickt allerdings jede Anfrage über die Server des Anbieters – und das wirft schnell Datenschutzfragen auf. Deshalb kann es sinnvoller sein, große Sprachmodelle lokal zu verwenden. Quellcode, Dokumente und Kundendaten verlassen den Rechner in diesem Fall nicht. Außerdem funktioniert ein lokal installiertes Modell auch ohne Internetverbindung und bietet oft eine höhere Antwortgeschwindigkeit.
Welches KI-Modell sich für die lokale Nutzung eignet, hängt aber nicht nur vom Einsatzbereich, sondern auch von der Hardware ab. Jedes Modell benötigt beim Laden und bei jeder Antwort unterschiedlich viel Speicher, Speicherbandbreite und Rechenleistung. Fehlt eine dieser Ressourcen, lässt sich das Modell entweder gar nicht laden oder es läuft nur sehr langsam. Inzwischen gibt es einige Tools, die dabei helfen, KI-Modelle zu vergleichen und das passende Modell für die vorhandene Hardware auszuwählen. Eines davon bietet Whatmodel.sh. Die Seite umfasst aktuell mehrere hundert Modelle. Jedes davon erhält einen Score auf Basis öffentlich zugänglicher Benchmarks. Die genaue Methode ist auf der Website erklärt. Daten, Scoring-Code und Benchmarking-Skript sind Open Source und auf Github zu finden.
So kann das Tool bei der Auswahl helfen
Auf Whatmodel.sh geben Nutzer:innen zunächst an, welche Art von KI-Modell sie suchen. Neben großen Sprachmodellen gibt es beispielsweise Bild- und Videomodelle. Anschließend legen sie den Aufgabenbereich fest, für den sie das Modell verwenden möchten. Zu den Auswahlmöglichkeiten zählen unter anderem Coding, Chatten/Schreiben und Web-Suche. Anschließend geben sie die verfügbare RAM- und GPU-Kapazität an. Zudem können sie ihr Budget pro Million Token angeben.
Daraufhin zeigt die Seite, welche Modelle auf dem Rechner laufen könnten, wie viel Arbeitsspeicher sie benötigen, wie schnell sie ungefähr sind und wie groß ihr Kontextfenster ist. Mithilfe des Vergleichstools lässt sich beispielsweise ermitteln, welches KI-Modell am besten lokal auf einem Mac läuft. Das lohnt sich für alle, die nicht nach dem globalen Benchmark-Sieger suchen, sondern das zu ihrer Hardware passende Modell finden wollen. Nutzer:innen können das Tool außerdem verwenden, um die API-Kosten zu vergleichen oder die besten Modelle je nach Aufgabe zu finden.

articles.title: Steam on Linux is going 64-bit as Valve leans harder on the platform
articles.text:
Ripple effect: One of the most popular pieces of computer software is about to deliver a better experience on Linux machines. The Steam client is going 64-bit, providing feature parity with versions designed to run on different operating systems.
A recent Steam Client Beta update brought the program into the 64-bit era on Linux. The native Linux version of the massively popular gaming client is now a 64-bit application, which means it gains access to a few significant enhancements and, hopefully, a more reliable software experience.
Until last week's beta update, Steam's main binary ran as a 32-bit application even on 64-bit Linux distros. Some components, such as steamwebhelper, were already 64-bit. Now the main client uses 64-bit code as well, which should significantly expand memory access and improve the software's overall security.
Steam is going 64-bit, but Linux users will still need to provide 32-bit libraries and graphics drivers for compatibility reasons. Valve said Linux operating systems that only work with 64-bit software are not supported just yet, which might further complicate the job of distro maintainers. The Fedora team floated dropping 32-bit library support last year, but withdrew the proposal after pushback over Steam compatibility – or lack thereof.
The same beta brings a few additional changes to Steam's experience. The gaming client now runs inside its own "Steam Runtime" container, which should help the program behave more consistently across different Linux distros. The same technology is used by Steam games, which can use either 32- or 64-bit code regardless of the client's architecture.
Another notable change is Steam Achievement Sets, a new way to organize and track in-game achievements across base game releases and additional downloadable content. The sets should also give developers a new type of seasonal goal. Games already supporting the new beta feature include Left 4 Dead 2, Portal 2, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and more than a dozen others.
Steam's new 64-bit architecture on Linux is a significant change, as Steam is becoming a major driving force behind Linux gaming experiences and products. Most of Valve's hardware devices rely on SteamOS, which is based on a special version of Arch Linux. Even modders are having a lot of fun exploiting the open source nature of SteamOS to build some interesting handheld projects.
