articles.title: Nvidia says the RTX 5090 isn't discontinued, but most listings are over $9,300
articles.text:
Why it matters: Reports of the RTX 5090's death may have been exaggerated. That's according to Nvidia, which recently confirmed that the flagship consumer card was still in production. However, that denial doesn't seem to line up with Nvidia's own US marketplace, where the RTX 5090 is conspicuously absent.
Prolific leaker MEGAsizeGPU last week wrote that Nvidia had "confirmed" the GB202 chip used in the RTX 5090 would no longer be used in new RTX 5090 cards. Instead, future supplies of the GPU would be used exclusively for RTX Pro Blackwell-based models.
 – MEGAsizeGPU (@Zed__Wang) October 10, 2026
Another leaker, Hongxing2020, said Nvidia would replace the RTX 5090 with a new RTX 5080 variant packing 24GB of VRAM.
Now, 4Gamers reports that Nvidia has denied the reports at an RTX Spark launch party event in Taipei, Taiwan.
Jeff Fisher, Nvidia's senior vice president of personal computing, talked about CUDA and how there would be no AI market today without it.
"The supply chain (capacity) is indeed somewhat constrained, but NVIDIA is fully committed to bringing products to market. Although there are other variants of the RTX 5090 chip, it has not been discontinued, and Nvidia will continue shipping, which is very important," Fisher said, according to the machine-translated site.
That all sounds pretty definitive, but it's at odds with Nvidia's official US marketplace. The option to see RTX 5090 cards has been removed completely, with the RTX 5080 sitting at the top of the list.
There are some RTX 5090 cards available on Newegg. The majority are over $9,300, with the most expensive model priced at $10,899. Amazon has just one, priced at $11,565. It ships from Germany in 2 to 3 weeks. There are almost none sitting on shelves in brick-and-mortar stores, either.
As for the RTX 5080 24GB, or Super, as it might be called, there are rumors it will launch next year. It's long been assumed that the Super series has been canceled, but there have been claims that it could land next year – or even sooner.
With the RTX 6000 series not expected until 2028 and rival AMD's RDNA 5 cards tipped to get here in late 2027, perhaps Nvidia will launch an RTX 5080 Super at some point, though we can only hazard a guess at its price.
As we all know, the situation comes down to the massive demand for AI products and the fact Nvidia makes a lot more money from these expensive professional and enterprise cards. Despite Fisher's claims, it wouldn't be a surprise to learn that the RTX 5090 is effectively dead.

articles.title: Stratospheric airship flew from US to Japan to test sky cell tower concept
articles.text:
Nearly 100 years after the dirigible Graf Zeppelin made the first nonstop airship journey across the Pacific Ocean, another airship has successfully completed a round-trip flight from New Mexico to Japan and back. But the significance of this modern feat was less about the journey’s length and more about its purpose: demonstrating how a lighter-than-air platform can act as a cell phone tower in the sky.
The trans-Pacific flight that took place over a month between August and September 2026 was the most notable milestone yet for Sceye, a US aerospace company based near Albuquerque, New Mexico. Sceye has developed an uncrewed platform filled with helium for buoyancy and equipped with an electric-powered propeller for active propulsion, allowing it to resist most strong winds and keep hovering over the same location for long periods. The platform also uses top-mounted solar panels and onboard batteries to stay powered for stratospheric operations around the clock.
“We can stay over an area of operation, and we do that in the stratosphere right around 60,000 feet, so we’re twice as high as air traffic and we’re above the jet stream, and yet 30 times closer than low-Earth orbit satellites,” Mikkel Frandsen, founder and CEO of Sceye, told Ars. “We can fly through day and night until the sun comes up the next morning and recharges the batteries, at which point we’re still at the same altitude and still over the same area of operation.”
Flying higher
There have been many past technology demonstrations and attempts to make stratospheric platforms commercially viable since the late 1990s, Frandsen said. In Sceye’s case, the company began testing a series of smaller prototypes in 2016 before eventually reaching the stratosphere with a 215-foot (65-meter) length version in 2021. The latest version extends to 270 feet (83 meters).
The lighter-than-air platform has also benefited from advances in material sciences that “were either not discovered or not understood back in the late 1990s,” Frandsen said. He highlighted the example of the discovery of graphene in 2004, which “greatly helped us optimize strength relative to weight on our hull, the energy density of our batteries, and performance relative to the area and weight of our solar panels.”
The design could eventually scale up to a high altitude platform system (HAPS) capable of lifting payloads as heavy as 551 pounds (250 kilograms). That would be between 25 and 50 times more payload capacity than competing stratospheric platforms like high-flying drones, according to Helena, a US nonprofit organization with a for-profit investment arm that has invested in Sceye.
Sceye’s current platform has already done multiple flight demonstrations with payloads exceeding 220 pounds (100 kilograms) and can provide up to 1 kilowatt of onboard power capability for any devices that it may be carrying.
A heavier payload and higher power capacity opens the door to bigger mission possibilities, such as someday using a single Sceye platform hovering in the stratosphere to provide mobile broadband coverage equivalent to 500 ground-based cell towers. That may prove useful for both enhancing commercial telecommunications services and providing emergency coverage during disaster scenarios.
Sceye’s high-altitude platform system (HAPS) seen from inside its hangar after launching from New Mexico on August 9, 2026.
Credit:
Sceye
Sceye’s high-altitude platform system (HAPS) seen from inside its hangar after launching from New Mexico on August 9, 2026.
Credit:
Sceye
Crossing the Pacific
The concept was put to the test after Sceye’s platform launched from its New Mexico base on August 9, 2026, and traveled more than 9,320 miles (15,000 kilometers) across the Pacific to reach Japan. That 13-day journey required the airship to navigate through strong winds and avoid potential bad weather “during a window of typhoon season,” said Johnny Truong, chief technology officer of Sceye.
The stratospheric platform has an auto-navigation system that allows the airship to fly on its own between point A and point B while accounting for factors like local wind conditions, Truong explained. That frees up human operators to focus on big-picture decisions, such as monitoring weather forecasts, running flight simulations for possible paths, and then chaining together a series of navigational waypoints for the smoothest possible journey.
The capability was first used during a previous 12-day flight from New Mexico to Brazil. But the monthlong mission to Japan and back—dubbed Service Test 1 (ST1)—was the longest test flight and deployment yet for Sceye’s platform.
“There were times when our actual plan trajectory and flight path was disrupted by a change in the weather,” Truong told Ars. “So what it would do was actually just park itself at a safe, quiet place in the weather and just station-keep a while until it moved on.”
The Sceye team monitors the performance of a high-altitude platform system (HAPS) during its roundtrip flight from New Mexico to Japan.
Credit:
Sceye
The Sceye team monitors the performance of a high-altitude platform system (HAPS) during its roundtrip flight from New Mexico to Japan.
Credit:
Sceye
Cell tower in the sky
The arrival over Shikoku—the smallest of Japan’s four main islands—allowed Sceye’s uncrewed airship to show how it could provide mobile broadband service from an operational altitude of about 54,000 feet (16.5 kilometers) to smartphones, laptops, and even drones. That demonstration was performed in partnership with the Japanese telecommunications firm SoftBank Corp, which has also invested directly in Sceye.
Sceye’s platform carried the equivalent of a 4G LTE base station for the demonstration, which simulated providing backup coverage in the case of an earthquake or similar large-scale disaster.
”It’s not the first time we flew a telco payload, but this is the first time where we actually flew into an area where we provide a live service,” Truong said. “What SoftBank did was, they disabled the cellular coverage area, and then we came in and we basically backfilled it.”
SoftBank’s team ran tests involving voice calls, text messaging and Internet web browsing, along with streaming YouTube videos and making video calls. They also verified that Sceye’s platform could support emergency alert messaging systems for earthquakes and tsunamis, along with supporting calls to a maritime emergency number.
The Japanese company even equipped drones with LTE cards to remotely control them using the Sceye-supported connectivity, along with receiving video transmissions from the drones. SoftBank also ran data throughput tests in several environments, including an open beach, a forest area with tree cover, and an indoor test inside a building.
The Sceye-supported connectivity passed testing in all three scenarios, although Truong acknowledged initially being unsure about whether the indoor test would succeed. Sceye’s team had decided not to run Sceye’s communications antenna at full power to minimize potential interference and to play it safe with local regulators.
For a separate edge computing experiment, a server aboard Sceye’s platform let SoftBank demonstrate an average roundtrip data-processing response time of 68 milliseconds. That supposedly represents a 40 percent reduction in latency compared to standard Internet-based cloud processing times.
Sceye’s high-altitude platform system (HAPS) seen above Japan during testing as a cell tower in the sky.
Credit:
Sceye
Sceye’s high-altitude platform system (HAPS) seen above Japan during testing as a cell tower in the sky.
Credit:
Sceye
Lasers in the stratosphere
The companies also tested setting up optical wireless communications using lasers to transmit data between Sceye’s platform in the stratosphere and towers or stations on the ground. A ground-based laser ranging system sent laser pulses toward Sceye’s moving platform, which carried a corner cube reflector that reflected laser signals back down to the ground-based system.
In the future, Sceye’s platform might act as a stratospheric relay station that links communications satellites in low-Earth orbit with ground infrastructure. That would help reduce the loss of optical signal involved in transmitting directly between satellites and ground stations through the Earth’s atmosphere, because there is much less signal attenuation when transmitting between space and the stratosphere.
Sceye’s HAPS could then act as a “reenergizer” to boost an optical signal received from space for retransmission down to the ground, or even switch over to radio frequency communication modes that can travel more cleanly through cloud cover down to the ground, Truong said.
Broader deployments of optical wireless communication could help handle the increased data rates expected of sixth generation (6G) mobile communications services, along with providing faster Internet and mobile connectivity to more remote regions of the world that are not connected to ground-based fiber-optic networks.
“You need those three layers to work together to make sure that nobody’s left behind, but also to make sure that you can get to the real-time services that are the promised land of 6G,” said Frandsen.
This could also provide additional resiliency for global communications at a time when the Internet’s undersea backbone of fiber-optic cables linking continents and islands faces greater threats from deliberate sabotage—not to mention accidental cable cuts from weighted fishing boat nets and ship anchors.
“You’ve seen stories where there’s a dispute and a boat for some reason forgets to raise their anchor and they suddenly take out that ocean cable,” Truong said. “Now you don’t have to worry about that because everything’s wireless… that leads to resiliency from an operational perspective.”
The trans-Pacific flight route of Sceye’s helium-filled platform as seen on September 1, 2026.
Credit:
Sceye
The trans-Pacific flight route of Sceye’s helium-filled platform as seen on September 1, 2026.
Credit:
Sceye
There and back again
By the time Sceye’s platform returned to New Mexico on September 5, it had traveled nearly 18,641 miles (30,000 kilometers) during its 30-day roundtrip to Japan and back.
The company and its partners are already looking ahead to future tests. SoftBank wants to perform additional testing around using the airship to quickly restore communications in disaster scenarios, along with potentially placing cameras and other sensors aboard to help with search-and-rescue operations, Truong explained.
“We can come in and basically place instant infrastructure and provide that service,” Truong said. “So from that perspective, it’s about being ready throughout the year and providing that service during those critical few days while you’re trying to restore service.”
But Sceye is also aiming to help provide regular cellular coverage to underserved areas where installing fiber-optic cables to provide Internet access is more economically prohibitive.
“A lot of our missions going forward are not a weeklong mission—they’re like multimonth to a yearlong mission,” Truong said. “We have one that we’re going to do earlier next year which is going to be anywhere from three to six months, with a plan to be a year-round kind of operation.”
Jeremy Hsu is a reporter exploring a wide range of topics across deep tech and AI. He has previously written for New Scientist, Scientific American, IEEE Spectrum, Wired, Undark Magazine and MIT Tech Review, among many other publications, about topics such as deepfakes, data centers, drones, battery tech, robotics, and GPS jamming. He also has a Master of Arts in Journalism from NYU, and a bachelor's degree from University of Pennsylvania in History and Sociology of Science, with a minor in English.

articles.title: Apple promises to ‘Pro and Tell’ on October 28, and we could finally get the touchscreen MacBook Pro we’ve been waiting for
articles.text:
Apple promises to 'Pro and Tell' on October 28, and this might be the long-awaited arrival of the touchscreen MacBook Pro
The new flagship MacBook might arrive alongside a refreshed iPad mini and iMac
- Apple tells us it will 'Pro and Tell' on October 28
- The touchscreen MacBook Pro, an iMac with M6, and an iPad mini with an OLED screen are likely incoming
- It comes in the middle of an incredibly busy product cycle for Apple
Apple’s on a roll! Just eight days after dropping the HomeView, HomePod mini 2, and Apple TV 4K, and four days before the iPhone Duo starts shipping, the Cupertino-based technology giant is teasing more.
In a post on X (formerly Twitter), Apple’s SVP of Marketing, Greg Joswiak, writes, “Can’t wait to pro and tell next week,” alongside an Apple logo being drawn. The same graphic was also posted to @HelloApple on Instagram with the caption, “About next week…” The latter gives us the timing and leaves us marking our calendars for a reveal similar to Apple’s recent home product launches. However, Joswiak’s post teases something Pro that could be on the horizon.
Alongside the teasers, Apple has also sent media invites for an experience in LA on October 28, 2026. That’s the same wording the company used to describe its ‘Welcome Home’ event, so I’d suspect there won’t be a formal keynote, but there will be plenty of hands-on time.
The teaser depicts the Apple logo being drawn using an array of colors, mostly silver, white, and blue, with small, vibrant pops of red, orange, and yellow. To me, it looks as though a finger could be drawing the logo, given the overall shape, or perhaps a brush of some sort is being used to create it.
Either way, it points to the likely arrival of new Macs or iPads. Remember, like most of Apple’s products, these devices feature an Apple logo on the back.
There’s been no shortage of rumors, and it’s likely that Apple will drop a significant update to the MacBook Pro family next week, finally delivering a touchscreen laptop.
That’s something the company has been pretty firm about ruling out, but it seems to have turned a corner if recent reports are to be believed. Both the new 14-inch and 16-inch models are expected to pair the first touchscreen on a Mac with an OLED display, delivering the same vibrant, rich viewing experience as an OLED iPhone or iPad Pro, all within a redesigned, slimmer notebook.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Under the hood, these flagship MacBooks will likely get Apple’s best chips, whether that’s the M6 or the M5 Ultra, which premiered with the Mac mini and Mac Studio in August 2026.
Recent reports also hint that the M6 could be coming to the iMac, which is due for an upgrade after launching with the M4 in 2024. A new entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro could also arrive with a design similar to the current generation, likely featuring the M6 chip instead of the M5 for better performance across the board, particularly for AI tasks.
Alongside the Mac, the iPad could also be in the mix, potentially hinted at by the vibrant colors and what appears to be a finer, brush-drawn Apple logo. Coming shortly after the iPhone Duo starts shipping, a major iPad mini upgrade is also rumored. It could carry a considerably higher price — a reminder that the current model starts at $699 / £699 / AU$949 — and add a ProMotion OLED display, a redesigned body, and a more capable chip under the hood.
I’ve been wishing for a redesigned iPad mini with Magic Keyboard support and a better screen for a while, so this would be music to my ears, and likely to many others’ too. The iPad lineup is still in pretty good shape, with the Air and Pro models already receiving updates with better processors earlier this year. Besides the iPad mini, the only other model likely due for an upgrade is the entry-level iPad, but it’s unclear whether it will be updated next week.
Either way, we only have a few more days to wait to see what Apple has been working on. After all, the company has promised to ‘Pro and Tell.’ Let me know what you’re most excited about in the comments below.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds. Make sure to click the Follow button!
Jacob Krol is the US Managing Editor, News for TechRadar. He’s been writing about technology since he was 14 when he started his own tech blog. Since then Jacob has worked for a plethora of publications including CNN Underscored, TheStreet, Parade, Men’s Journal, Mashable, CNET, and CNBC among others.
He specializes in covering companies like Apple, Samsung, and Google and going hands-on with mobile devices, smart home gadgets, TVs, and wearables. In his spare time, you can find Jacob listening to Bruce Springsteen, building a Lego set, or binge-watching the latest from Disney, Marvel, or Star Wars.

articles.title: Engineer builds tiny 3D-printed single-motor drone in their bedroom — 45-degree hinged rotor and sub-0.2ms firmware control pitch and roll
articles.text:
Engineer builds tiny 3D-printed single-motor drone in their bedroom — 45-degree hinged rotor and sub-0.2ms firmware control pitch and roll
Single-motor drones could be technically simpler than helicopters or quadcopters, but they require a lot more complex programming.
A software engineer who’s also into drones and 3D printing has shared a single-motor drone that they built inside their home and tested on their bed. Joshua Bird shared a video of how they created it on YouTube, highlighting the unique technique they used to maintain controllability and stability. The design used a combination of a hinged propeller, rapid changes to the motor’s rotation speed, and a custom flight controller and motor controller firmware that allowed the motor to react to necessary changes in under 0.2 milliseconds.
Most rotary wing aircraft require a mechanism to counteract the torque generated by the motor or engine and to change its flight direction, typically with the use of a swash plate to change rotor disk attitude and a secondary propeller. While this method has been effective for decades, it has made rotary-wing aircraft heavier and more complex. This single-motor drone cut the need for a secondary mechanism by constantly adjusting the speed of the motor — speeding it up produces more reaction torque while slowing it down applies opposite reaction torque. This essentially turns into a balancing act between these two forces to reduce the torque on the drone body to a more manageable level.
The hinged rotor also relies on the same mechanism for directional control instead of relying on a swashplate. Each rotor blade sits on a 45-degree hinge that makes it pivot when the motor accelerates. As this happens, one blade pitches up to produce more lift, while the other blade pitches down, reducing lift. By accelerating and decelerating the motor as needed, Bird would be able to change the drone’s roll and pitch movement. It also combines this with the main rotor torque, motor adjustments, and the 3D-printed stabilizing fins to produce effective yaw control as well.
This was the theoretical part — the majority of the build video focused on fixing issues, including the part where Bird built a high-speed camera using a Sony camera and a flash unit controlled by a microcontroller that gets its signals from the prototype drone’s motor controller and camera shutter. This home-made high-speed camera revealed that the drone’s propellers were too soft and had to be replaced with a 3D-printed version that used sturdier filament.
The creator had to launch several test flights from their bed, many of which resulted in a crashed drone and some wall damage as they fine-tuned the drone’s programming. Bird was eventually able to make the 3D-printed drone fly, although it was limited to the bedroom because of its fixed-base IR beacon navigation method. They said that they eventually want to add a linear camera to the build so that it could take off in other environments in the future.
While other researchers and engineers have built smaller, quieter drones, with China even revealing a mosquito-sized unit, Joshua Bird’s single-motor project is still a unique take on drones. But what made the YouTube video much more interesting is the problem-solving process and the solutions that came afterward. You can check out the complete video below and even start your own similar project by looking at the Single Propeller Drone GitHub repository.

articles.title: Making the internet better for AI agents might make it worse for everyone else
articles.text:
Making the internet better for AI agents might make it worse for everyone else
Millions of AI agents are descending on a web built for humans. Websites are trying to keep them out, but the arrival of these new visitors could transform the internet.
This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here.
Until recently, you could divide internet users into just two categories: bots and people. Websites have long allowed bots to perform automated tasks, like capturing the content of web pages, but rules govern what they can access and how they behave. The web, after all, is designed primarily for people, even if we occasionally have to solve puzzles and captchas to prove we are not bots.
But this is being entirely upended by the release of personal AI agents, which can do things for you online, like booking flights or hotel rooms. They have recently been unleashed at scale by the launch of apps like OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse. Muse was downloaded 5 million times in its first month, and agentic web traffic tripled from August to September.
The mingling of these agents with human visitors—on an internet designed largely to prioritize people—has gone poorly, with many websites blocking AI agents that consumers have sent to negotiate prices or plan vacations. Still, if the demand for agents keeps going up, the internet will be increasingly redesigned for them instead of us.
Such changes are coming because agents really do mark a third category of web visitor. They’re not humans, of course, and they use the internet at machine speed. But they’re not quite bots, either, because they’re acting on behalf of individual people to do tasks that can be perfectly legitimate and useful. They just work faster than a person would.
Since agents don’t fit into the systems we have for differentiating bots from people, some platforms (especially the more security-conscious ones) have opted to just ban them entirely. TechCrunch recently reported people having trouble deploying their agents to websites ranging from Pizza Hut to Yelp, which doesn’t allow AI to book restaurant reservations. Amazon has blocked Muse’s agents and is waging a court battle against the AI startup Perplexity to block its agents too. Though a judge recently ruled in favor of Perplexity, Amazon has filed an appeal in which it argues that AI agents threaten its advertising business by making it harder to distinguish between ads seen by humans and those served to bots.
These blocks are annoying for early adopters, but Ethan Mollick, an associate professor at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, predicts it will soon affect the whole web. Once it becomes common knowledge that AI agents can be sent to request refunds or negotiate prices, for example, agents will overwhelm customer service departments to the point where they become unusable by real people. “Humans will eventually get very annoyed when their agents aren’t allowed to do this on their behalf,” he recently wrote on LinkedIn.
If demand for personal agents grows, platforms will find ways to let them in. That’s especially true because the vast majority of agentic web traffic is to e-commerce sites, meaning that platforms have money to be made if they allow the legions of new AI agents to shop on behalf of real people. Indeed, the e-commerce giant Shopify is already welcoming the agents by giving them their own checkout lanes that bypass pages designed for humans.
The pressing question is what will happen to the internet for the rest of us in the process. We’ve grown used to a web where, even as it’s increasingly designed to exploit our attention, humans have at least remained the intended users. But that internet might yield to one optimized instead for the agents that will eventually outnumber us, making it even more miserable for the humans who are left.
How might this go? Perhaps websites become increasingly neglected as destinations for real people. Humans who want to browse and compare products themselves encounter worse interfaces. Verification systems are imperfect; imagine constantly being asked to verify that you’re a human, not an agent (and hey, maybe you’ll need to get your iris scanned to do so). That sweater you want doesn’t have one price listed for everyone but instead displays different prices to different people’s agents. You can never tell when your agent’s recommendation is influenced by advertisements or platform commissions.
That’s a far cry from the future promised by Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI, in which AI agents will give consumers greater power and bargaining leverage. But that promise is not outlandish. Agents are capable of genuinely helping people by fighting bogus medical bills or researching more affordable car insurance, for example.
Whether they can actually be used for these purposes depends on what rules are set for how agents interact with websites and what exactly they’re allowed to do.
These rules are still being written. Some of them will benefit all of us—neither consumers nor businesses want credit card information to be waved around by agents wherever they roam the web, for example, and rules to keep agents more secure are a good thing. It’s the more contested ones, like whether businesses can block agents from their websites or prevent them from negotiating better deals for consumers, that will determine whether the web becomes a highway for agents working for us or against us.

articles.title: Jubilee, FSD Africa partner with 7 BimaLab insurtechs to pilot inclusive insurance in Kenya - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
East African financial services group Jubilee and development agency FSD Africa have partnered with seven insurtech startups from the BimaLab Africa accelerator network to develop and pilot affordable insurance products for underserved Kenyans.
BimaLab, an FSD Africa initiative, has supported 135 startups across 28 African countries over the past six years, helping develop more than 300 insurance solutions that now reach over 6.5 million customers.
The programme targets SMEs, informal sector workers, farmers and low-income households, segments that remain largely uninsured. East Africa is estimated to have more than 10 million SMEs, which account for over 70 per cent of jobs, yet insurance penetration among the segment averages about one per cent.
The seven firms – Dukatech Solutions, Aura Insure Technologies, Inclusivity Solutions, DPE, Fiinovate, Agrails and Ibisa Network – were selected through a competitive process from BimaLab’s alumni network. They will go through an eight-week product co-creation process with Jubilee before joint pilots kick off in Kenya next month.
The work will focus on three areas – low-cost bundled and embedded insurance distribution, insurance solutions for SME ecosystems, and wellness and engagement models that link customers to health and care services. Successful solutions could later be rolled out in other East African markets.
“There is a large group of Kenyans who work, earn and run businesses every day but still have little or no insurance coverage. We need to meet people where they are, with products that are affordable, relevant and simple to access,” said Juan Cazcarra, deputy group CEO of Jubilee Group.
“Working with these seven insurtechs gives us a practical way to test different products and distribution models with customers and learn what works.”
At Jubilee, the programme will be run through J-Hub, the group’s innovation and technology arm.

articles.title: Sahi’s Dale Vaz wants an AI financial team in every pocket
articles.text:
Sahi’s Dale Vaz wants an AI financial team in every pocket
From plain-language trading strategies to a Discipline Score that flags overtrading, Sahi’s Kyro shows how AI could give every Indian investor a personal team of financial agents, in their own language.
Opening a trading account in India now takes minutes. Knowing what to do once you’re in is much harder.
This gap was the focus of Dale Vaz’s keynote at TechSparks 2026. The co-founder and CEO of fintech company Sahi argued that the last decade of fintech solved the issue of access, but not outcomes.
“Everybody here has a broking app,” Vaz told the audience. “But when you think about outcomes, do people really feel confident about what to do with their money? The numbers indicate most of us are still struggling.”
The intent-capability gap
Vaz described a familiar pattern among retail investors. People start investing, then struggle to make sense of their portfolios. A bad day in the market leaves them unsure about whether to buy, sell, or quit altogether.
The cause, he said, is complexity: too much jargon, too much data, and too many tools. Investors are left with two poor choices. They can spend years becoming experts, or they can trust someone promising guaranteed returns.
Regulator-led investor education has helped, Vaz said, but a wide gap remains between people’s intent to grow their money and their capability to do it.
Why generic AI falls short
AI is increasingly pitched as the answer. But Vaz cautioned that general-purpose chatbots carry three serious flaws when money is involved.
The first is hallucination. “A model is confidently wrong. It will never tell you it’s wrong,” he said. That might be acceptable for an essay, but not for financial decisions.
The second is missing context. A chatbot can answer 'should I buy HDFC stock?' without knowing that half your portfolio is already in banking stocks.
The third is accountability. If a general chatbot gives you bad guidance, there is no regulatory protection and no one to call.
Meet Kyro: A purpose-built assistant
Sahi’s answer is Kyro, an agentic AI assistant built into its app and web platform. Vaz called it a “vertical harness” around an AI model. If the model is the engine, the harness is the car.
Kyro combines three things: personal context from a user’s activity on Sahi, 28 expert skills written by Sahi’s research team, and more than 100 tools. Those tools give Kyro “hands and legs," he said. Users can set price alerts, create conditional orders, build custom scanners, or describe a trading strategy in plain language and have Kyro turn it into executable code.
Crucially, the AI model doesn’t do the calculations. It routes requests to Sahi’s backend APIs, which return deterministic results. “When you say add four plus five, the model calls the calculator that we have built,” Vaz explained. This design keeps numbers out of the model’s hands and reduces the risk of hallucination.
A constitution for trust
Sahi built Kyro around a set of rules it calls a constitution. Answers must be grounded in facts, and Kyro is designed to say “I don’t know” when it should. The user always presses the final buy or sell button. Every output must come with evidence a person can check.
“If AI could just magically make money for everybody, the people making the models would have made all the money,” Vaz said. “AI can help augment our skills as investors, but it can never really replace the individual.”
The system is designed to comply with SEBI regulations, with in-country inference, data logging, and full traceability of conversations.
Early results
Kyro has been tested with more than 11,000 traders in a closed user group. It has generated over 2.7 lakh responses at a 99.2% success rate, and 78% of users returned after their first interaction.
Some use cases surprised the team. Many traders treat Kyro as a sounding board for losses and discipline problems. Others talk to it in Gujarati, Tamil, and Marathi.
What Kyro won’t do yet
Asked whether Kyro acts as an advisor, Vaz was direct: it does not. It has strict rules against buy or sell calls. Advisory features would require a separate SEBI investment advisory licence, which Sahi plans to pursue.
Vaz also previewed a Discipline Score. Based on academic research into why retail traders fail, it will flag habits such as overtrading, oversized positions, and revenge trading.
Looking further ahead, Vaz sees AI agents running exchange-approved algorithms for retail investors, and a future where every Indian has “a team of AI-enabled agents” watching their risk, portfolio, and taxes in their own language.
“We are at the first minute of the first day,” he said.

articles.title: Bras robot et écran géant : Apple préparerait un nouveau HomeView qui vous suit du regard
articles.text:
Apple vient à peine de lancer son HomeView qu’une version plus ambitieuse fait déjà parler d’elle. D’après les informations du journaliste Mark Gurman, la marque travaillerait d’ores et déjà sur un modèle plus haut de gamme, capable de corriger l’un des principaux défauts de la proposition.
 Power On: Apple’s new HomeView shows the undeniable potential of a higher-end version with a robotic arm. https://t.co/NVMPS3cJOo
— Mark Gurman (@markgurman) October 18, 2026
Un écran qui se tourne tout seul
Comme le rappelle l’informateur, Apple propose actuellement deux versions du HomeView. L’un des écrans est pensé comme un cadre à poser au mur, tandis que l’autre peut se poser sur une table ou sur le plan de travail d’une cuisine. Quand plusieurs personnes entourent l’appareil, il faut le réorienter à la main. Chaque utilisateur doit tourner l’écran vers lui pour pouvoir s’en servir correctement. Apple voudrait corriger ce problème avec le futur HomeView.
D’après le journaliste Bloomberg, la future version serait équipée d’un bras motorisé capable de faire pivoter l’écran à 360 degrés en cas de besoin. Grâce à la reconnaissance vocale, déjà implémentée sur la version actuelle, l’appareil identifierait qui parle et se tournerait automatiquement vers son interlocuteur du moment. Le fonctionnement du bras rappelle évidemment Center Stage, la fonction qui recadre l’image sur vous pendant un appel vidéo, mais en version motorisée.
Ce n’est pas tout. Apple miserait aussi sur un écran plus spacieux. Le groupe miserait cette fois sur un écran de 9 pouces, contre 7 pouces pour le HomeView actuel. Selon Mark Gurman, Apple pourrait choisir de baptiser ce futur appareil « HomeView Max », « Ultra » ou « 360 ». Il ne remplacerait pas le modèle actuel, mais viendrait l’accompagner, enrichissant ainsi la gamme d’appareils Apple taillés pour la maison connectée. Selon Bloomberg, le HomeView robotisé pourrait arriver sur le marché dès l’année prochaine, voire en 2028. Gageons que ce modèle haut de gamme puisse faire son entrée sur le marché européen.
À lire aussi : Les rescapés de l’Apple Car réinventent la voiture… en s’inspirant du buggy lunaire d’Apollo
Un vieux projet de robot maison
L’idée d’un bras robotisé n’est pas nouvelle chez Apple. Après l’abandon du projet Apple Car, le géant de Cupertino avait réorienté ses ambitions robotiques de l’automobile vers la maison autour de 2024. Un appareil estimé autour de 1 000 dollars avait alors été évoqué par une série de fuites. Quelques mois plus tard, Apple avait même dévoilé le concept d’une lampe robotisée qui exprime des émotions et peut bouger. Ce concept était très proche de la fameuse mascotte des studios Pixar. Il ne s’agissait encore que d’un projet de recherche, mais il montrait bien dans quelle direction Apple ambitionnait d’aller.

articles.title: Apple anuncia otro evento y todo apunta a un cambio histórico en el MacBook Pro
articles.text:
Apple confirmó un segundo evento para octubre en donde presentará más dispositivos. A una semana de anunciar el HomeView y la actualización del Apple TV 4K, los de Cupertino preparan otra ronda de productos. La tecnológica envió invitaciones para su evento Pro and Tell, en el que podría debutar el rumoreado MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil.
De acuerdo con Bloomberg, Apple reveló que llevará a cabo un nuevo evento el 28 de octubre de 2026 en Los Ángeles. Según el periodista Mark Gurman, la compañía dedicará un día completo para presentar los nuevos MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil y un nuevo modelo de gama baja con el chip M6. Apple también aprovechará la ocasión para mostrar actualizaciones al iMac y al iPad mini.
Históricamente, octubre ha sido el mes que Apple reserva para presentar sus productos para usuarios avanzados. Mientras que septiembre es para el iPhone y el Apple Watch, octubre está orientado a los MacBook Pro, iPad Pro y versiones renovadas de otros productos. Estos eventos también sirven como escaparate para anunciar los nuevos chips Apple Silicon que llevarán los ordenadores que se venderán durante todo el año.
Esta ocasión no será diferente, ya que los de Cupertino preparan un nuevo MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil y chips M5 Pro y M5 Max. Tras años de rumores y especulaciones, Apple estaría lista para mostrar un dispositivo que competiría con otros portátiles 2 en 1 de la gama premium. Según el último reporte de Gurman, la tecnológica lanzará dos variantes de 14 y 16 pulgadas.
Un MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil y una función del iPhone
Aunque la característica más importante es la pantalla táctil, los nuevos MacBook Pro traerán una batería de novedades. El chasis debutará con un esperado rediseño y la pantalla OLED contará con la Isla Dinámica que encontramos en el iPhone. Esta función dejará de ser exclusiva de los móviles y dará el salto por primera vez a los ordenadores, ofreciendo compatibilidad nativa en macOS.
A diferencia de otros años, Apple repetirá los chips M5 Pro y M5 Max en sus portátiles más poderosos. Hace unos meses se reportó que la compañía canceló el desarrollo de los M6 Pro y M6 Max, dejando al M6 como único procesador de esa familia. Apple dará el salto a los M7 Pro y M7 Max, que se presentarán a finales de 2027 si la escasez de componentes lo permite.
Además de los MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil, la tecnológica prepara un modelo básico con chip M6 y pantalla mini LED con ProMotion. Además, se espera un iMac de 24 pulgadas actualizado al M6, pero sin cambios en el diseño ni la pantalla. Por último, la compañía también mostrará una actualización a la línea iPad en la que destaca un iPad Mini con pantalla OLED, así como un iPad Pro.
El evento Pro and Tell de Apple se llevará a cabo el próximo 28 de octubre de 2026 en Los Ángeles. Como siempre, en Hipertextual tendremos todas las novedades que se anuncien en esta y las próximas presentaciones.

articles.title: No esperes al Black Friday: el MacBook Neo cae ahora de precio
articles.text:
Cuando salió al mercado, el MacBook Neo partía de los 699 euros, un precio muy competitivo para el portátil de la firma de la manzana mordida. Al tiempo, y por la llamada crisis de la RAM, el portátil más barato de Apple subió de precio 100 euros. Aunque ahora, Amazon, lo ha vuelto a rebajar antes del Black Friday y puedes llevártelo por 759 euros. No es que la rebaja sea brutal (es un 5% de descuento), pero sí es cierto que encontrar un dispositivo Apple con descuento siempre se puede considerar un chollo.
Apple MacBook Neo de 13 Pulgadas con Chip A18 Pro 256 GB
Un portátil ideal para estudiantes
El MacBook Neo es perfecto para un usuario básico, ya no solo para estudio, sino también a nivel laboral. Su cerebro es el chip A18 Pro (el mismo que monta el iPhone 16 Pro), por lo que ofrece buen rendimiento para ofimática, navegación web e incluso ediciones sencillas de imágenes.
Su pantalla es de 13 pulgadas y si hay algo que lo caracteriza, es su ligereza (solo pesa 1,23 kg), lo que lo convierte en un equipo ideal para transportarlo a diario a la universidad o incluso a la oficina sin notar que lo llevas.
En cuanto a su batería, la compañía promete hasta 16 horas de streaming de vídeo y hasta 11 horas de navegación web, tiempo más que de sobra para cumplir con una jornada laboral o de estudios sin pasar por el cargador.

articles.title: Pluribus : un scénario « complètement fou » et un tournage imminent, la saison 2 passe à l'attaque
articles.text:
Alors que les nouvelles de la saison 2 filtraient au compte-gouttes depuis des mois, Rhea Seehorn, l’interprète de Carol Sturka, a confié à Deadline qu’elle partait « très bientôt » sur le plateau. Ses propos ont été publiés ce lundi 19 octobre, en marge d’une soirée de l’Academy Museum, à Los Angeles.
Un premier épisode « totalement barjot », selon Rhea Seehorn pour la saison 2 de Pluribus
L’actrice a déjà lu le script du premier épisode de la saison 2 de Pluribus. Elle le qualifie de « totalement barjot » (« absolute bananas»).
Elle n’a rien dévoilé de l’intrigue. Le contenu de la boîte laissée dans l’allée à la fin de la première saison reste l’une des grandes questions des fans. L’actrice rappelle seulement que chaque détail semé par Vince Gilligan a son importance.
Un tournage prévu fin octobre à Albuquerque
Le tournage doit commencer le 31 octobre à Albuquerque, au Nouveau-Mexique, selon le service de suivi Production List cité par Gold Derby. Vince Gilligan tourne ses séries dans cette ville depuis Breaking Bad. Rhea Seehorn y retrouvera le rôle de Carol, que Vince Gilligan a écrit spécialement pour elle.
La série est pourtant encore en pré-production, et son écriture n’est pas terminée. Mi-septembre, en coulisses des Emmys, Vince Gilligan expliquait que seuls les deux premiers épisodes étaient écrits, même si l’intrigue de toute la saison est arrêtée. En juillet, Matt Cherniss, responsable des programmes d’Apple TV, n’avait donné aucune date de sortie, sans écarter un retour en 2028.
Pluribus aborde cette suite avec six Emmy Awards remportés en septembre pour sa première saison, dont celui de la meilleure actrice pour Rhea Seehorn et celui du meilleur scénario pour Vince Gilligan.

articles.title: London’s Emerald secures €1.66 million to scale its preventive healthcare platform | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Emerald, a London-based preventive healthcare platform, has secured an additional €1.66 million (£1.4 million/$1.85 million) in funding. This brings the company’s total funding to date to €3.44 million (£2.9 million).
The latest funding includes an €832.2k (£700k) grant from Innovate UK, Emerald’s second award from the organisation, together with a further €832.2k (£700k) in venture capital investment secured after the award. All existing investors, along with new backers including Sequel and Highgoal, supported the round, and Emerald’s valuation increased from its previous funding round.
Alexander Badalyan, co-founder and CEO of Emerald, explained, “There’s huge demand for access to simple healthcare tools that move beyond just testing. People want to understand what those results mean and the steps they can take to boost their long-term health – informed by guidance from trusted medical experts.
“A preventative approach to healthcare significantly improves long-term health outcomes by providing a more holistic view of a patient’s health, highlighting potential issues before they become critical, and empowering people to enter the right pathway earlier.
“Achieving this ambition is a cornerstone of the current Government’s current health agenda – but the NHS cannot deliver this shift alone. Government efforts must be matched with innovative solutions that are able to have widespread reach. Emerald has unlocked access to millions of potential users through its partnerships – with ambitions to become the UK’s go-to platform for long-term health management. This additional funding allows us to build on the demand we’re already seeing, deepen these partnerships, and expand care.”
Founded in 2024, Emerald says its platform combines in-clinic laboratory screening with a digital platform that brings results, wearable data and health history together in one place. This approach helps members identify potential health risks earlier and empowers them to take control of their long-term health.
Explaining its differentiating factor, Emerald notes that traditional health checks capture one moment in time, whereas the UK startup connects comprehensive testing with users’ past results, lifestyle, and wearable data to reveal patterns, priorities, and changes.
It further notes that every member is paired with a GP who can diagnose, prescribe, and make formal referrals into both private and NHS care where appropriate.
The company highlighted that it is clinician-founded and Care Quality Commission registered, offering regulated activities including diagnostic and screening procedures and treatment of disease, disorder or injury. The platform is also authorised as a UKCA Class I medical device with the MHRA.
Since the beginning of 2026, the company reported that it has grown its member base tenfold and has now processed more than 100k laboratory tests, with repeat-screening data. According to the startup, this data highlights improvements in cholesterol levels for two out of three users, blood sugar levels dropping by a third, and reduced inflammation amongst members dropping by almost half. In January this year, the company announced the closure of its €1.78 million ($2 million) pre-Seed round.
Emerald also mentioned that it has significantly expanded its clinical capabilities and, over the last 12 months, it has announced partnerships with Pluxee, Epassi, Yonder and other businesses across the employee benefits, FinTech and fitness sectors to scale its offering.
With this approach, the company intends to enable employers to include its services as part of their existing benefits offering.
Chris Sawyer, Innovation Lead, Digital Health at Innovate UK, said, “Connecting earlier health insights with appropriate care is an important opportunity for healthcare innovation in the UK. Through this award, we are supporting Emerald’s development of AI-enabled technology designed to help clinicians deliver more personalised, proactive care. We look forward to seeing the project progress and the impact it could have on health outcomes.”
The company plans to use this additional funding to support commercial expansion and further development of its products and clinical services as the platform aims to reach one million members over the next three years.
The Innovate UK grant will specifically support the expansion of Emerald’s AI applications and underlying technology, with the aim of improving healthcare outcomes across the UK.

articles.title: Samsung va utiliser la technologie TSMC pour les prochaines puces mémoire de Nvidia, selon un journal coréen
articles.text:
TSMC est clairement le monstre de la fonderie actuellement. Et ce tellement que ses concurrents directs se mettent à utiliser ses procédés pour les plus gros clients.
Samsung est le leader mondial aujourd'hui des composants mémoires. Mais si le géant sud-coréen est aussi le concurrent le plus crédible de TSMC dans les procédés de production des puces les plus avancées, il reste tout de même bien moins prisé que le leader taïwanais. Une situation illustrée par cette première étonnante !
Samsung va user d'un procédé en 3 nm de TSMC pour la mémoire HBM destinée à NVIDIA
C'est une nouvelle intéressante qui vient de nous être apprise par le média sud-coréen Seoul Economic Daily, et dont Reuters se fait l'écho. En effet, d'après ce dernier, Samsung va faire appel au procédé en 3 nanomètres développé par TSMC.
Ce dernier va être utilisé pour produire les puces de base des composants mémoires HBM de dernière génération qui sont destinées à NVIDIA - la NVHBM (NVIDIA High Bandwidth Memory). Une architecture de mémoire conçue par NVIDIA et qui offre des gains de performance importants par rapport au HBM4e.
Une demande qui émane de NVIDIA
Cette annonce est la conséquence de la volonté de NVIDIA de standardiser la production et la validation de ce composant. La firme de Jensen Huang a ainsi demandé aux trois grands noms de la RAM, SK Hynix, Micron, et donc Samsung, d'utiliser le même procédé en 3 nanomètres de TSMC.
Après une revue interne de la demande, Samsung a finalement accepté la requête de NVIDIA. Le Sud-coréen va tout de même en parallèle continuer à produire son HBM standard ainsi que les composants sur mesure destinés à d'autres clients. Maintenant, reste à savoir si cette première d'une collaboration entre TSMC et Samsung fera école - et pourra être requise par d'autres clients - ou si Samsung fera en sorte de garder le côté unique de ce partenariat.
Source : Reuters

articles.title: Google baut Gemini schon wieder um – welche Werkzeuge jetzt verschwinden und was sie ersetzt
articles.text:
Neues Namenschaos bei Google Gemini: Welche Funktion künftig welche Aufgabe übernimmt
In der KI-Anwendung Gemini baut Google in den kommenden Wochen gleich zwei zentrale Funktionen um und vergibt dafür neue Namen. Die bisherigen, für Einzelaufgaben angepassten KI-Helfer namens „Gems“ heißen künftig „Skills“, während der erst im Frühjahr vorgestellte Hintergrund-Agent „Gemini Spark“ seinen Eigennamen verliert und im Chat schlicht unter der Bezeichnung „Tasks“ läuft.
Mit dem Umbau löst Google verstreute Untermenüs auf und verlagert die Werkzeuge direkt in das zentrale Eingabefeld des Chatbots, wie das Unternehmen in einem Blogbeitrag mitteilt. Für Nutzer:innen bringt die Umstellung zwar neue Kombinationsmöglichkeiten, führt aber auch zu gestrichenen Funktionen, höheren Hürden beim Datenschutz und einer unübersichtlichen Doppelstruktur bei Zeitplänen.
Aus Gems werden Skills: Modulare Arbeitsanweisungen im offenen Markdown-Format
Wer Gemini bisher für wiederkehrende Aufgaben wie das Redigieren von Texten anpassen wollte, musste dafür ein sogenanntes „Gem“ anlegen und jedes Mal ein separates Chatfenster öffnen. Laut einer Ankündigung im Google-Workspace-Blog lassen sich solche gespeicherten Eingabebefehle (Prompts) sowie angehängte Referenzdateien künftig als „Skills“ direkt im laufenden KI-Chat nutzen.
Der Aufruf erfolgt über einen Schrägstrich oder künftig über das Klammeraffen-Symbol direkt in der Textzeile, wobei sich anders als früher auch mehrere Skills in einer einzigen Anfrage kombinieren lassen. Technisch nutzt Google dafür den offenen Standard „SKILL.md“ auf Basis der einfachen Auszeichnungssprache Markdown, sodass Nutzer:innen ihre hinterlegten Regeln als Textdatei herunterladen und in Programme anderer Anbieter übertragen können.
Der Wechsel ist allerdings mit Einschränkungen verbunden, da bestehende Gem-Funktionen wie die Arbeitsfläche „Canvas“, die Websuche „Deep Research“ sowie die Video- und Musikgenerierung zum Start nicht mit Skills funktionieren. Zudem synchronisiert Google die erstellten Skills nicht zwischen der Gemini-App und den Workspace-Anwendungen wie Docs oder Gmail, wie aus der zugehörigen Dokumentation für Administrator:innen hervorgeht.
Für private Google-Konten setzt die Nutzung von Skills außerdem voraus, dass die Speicherung der eigenen Aktivitäten in den Kontoeinstellungen eingeschaltet ist. Ab dem 17. November 2026 wandelt Google bestehende Gems auf Privatkonten automatisch in Skills um und stellt im selben Monat auch das Experimentier-Werkzeug „Opal“ für Mini-Anwendungen ein.
In Unternehmen und Organisationen mit Workspace-Lizenzen verzögert sich die Einführung derzeit noch. Die alten Gems lassen sich dort noch länger nutzen und werden für Geschäftskund:innen erst ab dem 1. März 2027 sowie für Bildungseinrichtungen ab dem 1. Juni 2027 abgeschaltet.
Abschied von Gemini Spark: Hintergrund-Agent wandert als Tasks in das Chatfenster
Noch kurzlebiger war der Name von Googles eigenständigem KI-Agenten, einem Programm, das mehrstufige Arbeitsaufträge selbstständig im Hintergrund abarbeitet. Google-Vizepräsident Josh Woodward hatte den Assistenten erst auf der Entwicklerkonferenz Google I/O im Mai 2026 unter der Bezeichnung „Gemini Spark“ vorgestellt.
Nur fünf Monate später streicht der Konzern den eigenen Menüpunkt wieder aus der Seitenleiste und verlagert die Funktion in das Hauptfenster, wie 9to5Google berichtet. Über dem Texteingabefeld sitzt nun ein Umschalter namens „Task“, über den sich bis zu 15 mehrstufige Aufträge gleichzeitig starten lassen, etwa zum Aufräumen des E-Mail-Postfachs oder zur Preisüberwachung von Flügen.
Um Aufgaben auf Webseiten auszuführen, greift Gemini laut dem Support-Dokument zu Tasks und Workflows entweder auf den lokalen Chrome-Browser des Computers samt eingeloggten Konten zu oder nutzt einen fernsteuerbaren Browser auf Googles Cloud-Servern. Dieser sogenannte Remote-Browser arbeitet Aufträge auch dann weiter ab, wenn das eigene Smartphone oder Notebook ausgeschaltet ist.
Zwar soll das System vor sensiblen Schritten wie Einkäufen, Passworteingaben oder dem Versenden von Nachrichten eine Bestätigung einholen, doch Google weist in den Unterlagen selbst darauf hin, dass diese Schutzmechanismen fehleranfällig sind. Läuft ein Auftrag während der Abwesenheit der Nutzer:innen über die Cloud, lassen sich unbeabsichtigte Aktionen oder die Weitergabe persönlicher Daten an Dritte unter Umständen nicht rechtzeitig aufhalten.
Doppelte Zeitpläne in Gemini und Einschränkungen für den DACH-Raum
Unübersichtlich wird die Bedienung zudem dadurch, dass Google in der Seitenleiste unter dem Begriff „Zeitpläne“ (Schedules) zwei technisch getrennte Systeme nebeneinander führt. Einfache Zeitpläne für normale Chats führen lediglich Textanfragen zu festen Uhrzeiten aus und berechnen die Antwort bis zu eine Stunde im Voraus, wie Google in der Hilfe zu Zeitplänen in Chats erläutert.
Davon getrennt existieren Zeitpläne für die neuen Tasks, die als automatische Auslöser für mehrstufige Hintergrundaufträge dienen. Laut der Dokumentation zu Zeitplänen für Tasks starten diese nicht nur nach der Uhrzeit, sondern reagieren über Filter auch auf neu eintreffende E-Mails in Gmail oder auf aktuelle Nachrichtenereignisse.
Für Anwender:innen in Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz bleibt dieser zweite Teil der Neuerungen vorerst gesperrt, da Google die Europäische Union und die Schweiz bei den cloudbasierten Tasks und den zugehörigen Ereignis-Zeitplänen derzeit ausnimmt. Die neuen Skills sowie die einfachen Zeitpläne für normale Chats schaltet das Unternehmen hingegen auch im deutschsprachigen Raum für kostenlose und kostenpflichtige Konten frei.
Dort, wo die Funktion verfügbar ist, setzt die Aufgabenautomatisierung über Tasks neben einem Mindestalter von 18 Jahren ein kostenpflichtiges Abonnement der Stufen Google AI Pro oder Ultra voraus. Wer hierzulande eigene Gems nutzt, sollte seine hinterlegten Anweisungen und Wissensdateien vor der automatischen Umstellung am 17. November 2026 dennoch lokal sichern, falls benötigte Werkzeuge in den neuen Skills noch fehlen.

articles.title: Onafriq negotiated Baxi’s sale months before its closure
articles.text:
When Onafriq announced it was shutting down Baxi, its Nigerian agent banking business, on October 16, it marked the end of a five-year expansion effort that began when the company acquired one of Nigeria’s largest independent agent banking networks. But months before announcing the closure, the pan-African payments company had been negotiating a sale of Baxi.
The proposed sale, which covered the entire agency banking operation active only in Nigeria, remained unresolved as of July, according to Onafriq’s audited financial statements filed in the United Kingdom.
In the statement announcing Baxi’s closure, the company cited inflation, naira depreciation, rising operating costs, shrinking margins, and growth in alternative payment methods such as account-to-account (A2A) transfers, which weakened offline payments. It said the economics of running an offline agent network had become unsustainable.
Onafriq’s statement did not mention the prospective buyer or the status of the negotiations. As of July 29, when the accounts were approved, negotiations were still ongoing, and Onafriq said it could not reliably estimate the structure, timing, or financial impact of a sale.
“During 2026, Onafrıq Nigeria Payments Limited entered into a non-binding memorandum of terms with a purchaser in respect of the proposed divestment of the agency business,” the company said in the financial statements. “The proposed transaction contemplates the sale of 100% of the agency business and related operations, subject to the terms and conditions to be agreed between the parties in a definitive asset purchase agreement.”
By then, the business had already suffered a sharp financial decline. Onafriq’s agency services revenue fell 56% to $13.4 million in 2024, from $30.4 million the previous year. The company also wrote off the remaining $4.56 million in goodwill tied to its Nigerian payments business, reflecting a decline in the value it expected to recover from the investment.
The attempted sale reversed the strategy that brought Onafriq into Nigeria. The company had acquired Baxi to connect a vast network of cash-based agents to its pan-African payments infrastructure.
Five years later, it was looking for an acquirer to take over that network. By October, it was telling Baxi’s agents—over 460,000 as of 2025—to move their funds elsewhere.
An unfinished sale
Baxi’s declining revenue was only part of its financial troubles. Although Onafriq cut agency services costs from $17 million in 2023 to $8.7 million in 2024, gross profit fell even faster, declining by 65% from $13.4 million to $4.7 million, according to its financial report.
The group’s agency business generated about $35 in gross profit for every $100 in revenue in 2024, down from $44 the previous year. That left considerably less money to cover salaries, technology, and other operating expenses.
By the time Onafriq began negotiating a sale in 2026, its agency services generated substantially less gross profit than they did two years earlier. The business also operated company-owned point-of-sale (PoS) terminals and provided short-term credit to agents whose wallet balances were running low.
According to Onafriq, agents typically had one to seven days to repay the loans, with interest rates ranging from 2.5% to 7% for each loan. The company funded the credit from its own resources, assessed agents’ creditworthiness, and collected repayments and managed defaults.
In July 2026, Onafriq said its Nigerian subsidiary, Onafriq Nigeria Payments Limited, owed ₦13.8 billion ($10.4 million) to Zenith Bank, a Nigerian tier-1 lender, and ₦6.1 billion ($4.6 million) to Stanbic IBTC Bank, a mid-tier bank, in outstanding overdrafts, bringing the total to ₦19.9 billion ($15 million), its filings showed.
“We entered Nigeria with conviction and commitment, but did not achieve the outcome we set out for,” Dare Okoudjou, Onafriq’s founder and chief executive officer, said in the statement announcing Baxi’s shutdown in Nigeria.
The economics behind Baxi’s retreat
Onafriq had already begun writing down the value of its Nigerian payments business before Baxi’s shutdown. It wrote off $2.4 million in goodwill in 2023 and the remaining $4.56 million in 2024, according to its filings.
Goodwill is the extra value recorded when a company buys a business, beyond the value of its identifiable net assets. The write-offs meant Onafriq no longer expected the business’s future earnings to justify that extra value.
However, other parts of Onafriq’s group-wide business were performing better. Revenue from money transfer fees grew by 20% to $43.9 million in 2024. The group’s card fee revenue also jumped 22%.
The contrasting performance helps explain why Onafriq retained its payments network and card-issuing services while closing Baxi. Yet, Nigeria’s wider PoS market presented a more complicated picture.
According to the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS), the country’s payments switch, PoS transactions’ value rose 79% to ₦18.78 trillion ($14.1 billion) in the first quarter of 2026. The number of deployed PoS terminals had more than doubled, from 2.45 million at the end of 2023 to 5.56 million at the end of 2024.
But the growth in transaction value concealed a much slower increase in the number of payments. In 2024, NIBSS data showed PoS transaction volumes rose by just 8%, from 1.4 billion to 1.5 billion, even as deployed terminals increased by 127%.
The number of terminals was expanding much faster than the transactions passing through them. For agent banking providers, more devices in the market meant greater competition for customers, without a corresponding increase in the number of transactions from which they could earn commissions.
Nigeria added PoS machines faster than transactions
Between 2023 and 2024, deployed PoS terminals more than doubled, but transaction volumes barely grew. Explore what that meant for the number of transactions per terminal, as Onafriq’s Baxi business struggled.
In 2024, Nigeria recorded roughly 270 annual PoS transactions for every terminal deployed at year-end, compared with about 571 in 2023.
Meanwhile, Baxi’s economics were deteriorating
Onafriq’s reported agency services figures show what happened to the business as Nigeria’s wider PoS network expanded. These are group agency services figures, not a measure of transactions per Baxi agent.
Competition was also coming from much larger operators. Moniepoint, one of Baxi's rivals, already had over 800,000 PoS terminals in Nigeria at the end of 2024. By 2026, the number had grown to over one million active PoS terminals in the country.
The Nigerian fintech unicorn said it served over six million businesses in 2025, underscoring the scale of the networks Baxi was competing against, which made its business hard to justify.
From expansion to exit
Onafriq entered Nigeria's agent banking market in October 2021, when the company, then known as MFS Africa, announced its acquisition of Capricorn Digital Limited, the company behind Baxi. The deal was completed in March 2022 after receiving the Central Bank of Nigeria's (CBN) approval.
At the time, Baxi had more than 90,000 agents providing cash withdrawals, transfers, and bill payments. The network processed over $1.6 billion in transactions in 2021, making it one of Nigeria's largest independent agent banking networks.
The acquisition was intended to connect Baxi's physical distribution network to MFS Africa's cross-border payments infrastructure. In June 2022, the company also secured debt financing from Stanbic IBTC Bank to support Baxi's expansion.
Five years later, Onafriq is dismantling that strategy. Following the shutdown, it said it had transferred Baxi's agents to another principal bank and given them 30 days to move their funds to a principal bank of their choice.
Onafriq will continue operating in Nigeria through its payments network and card-issuing services, but without the agent banking business it acquired to establish a foothold in the country's offline payments market.

articles.title: NestJS 12: ESM Packages, Standard Schema Validation and Native Observability
articles.text:
NestJS, the TypeScript framework for building server-side Node.js applications, has released version 12, a major release that moves its core packages to ESM, adds first-class Standard Schema validation, rebuilds the CLI and introduces an official observability SDK. It follows April's roadmap, and creator Kamil Myśliwiec's announcement on X has passed 1,100 likes and 66,000 views.
The ESM change is the headline, largely because it asks so little of existing teams. Core packages now ship as ESM, but CommonJS applications keep working through Node.js require(esm) support, which is why v12 requires Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+. nest new now asks whether to generate a CJS or ESM project, with ESM projects defaulting to Vitest and oxlint, while Rspack replaces webpack as the monorepo bundler. Developer Anton Chapala's preview benchmarks found no meaningful startup or memory gains from ESM, concluding it "is a massive cleanup of tooling and configuration debt" rather than a performance upgrade.
Day-to-day ergonomics change most around validation. Route decorators such as @Body(), @Query() and @Param() accept a schema option taking any Standard Schema compatible object, so Zod, Valibot and ArkType work without third-party wrappers once the new pipe is registered.
class-validator remains the documented default. Blogger iiaku argued that building on a spec rather than on Zod directly "keeps the choice in my hands while removing the boilerplate", though a commenter on ByteIota's preview coverage noted that types must still be annotated by hand because Nest continues to rely on legacy TypeScript decorators.
The most debated addition is @nestjs/observe, which hooks into Nest's own lifecycle through a new instrument option instead of patching the HTTP server, reporting traces in terms of controllers and providers. APM vendor Scout Monitoring acknowledged the richer context but warned the SDK is "NestJS-only", lacks cross-stack correlation out of the box and risks "vendor lock-in at the framework level". A new nest deploy command, forwarding to the Mau platform, points the same way towards first-party services.
The NestJS Observe dashboard, source: Trilon
Upgrading from v11 means installing the latest CLI with npm i -g @nestjs/cli@latest and running nest upgrade, which moves every @nestjs/* package to v12, bumps TypeScript to v6 and applies mechanical changes such as the GraphQL Playground to GraphiQL switch and the NATS v3 client swap.
It deliberately does not convert projects to ESM, Vitest or oxlint. The migration guide covers the rest, including lifecycle hook ordering and Joi v18.
One GitHub issue prompted docs noting AWS Lambda runtimes need --experimental-require-module, while others report path aliases breaking under ESM and Fastify middleware exceptions hanging. The follow-up v12.1 has since added built-in cookies, CSRF protection and security headers.
NestJS is an open-source, MIT-licensed framework for building efficient and scalable server-side applications with TypeScript. It combines an Angular-inspired module and dependency injection architecture with Express and Fastify support, and has more than 76,000 stars on GitHub.

articles.title: Lua hoje: confira a fase da Lua desta terça-feira 20/10/2026
articles.text:
Hoje, 20 de outubro de 2026, a Lua está na fase crescente e 72% visível. Confira o calendário completo de fases da Lua deste mês, de acordo com o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet).
Confira as próximas fases
As fases da Lua no mês de outubro de 2026 começam no dia 3 com a chegada da Lua Minguante, às 10h26 (horário de Brasília). Depois disso, no dia 10, foi a vez da Lua Nova, que chegou às 12h50. A Lua Crescente surgiu às 13h13 do dia 18. Por fim, vem a Lua Cheia, dia 26, à 1h13.
Leia mais:
- Entenda o que é a Lua, como e quando ela se formou
- Saiba como tirar a melhor foto possível com uma câmera de celular
- 7 dicas para fotografar a lua com seu celular
Calendário fases da Lua em outubro de 2026
- Lua Minguante: dia 3, às 10h26
- Lua Nova: dia 10, às 12h50
- Lua Crescente: dia 18, às 13h13
- Lua Cheia: dia 26, à 1h13
O que é o ciclo lunar?
Uma lunação ou ciclo lunar, como é chamado o intervalo de tempo entre luas novas, é sutilmente variável, com média de duração de 29,5 dias. Durante esse período, ela passa pelas quatro fases principais (nova, crescente, cheia e minguante), e cada uma se prolonga por aproximadamente sete dias.
Também existem as “interfases”: quarto crescente e crescente gibosa (entre as fases nova e cheia) e minguante gibosa e quarto minguante (entre a cheia e a minguante).
Entenda cada fase da Lua
Lua Nova
Na Lua Nova, o satélite se posiciona entre a Terra e o Sol. Isso faz com que o lado iluminado da Lua fique voltado para o Sol, enquanto o lado escuro fica voltado para nós. Por esse motivo, a Lua não é visível no céu noturno. Essa fase marca o início de um novo ciclo lunar e está relacionada ao recomeço e a novas possibilidades.
Lua Crescente
Depois da Lua Nova, surge a fase Crescente. Aos poucos, uma pequena faixa iluminada começa a aparecer no céu, aumentando noite após noite. No início, vemos apenas um fino arco de luz, mas com o passar dos dias a parte iluminada cresce até que metade da Lua esteja visível, momento chamado de Quarto Crescente. Essa fase simboliza crescimento, desenvolvimento e a construção de novos caminhos.
Lua Cheia
Na Lua Cheia, a Terra se encontra entre o Sol e a Lua. Isso permite que o lado lunar voltado para nós receba luz por completo, tornando-se totalmente visível e brilhante no céu. É o período de maior intensidade luminosa, quando a Lua nasce no horizonte exatamente no momento em que o Sol se põe. A Lua Cheia é associada à plenitude, ao auge de processos e à energia em seu ponto máximo.
Lua Minguante
Após a Lua Cheia, a luz da Lua começa a diminuir gradualmente. A cada noite, vemos menos da sua superfície iluminada. Quando apenas metade dela está visível, ocorre o Quarto Minguante, fase oposta ao Quarto Crescente. A Lua continua a perder luminosidade até chegar novamente à Lua Nova, reiniciando o ciclo. A fase Minguante simboliza reflexão, encerramento e preparação para novos começos.
Qual a fase da Lua hoje?
Hoje a Lua está na fase Crescente.
Flávia Correia é jornalista do Olhar Digital, cobrindo Ciência e Espaço.

articles.title: Deux nouvelles caméras pour suivre les mouvements au jardin
articles.text:
D-Link : deux caméras de surveillance motorisées à moins de 85 € pour surveiller votre extérieur
Jardin sous bonne garde
Avec les DCS-6530 et DCS-8530, D-Link propose de surveiller une terrasse ou une entrée en 2K ou en 3K. Toutes deux peuvent suivre les mouvements et enregistrer sur microSD et, cerise sur le gâteau, sans abonnement obligatoire.
D-Link DCS-8530
D-Link DCS-6530
D-Link ajoute deux caméras Wi-Fi motorisées à son catalogue aux prix conseillés de 65,90 € pour la DCS-6530 et de 84,90 € pour la DCS-8530. Elles sont déjà en rayon. Sans fil pour la communication donc, mais elles fonctionnent sur secteur. Il faudra donc prévoir une prise à proximité.
Ça tourne dehors
La DCS-6530 filme en 2304 × 1296 pixels et dispose d’une rotation de 340°, avec une inclinaison sur 90°. Son boîtier IP65 est destiné à une installation extérieure sous abri indique D-Link. La DCS-8530 passe à 2880 × 1620 pixels, tourne sur 350° et bénéficie d’une protection IP66, un peu plus résistante aux projections d’eau. La première se connecte en Wi-Fi 6 sur la bande 2,4 GHz ; la seconde utilise le Wi-Fi 5, mais accepte aussi le 5 GHz.
Les deux modèles proposent la détection de personnes et le suivi automatique des mouvements. La DCS-8530 ajoute la reconnaissance des véhicules, utile pour une entrée de garage. L’application mydlink permet de consulter les images et de recevoir des alertes, tandis qu’un microphone et un haut-parleur servent à échanger quelques mots à distance.
La nuit porte couleur
D-Link annonce une vision nocturne en couleur sur les deux modèles. La DCS-6530 possède deux projecteurs et un éclairage infrarouge d’une portée annoncée de 8 m, contre 15 m pour la DCS-8530.
Les vidéos peuvent être enregistrées en continu sur une carte microSD jusqu’à 512 Go, non livrée par défaut. Si on souhaite ajouter la sécurité du stockage dans le cloud, il faudra en en revanche un abonnement mydlink.

articles.title: Aproveite: Nintendo Switch 2 entra em oferta relâmpago no Mercado Livre • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Aproveite: Nintendo Switch 2 entra em oferta relâmpago no Mercado Livre
Switch 2 com proposta multiuso e acesso a jogos exclusivos da Nintendo recebe raro desconto de 15% no Pix, mas promoção acaba ao meio-dia de hoje!
O Switch 2 está saindo por apenas R$ 3.814 no Pix no Mercado Livre. O mais recente console da Nintendo, que possui uma proposta de múltiplo uso e acesso a jogos exclusivos, recebe desconto de 15% sobre o preço original de R$ 4.499.
Embora não seja o menor preço histórico, esta é uma rara chance de adquirir o console por um preço menor, mas corra (mesmo!): a oferta relâmpago acaba ao meio-dia desta segunda-feira (19).
O destaque do Switch 2 é sua proposta como console híbrido. Assim como seu antecessor, o sistema mais vendido da Nintendo, ele pode ser usado conectado à TV por meio da dock, como portátil com os Joy-Cons conectados, ou como semiportátil apoiado sobre uma mesa.
Sua tela LCD de 7,9″, usada nos modos portátil e semiportátil, conta com resolução Full HD e taxa de 120 fps. Quando ligado à dock, o sistema suporta 4K a 60 fps ou 120 fps em 1080p e 2K, com HDR10 em TVs compatíveis, oferecendo uma experiência gamer fluida.
O hardware interno inclui um chip Nvidia T239 customizado, 12 GB de RAM e 256 GB de armazenamento expansível com cartões microSD especiais. Os Joy-Cons podem ser usados como um mouse quando apoiados em uma superfície, e a dock traz uma porta Ethernet nativa para conexões de rede mais estáveis.
O Switch 2 suporta boa parte da biblioteca do Switch original, e tem acesso a inúmeros games de franquias exclusivas da Nintendo, como Mario, The Legend of Zelda, Pokémon, Donkey Kong e Metroid, indisponíveis em sistemas concorrentes.
Sua bateria de 5.200 mAh resiste a até 6 horas de uso, segundo a fabricante. A dock é capaz de carregar o sistema quando usado como console de mesa, sem interromper a jogatina.
O Switch 2 (apenas R$ 3.814 no Pix) tem acesso ao Nintendo Switch Online, serviço que oferece jogos em rede e benefícios exclusivos para assinantes, como games clássicos de sistemas legados da companhia centenária de Quioto.

articles.title: Microsoft fixes game, app crashes caused by recent Windows update
articles.text:
Microsoft has fixed a known issue that caused games and Windows 11 apps using AC-3 (Dolby Digital) audio decoding to crash after installing the September 2026 preview update (KB5124010).
While KB5124010 is an optional update that requires clicking a "Download and install" link (reducing the number of potentially affected Windows users), it installs automatically on devices where the "Get the latest updates as soon as they're available" option is toggled on.
"In some cases the application can fail to launch, or close without warning. In other cases the application will work normally until certain features are used, such as playing music," Microsoft said when it acknowledged this issue two weeks ago. "Affected applications may vary and can include games, media players, and certain productivity applications."
However, it added that many modern apps that don't use Windows' built-in audio decoding for this type of encoding aren't affected, and that modern apps that use the legacy AC-3 codec often include their own audio decoding components.
In a new update to the Windows release health dashboard, Microsoft said the KB5127648 October 2026 Patch Tuesday update addresses this known issue and advised affected users to install it on affected systems running Windows 11 24H2 and later.
"We recommend you install the latest security update for your device as it contains important improvements and issue resolutions, including this one," it said.
Over the last several years, Microsoft has resolved multiple other audio issues impacting various software and Windows components.
For instance, two years ago it confirmed a bug that caused game audio to unexpectedly jump to full volume when using USB DAC sound systems and blocked Windows 24H2 upgrades on devices with incompatible Intel Smart Sound Technology (SST) audio drivers because of blue screen of death (BSOD) issues.
Last year, in January 2025, Microsoft addressed a similar issue that triggered audio playback problems on Windows 11 24H2 systems with USB audio device drivers and lifted a safeguard hold preventing upgrades because an incompatibility issue caused Bluetooth headsets and speakers to malfunction on systems with Dirac audio improvement software.
More recently, in September, Microsoft released emergency updates to fix another bug that triggered USB audio issues after installing the September 2026 KB5124008 and KB5124012 security updates.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.
