articles.title: Rivian's CEO says autonomy will enable 'dramatically different' vehicle designs | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Rivian is going full steam ahead on developing autonomous vehicle software for its EVs, to the point that it is willing to delay profitability. Founder and CEO RJ Scaringe said last week at TechCrunch Disrupt that he thinks autonomy will allow his company to build radically different kinds of vehicles than the outdoorsy SUVs and trucks it currently makes.
“Where it gets really interesting is when you think beyond R2 and R3 and start to imagine the form factors that you want to build for a personally owned autonomous vehicle. You know, it opens up all kinds of design opportunities. It can create dramatically different experiences,” he said in an interview with TechCrunch. “I’m wildly excited about what the next 10 years look like in transportation because of what this enables us to dream and think about.”
This is not a new idea, to be sure. A decade ago, autonomous vehicle companies, legacy automakers, and many others promised that autonomy, combined with the proliferation of battery-electric drivetrains (which are simpler and take up less space than their gas-powered predecessors), would produce a Cambrian explosion of new mobility form factors.
This led to all kinds of crazy concepts getting bandied about at the time. Mercedes-Benz touted a bubbly pod-like design, as well as a long sedan packed with tech. Toyota and others dreamed up “rooms on wheels.” Hyundai once even showed off its idea for a car with legs.
This promised design revolution never escaped the concept and prototyping phase. Autonomy took longer than those companies anticipated to develop, and automakers (new and old) struggled with the harsh realities of manufacturing and selling an entirely new category of vehicle.
The difference now is that Scaringe’s comments come at a time when there are real robotaxis roaming the streets of multiple cities around the world. The software that powers them has seemingly developed to a level that is capable enough to operate them safely on public roads at scale, even if there are still some issues to work out when it comes to integrating them into the urban fabric of cars, bikes, pedestrians, and emergency vehicles. The components that make up electric vehicle motors and batteries have gotten cheaper, and companies like Tesla and Rivian (and many more in China) have gotten better at building them at scale.
Rivian has a lot of work ahead before it gets to driverless vehicles. The company is at the beginning of its effort to scale production of the R2 SUV, which it needs to get right in order to reverse years of losses that it incurred to become a major EV player.
On the autonomy side, Rivian is just a few years removed from completely reworking its approach to self-driving software, and it still has a ways to go.
The company has shipped a driver-assistance system that allows drivers to take their hands off the wheel, while still watching the road. It has promised that, by the end of this year, that software will be capable of driving from start to finish — which the company calls “point-to-point navigation” — without intervention, though still under driver supervision. And it is working toward full autonomy, which it plans to deploy in robotaxi versions of its R2 SUV that will be available on Uber’s ride-hail app.
But if Rivian achieves full autonomy, most of that driving will be done in personally owned vehicles, Scaringe said in the interview, echoing previous comments he’s made.
“You know, 95% of the miles driven in the United States — so this is trillions of miles — 95% of these miles are in things that we personally own, so like you own it, or your household owns it. And so our view is it’s unlikely, even with Level 4 capabilities, that we’re going to see a dramatic societal shift away from that,” he said, referencing the Society of Automotive Engineers’ classification for autonomous vehicles that operate in a specific area.
That figure “may go from 95% to 90%, it may go from 95% to 80%, but still the vast majority of the miles driven for a lot of societal and psychological reasons are likely to stay the same,” he said.
It’s this belief that has Scaringe dreaming about the design of a fully autonomous, personally owned Rivian, he said.
As for what that looks like, though, Scaringe was mum.
“So we did R1, then we did R2, then we did R3. The thing after R3 is going to be called R4 — we just haven’t shown what it looks like,” he said. “It’s going to be cool. It’s going to be great.”

articles.title: Fragmentos de estátuas do faraó Ramsés II são encontrados "sem querer" no Egito
articles.text:
Duas estátuas de um dos faraós mais longevos e importantes da história egípcia foram encontradas. A descoberta foi feita por Khaled el-Shahat, um trabalhador local que encontrou vestígios das peças em sua propriedade, na vila de Behbeit El Hagar, na província de Gharbia.
Ao encontrar os fragmentos, Khaled informou o Ministério do Turismo e Antiguidades do Egito, que enviou uma equipe de escavação ao local. A descoberta foi divulgada na semana passada em comunicado da organização no Facebook.
A vila de Behbeit El Hagar faz parte de um importante sítio arqueológico do Baixo Egito. Às margens de uma ramificação do rio Nilo, o local abrigou um templo dedicado a Ísis, uma das deusas mais veneradas do Egito Antigo.
Para quem tem pressa:
- Duas estátuas de Ramsés II, um dos faraós mais importantes do Egito Antigo, foram encontradas na vila de Behbeit El Hagar, no Egito;
- Uma das peças representa a cabeça do faraó com duas coroas e pode ter pertencido a uma estátua de oito metros. A outra tem 2,4 metros de altura e mostra Ramsés II usando o nemes, um acessório tradicional dos faraós;
- O local abrigou um antigo templo dedicado à deusa Ísis e já revelou outros vestígios ligados a Ramsés II. Pesquisadores alertam que o crescimento urbano pode ameaçar a preservação do sítio arqueológico.
Ramsés II e o Egito Antigo
Filho de Seti I e Tuia, o faraó Ramsés II foi um dos maiores governantes do Egito Antigo. Chegando ao poder ainda jovem, aos 14 anos, ele ficou conhecido não somente por suas habilidades militares, mas também por sua “diplomacia”.
Com cerca de 66 anos de reinado, entre 1279 e 1213 a.C., Ramsés II teve mais de 100 filhos e foi casado com a rainha Nefertari, famosa e influente figura política do período. Considerada a “esposa favorita de Ramsés II”, possuía habilidade de leitura e escrita em hieróglifos, algo raro até mesmo entre a realeza.
Conhecido como “o governante dos governadores”, Ramsés II também deixou um importante legado arqueológico. Com templos e construções monumentais, foi um dos faraós que mais investiram em estátuas e obras em sua homenagem.
Seu templo funerário, o Ramesseum, na atual cidade de Luxor, contava com uma estátua de aproximadamente 17 metros de altura. O local também era dedicado à adoração de deuses como Amon-Rá, Ptah e Osíris.
Leia mais:
- Tecnologia revela que o Egito Antigo teve uma rainha com poder de rei há 5 mil anos
- Arqueólogos encontram “porta” de 4,7 mil anos que ligava mundo dos vivos ao dos mortos
- Após 4 mil anos, é revelado o segredo das princesas do Egito Antigo
As estátuas encontradas
A imagem divulgada representa um fragmento de uma das estátuas encontradas. A peça retrata a cabeça de Ramsés II com uma coroa dupla conhecida como “Nesu Bety“, que simboliza a união do Alto e do Baixo Egito sob o governo do faraó. Estima-se que a estátua completa tivesse oito metros de altura, enquanto apenas o rosto e a coroa medem 1,6 metro.
Na parte traseira da estátua há uma inscrição hieroglífica com o nome “Hor-Ka-Nakht-Mery-Maat”. Essa denominação alternativa de Ramsés II estaria ligada a um título associado ao deus Hórus. Seu significado seria algo como “Touro Forte, Amado da Justiça e da Verdade”.
A outra estátua encontrada tem 2,4 metros de altura e representa Ramsés II usando um “nemes“, acessório semelhante a um lenço utilizado por faraós. Na base do monumento, há duas inscrições: “Rei do Alto e Baixo Egito” e “Filho de Rá”, em referência ao deus do Sol do Egito Antigo.
Os achados relacionados a Ramsés II não são novidade no sítio arqueológico de Behbeit El Hagar. Em 2017, outros fragmentos associados ao faraó foram encontrados nas proximidades do templo de Ísis.
Além de mostrar o investimento do faraó em monumentos e construções em sua homenagem, as descobertas também reforçam a importância da preservação do local. Mahmoud Emam, pesquisador da Universidade do Cairo que participou das pesquisas realizadas em 2017, afirmou que o crescimento urbano da região pode dificultar as investigações e degradar vestígios históricos, tornando necessário um cuidado maior com a área.
Ana Figueiredo é editora de tecnologia do Olhar Digital. É formada em Jornalismo pela Universidade Federal de Uberlândia (UFU).

articles.title: Deux palettes de cartes graphiques Nvidia ont disparu : la cargaison valait 440 000 euros
articles.text:
Où sont passées deux palettes remplies de cartes graphiques haut de gamme, des RTX 5090 de Nvidia ? Voici la question que se pose le distributeur brésilien Oderço, dont la cargaison semble avoir été perdue après son arrivée dans un aéroport. Une affaire pas banale : la marchandise est évaluée à 2,5 millions de réais brésilien, soit près de 440 000 euros de prix de revient. C’est d’autant plus troublant que les cartes graphiques comme celle-ci sont très recherchées : elles permettent de faire fonctionner des IA, ou bien de miner des cryptomonnaies.
Une soixantaine de RTX 5090 disparaissent dans un aéroport au Brésil
Ce 16 octobre, le distributeur brésilien d’informatique Oderço a publié une vidéo sur ses réseaux sociaux. Il y révèle l’affaire de la disparition de ces cartes graphiques. Au total, une soixantaine de cartes graphiques auraient disparu, si l’on en croit les estimations de Toms’s Hardware. Réparties sur deux palettes, ces GeForce RTX 5090 sont fabriquées par Zodiac, avec plusieurs versions commercialisées.
Selon Oderço, les deux palettes sont bien arrivées au terminal de fret de Guarulhos, l’un des principaux aéroports d’Amérique latine, situé près de São Paulo. Mais ensuite, plus rien : lors des étapes suivantes de la chaîne logistiques, plus aucune nouvelle de ces palettes. Le distributeur n’a pas indiqué quand est-ce que cette perte a été constatée. Une surprise de taille pour Oderço : son président Oderço Matos l’affirme, jamais une marchandise n’a disparu en 38 ans d’activité.
Dans sa vidéo, Oderço Matos demande des explications à GRU Airport, à l’administration fiscale brésilienne ainsi qu’à la police fédérale : « J’aimerais savoir où elles sont. Deux palettes ne disparaissent pas toutes seules dans un aéroport international. » De son côté, GRU Airport reconnaît l’incident et indique avoir engagé les démarches nécessaires depuis. L’entreprise qui exploite cet aéroport de Guarulhos précise avoir prévenu les autorités et qu’une procédure d’indemnisation a été enclenchée. Mais pour le moment, on ignore ce qui a pu arriver à cette marchandise de cartes graphiques : erreur de manutention, problème douanier, vol. Toutes les hypothèses restent possibles.
Pourquoi la disparition de ces cartes graphiques est sensible
Lancée en janvier 2025, la RTX 5090 est la carte graphique grand public la plus puissante de Nvidia. Avec ses 32 Go de mémoire en GDDR7, elle est très recherchée chez les joueurs PC, puisqu’elle permet de faire fonctionner n’importe quel jeu avec les meilleurs paramètres graphiques. Problème, elle est parfois difficile à trouver et surtout, elle est chère. En France, sa Founders Edition avait été lancée il y a près de deux ans à 2 349 euros. Comptez plutôt… 6 500 euros en ce moment, comme l’a fait remarquer Cowcotland.
Une envolée des prix qui n’est peut-être pas terminée. Nvidia l’a reconnu après des rumeurs de l’arrêt de la production, l’entreprise a des problèmes d’approvisionnement. Des problèmes qui sont liées au fait que les fabricants se concentrent sur des puces faites pour faire fonctionner des IA. Elle privilégient ces modèles à plusieurs dizaines de milliers d’euros qui ne sont pas destinés au grand public, dont Nvidia. Si ces deux palettes ont été volées, les voleurs pourront revendre ces cartes graphiques, qui pourront être utilisées pour faire fonctionner quelques modèles d’IA, ou bien miner des cryptomonnaies.

articles.title: CoreWeave’s debt is becoming the whole AI industry’s problem
articles.text:
CoreWeave had a bad week last week. Its bonds slipped into distressed territory by a common definition — when investors demand 1,000 basis points more in yield than they’d get from government bonds. Last Tuesday Chamath “SPAC King” Palihapitiya noticed the distressed debt, and also asked whether the AI buildout was a private credit bubble. Its shares are down more than 20 percent since Tuesday’s close, which is kind of a lot! There even seemed to be some collateral damage in the market on other AI companies, too.
CoreWeave’s debt is becoming the whole AI industry’s problem
Does anyone else hear that ticking sound?
Does anyone else hear that ticking sound?
Now, I have also asked if the AI industry is a bubble, but when the SPAC King echoes concerns held by a lady whose ongoing question about AI is “How are we planning on affording this, champs?”, that’s a very different signal. When I say “yikes,” it’s one thing. When Elon Musk says it, that’s something else.
When you talk about wanting to tap into the enormous sums of money that insurers have, that’s the kind of thing that makes investors afraid that CoreWeave is going to borrow even more
To make things worse for CoreWeave, Brannin McBee, one of the company’s cofounders, told the Financial Times — also last week, on the same day as Palihapitiya’s post — that the company wants to have its debt be investment-grade, rather than junk, so that it can borrow from insurers, as their capital is, in his words, “unlimited.” This is not entirely unreasonable — earlier this year, CoreWeave secured its first investment-grade chip loan. But when you talk about wanting to tap into the enormous sums of money that insurers have, that’s the kind of thing that makes investors afraid that CoreWeave — already a massive debtor — is going to borrow even more.
“The problem is not that credit profiles have changed in the last year, it’s that we’ve got another year and a half of supply coming,” Bloomberg quoted John Yovanovic, co-head of leveraged finance at MetLife Investment Management, as saying.
I have seen people suggest that this means the AI bubble is bursting. I am not so sure. A plunging stock price is not necessarily financial doom. Stocks are an expression of confidence in a company’s future, not a reflection of day-to-day business. But CoreWeave has a lot of very expensive debt, and if that debt gets more expensive, that makes it even harder for CoreWeave to turn a profit.
CoreWeave is the poster child for AI debt, and as of its second quarter earnings, owed more than $35 billion. That’s partly because it pioneered GPUs as collateral for loans, and partly because CoreWeave doesn’t have a real business beyond selling compute, a business on which it does not make money — the company lost more than a billion dollars in the first half of the year.
The anxieties investors have around CoreWeave are, in fact, present for all neoclouds
So why am I not ready to do a victory lap on this? After all, I have suggested that this business is long-term unsustainable. The answer is “remaining performance obligations” from its customers — $103.7 billion of them as of the second quarter. About 40 percent of that money is due to CoreWeave in 2028, and the companies who’ve agreed to these contracts can’t cancel them except under some very limited circumstances. Its biggest customers are Microsoft, OpenAI, and what is probably Nvidia, though CoreWeave doesn’t disclose who its third-biggest customer is. Those three generated almost three-quarters of the company’s second quarter revenue.
Microsoft and Nvidia are probably good for the money — at least, as long as it benefits them to be good for the money. (I suspect they realize that if CoreWeave goes belly-up, there will be plenty of collateral damage in the market, so they are unlikely to push the company over the edge themselves.) OpenAI is shakier, but unless OpenAI is in significantly more financial distress than we all realize, CoreWeave is probably fine for a while. As long as it can continue to pay off its debt, the music keeps going. Only when the AI boom falters are we going to find out if it’s actually a viable business.
Still, the angst around CoreWeave has made things shaky for other companies that have taken out significant debt in the AI buildout — Oracle’s shares, for instance, which have fallen almost 10 percent in the same timeframe. There’s been a sell-off in Oracle bonds, too. The anxieties investors have around CoreWeave are, in fact, present for all neoclouds. It’s just not clear the bare-metal business is a good one.
Anyway, some people are buying the dip.

articles.title: Tenstorrent secures $1.5 billion USD at $6.2-billion valuation to challenge GPU dominance
articles.text:
Canadian-founded, United States (US)-based AI infrastructure company Tenstorrent announced today that it has closed $1.5 billion USD ($2.1 billion CAD) in Series E funding to fuel its global expansion plans.
The equity round, which was led by new US investors Trace Capital and Innovation X, gives Tenstorrent a post-money valuation of $6.2 billion USD (almost $8.8 billion CAD), more than twice the $2.6 billion USD mark that Tenstorrent was valued at when the company closed its nearly $700-million USD Series D in late 2024. Since then, Tenstorrent has begun shipping its Galaxy servers commercially.
“The future of compute is open, scalable, and owned by the people building on it.”
Jim Keller, Tenstorrent
Tenstorrent plans to use this capital to fund volume manufacturing of those Galaxy servers, the development of next-generation hardware and intellectual property (IP), and hiring, as it looks to compete with Nvidia and other established AI chipmakers and challenge traditional graphics processing unit (GPU) dominance in AI with an open-source approach it claims is cheaper, more scalable, and easier to customize.
“We built one architecture and sell it at every size,” Tenstorrent CEO Jim Keller said in a statement. “The future of compute is open, scalable, and owned by the people building on it.”
A Tenstorrent spokesperson told BetaKit over email that Canadian investors also participated in the round, but declined to share specific names. Tenstorrent’s existing Canadian backers include Export Development Canada, Toronto’s Georgian, and the Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan. Montréal-based early Tenstorrent investor Real Ventures sold its stake last year, returning the entirety of its $88-million third fund.
The Tenstorrent spokesperson also declined to share any more details regarding the structure of its Series E, including whether it involved any secondary capital, or disclose Tenstorrent’s total funding to date.
RELATED: US chip giant AMD to acquire Taalas
Founded in 2016 in Toronto by former AMD employees Ljubisa Bajic (who went on to build Taalas, which AMD recently agreed to acquire), Ivan Hamer, and Milos Trajkovic, Tenstorrent is developing what the company describes as “a general-purpose AI platform” for running large language models, video models, and image models.
The firm builds and sells AI compute “at every level,” from single cards and workstations to racks and superclusters, providing the hardware necessary for AI training and inference. Tenstorrent’s customers include chip designers, sovereign infrastructure providers, and inference platforms. The company also licenses its AI and RISC-V IP to clients who want to own and customize their silicon, including LG and Samsung.
Tenstorrent is betting that the future of AI inference is open-source, and views its software as a differentiator compared to competitors. “We built a scalable, open-source software stack because we believe customers want flexibility and control,” the Tenstorrent spokesperson said, adding that, “AI models keep changing, so hardware has to run whatever comes next.”
Tenstorrent’s clients and partners include FinTech firm Virtu Financial, data centre provider Equinix, and AI companies like ai& and Smallest.ai.
Keller, a renowned chip designer who also previously worked at AMD as well as Apple, Intel, and Tesla, took over for Bajic as Tenstorrent CEO in 2021. Tenstorrent quietly relocated from Canada to the US in 2023, moving its headquarters from Toronto to Santa Clara, California, to raise more money from American investors and prepare for an eventual initial public offering (IPO) on the Nasdaq or New York Stock Exchange.
RELATED: AI chipmaker Tenstorrent closes nearly $700-million USD Series D at $2.6-billion valuation
Despite this, Tenstorrent has retained a strong presence in Canada; Toronto remains its largest office, housing 200 of its 1,000 employees. The company also still makes a number of its parts at Vexos Canada’s Markham site.
This summer, The Information and Bloomberg reported that Tenstorrent has drawn takeover interest from larger US chipmakers Intel (Keller’s previous employer) and Qualcomm. While Keller told EE Times that he has met with the CEOs of both firms to pitch them on Tenstorrent’s hardware IP, he said an IPO remained the company’s target at that time.
The Tenstorrent spokesperson declined to comment on those reports, the status of those discussions, or the company’s IPO ambitions.
Last year, Tenstorrent made an acquisition of its own, snapping up Blue Cheetah Analog Design to bolster its in-house chip design capabilities, reportedly explored another fundraise, and shed 7.5 percent of its workforce amid a shift from enterprise to developer sales.
UPDATE (10/19/26): This story has been updated to note that Real Ventures sold its stake in Tenstorrent last year.
Feature image courtesy Tenstorrent.

articles.title: SA-founded clinical AI startup Healthleap raises $38m seed, Series A funding - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South Africa-founded clinical AI startup Healthleap has raised US$38 million in combined seed and Series A funding as it looks to expand its offering to more conditions.
Founded in South Africa in 2022 by siblings Josiah and Jemima Meyer, Healthleap has developed a platform that screens hospital patients for conditions that often go undiagnosed.
The platform reads each patient’s full electronic health record (EHR) every morning, including notes, labs, vitals, orders and problem lists, and flags risk. It then pushes risk scores into clinicians’ existing EHR workflows, showing care teams which patients need attention first.
Healthleap has initially focused on malnutrition, but now plans to expand its offering to cover additional conditions after raising the US$38 million round. The funding came from Sequoia Capital, First Round Capital and Hummingbird Ventures, and will also be used to grow Healthleap’s engineering, sales, customer success and product teams. The platform will be expanded to cover conditions including congestive heart failure, pressure ulcers and a range of hospital-acquired infections.
“Every week, millions of patients leave hospitals with unresolved health conditions that will erode their health and cost up to 10x more to treat in the long term,” said Josiah Meyer, co-founder and chief executive officer (CEO) of Healthleap. “Our goal is to help improve care and save lives by identifying those conditions now.”
Alfred Lin, partner at Sequoia Capital, said Healthleap was focused on finding patients who are being missed and getting them the care they need.
“The impact for both patients and hospitals has been inspiring, with one hospital seeing 39 per cent more malnutrition cases identified and treated, and US$11 million in incremental revenue in a single health system,” he said.
Josh Kopelman, co-founder and partner at First Round Capital, said the firm was drawn to Healthleap’s vision of every hospital using real-time AI to spot overlooked clinical risk, improve care and unlock reimbursement revenue.

articles.title: Protección de Datos alerta de un récord de brechas de seguridad
articles.text:
Protección de Datos alerta de un récord de brechas de seguridad
En el primer semestre se registraron tantos incidentes como en todo 2025, lo que se achaca al aumento de la ciberdelincuencia
La Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD) ha registrado un aumento importante en las brechas de datos personales notificadas durante el primer semestre de 2026. Entre enero y junio se recibieron 3.027 notificaciones, un 138% más que en el mismo periodo del año anterior. La cifra de brechas notificadas en el primer semestre supera a las recibidas durante todo 2025, lo que desde la AEPD achacan al creciente impulso del cibercrimen.
El incremento de las notificaciones coincide con la persistencia de amenazas ya observadas en periodos anteriores, como las asociadas a la ciberdelincuencia. El ransomware (los programas informáticos con los que los ciberdelincuentes secuestran equipos y piden un rescate para liberarlos) continúa provocando brechas de datos personales en organizaciones de distintos sectores y puede comprometer tanto la disponibilidad como la confidencialidad de los datos.
Asimismo, la Agencia detectó en marzo que un incidente producido en un único encargado del tratamiento (cuya identidad no puede revelar) provocó una brecha de datos personales en múltiples responsables. En julio, las notificaciones relacionadas con establecimientos hoteleros y sus encargados del tratamiento, generalmente proveedores de software de gestión de reservas, contribuyeron al aumento de las notificaciones recibidas por la AEPD.
En muchas de estas brechas, terceros no legitimados acceden a datos personales de clientes y a información de sus reservas, que posteriormente puede ser utilizada para realizar intentos de fraude.
La Agencia recuerda que notificar la brecha de datos personales a la Agencia es tan importante como informar a las personas afectadas. Esta comunicación, sobre todo en casos de riesgo alto, es clave para que las personas afectadas puedan valorar el riesgo de acuerdo con sus circunstancias particulares, y tomar las acciones que consideren apropiadas. En el primer semestre del año hubo más de 71 millones de comunicaciones a interesados al apreciarse la posibilidad de riesgo alto, según datos de la AEPD. Esa comunicación a las personas por parte del responsable del tratamiento es un elemento clave para determinar una respuesta diligente por su parte.
La Agencia ofrece varias herramientas para ayudar en la toma de decisiones a las organizaciones que puedan sufrir una brecha de datos personales. Asesora Brecha ayuda a valorar la obligación de notificar sin dilación indebida a la Agencia, mientras que Comunica-Brecha RGPD presta asistencia para decidir si las organizaciones deben comunicar la brecha de datos a las personas afectadas.

articles.title: Blue Origin veut lancer New Glenn plusieurs fois par semaine : la guerre des titans face à SpaceX est lancée
articles.text:
Blue Origin vise plusieurs lancements de New Glenn par semaine d’ici à la fin de la décennie. Un objectif vertigineux pour une fusée clouée au sol depuis le mois de mai.
Si la fusée géante a été couronnée de succès pour ses deux premiers vols, elle a vécu une année 2026 difficile. Après avoir placé un satellite sur la mauvaise orbite en avril, New Glenn a explosé sur son pas de tir un mois plus tard, détruisant tout le pas de tir au passage. Depuis, Blue Origin n’a plus de rampe de lancement pour son lanceur, et prévoit un retour des vols début 2027. Mais cela ne l’empêche pas de voir très grand.
New Glenn va monter en puissance
Ainsi, l’entreprise prévoit d’ajouter deux pas de tir supplémentaires pour New Glenn au Cap Canaveral, en Floride, en plus de deux autres déjà en construction. Elle veut aussi acquérir deux navires pour récupérer le premier étage de la fusée. Un nouveau centre d’intégration, bâti avec la Space Force, est également au programme : il permettra de préparer quatre satellites à la fois avant leur envoi dans l’espace.
Ce n’est pas tout. Une expansion industrielle estimée à 330 millions de dollars, qui doit s’achever à l’été 2027, permettra de fabriquer jusqu’à 150 étages supérieurs par an. Ils seront destinés à la version plus puissante de la fusée, New Glenn 9x4, capable d’emporter 70 tonnes en orbite basse et plus de 20 tonnes vers la Lune. C’est elle qui devrait être à l’œuvre dans le cadre du programme Artemis.
« Nous investissons dans des outils automatisés d’usinage, de soudage, de manutention et de contrôle qui rendent la production plus homogène et plus reproductible. Ces systèmes aident nos équipes à détecter les problèmes plus tôt et à concentrer leur expertise sur les tâches à plus forte valeur ajoutée », explique Blue Origin dans un billet de blog.
Une fenêtre s'ouvre
Le défi est de taille, car l’entreprise de Jeff Bezos doit prouver qu’elle est en mesure de supporter une cadence de vol hebdomadaire solide. À titre de comparaison, SpaceX a réalisé 165 missions avec sa fusée Falcon 9 en 2025, tandis qu’Elon Musk imagine plusieurs décollages par jour de sa mégafusée Starship. New Glenn, elle, n’a pris son envol que trois fois depuis début 2025.
Mais elle a un coup à jouer, alors que SpaceX devrait petit à petit mettre sa Falcon 9 à la retraite. Le besoin en nouveaux lanceurs est immense et à ce jour, Blue Origin est la seule autre entreprise à être capable de récupérer son premier étage. Reste à voir si elle saura monter en puissance sans autre déconvenue.

articles.title: Is your marketing AI tool driving profit or just noise? CleverTap co-founder Anand Jain weighs in
articles.text:
Is your marketing AI tool driving profit or just noise? CleverTap co-founder Anand Jain weighs in
At TechSparks 2026, CleverTap co-founder Anand Jain explained why marketing teams must move beyond basic generative AI productivity tools and adopt autonomous, real-time decisioning systems that drive genuine business profit.
Most marketing teams today use AI to save time on tasks such as drafting emails, creating image variants, and summarising long documents. However, Anand Jain, Co-founder and Chief Marketing Officer of CleverTap, a customer engagement and marketing automation platform, says basic tools that do these jobs rarely improve company profits.
In a masterclass on marketing strategy at TechSparks 2026, Jain urged leaders to look beyond simple shortcuts.
“We are going to talk about how you go from using AI for fun and games all the way to using AI to generate actual business results," he said.
While creating content using AI makes the job faster and saves time, Jain questioned whether it truly drives growth. "Is it actually going to impact business results or is it just more of the same?”
Traditional digital campaigns usually operate on a push model wherein companies decide what they want to sell instead of understanding what consumers want to buy. Whereas, a local shop assistant in an offline channel remembers a customer’s personal taste, notices immediate reactions, and suggests items tailored to their budget and style. Digital marketing must adopt a similar mindset.
“Not what I want to sell, (but) what my customer wants to buy. So you flip this around,” Jain said.
Instead of broadcasting generic promotions to large groups, modern marketing engines should interpret live customer actions to match individual needs.
This approach marks a shift towards the highest level of AI maturity, known as 'real-time decisioning'.
Marketing technology generally progresses through three stages. Level 1 focuses on basic time-saving tasks, level 2 covers experimentation such as A-B testing (comparing two ad versions to see which works better), and level 3 achieves true automated decisioning.
“You start with productivity, then you do experimentation, and the hardest thing is decisioning. When you actually are building an entire system for a party of one and that one person could be one out of several million that show up on your app or your website,” Jain noted.
Instead of bombarding users with discount codes, decisioning offers gentle helpful steps first, such as establishing brand trust or explaining product benefits.
Real-time decisioning relies on a single data hub that combines a customer’s historical profile with their immediate live actions. Traditional A-B testing usually stops after selecting one fixed winner, but decisioning uses reinforcement learning, a smart system that learns continuously from user responses and adjusts offers on the fly.
Furthermore, instead of relying only on propensity scoring (calculating how likely someone is to buy), decisioning uses uplift modelling. This method identifies the specific nudge, message, or channel needed to encourage an individual user to take their next positive step.
As automated systems manage campaign delivery across thousands of message options, the role of the marketer shifts from execution to strategic direction. Rather than manually drafting creative variants, marketers define high-level goals and establish strict operational limits.
“Your job is to create budget guardrails, brand guardrails, regulatory guardrails. Do not use the word 'free' if you are offering something, if you are a bank,”Jain emphasised.
By establishing clear boundaries, marketing leaders empower smart decisioning engines to work independently, keeping brand messaging safe while driving genuine commercial profit, he added.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Inside the Underground Market for Know Your Client Services
articles.text:
In February 2026, the operator of OnlyFake pleaded guilty in the United States for his role in a service that generated more than 10,000 fraudulent digital identity documents. Customers could create passports, driver’s licenses, Social Security cards, and documents from dozens of countries, then choose whether each appeared as a scan or a photograph of a physical ID.
According to the U.S. Department of Justice, the documents allowed cybercriminals to conceal their identities, circumvent identity checks at banks and cryptocurrency exchanges, and launder money.
The activity extends beyond fabricated documents. In underground communities monitored by Flare's platform, actors advertise manipulated photographs and videos, assistance with live identity verification, and accounts they claim have already passed identity checks.
Each year, Flare collects hundreds of thousands of search results related to Know Your Client (KYC) services and the trade in verified accounts. Activity observed between March and September 2026 shows how these offerings are packaged and promoted across underground markets.
What is KYC?
It is the process that financial institutions use to establish a customer’s identity and assess the risk of providing services to them.
Depending on the level of risk, they may validate the document, compare its photograph with a live image, confirm control of contact details, request information about the source of funds, and screen the customer against sanctions and politically exposed person lists.
KYC continues after the account opening through transaction monitoring and additional verification when information changes or activity appears unusual. The Financial Action Task Force describes customer due diligence as identifying the customer, understanding the purpose of the relationship, and monitoring it over time.
Is a Fake Identity Already Getting Past Your Checks?
Underground sellers package forged documents, deepfakes, and live verification help to pass identity checks.
Flare monitors criminal forums for exposed identities, stolen credentials, and active sessions, so you can invalidate access before it becomes account takeover or fraud.
Free 2-Week Trial
How KYC identity fraud works
The steps and image below illustrate how actors assemble the elements used in KYC identity fraud:
- Identity data establishes the applicant’s claimed personal details.
- Documents are presented to substantiate those details.
- Photographs or videos associate the claimed identity with a face.
- Device and browser preparation makes the application session appear consistent with a legitimate customer’s.
- Live verification is attempted by a human operator or with synthetic media.
Building the identity package
In March 2026, Flare observed a forum seller offering generated or edited identity and financial documents tailored to individual verification requests, including bank statements and other records that platforms may use to confirm an applicant’s address, income, or account ownership.
The offer of complete KYC packages shows how sellers adapt several documents to the requirements of a particular platform or customer. Names, photographs, addresses, and other details must remain consistent across the application because a mismatch can trigger rejection or further review.
This preparation creates the identity package later used during the facial or live verification stage.
Bypassing live identity checks
Many KYC systems compare the photograph on an identity document with a live image of the applicant. Some use passive liveness checks, which analyze a short camera recording for signs of a real person. Others use active checks that ask the applicant to turn their head, speak, blink, or read numbers shown on screen.
To bypass these checks, actors advertise altered photographs and AI-generated videos based on the face shown in the identity document. Some tools claim to change the operator’s appearance during a live session, allowing the false face to follow instructions in real time by replacing the image coming from the physical camera with altered footage.
Flare also observed advertisements for “human KYC,” in which a person completes facial or video verification using identity material prepared for the application.
In one recruitment post, an actor sought someone who could use deepfake tools to alter the camera image during a live check and appear as the person named in the identity documents.
In another example, Flare researchers observed a threat actor advertising guidance for a live number-reading check. The applicant must respond to content presented during the session, thus the offered bypass requires coordination and adaptation rather than the submission of a prepared object.
Support after the account is delivered
Flare researchers observed sellers offering continued verification and account-recovery assistance after delivering a completed account, and the recruitment post above included help when a platform requested another identity check following handoff.
When a later check requires the identity material or participant used during enrollment, the buyer may remain dependent on the seller, extending the original KYC service beyond the sale and helping preserve the appearance that the verified customer still controls the account.
Detecting KYC abuse
FinCEN has warned financial institutions that criminals are using deepfakes and fraudulent identity documents to bypass customer verification controls.
Its alert recommends examining the complete application because differences between the applicant’s identity information, supporting records, facial images, and account activity may reveal that several elements were prepared by different people or tools.
NIST recommends collecting identity documents and facial images directly during the verification session, checking whether they have been altered, and detecting software that replaces the footage from a physical camera.
Unpredictable instructions, such as asking an applicant to make a particular movement or read changing numbers, can make prepared recordings harder to use, while information about the device can help determine whether the session comes from ordinary customer equipment.
Applying these checks together gives organizations a better chance of detecting the combined use of false documents, deepfakes, and human operators described in underground KYC advertisements.
Flare gives organizations additional visibility by monitoring criminal forums for exposed identities, stolen credentials, active login sessions, and threats connected to their organization. Security teams can use these alerts to identify affected accounts, invalidate exposed access, and investigate identity-related activity before it develops into account takeover or further fraud.

articles.title: True Detective : on connaît enfin le duo d'acteurs de la saison 5, et c'est prometteur
articles.text:
True Detective : on connaît enfin le duo d'acteurs de la saison 5, et c'est prometteur
La prestigieuse série policière de HBO vient de dévoiler les deux grands noms qui seront au centre de sa cinquième saison, dont le tournage doit débuter en 2027.
La nouvelle enquête de True Detective est un peu plus proche de nous. Plus de deux ans après avoir été officiellement renouvelée pour une saison 5, la série de HBO Max est enfin en train de montrer de nouveaux signes de vie avec la révélation de son casting principal et de son ô combien important duo d'enquêteurs central : Nicolas Cage et Antonio Banderas.
Nic et Antonio après Woody et Matthew
Alors que des rumeurs entouraient déjà la présence de Nicolas Cage depuis plusieurs semaines, l'information a été officialisée ce week-end via une courte vidéo sur les réseaux sociaux de HBO Max.
Dans ce court "teaser" de 20 secondes, on peut voir les acteurs principaux des 4 précédentes saisons de la série, avant de voir apparaître les noms de Cage et Banderas, et un laconique "In Production 2027", annonçant un tournage pour l'année prochaine.
- Regardez la vidéo d'annonce de HBO :
Cage. Banderas. 
Season 5 of #TrueDetective starts production in 2027. pic.twitter.com/dLnG9hfCMo
— HBO Max (@hbomax) October 16, 2026
Nicolas Cage et Antonio Banderas prennent ainsi la suite de prestigieux acteurs, Matthew McConaughey et Woody Harrelson (saison 1), Colin Farrell, Rachel McAdams, Taylor Kitsch et Vince Vaughn (saison 2), Mahershalah Ali et Stephen Dorff (saison 3), et enfin le duo Jodie Foster et Kali Reis qui officiait dans la quatrième saison sortie début 2024.
Avec ce casting, True Detective continue sa tradition de couples d'acteurs talentueux, et parfois atypiques. Même s'il n'est plus vraiment besoin de les présenter, il est bon de la qualité unique d'un acteur comme Nicolas Cage. Lauréat d'un Oscar en 1996 pour Leaving Las Vegas, il a une carrière de plus de 50 ans avec des films aussi cultes et divers qu'Arizona Junior, Sailor & Lula, Rock, Volte/face, Benjamin Gates, Lord of War, Spider-Man : New Generation ou encore la récente série Spider-Noir.
De son côté, la carrière d'Antonio Banderas est tout aussi vertigineuse. L'acteur espagnol travaille depuis les années 80, et a tourné pour de grands noms tels que Pedro Almodovar, John McTiernan, Brian De Palma, Jonathan Demme, Neil Jordan ou encore Steven Soderbergh. Il a remporté le Grand Prix d'Interprétation masculine à Cannes pour le film Douleur et gloire en 2019.
L'histoire de cette saison 5 de True Detective est encore inconnue, mais on sait que les personnages incarnées par Nicolas Cage et Antonio Banderas s'appeleront respectivement Henry Logan et Rai Garcia, et que l'intrigue se situera dans la réserve sauvage de la Baie de Jamaica, au sud de New York.
Nous savons également que ce nouveau chapitre de la série sera toujours dirigé par la showrunneuse Issa López, déjà aux commandes de la saison 4. Il est bon de rappeler que Nic Pizzolatto, le créateur original de la série, n'est plus que simple producteur depuis cette même saison 4, qui fut aussi la plus regardée de l'histoire du show.
Aucune date de sortie n'a encore été annoncée pour cette saison 5, mais avec un tournage prévu pour 2027, il ne faut pas l'attendre avant 2028 sur la plateforme de streaming HBO Max.

articles.title: Des pirates se servent peut-être de votre serveur Plex pour miner des cryptos
articles.text:
Vous hébergez vos films et vos séries sur Plex ? Mettez votre serveur à jour sans tarder. Des pirates exploitent actuellement plusieurs failles du Plex Media Server pour générer des cryptomonnaies et gagner de l’argent. Les premières attaques réussies ont eu lieu il y a quelques jours.
À lire aussi : Des pirates profitent d’une fenêtre invisible pour miner de la cryptomonnaie grâce à votre PC
Un outil pirate qui combine 4 failles de sécurité
Les offensives reposent sur l’utilisation d’un outil pirate, Plex2Shell, récemment apparu en ligne. Cette méthode d’exploitation consiste à combiner quatre vulnérabilités pour exécuter du code sur le serveur sans avoir à s’identifier. En clair, un pirate n’a besoin ni du mot de passe, ni du moindre compte pour prendre le contrôle d’un serveur Plex à l’insu de son propriétaire.
Une fois à l’intérieur du serveur, les attaquants installent XMRig, un logiciel bien connu qui mine de la cryptomonnaie en exploitant la puissance des composants. Ce processus n’est pas sans effets sur le fonctionnement du serveur Plex. Rapidement, celui-ci va se mettre à ramer et à surchauffer. C’est pourquoi un appareil qui se met tout à coup à dérailler doit vous alerter. Notez que XMRig est massivement utilisé par les pirates qui souhaitent gagner facilement des cryptomonnaies. Fin de l’année dernière, le malware était déjà impliqué dans une vaste cyberattaque chinoise reposant sur React2Shell, une faille dans des composants utilisés pour faire fonctionner des sites web.
À lire aussi : « La partie émergée d’un iceberg » – après les frigos, quels appareils risquent aussi de se faire pirater ?
Comment se protéger des cyberattaques contre Plex ?
Pour éviter que des hackers prennent le contrôle de votre serveur, on vous recommande chaudement d’installer la dernière version du logiciel Plex Media Server. Bein avant le début des attaques, Plex a d’ailleurs corrigé les failles avec une mise à jour. Plex recommande de passer à Plex Media Server 1.43.3 (et Plex Desktop 1.115.0), ou à une version plus récente, pour éviter de se retrouver dans le viseur des pirates.
Attention, sur les boîtiers de stockage en réseau NAS et sur les installations via Docker, la mise à jour ne se fait pas toujours toute seule. Il vaut mieux vérifier à la main le numéro de version de votre serveur.

articles.title: 'A painstaking restoration': I saw behind-the-scenes of Hammer's Dracula 4K Blu-ray film reconstruction, and it's given me a new appreciation my discs
articles.text:
I knew film restoration for 4K Blu-ray couldn't be easy, but after seeing the process for Hammer's Dracula in action, I have a newfound appreciation for every disc
Giving to new life to this iconic horror
As a big 4K Blu-ray fan, it was a delight to visit the team at Silver Salt restoration several weeks ago, where I learned about the 4K Blu-ray restoration and HDR mastering process. I looked at the meticulous restoration work that goes into taking a film from its negatives, all the way to the finished product we collectors have stuffing our shelves.
During my visit, I got to speak to the team and hear their in-depth knowledge and expertise, and while we discuss plenty of movies and projects Silver Salt had worked on, the main movie I was there to discuss was the 1958 Hammer classic Dracula (known as Horror of Dracula in the US) starring Christopher Lee as the titular vampire, with Peter Cushing as Van Helsing.
Arguably Hammer’s most iconic movie and easily one of Silver Salt’s biggest projects, I saw a glimpse into the work being done to bring this classic flick to new life.
A painstaking restoration
For a more in-depth look at the initial stages before the restoration process (table inspection, cleaning and scanning) check out my previous article here. Once the digital files have been scanned in, these DPX files are handed over to the restoration artists, who must then go through the painstaking process of removing excess dirt, tidying up film grain (but not too much) and a general maintenance and tidy on each individual frame.
After being shown some of the work that goes into this restoration process on other titles (which you can again read about in my previous article) I speak with Paul Gowlett, the Project Lead for Hammer at Silver Salt Restoration. He’s overseeing Dracula and gives me a glimpse into the work that’s gone into revitalising this Hammer classic.
One particularly arduous process he shows me involves the movie’s opening sequence (a shot of the exterior of the castle, walking amongst some tombstones). During this shot, which lasts approximately 90 seconds, Gowlett points to the bottom of his monitor and points out a hair.
“It was part of the original presentation of the film, but was a production issue of the cleaning the camera gate, it is not intentional” he tells me. This brings me back to an earlier conversation I’d had with Anthony Badger, Head of Restoration at Silver Salt. He said “It can be a bit of an ethical dilemma on how much we intervene, but we need to consider if an extreme problem will take you out of the story.” Although the hair was part of the ‘original film’ it could serve as a distraction.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
A shot of Christopher Lee as Dracula, with the original file on the left and the remaster on the right, the latter of which shows much more color and depth
Gowlett informed me that each individual digital frame had to be checked for this hair. Each frame was removed digitally by using information from frames from later on in the shot, leading to the final image. The final result: a staggering 2000 frames. When I asked Gowlett how long it had taken him to remove this hair, he said several days. All for 90 seconds of footage. It was just a clear indication of how much work had gone into this project.
The other issue the team found with the original film (which was prevalent in the digital files) was a heavy amount of yellow staining. This yellow staining was only apparent when isolating the ‘blue channel of the image’ in the restoration process. Along with the hair and this staining, the team also made sure to ‘de-flicker’ the image to make the colours more stable throughout.
A stunning grade and updated soundtrack
Once the restoration work is complete, the files are handed over for grading. Dracula is being handled by Ray King, Head of Film at Silver Salt, while also being overseen by Mark Stanborough, Head of Restoration, Hammer Films, but during my visit, it’s Ray’s grading I’m seeing in action.
King has worked on most, if not all, of the Hammer titles handled by Silver Salt. He shows me how Peter Cushing’s skin tone has taken on a red tint after applying the HDR grade, saying how it’s the old stage makeup used during these sorts of productions being picked up during the grade. With some alterations, the result looks natural and lifelike, breathing new life into all characters in the clips I saw.
I’m also shown the opening title sequence again, only this time with the blood-red ‘Dracula’ text overlaid. To get this, King had to separate out the picture and the words into two separate layers, to get that blood-red color on the words themselves. He told me the color of the titles had faded, so he separated the layers and grades here to get the colors worthy of the words.
Color fade was an issue with the original raw files, but the HDR remastered grade revistlized these colors
Color fade was also true of the original elements that had been scanned in. A lot of the beautiful, bold colors weren’t popping as much and after showing me the red, green and blue waveforms, which highlighted the colors' degradation, he then showed me the picture after the grade had been applied. The difference was staggering.
The ornate furnishings, particularly a set of lush, velvet red curtains, now dazzled thanks to HDR. Instances of blood popped on screen and even clothing had a more dynamic, modern-day look to them. Again though, it was the skin tones of the people on screen that really impressed me, as this seemed to give the movie an almost-modern look. “Once we’re done, some of these movies like they could have been filmed last week” King says, rightfully admiring the HDR grade before us.
Even darker scenes have been given a facelift. Black tones are richer, deeper and, when paired with candlelight or lamps, create strong contrast that would look superb on some of the best OLED TVs. The grade in every clip I’m shown is nothing short of masterful and having tested multiple Hammer titles as part of the Blu-ray Bounty, Dracula is set to be the best.
I discussed with Stanborough later on about the new 5.1 soundtrack, something that’s been included with those other Hammer titles I tested. Stanborough talked to me about the process.
To achieve the 5.1 surround, AI was used to split the dialogue and music tracks before being mixed in a studio. “60-70% of the film is in surround, which is quite nice” but he also stressed the importance of “trying not to go too far and staying sympathetic to the original theatrical experience”.
When the movie returns to cinemas on 16th October (on a two week run until 1st November), viewers will experience the 5.1 soundtrack and HDR grade. The 4K disc lands on 23rd November, but whether you can get along to a cinema screening or are getting the 4K disc for your collection, after what I’ve seen and heard, fans will be in for a treat.
Dracula is in UK cinemas now, with the 4K UHD Limited Edition and Standard Editions arriving 23rd November. Check here for your nearest screenings.

articles.title: How Five35 Ventures made 3.5 its investment from one deal
articles.text:
In April 2022, Five35 Ventures, a gender-focused venture capital firm, wrote one of its first cheques to Complete Farmer, a Ghanaian agritech company that connects smallholder farmers to buyers, inputs and financing.
In March 2026, it sold its entire stake. Five35 says the sale returned 3.5 times its money, an internal rate of return of 38% over four years, and that Complete Farmer’s valuation rose from $6 million to $49 million over the same period.
Five35 is a pan-African fund that writes pre-seed and seed cheques into tech-enabled companies, focusing on markets beyond the big four of Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt and South Africa.
“We invest in exceptional businesses first, and the gender lens helps us find overlooked ones,” said Hema Vallabh, Five35’s founding partner. “Turning that value into realised returns for our investors is the real test of our success. Over the next six to 18 months, we will write bigger cheques now that we have an anchor, invest more in secondary markets, and then move into our harvest period, where we will look harder at exits.”
Exits are rare in African venture capital and rarer in agritech, according to Briter, which calls exit routes the sector’s tightest constraint, as fragmented supply chains and heavy working capital needs make it hard for companies to scale.
Vallabh, an engineer who founded the women’s entrepreneurship platform WomHub, runs the fund with general partner Fatou Touré. Five35 was raising $30 million in 2022. When the capital winter hit, Vallabh cut the target and raised her first $1 million through cheques starting at $35,000, mostly from first-time investors. The Mastercard Foundation Africa Growth Fund came in as an anchor in late 2025, and she expects to close in the next three to six months.
The sale was partly a commercial call and partly a strategic one: a first-time manager still raising money needed to show investors it could return cash.
Vallabh explains below what Five35 means by a gender lens, why it sold its best performer early, how it raised money as a first-time manager, and what female founders face when they pitch that most investors never see.
This interview has been edited for length and clarity.
How do you invest on the continent?
We invest at pre-seed and seed in companies that are significantly tech-enabled, and we are sector agnostic. We are pan-African, with a bigger focus on sub-Saharan Africa and a small allocation for North Africa. We invest in the big four of South Africa, Nigeria, Egypt and Kenya, and we are also excited about secondary markets such as Ghana, Senegal and the DRC.
We invest with a gender lens, and for us that goes beyond female founders. Our definition is about intentionality. A company can be co-owned or co-led by women, with a woman in a real leadership role such as CEO or CTO.
It can have an intentionally female workforce, with women spread across the business and not only at the lower levels. Or it can have an intentionally female customer base. The test is how we get more women participating in economic activity, living better lives and making more money.
For the customer base, the example I use is a male founder who builds a maternal health app. He is deliberately serving women, and those women become healthier and more economically active. We are a fully gender-lens fund, and for every investment, it has to be clear why we consider it one.
Complete Farmer has a male founder. How does it fit your gender lens?
It is a good example of our thesis. Desmond is a male founder, but Complete Farmer is a B2B and B2C platform, and when we invested, about 55% to 60% of its customers were women. Women also made up about 80% of its post-harvest workforce.
Because of the platform, more female farmers were taking their produce to market more efficiently and more profitably. The model gave farmers a market before they planted, which made their income more predictable and reduced waste. The gender impact was built into what made it a commercially compelling business.
Why did you build Five35 around a gender lens?
I have worked in this space for 20 years. I am an engineer turned entrepreneur turned investor. My first organisation was a non-profit that helped get more women into engineering. I later turned it into a commercial business, WomHub, which today works across talent, incubation and acceleration, co-working spaces and capital.
Someone who starts a fintech fund usually comes from banking. Gender is my specialisation. It is the right thing to do, and it is also an overlooked market that repeatedly shows better returns. Our pipeline comes from the WomHub network and two decades of work, and our partners help us support founders in ways other funds cannot.
At pre-seed and seed, you are backing the founder more than the numbers, because the numbers are not there yet. Research shows female founders are disadvantaged at this stage because they do not fit the mould.
Pitch competitions, to put it a little facetiously, are designed for the very articulate white male American founder. A more introverted founder may not pitch as well and still be very good at building her business. That is why we need more fund managers and investment committee members who look like the founders we want to back.
You argue that gender-lens investing is commercial. On what basis?
Our name comes from data. Research shows that adding more female entrepreneurs to the African economy could lift GDP by up to 5%, and that diverse teams can deliver a 35% higher return than all-male teams when the playing field is level. Our job is to help level it.
Our investors expect competitive financial returns, as they would from any other venture fund. We compete for capital with gender-agnostic funds. We care about impact, including job creation, and we want it alongside strong financial returns.
You see this in our portfolio. We first made 16 small investments, which I call our track record builders, and Complete Farmer was one of them. After our anchor investment, we made two new investments and three follow-ons. We now have 18 investments and a zero per cent failure rate. A few are struggling, and none has folded, and we are in year four, going into year five. These are unrealised gains, and the fund overall sits at about 2x.
Agritech exits are rare. What did Complete Farmer do differently?
Part of it was deliberate, and part of it was timing. Agritech is hard to scale because supply chains are fragmented, working capital needs are different, and operations are complex.
Complete Farmer did more than build an app for farmers. It built a full commercial supply chain platform that solved real problems on both sides of the market. Connecting production to predictable demand was unusual.
It also had strong leadership and strong execution, and it showed commercial viability fairly early. I am yet to see a solution in the market as complete as theirs. They have competitors in individual verticals, and building the full platform is what sets them apart.
Why did you invest?
They met our core criteria: pan-African, tech-enabled, early-stage, and gender lens. They were solving a problem on both sides of the market, and they had a strong founder.
Desmond was not positioning itself as a gender-lens company. When we looked closely, the strong female customer base was almost incidental. We saw a way to add value by helping them make that intentional and by helping with teams and governance. We were a small investor working alongside others, so I do not claim his success is because of us. But we knew where we could help a company that was already growing strongly.
Why did you sell in March?
It was the right time, and it made commercial sense. When Complete Farmer was raising its next round, we considered doubling down, but the valuation was beyond our range. Anything we could add would have been too small to matter.
We did discuss staying in for a bigger exit later. We will never know how that would have turned out. There was also a strategic reason. Our target as a fund is at least three times the money on invested capital, and this exit exceeded it. As a first-time fund that is still fundraising and heading into its harvest period, we needed to show that we can deliver exits. Going through a real exit process was also a learning experience.
We did not sell because we lacked faith in the company. They were one of our strongest performers and still have potential. It was a commercial decision, a fundraising decision and a disciplined capital allocation decision.
Who bought your stake?
We cannot disclose the buyer because of confidentiality agreements. It was a secondary transaction, and we sold our entire position.
Which other portfolio companies are close to an exit?
We are still in our investment period, and our focus is on deploying capital and doubling down on our strongest performers. We will invest quite aggressively over the next 18 months. We keep assessing liquidity, and sometimes the market approaches us to ask whether we will sell a position, but we are not actively chasing exits. Give us two or three years, and then we will be thinking seriously about them.
What support do you give founders beyond capital?
We are entrepreneurs investing in entrepreneurs, and we have a structured value creation method. We run portfolio community sessions for peer learning. One of our companies has made two acquisitions and walked the others through how it did them. We also work with each company on what it needs at this stage, such as building teams, governance structures and systems.
Our anchor, the Mastercard Foundation Africa Growth Fund, adds a second layer of technical assistance for our portfolio, both cash and in-kind. Through us, companies such as Complete Farmer can reach support they would not otherwise get.
We also lead by example on the gender lens. One female founder told me she does not think twice about sending me a WhatsApp message at 10 pm, whereas she would worry about it being misread if she sent it to a male fund manager. The level of sexual harassment female founders face when pitching is a systemic problem that we have to talk about, and many do not feel safe in rooms where nobody looks like them.
I had a baby in the last two and a half years, and I was fundraising while pregnant. Many of our founders told me they did not know that was possible. A female founder raising while pregnant gets asked how committed she really is or whether her life will change after the baby. A male founder rarely faces those questions. We build support for these realities into how we work, before and after we invest.
What was fundraising like as a first-time manager?
Tough. Fund managers have to raise from LPs before we can invest, just as founders raise to grow. Fatou and I are both first-time fund managers.
When I conceived Five35 around 2021, the market was in its heyday, with a lot of liquidity on the continent. Then the capital winter hit. We started with ambitious targets, and we had to adapt and aim for a smaller fund.
I went to my own network first. I looked for strong women, often executives, who had made money and invested in property or stocks, or as angels, but had never considered venture capital as an asset class or invested as an LP.
Through what I call the 35 Club, we took cheques from $35,000 upwards, mostly from women, and raised our first $1 million. Small cheques from individuals would never get us to a fund of $15 million or $20 million, and they let us make our first investments and build a track record. When we approached institutions, we could answer the question every first-time manager gets: what is your track record?
That led to our anchor investment from the Mastercard Foundation Africa Growth Fund, and other investors came in around it. We are now in what we call the final circle, with a small allocation is left, and we hope to close in the next three to six months. Would I have liked to raise more? Yes. The market has not allowed it yet.
How do you structure your investments?
We are a pure equity fund and do not do debt. Our preferred early-stage instrument is a SAFE, and that is how we first invested in Complete Farmer and most of our other companies.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. articles.title: La psicología dice que las personas que dejan el móvil boca abajo no es para ocultar nada; en realidad, es una táctica para evitar distracciones
articles.text:
Una comida, dos personas. Antes de que llegue la primera ración, uno de los comensales gira su teléfono y lo deja sobre el mantel con la pantalla hacia abajo. Hay quien lo interpreta como desconfianza, pero la explicación es otra: quiere librarse de las notificaciones y las llamadas entrantes y de la presión constante de estar disponible en todo momento. Al fin y al cabo, es solo una interpretación, y no se apoya en ningún experimento científico que estudie sus motivaciones.
Lo que sí han estudiado los experimentos es el efecto de tener el móvil a la vista.
En la Universidad de Essex, Andrew Przybylski y Netta Weinstein realizaron un experimento con parejas de desconocidos que hablaban entre ellos durante diez minutos con un teléfono o un cuaderno sobre una mesa cercana.
En su trabajo, publicado en el Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, el teléfono se asoció con una menor cercanía y una conversación de menor calidad y, en un segundo experimento, con una menor confianza y empatía, aunque solo cuando hablaban de algo personal: con un tema trivial no hubo diferencias. Después, otro grupo de científicos, ya fuera del Reino Unido, llevó la comparación a conversaciones reales.
Shalini Misra, de Virginia Tech, observó 100 conversaciones reales entre dos personas en entornos informales. Aquellas que tuvieron lugar sin ningún dispositivo a la vista salieron mejor valoradas. “En presencia de un dispositivo móvil hay menos contacto visual”, resumía la investigadora.
Matt Johnson, profesor en la Hult International Business School, recopiló varios de estos trabajos en su artículo ‘The Psychology of the Face-Down Phone’ (la psicología del móvil boca abajo). Según los experimentos que recoge, no hace falta usar el aparato para que afecte a la atención, y cuanto más difícil es la tarea, más pronunciado es el efecto.
También repasa los experimentos de Elizabeth Dunn (Universidad de Columbia Británica): en grupos de tres a cinco personas sentadas en una cafetería, quienes tenían el teléfono sobre la mesa (¡cualquiera podría hacer esto!) se sintieron más distraídos y disfrutaron mucho menos del encuentro.
¿Y qué ocurre con la práctica de poner el móvil boca abajo?
El experimento más conocido sobre el tema es el de “pérdida cognitiva” (“brain drain”) de Adrian Ward y sus colegas de la Universidad de Texas en Austin, en el que 520 estudiantes realizaron una serie de pruebas de memoria y razonamiento. El móvil se situaba o en otra habitación, o en el bolsillo o el bolso de los participantes, o sobre la mesa, donde se les indicaba que lo pusieran boca abajo en un sitio marcado del escritorio.
Fueron las personas que lo dejaron sobre la mesa las que obtuvieron los peores resultados en las pruebas. Según el trabajo, publicado en 2017, la mera presencia del propio smartphone reduce la capacidad cognitiva disponible, aunque no se use ni se piense en él.
Quienes lo dejaron en otra habitación obtuvieron los mejores resultados, mientras que los del bolsillo o del bolso obtuvieron resultados intermedios. Girar el móvil lo quita de la vista, pero el cacharro sigue ahí. En un segundo experimento del mismo trabajo, el efecto se mantuvo con el teléfono apagado del todo, algo que se repasaba en mayo de 2026.
¿Son suficientes las pruebas?
No del todo. Una réplica directa del experimento hecha en la Universidad de Western Ontario, publicada en Acta Psychologica en octubre de 2022, encontró que el efecto no se repetía: no hubo diferencias entre tener el móvil sobre la mesa, en el bolsillo o fuera.
Sin embargo, un equipo de la Universidad de Augsburgo juntó 22 estudios en un metaanálisis publicado en Behavioral Sciences en septiembre de 2023 y sí encontró el efecto, sobre todo en pruebas de memoria y atención, más débil en tareas sencillas y más fuerte en los estudios hechos en Asia que en los de Europa y Norteamérica.
Además, se aconseja precaución al sacar conclusiones sobre quien deja el móvil boca abajo, porque puede hacerlo por razones muy variadas: educación, costumbre o pura comodidad.
Cómo hacer que el gesto sirva para algo más
La forma más sencilla de que girar el teléfono tenga sentido es que lo silencie. Esta opción está disponible en los teléfonos Pixel de Google, en la función Silenciar al girar, que llegó a los Pixel 2 en noviembre de 2019 con una actualización de Bienestar digital y activaba el modo No molestar al poner el teléfono boca abajo.
Los propietarios de iPhone no tienen esta función incorporada, pero los modos de Concentración se pueden activar a mano o programar para que se enciendan solos a una hora concreta. Esto último es útil si la comida o la reunión tiene una hora fija.
Por último, no existe ningún ajuste, ni en iPhone ni en Android, que elimine la distracción de tener el móvil cerca durante una comida o una reunión. En el experimento de la Universidad de Texas en Austin, lo que mejor funcionó fue dejar el teléfono en otra habitación; la réplica de Western Ontario no encontró esa diferencia, y el metaanálisis de Augsburgo sí encontró el efecto, sobre todo en memoria y atención.

articles.title: Elon Musk promises to give every child in America a free SpaceX share next year
articles.text:
What just happened? Elon Musk makes a lot of big promises, not all of which come to pass, but it's hard to see how he'll renege on this one. The world's richest person says he will give one of his SpaceX shares to every child in America next year, adding that "this will be the first of many."
Musk explained the plan on his X platform. He didn't elaborate, so we don't know details such as what ages will qualify for a free share, how he intends to distribute them, and exactly when the giveaway will take place in 2027.
 – Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 19, 2026
It's estimated that Musk would be required to give a share to around 72 million people under the age of 18. SpaceX's share price is currently $146, so that would represent stock worth about $10.5 billion.
Musk certainly has plenty of SpaceX shares to hand out. The company's SEC filing in August showed he owned 6.42 billion shares as of June 30, including shares held in trusts for which he acts as trustee, restricted stock, and shares that could be issued upon exercising options.
Musk's announcement comes soon after Anthropic, xAI's rival, said it would commit 5% of its shares to a fund that will make donations for the "public good." The company later said that the fund could also receive another 2% of the firm's shares at its board's discretion. Anthropic's IPO could value the firm at more than $1 trillion
Musk responded to the Anthropic announcement by writing "I recommend giving the shares directly to the public. This is what I will be doing."
The moves also echo the thinking behind Trump Accounts, the tax-advantaged investment accounts for children that give eligible US citizens born between 2025 and 2028 a $1,000 government-funded head start. Families, employers, and other donors can add money, which is invested in funds tracking US stocks to help children build wealth as they grow up.
There's already a SpaceX connection to the program. The company's chief operating officer, Gwynne Shotwell, has pledged more than $320 million of her own SpaceX stock to help fund Trump Accounts for over two million children.

articles.title: Rank Math PRO WordPress Plugin Compromised in Supply Chain Attack
articles.text:
Users downloaded malicious versions of Rank Math PRO last week, after the WordPress SEO plugin was compromised in a supply chain attack.
Some version 3.0.123 packages contained malware that could allow attackers to take over websites if the plugin was activated, Rank Math says.
All users who downloaded or updated their plugin to the affected version between October 15, 2026, at 20:02 UTC and October 16, 2026, at 07:12 UTC might have been infected.
“We immediately removed the affected files and released a clean version, Rank Math PRO v3.0.124,” Rank Math says.
All users who installed and activated version 3.0.123 of the plugin during the affected window should treat their websites as compromised and should restore them from a clean backup created before the incident.
The malware may provide the attackers with persistent access to the compromised websites and could expose credentials, API keys, and other secrets.
According to Rank Math, the malware may recreate a hidden backdoor upon each page visit, and its persistence mechanism could make manual cleanup a difficult task.
Users who cannot restore the site from a backup should delete the Rank Math PRO plugin folder, remove a malicious database entry, block the attacker’s domain rank1cdn[.]com, and find and remove suspicious PHP files and unknown administrator accounts.
The malware may also deploy fake WordPress core files, modify .htaccess files to add rules for .cache files to execute as PHP code, drop .cache files containing PHP code, schedule tasks and cron jobs, modify other plugins and themes, and upload other files.
Additionally, the attackers could make changes outside the WordPress installation, and site admins should also look for SSH authorized_keys files, crontabs from other system users, suspicious processes, and other locations the web server user has write access to.
After verifying the website is clean, users should change all their passwords and install a clean version of Rank Math PRO.
